Errors are self-contained by construction: no URL, no request headers, no raw `cause` — only the machine `causeCode` survives, because Node/undici network messages embed `host:port` and may embed more in future runtimes. The only retained server strings (status text, raw `Retry-After`, observed content type) are scrubbed against the request's own credential material (whole sensitive-header values plus the credential-after-scheme for `Authorization`-style headers, matched with the D-025 `SENSITIVE_KEY_NAMES` vocabulary extended by one HTTP-specific rule — the `X-` extension prefix is stripped before the normalized-key lookup, so `X-Api-Key` stays in the scrub set; review finding), so a provider echoing a key back cannot smuggle it into an error (§15.4); marker-secret tests pin every failure class. (5) **Non-2xx = observation** — `TransportStatusError` carries `status`, scrubbed `statusText`, and the raw `Retry-After` value for tasks 106/107; the transport never retries and never parses. (6) **GET-only, `redirect: 'error'`** — the verified D-038 endpoints are stable GETs; refusing redirects removes any cross-origin credential-forwarding reasoning; widening the seam (methods, bodies) is a successor decision. `fetchImpl` is injectable (the logger-destination pattern) so classification is pinned against exact runtime shapes without patching globals.

**Reasons.** The done-condition — mock-server cases for every §7.2-required transport failure — makes real-socket reproduction the acceptance bar, and several design points needed pinning against the runtime rather than assumed: probed on Node 22.13.0, a refused connection is `TypeError: fetch failed` + cause `ECONNREFUSED` (but only on an unprivileged port — port 9 is a fetch-spec bad port producing a codeless `bad port` error), DNS failure is the same shape with `ENOTFOUND`, socket destruction before or during the body surfaces as `UND_ERR_SOCKET`/`terminated`, and undici's fetch does not use `node:http`'s agents — which is why the suite's no-network guard intercepts `*.invalid` hostnames inside its fetch wrapper _before_ DNS resolution, so the guarded integration case honestly pins the guard rejection as kind `network` while the `dns` class itself is pinned by unit tests against the verified `ENOTFOUND`/`EAI_AGAIN` shapes. A single total deadline was chosen over connect/body phase splits because §7.2 provides one number and phase-split timeouts would need two configuration values the spec does not define; `AbortSignal.any` composes without mutating the caller's signal. The transport-level cap is justified independently of §7.4: an unbounded read is a memory-exhaustion vector from a hostile or broken provider, and 64 KiB is the only response size the spec names. Two failure shapes the landed mock server (task 026, untouchable by the disjoint-file-set rule) cannot express — a body trickling slower than the deadline and a socket destroyed mid-body — are produced by file-local `node:http` servers inside the integration spec, still on 127.0.0.1. §17.1's "invalid JSON" bullet stays adapter-side: §7.2 maps invalid payloads to `Format changed` (§7.3 precedence ranks it above `Unreachable`), which is a parse outcome, not a transport class — the transport delivers text and the adapter parses.

**Consequences.** Task 099's Z.ai adapter builds on `providerFetch` and never calls `fetch` directly; task 105 maps `TransportError.kind` to §7.2 collection outcomes (D-034's outcome enum); tasks 106/107 receive `TransportStatusError.status`/`retryAfter` as their inputs. The taxonomy's kind strings, class names, and the no-echo error contract are API for those tasks: renaming any of them requires a successor decision. `DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` (15 000) and `MAX_RESPONSE_BODY_BYTES` (65 536) are the constants the polling configuration (062) and sanitizer (102) align with. The scrub's scheme-aware extraction means a bare credential echoed anywhere in retained strings redacts even when the scheme token is absent. The guard-interception behavior of `*.invalid` is now documented contract for every future transport test (105/106 inherit the same pin).

## D-043 — The verified Z.ai peak schedule ships as example configuration data with dossier provenance (spec §9.1, §9.2)

**Date:** 2026-10-30 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§9.1](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#91-official-zai-schedule), [§9.2](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#92-configuration-and-validation), [§6.2](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#62-configuration-contract) · **Tasks:** [112](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-014, D-018

**Decision.** Task 112's encoding artifact is `docs/config.example.json` — a complete example `config.json` (all six sections at their spec defaults, one provider, one account) whose `providers["zai-coding-plan"].peakHours` is spec §9.2's sample verbatim: window `zai-weekday-peak`, Monday–Friday `14:00`–`18:00`, `multiplier: 1.0`, **explicit** `offPeakMultiplier: 0.5` (§9.2: "for the Z.ai schedule it must explicitly be `0.5`"), `timezone: "Asia/Singapore"`. Pinned interpretations: (1) **Provenance lives in documentation, not the JSON** — the contract closes every object (`additionalProperties: false`, D-014) and `parseJson` is strict `JSON.parse`, so a provenance key, `$schema` pointer, or comment inside the example would make it fail the very validation it exists to demonstrate; the official source URLs (<https://docs.z.ai/devpack/overview> corroborated verbatim by the Team Plan page), both retrieval dates (spec §9.1's 2026-10-28 check; task 094's 2026-10-30 re-verification), and the rate semantics (peak `1.0` = the standard credit rate itself; off-peak `0.5` = "charged at 50% of the standard credit rate", sources 1 and 14) are documented in the dated task-112 section of `docs/providers/zai-coding-plan.md`, with a pointer added in `docs/config-schema.md`. (2) **The example demonstrates the `apiKeyEnv` secret source** (§6.3) rather than a placeholder `apiKey` — no secret-shaped string belongs in a committed artifact (§15, §17.1 discipline). (3) **`app.timezone` is `UTC`** in the example — a valid IANA name deliberately different from the schedule zone, illustrating §9.2's independence of the display and schedule time zones. (4) **The example is data only**: no schema or `src/` change; `test/integration/example-config.spec.ts` consumes the landed parser read-only (`loadConfigFile` on the committed file) and pins both halves of the done-condition executably — the parsed schedule equals the verified schedule, and the dossier section contains the source URLs, both retrieval dates, and the example path. Legacy plan V2 request multipliers (dossier source 9: "1×/3×", "0.4×/1.2×") are deliberately not encoded — they meter legacy requests, not current credits plans.

**Reasons.** The layout note fixes placement ("example configuration (112) in `docs/`", `docs/architecture/package-layout.md`), and `*.example.json` naming keeps tooling from mistaking it for a live `config.json`. Encoding §9.2's own sample verbatim is the strongest reading of "the example config matches the official source": the sample is the spec's transcription of the official pages, and task 094 re-verified both statements on those pages verbatim. Keeping provenance out of the JSON is forced by the closed contract and serves the artifact's purpose — an example that cannot load through the real parser would document a configuration the application rejects. The provenance test follows the repository's executable-docs-contract pattern (`config-schema-published.spec.ts` precedent): the done-condition ("includes the retrieval date/link") becomes a check instead of an assertion in prose. `apiKeyEnv` over a placeholder key avoids shipping a string that looks like a credential — the same discipline fixtures follow. Schedule interval _calculation_ stays out (task 114) and schema validation rules landed with 061/067; this task adds exactly the seed data D-014 item 6 said vendor values would be.

**Consequences.** `init` (future task) and any future schedule re-verification (task 127) update the schedule by editing the example (and its test-pinned values) plus a new dated dossier section — a schedule change that skips the test fails `make check`. The example path, the provider key `zai-coding-plan`, and the window id `zai-weekday-peak` are now referenced from three artifacts (example, dossier, test) and `docs/config-schema.md`; moving any of them requires updating all references. The provenance section of the dossier is the canonical place future rate-semantics changes must land before the example changes.

## D-044 — CLI dispatch skeleton: parseArgs strict parsing, the 0/1/2 exit-code contract, an injected writer seam, and a jiti-compatible launcher delegation (spec §5.2)

**Date:** 2026-10-30 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§5.2](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#52-cli-commands), [§5.1](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#51-supported-environment) · **Tasks:** [128](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-012

**Decision.** Task 128 pins the CLI's mechanical contract, into which tasks 129–145 plug command bodies: (1) **Parsing** — `node:util` `parseArgs` in strict mode (built-in, no new dependency) over per-command option tables declared in `src/cli/commands.ts`; every command automatically gets `-h, --help` — a reserved-name guard in `parseCommandArgs` fails any table that shadows it loudly; options carry an optional `description` rendered in command help; `parseArgs` failure messages are trimmed to their first sentence and decapitalized because Node appends generic `--`-placement advice that buries the actual problem. (2) **Exit codes** — 0 success (including `--help`, `--version`, and the no-arguments general help: an empty invocation is a question, not an error); 1 command failure (a thrown handler error or a not-yet-implemented command — valid usage, missing feature); 2 usage error (unknown command/subcommand/option, missing `service` subcommand, unexpected argument — including a bare end-of-options `--`). (3) **Output** — `console` stays banned in `src/**` (spec §15.4 rule), and the CLI's stdout/stderr product flows through the injected `CliOutput` seam (`systemOutput()` = direct `process.stdout`/`stderr` writes, the pre-logger fatal-diagnostics precedent of `src/server/main.ts`); help and version go to stdout, every error to stderr as `quotameter [<command path>: ]<message>` with a `Try 'quotameter … --help'` hint on usage errors. (4) **Precedence** — at global level `--version` beats `--help`; at command level flags are validated before help is shown, so `status --bogus --help` is a usage error rather than disguised help. (5) **Pluggability** — `runCli(argv, deps)` in `src/cli/main.ts` never calls `process.exit` and takes the version (the launcher reads `package.json`; `src/` cannot import it — the layout test forbids imports leaving `src/`), the output sink, and the whole command table as injections; subcommand nesting is exactly one level (`service install`/`uninstall`), all §5.2 defines. (6) **Launcher** — `bin/quotameter.mjs` keeps its runtime gate first, answers a leading `--version`/`-v` itself (printing exactly the bare package version — the fixed CI install-smoke contract), then delegates via a dynamic import resolved as `mod.runCli ?? mod.default?.runCli` (jiti mounts the TypeScript module as CommonJS during development/tests; the published build is real ESM). The specifier is deliberately `'./../src/cli/main.js'` rather than `'../…'`: jiti's loader hook skips specifiers not starting with `./` or `file://`, and the plain form falls through to Node's resolver, which cannot map the `.js` spelling onto the TypeScript source. An import failure with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` (the tarball ships `bin/` without compiled `src/` until the packaging tasks) reports a clear reinstall message and exits 1 instead of a resolver stack trace; any other module failure surfaces as itself. All exits after the gate set `process.exitCode` and let the event loop drain — an immediate `process.exit()` can truncate buffered pipe writes.

**Reasons.** The done-condition — all §5.2 commands in help, unknown commands failing clearly — fixes the command set (init, run, start, stop, restart, reload, status, logs, service install/uninstall, passwd, doctor, in spec order and wording) and leaves parsing, exit codes, output routing, and launcher mechanics as the design space. `parseArgs` strict mode is a standard-library parser with per-command option bags, so no flag grammar is hand-rolled and no dependency added (the task's constraint); its verbose error tail is cosmetic damage contained by the first-sentence trim, pinned by tests on the pinned runtime. The 0/1/2 split is the classic CLI convention (usage ≠ failure) and gives scripts a stable contract before real commands exist; stubs exit 1 because the invocation was valid — silently succeeding (bootstrap's exit-0 "not implemented" line) would mislead automation. The writer seam satisfies both the letter of the `no-console` lint rule and its intent: CLI output is product, not logging, and tests assert exact bytes through a recorder. The version injection keeps `src/cli` free of `package.json` reads (a layout violation) and lets unit tests pin `--version` without filesystem fixtures. The launcher's fast path preserves two landed contracts untouched — the CI assertions that `quotameter --version` prints exactly the package version and that Node below 22.13.0 fails with the gate message naming the minimum — because a static import would hoist above the gate, delegation is dynamic; the `runCli ?? default` shape was verified empirically in both worlds (jiti 2.7 on Node 22.13.0 and real ESM), as was the `./`-prefix requirement.

**Consequences.** `src/cli/` gains `main.ts` (dispatch), `commands.ts` (the table, context/handler types, the shared `notImplemented` stub), `parser.ts` (`parseCommandArgs`, `UsageError`), `help.ts` (pure renderers), and `output.ts` (`CliOutput`, `systemOutput`); `bin/quotameter.mjs` extends to delegation. Tasks 129–145 each replace one `stub(...)` row with a real handler plus its option declarations — the dispatcher, parser, and help renderers pick them up without structural change. The error-line format, exit codes, help layout, and the bare-version `--version` output are CLI contract: changing any of them requires a successor decision. `test/unit/cli-dispatch.spec.ts` pins the dispatch contract in-process (injected recorder and fake tables) and `test/integration/cli-bin.spec.ts` pins the launcher child-process behavior via jiti, extending task 060's runner pattern. The launcher fallback message and the `mod.runCli ?? mod.default` interop are removed by the packaging tasks (184–186) once compiled `src/` ships in the tarball.

## D-045 — Mutation testing moved from the push gate to a daily scheduled workflow with issue triage (supersedes the per-push placement of task 055)

**Date:** 2026-10-30 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§17.3](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#173-enforced-quality-thresholds) · **Tasks:** [055](plan/tasks.md)

**Decision.** Stryker mutation testing no longer runs in the per-push CI job or in `make check-all`; it runs once a day (02:17 UTC, plus manual dispatch) in `.github/workflows/mutation.yml` against `master`. The workflow upserts a single rolling GitHub issue labeled `mutation-report` (body = latest report, one comment per run preserves history) and fails visibly when the score is below the configured break threshold. `make check-all` therefore mirrors the per-push CI exactly (static, audit, licenses, coverage-gated tests, build, E2E, packaging); `make mutation` remains for manual runs, and the JSON reporter was added to `stryker.config.mjs` to feed the issue.

**Reasons.** The mutation phase grows linearly with `src/**` (453 mutants at task 055 → 3,555 after Stage 7–9 foundations) and reached ~30 minutes on 8 cores, dominating every push, every `make check-all`, and every cycle finalization while its per-commit signal rarely changed between commits. §17.3's intent for mutation is guarding the critical modules over time, not blocking each push; a daily cadence with a persistent triage issue preserves the visibility (score, per-file table, survived-mutant list with `file:line`) at 1/30th of the cost. The break threshold (60) still fails the daily job — visibly, in the issue — instead of silently.

**Consequences.** Push latency and cycle finalizations drop by the mutation runtime; a below-threshold regression is noticed at most one day late, surfaced by the issue. The per-push CI and `make check-all` stay in exact parity (the invariant documented in `docs/agents/gotchas.md`). When the critical modules named by §17.3 (reset detection, peak-hours, sanitization, downsampling) all exist, revisit the `mutate` scope and per-module thresholds from the daily report's data. History note: task 055 placed mutation in per-push CI; this decision changes the placement, not the tooling or thresholds.

## D-046 — The `quota_events` table: §12.1 reset-event rows with a CHECK-enforced JSON evidence contract, account-pinned snapshot reference, and the spec-named account/metric/time index (spec §11.2, §12.1)

**Date:** 2026-10-30 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§11.2](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#112-required-logical-tables), [§12.1](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#121-quota-reset-events), [§8.2](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#82-accounts), [§11.1](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#111-database-settings) · **Tasks:** [085](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-014, D-021, D-027, D-031, D-032, D-034, D-036, D-039

**Decision.** `0005-quota-events` — the fifth entry of the canonical `MIGRATIONS` list (schema version 5) — creates the `quota_events` table, its spec-named index, and the parent key its account-pinning foreign key needs, as one STRICT `CREATE TABLE` plus `CREATE INDEX`/`CREATE UNIQUE INDEX` statements through `context.database` (no transactions inside; D-027), with these pinned interpretations: (1) **Column set exactly §11.2's row** — `account_id TEXT NOT NULL`, `metric_key TEXT NOT NULL` (the same non-empty-string semantics as `metric_values.metric_key`; §11.2 lists no window or enum columns for events — the D-032 exact-set rule — so window evidence lives in `details`), `event_type TEXT NOT NULL`, `event_at INTEGER NOT NULL` (§11.1 epoch ms, writer-supplied, no SQL default), nullable `run_id INTEGER` (the optional snapshot id, carried by the D-036 identity), `details TEXT NOT NULL`. Names refined per §11.2's "may refine physical details": `event_type` for the spec's "type" (qualified the way `accounts.status` and `collection_runs.outcome` carry their spec words — a bare `type` column reads as `sqlite_master.type` in ad-hoc SQL), `event_at` for the house `_at` epoch-ms suffix. (2) **Event type is the closed version-1 set** — `quota_events_type` admits exactly `'RESET'`, case-sensitively; §12.2's gap/failure markers are API vocabulary computed from `collection_runs`, never stored event types, and a future event type is a code change plus a migration (§11.2 "type (`RESET` in version 1)"). (3) **`event_at` follows §12.1's rule and is deliberately unpinned** — the previous point's `resetsAt` when it lies between the two compared snapshots, else the new snapshot's collection time; both are writer-supplied values from the compared points, not database time, and it is not FK- or CHECK-tied to the referenced snapshot's `collected_at` because the two legitimately differ (and CHECKs cannot span tables — the D-032/D-034 clock-skew leniency). (4) **The `details` JSON contract: a SQL-enforced audit minimum plus a writer vocabulary.** Storage enforces, in declaration order: `quota_events_details_json` (`json_valid` — declared first so malformed JSON fails by constraint name before the shape checks' `json_type` would throw an un-named error), `quota_events_details_object` (`json_type(details) = 'object'`), `quota_events_details_reason` (a `$.reason` that is text and non-empty — which §12.1 condition fired and any conservative-approach exception note), and `quota_events_details_points` (`$.previous` and `$.current` are objects — the §12.1 compared points, "each new snapshot with the previous **valid** point"). The path checks coalesce a missing key's NULL `json_type` to a mismatch because in SQLite a NULL CHECK result passes — the plain `= 'text'` form demonstrably admitted `{"previous":{},"current":{}}` on the pinned runtime (found by empirical probe, not assumed). Beyond the minimum, `details` is the D-046 **writer contract**: camelCase point fields (`runId`, `collectedAt`, `used`, `remaining`, `percentUsed`, `percentRemaining`, `resetsAt` — only those the compared points actually carried), optional `tolerance` (the rounding tolerance condition 1 applied), and optional `eventTimeSource` (`'previous_resets_at'` | `'current_collected_at'`); tasks 117/118 produce it and task 088's repository encodes/decodes it. CHECKs cannot validate per-key membership of arbitrary objects (the D-039 JSON-rejection rationale), so SQL stops at the trio every §12.1 reset event is meaningless without. The reason is deliberately a free non-empty string, not a CHECK enum: the reason vocabulary is detection policy, not a stated record property (the D-034 rule). (5) **Account/snapshot linkage = the D-036/D-039 both-foreign-keys shape** — the composite `(account_id, run_id)` references `snapshots (account_id, run_id)` `ON DELETE CASCADE`, a parent key this migration exposes by adding the unique index `snapshots_account_run` (unique-by-`run_id` anyway — the redundant-parent-index price D-036 and D-039 already paid for structural pinning), alongside the direct `account_id → accounts` FK. One constraint proves the snapshot exists and the event's account matches it — a mismatched event would corrupt exactly the account/metric/time index this table exists to serve — and the parent-side NO ACTION default freezes a referenced snapshot's identity against post-hoc UPDATEs. A NULL `run_id` satisfies the composite FK (SQLite treats any NULL child key as satisfied) while the direct FK still proves the account exists. (6) **No primary key, no UNIQUE constraint** — no query references an event id (§13 returns event lists), so none is minted (the D-036/D-039 no-second-identity rule), and §12.1 states no per-snapshot event uniqueness, so none is invented; duplicate prevention is the writer's (one comparison per metric per snapshot, task 117). (7) **Index** — `quota_events_account_metric_time (account_id, metric_key, event_at)` is §11.2's "events by account/metric/time" wording, named the D-034 way; its leading `account_id` serves both cascade scans (the D-034 one-index-two-jobs pattern), and no retention-leading index is added (§11.2's required list names only account/metric/time; retention is task 091's).

**Reasons.** The done-condition — event queries indexed, deletion behavior tested — plus the task scope (storage shape only; detection 117/118, repository 088, retention 091 are not this task's) fixes the table as the §11.2 row and leaves the design freedom in the JSON contract, the linkage, and the index — each resolved by the landed house pattern rather than a new debate. The JSON evidence contract splits at exactly the line SQLite can enforce: validity, object-ness, and the audit-minimum keys are CHECK-expressible (with the NULL-coalesce repair the probe made necessary), while per-key membership of arbitrary point objects is not — the same expressibility boundary D-039 hit, resolved there by a bitmask and here by a writer contract, because §11.2 explicitly demands a JSON details column and the evidence vocabulary is open-ended by nature (percentage-only metrics, absent reset times, future detector notes). The composite-FK account pinning is D-036's technique applied for D-039's reason: an event claiming one account while citing another account's snapshot would silently mis-file the event in the timeline queries the index serves, and "unrepresentable-invalid beats writer-validated-valid" has carried three schema tasks in a row (D-032 charsets, D-034 enum, D-036/D-039 linkages); the redundant parent index is the known, twice-paid price. The optional-`run_id` reading keeps §11.2's word ("optional snapshot id") against the practical always-present evidence snapshot — the D-034 encode-only-what-the-spec-states rule. No `event_at`-leading retention index: §11.2's required list is the spec's own scope decision, snapshots and runs carry the same daily-cleanup shape, and 091 owns that job.

**Consequences.** `MIGRATIONS` carries five entries; a fresh database migrates to schema version 5 at startup, `schemaVersionStatus` reports `up-to-date` at version 5 after the run, and the schema-4→5 forward test §11.4 requires lives in `test/integration/quota-events.spec.ts`. Task 081–084 canonical-set pins in `test/integration/accounts.spec.ts`, `collection-runs.spec.ts`, `snapshots.spec.ts`, and `metric-values.spec.ts` were updated to the grown set (D-031's planned growth, recorded here as those tests' deliberate fixture changes), and `snapshots.spec.ts` gained `snapshots_account_run` in its pinned index list — with one behavioral side effect recorded there: the duplicate-run UNIQUE violation is now reported against the two-column parent key (`snapshots.account_id, snapshots.run_id`) rather than the `run_id` autoindex, because SQLite checks the newer index first; the test accepts either form. Task 088's repository owns typed reads/writes, supplies `event_at` per §12.1's rule from the compared points (D-021), serializes `details` (and may rely on the CHECKs to reject malformed evidence), and maps `event_type`; tasks 117/118 own detection and the reason vocabulary; 091's cleanup deletes events by the account/time scans the existing index serves. The table, column, constraint, and index names (including `snapshots_account_run` and `quota_events_account_metric_time`) and the `details` audit-minimum keys are on-disk contract: renaming any of them, or widening `event_type`, requires a successor decision (a future event type migration must also revisit the `details` CHECKs, which assume §12.1's comparative evidence shape). Raw `DatabaseSync` test handles default to `foreign_keys=OFF` (D-034's pinned note) — the FK tests set the pragma explicitly.

## D-047 — Z.ai adapter contract: allowance/consumed value semantics, integer-percent scale, stable metric identities, per-endpoint degradation (spec §8.3, §8.4, §7.2)

**Date:** 2026-10-30 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§8.3](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#83-zai-coding-plan-integration-contract), [§8.4](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#84-normalized-snapshot-and-metric-model), [§7.2](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#72-retry-and-error-behavior) · **Tasks:** [096](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-010, D-038, D-040, D-042

**Decision.** Task 096's dossier section ("Adapter contract — implementation-facing rules for tasks 098-100") pins what D-038/D-040 deliberately left open, as the contract tasks 098–100 implement against: (1) **Value semantics** — `limits[].usage` is the window **allowance** (→ `limit`), `currentValue` the **consumed** amount (→ `used`), `remaining` the remainder: the only reading consistent with the observed identities `currentValue + remaining = usage` and `usageDetails` summing to `currentValue`. The prototype's "used/total" rendering of `usage` is rejected as a display artifact contradicted by the arithmetic. An entry whose supplied triple violates `used + remaining = limit` is emitted invalid (numeric values dropped, `resetsAt` retained per D-010, stable `invalidReason` strings supplied in the section) — not a parse error, and the response's other entries survive. (2) **`percentage` is integer percent (0–100), not per-mille** — the capture's `percentage: 19` against an ≈18%-consumed 5-hour quota (main-session capture-time context, recorded as given evidence) fits percent only; the monthly `percentage: 1` at exactly one per-mille consumed cannot discriminate, which is why 095's echo kept the question open. Rounding direction is unpinned: the adapter passes values through verbatim; `percentRemaining = 100 − percentUsed` (always derived, listed in `derivedFields`, so the two sum to exactly 100); `percentUsed` derives as `100·used/limit` only when `percentage` is absent and both fields are supplied; percentages are never cross-validated against absolutes (integer rounding makes 1-vs-0.1% expected noise), and absolutes are never derived from percentages. (3) **Recognition identities** — entries recognized by `(type, unit)`: `(TIME_LIMIT, 5)` → `mcp-monthly`/`MONTHLY`/`REQUESTS`; `(TOKENS_LIMIT, 3)` → `tokens-5h`/`ROLLING_WINDOW` with `windowSeconds = number × 3600` and `PERCENT` while only `percentage` is supplied; `unit 6` (either type; unobserved) → `weekly-quota`/`WEEKLY`. Unknown `(type, unit)` pairs are skipped and logged — not metric rows (no invented series keys fragmenting `metric_values` history) and not parse errors; `limits: []` or all-unknown entries are a valid zero-metric snapshot. (4) **`planName` = `data.level` verbatim**, fallback = the subscription record with `inCurrentPeriod === true`, else the first `status === "VALID"`, else absent. (5) **Envelope** — success is `code ∈ {0, 200}` in number or string spelling (prototype tolerance); anything else — other/missing `code`, wrong-typed containers — is a parse error (`Format changed` via task 105) with `msg` retained as the sanitized diagnostic; error codes are never interpreted (no sample exists). Strictness is two-tier: envelope/containers strict, entry fields tolerant. (6) **Cycle policy** — all three D-038 endpoints are fetched sequentially per cycle through `providerFetch`; endpoint 1 (quota) failing — transport or parse — fails the cycle, endpoints 2 (subscription) and 3 (reset cards) fail soft (context lost, cycle succeeds, failure logged); reset-card data maps nothing in v1 (card shape is prototype-source only) but stays fetched — its `last*ResetTime` fields are the provider's declared-reset record (the same kind of evidence §12.1's detection acts on via metric `resetsAt`; nothing persists them in v1), and re-adding a dropped request would be a contract change. `validateCredentials` (098) uses `GET /api/coding/paas/v4/models`, status-based: 2xx valid, 401/403 rejected, any other outcome unavailable. (7) **Flagged assumptions** (ledger in the section, each with its falsifier): auth rejection is assumed HTTP 401/403 per §7.2 — an envelope-encoded rejection would read `Format changed`; absolute-bearing `TOKENS_LIMIT`/weekly entries (unobserved) map under the arithmetic reading with `unit: CREDITS` (094's documented credit metering beats the `TOKENS` type name); the `application/json` content-type declaration and freedom from extra required request headers are assumed; `targetType=PERSONAL` is the only defined scope; subscription record selection prefers `inCurrentPeriod` on the strength of one capture where the candidate rules coincide.

**Reasons.** D-038's consequences reserved exactly these choices for 096 ("096 decides the metric mapping and the error schema"), and the done-condition — another developer implements without guessing — forces a decision on every §8.4 field even where evidence is single-sourced. The arithmetic reading is forced by two independent identities the capture and the fixtures preserve; the percent scale is forced by the 19-vs-≈18% correspondence (per-mille would read 1.9%); skipping unknown entries rather than invalidating the response follows §8.3's "not every plan necessarily exposes every field" and keeps unknown shapes out of the series namespace; soft-failing the context endpoints follows §7.2's purpose (protect metric values — which originate only on endpoint 1) rather than applying its letter per-endpoint-blind and discarding healthy cycles; status-based credential validation follows from the never-captured models body. Where the evidence is a single capture, the ledger records the chosen behavior and the falsifier instead of pretending certainty — the dossier's append-only sections then carry any future revision.

**Consequences.** Tasks 098/099/100 implement against the dossier section (requests, envelope rules, recognition and mapping tables, `invalidReason` strings, assumption ledger); task 097's remaining synthetic fixtures (weekly `unit 6` entry, non-empty reset cards, error envelopes, HTTP errors, percentage-less `TOKENS_LIMIT`) are exactly the states this contract marks unobserved. The stable metric keys (`mcp-monthly`, `tokens-5h`, `weekly-quota`), the value-semantics reading, and the percent scale are adapter contract: a capture contradicting any of them (for example `percentage > 100`, a healthy entry violating `currentValue + remaining = usage`, or absolute `TOKENS_LIMIT` values that are demonstrably not credits) requires a D-047 successor, new fixtures, and a new dated dossier section — never a silent adapter change. Z.ai publishing an official quota API supersedes the whole cluster (D-038's closing condition).

## D-048 — Provider error classification: the seven-outcome seam over D-042's taxonomy, with §7.2 metadata and §7.3 precedence as data (spec §7.2, §7.3, §11.2)

**Date:** 2026-10-30 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§7.2](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#72-retry-and-error-behavior), [§7.3](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#73-account-status-precedence), [§11.2](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#112-required-logical-tables) · **Tasks:** [105](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-013, D-034, D-038, D-041, D-042

**Decision.** `src/services/polling-outcomes.ts` (the 093–111 placement row's `src/services/polling*` home; services may import the provider core, which consuming D-042's `TransportError` requires) exports the pure classifier and its pinned tables. Pinned interpretations: (1) **Output vocabulary is D-034's enum verbatim** — `COLLECTION_OUTCOMES` is exactly the seven values the `0002-collection-runs` CHECK accepts, and the parity is proven in both directions against the migrated database, not the source text: `test/integration/polling-outcomes.spec.ts` reads the `collection_runs_outcome` CHECK values back from `sqlite_master` and compares them to the constant as sets, inserts one classifier-derived row per outcome, and proves a bogus value unwritable. The canonical `MIGRATIONS` set is applied with no length or version pin so parallel tasks (085+) appending entries cannot break the spec. (2) **Kind mapping** — `timeout` → `timeout`; `dns`/`connection`/`socket`/`network` → `network_error`; `http-status` → by class; `response-too-large`/`content-type` → `parse_error` (the response was not the expected JSON contract — a 2xx whose media type is wrong or whose body blew the 64 KiB cap is a contract break, and D-042's error classes for these carry no status to retain; documented as the one metadata gap a future transport change could close); `aborted` → the pseudo-outcome `'cancelled'`. (3) **Status classes** — 401/403 → `auth_error`, 429 → `rate_limited`, 500–599 → `server_error`, and **every other status (100–499) → `parse_error`**: §7.2 has no row for an unexpected non-5xx error status, D-038 records the Z.ai quota endpoints as undocumented with drift required to surface as `Format changed`, and `server_error` must stay 5xx-only because §7.3 defines `Unreachable` as "network issue, timeout, or 5xx" — exactly the three outcomes mapped there. A property test pins totality, class rule, status retention, and determinism over the whole 100–599 space. (4) **§7.2 metadata as data** — `retryable` is true only for `network_error`/`timeout`/`server_error` (§7.2's first row; 429 and 401/403 are "do not retry within the current cycle", and a parse failure is deterministic); `retryAfterRaw` passes the scrubbed raw header through untouched (parsing and the one-hour cap are 107's), and `retryAfterEligible` is true only for `rate_limited` — §7.2 sanctions deferral only in its 429 row, so a 503's `Retry-After` is retained as evidence but never honored; eligibility is orthogonal to header presence (a legal 429 without one, D-034). `httpStatus` is retained whenever a response arrived, `errorMessage` is always D-042's static-and-scrubbed message (or the adapter's static reason) and `undefined` on success, matching `collection_runs_success_clean`. (5) **§7.3 precedence as data** — `FAILURE_STATUS_PRECEDENCE` pins ranks 1–3 (`auth-rejected` > `format-changed` > `unreachable`) and `STATUS_CONTRIBUTION_BY_OUTCOME` maps every outcome: the three unreachable-class failures → `unreachable`, `auth_error` → `auth-rejected`, `parse_error` → `format-changed`, and **`rate_limited` → none** — §7.3's list has no rate-limit status and `Unreachable` cannot absorb one, so a 429 cycle simply was not a success and the age-based `Stale`/`Collecting`/`Fresh` states (time-derived, task 111) govern; `success` → none likewise. Task 111 consumes the array and record without re-deciding. (6) **`'cancelled'` is outside the enum on purpose** — a caller abort is service lifecycle, not a provider failure: never retried, no status contribution, and unwritable as an outcome (the integration spec pins SQLite's rejection), so no writer can persist it by accident; how a cancelled cycle is recorded or skipped is task 110's. (7) **Fail-fast inputs** — `classifyParseFailure` rejects a blank `reason` and a status outside 100–599; `classifySuccess` validates likewise; the status branch of `classifyTransportError` routes `TransportStatusError.status` through the same 100–599 check, and an `http-status` kind arriving without a `TransportStatusError` instance (a base-class construction carrying no status) is rejected loudly instead of being guessed into the network family — while the exhaustive `kind` switch turns a future D-042-successor kind into a compile error rather than a silent, retryable `network_error` (review findings, D-013 style, D-034's own CHECK range).

**Reasons.** The done-condition — "status priority and outcome persistence are covered by tests" — makes the classifier's job producing exactly what 106/107/110/111 consume, and every policy question they own (delay schedule, cap parsing, run recording, state machine) had to stay out. The two judgment calls the spec leaves open were decided from its own text: `rate_limited`'s absent §7.3 status (none, because `Unreachable`'s parenthetical is a closed definition) and the unexpected-status home (`parse_error`, because D-038's undocumented endpoints make "the contract changed" the actionable diagnosis and `server_error`'s §7.3 meaning forbids diluting it). Database-back parity was chosen over source-text parity because the CHECK is on-disk contract (D-034) and reading it from the migrated database proves the shipped schema, not a regex over a string that happens to sit next to it; reading it also survives 085+'s appended migrations without a fixture edit. The `'cancelled'` pseudo-outcome follows D-042's own precedent of keeping caller lifecycle (the `aborted` kind) distinct from provider failures — folding it into `network_error` would show `Unreachable` after every shutdown abort, which §7.3's semantics contradict.

**Consequences.** Tasks 106/107 receive `retryable`/`retryAfterRaw`/`retryAfterEligible` as their complete inputs; task 110 receives outcome, `httpStatus`, `errorMessage`, and the `'cancelled'` exception it must not write as an outcome; task 111 receives `FAILURE_STATUS_PRECEDENCE` and `STATUS_CONTRIBUTION_BY_OUTCOME` as the failure half of the §7.3 chain and adds the time-derived half. `COLLECTION_OUTCOMES`, the kind/status mapping, the precedence array, the contribution record, `retryAfterEligible`'s 429-only rule, and `'cancelled'`'s unpersistability are contract: changing any of them requires a successor decision. Task 099's adapter signals parse failures through `classifyParseFailure`'s `{ httpStatus?, reason }` input — the adapter-facing shape this decision fixes; `outcomeForHttpStatus` stays private and can be promoted by a successor task (098) if credential validation wants it. A future transport that retains status on `response-too-large`/`content-type` (a D-042 successor) closes metadata gap (2)/(3) without touching this module's outcomes.

## D-049 — The synthetic Z.ai fixture matrix: audit-driven scope, labeled assumption shapes, and recorded no-fixture rows (spec §8.3, §17.1)

**Date:** 2026-10-30 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§8.3](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#83-zai-coding-plan-integration-contract), [§17.1](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#171-required-test-coverage) · **Tasks:** [097](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-038, D-040, D-042, D-047

**Decision.** Task 097's fixture matrix is derived by auditing the task-096 adapter contract row by row: every row that can manifest as a parseable response body gets a minimal single-purpose synthetic fixture under `test/fixtures/synthetic/` (19 files), every **verified** row was already covered by the 095 sanitized set (deliberately unchanged — the audit found no verified shape missing), and rows that cannot be JSON fixtures are recorded rather than forced. Pinned rules: (1) **Assumption shapes are labeled at the index** — `zai-quota-limit-weekly.json` (A1, with absolutes → `CREDITS` per A5), `zai-quota-limit-tokens-absolute.json` (A5), `zai-customer-package-reset-cards.json` (A4: card objects `{available, expireTime}` from the prototype source; non-null `lastWeekResetTime` unobserved), `zai-envelope-error.json` (A2: invented `code`/`msg` failure envelope and `success: false` spelling), and `zai-subscription-list-divergent.json` (exercises the assumed A9 rule; its `EXPIRED` status value is invented — only `VALID` was
observed, and its records carry distinct `productName`s — beyond the observed `GLM Coding Pro`,
invented compositions of the documented Lite/Pro/Max tier names — so the selection winner is
observable through the only mapped field, the `planName` fallback; a divergent fixture whose
candidates share one `productName` would be output-indistinguishable and could not falsify the
rule). No synthetic file may be mistaken for an observation. (2) **`zai-models.json` is never parsed**: the `/models` body was never captured and 098's validation is status-based (D-047); the file exists only as a mock-server stand-in and its OpenAI-style shape is invented. (3) **No-fixture rows, by design:** HTTP-level failures (401/403 per A3, 429, 5xx, timeout, oversized, content-type) — the D-042 transport rejects non-2xx responses and transport errors before parsing, so no code path would consume a body fixture; the task-026 mock server owns those scenarios — and trivial cross-cells (`code: "0"`,
non-string `data.level`, a subscription list without any `inCurrentPeriod` record, a
success-code envelope with `success: false`, a wrong-typed `code`, and an absent `limits`
key or `data: null`), which are one in-test mutation away from shipped fixtures. (4) **Multi-entry fixtures never collide on metric keys** — `zai-quota-limit-invalid-entries.json` uses one entry per key (`tokens-5h`, `mcp-monthly`, `weekly-quota`) so every invalid shape is observable, and the wrong-typed-`nextResetTime`-on-a-valid-entry case is a separate file precisely because a fourth entry would be skipped by first-wins. (5) **Value invention extends D-040's discipline to synthetic files**: no capture exemplar quoted in the dossier (1000/1/999, 19, 23) and no sanitized-set literal (2000/2/1998, epochs 1795885500000/1793353200000, `customerId` 41002938, its ids/dates/prices) is reused; a shared "baseline healthy monthly entry" (1200/60/1140, 5%) recurs across five files so value differences are meaningful, and the synthetic `customerId` 52714903 belongs to one invented account across the divergent subscription and reset-card fixtures.

**Reasons.** The done-condition — "no secret or private account data is present and every mapping has a fixture" — plus §17.1's vocabulary (full, partial, empty, unknown-field, changed-schema, different-plan, different-unit; invalid values never become zero) and 095's hand-off list fix the coverage bar; the 096 ledger fixes what must stay assumption-labeled (its A-entries define what must **not** get a "verified" fixture). Minimal single-purpose files keep every cause→effect pair legible for the parsing tests (099/100). Forcing a fixture for transport-level failures would create a file no adapter branch can ever read — the honest artifact there is the recorded audit row; the same argument makes trivial cross-cells in-test mutations rather than files.

**Consequences.** Tasks 098/099/100 consume the matrix through the row→fixture map in `test/fixtures/README.md`; synthetic values are git-stable and assertable, unlike the sanitized set ("assert shapes, not values" stays sanitized-only). Adding shapes later means appending files plus index rows. A future capture that falsifies a ledger entry (weekly entry observed differently, card shape corrected, absolute `TOKENS_LIMIT` values that are not credits) requires new fixtures, a new dated dossier section, and a D-047/D-049 successor — the affected assumption-shaped files are then replaced or explicitly deprecated, never silently edited.

## D-051 — The `raw_responses` table: one bounded sanitized parse-failure payload per run, parse-error linkage and byte cap structural, the task-103 retention index (spec §7.4, §11.2)

**Date:** 2026-10-31 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§7.4](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#74-sanitized-raw-responses), [§11.2](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#112-required-logical-tables), [§11.1](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#111-database-settings), [§11.3](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#113-retention-and-cleanup) · **Tasks:** [086](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-014, D-021, D-027, D-031, D-032, D-034, D-036, D-039, D-041, D-046, D-048

**Decision.** `0006-raw-responses` — the sixth entry of the canonical `MIGRATIONS` list (schema version 6) — creates the `raw_responses` table and its retention index as one STRICT `CREATE TABLE` plus one `CREATE INDEX` statement through `context.database` (no transactions inside; D-027), with these pinned interpretations: (1) **Column set = §11.2's row plus the two D-036 FK carriers** — `run_id INTEGER NOT NULL UNIQUE` (the run reference of "one per run"), `captured_at INTEGER NOT NULL` (§11.2's "timestamp", the house `_at` epoch-ms suffix, writer-supplied from the injected clock, D-021, no SQL default — the value task 103's 30-day policy compares), nullable `http_status INTEGER`, nullable `content_type TEXT`, `body TEXT NOT NULL`, plus `account_id TEXT NOT NULL` and `run_outcome TEXT NOT NULL` carried solely so the parse-error linkage can compare against the run's own columns — the D-036-documented bend of the exact-set rule, paid once per table that needs it; `account_id` additionally leads the retention index. §7.4 names no content type, §11.2's row does ("content type"), so the column is here. (2) **One raw record per run is structural** — a plain `UNIQUE` column on `run_id`, deliberately not `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY`: D-036's verified finding is that a NULL inserted into a NOT NULL rowid alias is silently replaced by a fresh auto-assigned id (attaching the payload to an arbitrary run), while the plain UNIQUE column rejects NULL; and no second identity column exists because no query references a raw-response id (`doctor --raw` reads by run/account) — the D-036/D-039/D-046 no-second-identity rule. No `AUTOINCREMENT`: cascading deletion makes recycling harmless (D-034). (3) **Parse-failure-only linkage via the D-036 composite-FK technique** — `(account_id, run_id, run_outcome)` references `collection_runs (account_id, id, outcome)` `ON DELETE CASCADE`, the parent key task 083 already exposed as `collection_runs_account_id_outcome` (no new parent index), with `raw_responses_parse_error_only` pinning the child's `run_outcome` to `'parse_error'`. One constraint proves three §7.4/§11.2 properties of the record: the run exists, it belongs to the same account, and its outcome is `parse_error` — so a successful run (and every other §7.2 failure class: auth, rate-limit, network, timeout, server) can never carry a raw record, and a payload can never be filed under an account whose run it was not. The parent-side default (`ON UPDATE NO ACTION`) additionally freezes a referenced run's outcome and account against post-hoc UPDATEs — a run whose payload was kept cannot be reclassified after the fact. `run_outcome <> 'success'` was rejected as weaker than §7.4's own words ("store a provider response **only** when parsing/schema validation fails" would still admit auth_error payloads); a plain run FK plus writer discipline was rejected for the D-036 rationale verbatim (CHECKs cannot span tables, and the stated record property would be unenforced). (4) **The 64 KiB cap is SQL, and it counts bytes** — `raw_responses_body_size` is `octet_length(body) <= 65536`, the number interpolated from the new exported `RAW_RESPONSE_MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES = 64 * 1024`. Bytes, not characters, decided explicitly: D-041's cap is 65536 UTF-8 **bytes** (`Buffer.byteLength`, truncation marker included), SQLite's `length()` counts code points (up to 4 bytes each — a character bound would admit 256 KiB) and stops at an embedded NUL, while `octet_length()` counts the full UTF-8 byte length, NUL included (SQLite ≥ 3.43; the pinned runtime carries 3.47.2; both behaviors verified empirically on it). At-cap passes — the D-041 sanitizer can emit exactly 65536 bytes — and one byte over is rejected. Because the layout DAG forbids storage importing providers, the constant is re-declared in `src/storage/migrations.ts` and `test/integration/raw-responses.spec.ts` drift-tests it against D-041's `MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES` for equality and pins the numeric literal inside the migrated `sqlite_master` CHECK text: a sanitizer-cap change without a successor migration fails tests instead of silently diverging. (5) **`body` is NOT NULL and may be empty** — an empty body is itself a parse failure (`JSON.parse('')` throws; the sanitizer passes `''` through), so unlike `error_message` (D-034) there is no non-empty CHECK; no charset or NUL guard either, because the row stores the sanitizer's output and must accept every state the domain can produce (the D-039 rule against invented bounds). (6) **Evidence columns mirror D-034's shapes** — `http_status` is NULL or a real 100–599 status, NULL being a state the domain produces (D-048: `response-too-large` and `content-type` parse failures carry no retained status); `content_type` is absent-or-non-blank (the `accounts_plan_nonempty` precedent): the header value verbatim when the transport saw one, absent when it did not — unbounded by design, because §7.4's cap is the payload's, the transport's header-size limit bounds what can arrive, and a schema-side bound would reject states the domain can produce (the D-039 rule). (7) **Index `raw_responses_account_time (account_id, captured_at)`** — §11.2's required-index list names no raw_responses index, so this is the task-delegated decision: one index serves task 103's per-account policy scans (newest-first `LIMIT 20` for the record cap, `captured_at` ranges for the 30-day expiry), the account-FK cascade scan (the D-034 one-index-two-jobs pattern), and the `doctor --raw` per-account listing; the `run_id UNIQUE` autoindex serves the run cascade — no extra foreign-key indexes. Retention **execution** stays task 103's; this is only the shape that makes 20-per-account/30-days enforceable.

**Reasons.** The done-condition — "the schema cannot store multiple raw records for a single run" — makes the per-run uniqueness structural-enforced, and the task's own scope notes added the success-exclusion and the byte bound as SQL-level duties; every question the spec leaves open was resolved by a landed house pattern rather than a new debate. The D-036 composite FK was chosen because it is the only SQLite mechanism that expresses "a parse-failed run of this account" as a property of the stored rows themselves (CHECKs cannot span tables; a partial unique index cannot serve as an FK parent; a trigger has no precedent in this schema and adds on-disk objects), and because it simultaneously closes the account-consistency hole a plain run FK would leave — the fourth application of the technique (D-036 success linkage, D-039 denormalization pinning, D-046 account pinning, here parse-error pinning). `octet_length` over `length` follows from measuring what D-041 actually caps: the empirical probes on the pinned runtime showed `length()` both mis-scales (code points) and truncates at NUL, either of which would let oversized payloads through, while `octet_length()` is exact — and the multibyte at-cap/over-cap tests pin the choice against regression to a character bound. The re-declared constant plus drift test keeps the DAG intact while making the two 64 KiB values one contract mechanically — the alternative (importing the provider constant) would break the executable layout rule, and a comment would drift silently.

**Consequences.** `MIGRATIONS` carries six entries; a fresh database migrates to schema version 6 at startup, `schemaVersionStatus` reports `up-to-date` at version 6 after the run, and the schema-5→6 forward test §11.4 requires lives in `test/integration/raw-responses.spec.ts`. Task 081–085 canonical-set pins in `test/integration/accounts.spec.ts`, `collection-runs.spec.ts`, `snapshots.spec.ts`, `metric-values.spec.ts`, and `quota-events.spec.ts` were updated to the grown set (D-031's planned growth, recorded here as those tests' deliberate fixture changes). Task 088's repository owns typed reads/writes, supplies `captured_at` from the injected clock (D-021), passes the `'parse_error'` carrier value alongside the run reference (the D-036 snapshots discipline), and stores `sanitizeRawResponse`'s output as-is — its 64 KiB guarantee is now also the table's; task 103 builds the 20-per-account/30-days cleanup and the CLI-only `doctor --raw` path on the `(account_id, captured_at)` index and may rely on the parse-error linkage having already excluded every other outcome. The table, column, constraint, and index names (including `raw_responses_account_time`), the byte bound and its bytes-not-characters semantics, and the `parse_error`-only linkage are on-disk contract: renaming any of them, widening the linkage, or changing the cap requires a successor decision. Raw `DatabaseSync` test handles default to `foreign_keys=OFF` (D-034's pinned note) — the FK tests set the pragma explicitly.

## D-052 — Z.ai credential validation: status-based three-result seam over the transport, a provider-neutral two-error taxonomy, and the adapter island's first module (spec §8.1, §8.3)

**Date:** 2026-10-30 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§8.1](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#81-provider-interface), [§8.3](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#83-zai-coding-plan-integration-contract) · **Tasks:** [098](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-013, D-038, D-042, D-047, D-048, D-049

**Decision.** `src/providers/zai-coding-plan/` (the first adapter island: `index.ts` barrel, `provider.ts` skeleton, `validate.ts`) implements `validateCredentials` per the dossier's endpoint-4 rule and pins what that rule leaves open. (1) **Shape is the 070 contract, not 105's vocabulary** — `Promise<void>` that resolves on valid and rejects with one of two provider-neutral errors; `COLLECTION_OUTCOMES` is unusable here twice over: the layer rules forbid an adapter importing `src/services/`, and the dossier's rule collapses network/timeout/5xx/429/content-type into a single "unavailable" result that the seven-outcome enum deliberately splits for collection cycles (a 429 during a manual check is "try later", not a rate-limit outcome). (2) **The taxonomy is structural, not just nominal** — `CredentialCheckError` carries `kind: 'credentials-rejected' | 'provider-unavailable'`; subclasses `CredentialsRejectedError` (`httpStatus: 401 | 403`) and `ProviderUnavailableError` (`transportKind`: the D-042 kind, `httpStatus?` when a response arrived) add non-secret facts. The `kind` field is the discriminator for consumers that cannot import adapter types (services, CLI): the 070 contract's wording — `validateCredentials` "rejects with a provider-neutral error" (`registry.ts`, the spec §8.1 interface's landed JSDoc) — is satisfied structurally, and the vocabulary stays island-local until a second provider needs it (promotion to `providers:core` is a successor decision). (3) **"2xx → valid" means "`providerFetch` resolves"** — the check is status-based through the mandated transport, so a 2xx that fails the transport's `application/json`/64 KiB gates surfaces as a transport error and reads `provider-unavailable` (inconclusive), never valid and never rejected; the body is never parsed at all (D-049: `zai-models.json` is a stand-in; envelope-error and malformed-envelope bodies served with 200 resolve as valid, pinned by test). (4) **Classification is a pure exported seam** (`classifyCredentialCheckFailure`, the polling-outcomes pattern) that is total without a per-kind switch: `TransportStatusError` + 401/403 → rejected (A3), every other `TransportError` → unavailable; there is no fail-fast arm because the signal-less check cannot produce `aborted` (dossier) and an unpredicted transport failure must still answer a "test connection" request, not crash it. (5) **Options seam** — `codingBaseUrl` (default `https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4`, dossier sources 3/6; the check URL is base + `/models`) and `timeoutMs` (default §7.2's 15 s; any positive finite value, the transport's own rule — the 5–60 s configuration range is enforced where configuration enters); both validated at construction with echo-free `TypeError`s (fail fast, D-013's spirit). (6) **The `fetchSnapshot` stub** — 070 types the method as required and `ProviderRegistry.register` checks it is a function, so the skeleton ships a loud async rejection with a pinned exported message naming task 099 instead of omitting it and failing assembly.

**Reasons.** The dossier (D-047's endpoint-4 paragraph) fixes the request, the status-based rule, the A3 assumption, the Authorization-only header set (A7), and the no-retry/single-GET discipline; what it leaves to this task is the boundary representation. Two results must be distinguishable without importing the island (the 070 contract's "provider-neutral error" wording plus the layer DAG), which forces a structural discriminant over exported-class instanceof. The gates-on-2xx reading is forced by mandating `providerFetch`: the transport resolves only for 2xx JSON within the cap, so "valid" is exactly "the verified flow delivered a 2xx" — the alternative (treating a gate-failing 2xx as valid) would require bypassing the shared transport. Rejected-vs-unavailable must not collapse (§7.2 keeps them apart for polling: `Auth rejected` pauses polling, `Unreachable` does not), and unavailability must not read as a verdict on the key. The key-never-logged guarantee (§8.1/D-013) is preserved compositionally: errors are built only from static English plus transport fields D-042 already scrubbed against the request's own credential material, and `account.secret` is read exactly once, into the header.

**Consequences.** The adapter's later tasks (099/100) add `fetchSnapshot` and mapping without touching `validate.ts`; composition-root registration (a later assembly task) imports only the island barrel. The `kind` vocabulary, the two error classes' fields, the default endpoint URL, the options names, and the stub message are contract: changing any requires a successor decision. A first observed bad-key response that is not HTTP 401/403 (A3's reopen trigger — e.g. an envelope-encoded rejection reading 200 + error `code`) requires a new dated dossier section, a D-047/D-052 successor, and new fixtures before the classification may change. A second provider needing the same vocabulary promotes the taxonomy to `providers:core` in its own decision.

## D-053 — Z.ai snapshot collection: the endpoint trio behind two failure surfaces, mapping as a pure module owned by 100, and the §7.4 hand-off on the parse error (spec §7.2, §7.4, §8.1, §8.3, §8.4)

**Date:** 2026-10-30 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§7.2](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#72-retry-and-error-behavior), [§7.4](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#74-sanitized-raw-responses), [§8.1](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#81-provider-interface), [§8.3](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#83-zai-coding-plan-integration-contract) · **Tasks:** [099](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-010, D-025, D-040, D-041, D-042, D-047, D-048, D-049, D-052

**Decision.** Task 099 implements `fetchSnapshot` as three modules in the adapter island: `snapshot.ts` (cycle orchestration, strict envelope/container validation, endpoint-2 record selection, fail-soft policy, `SnapshotParseError`) and `mapping.ts` (the pure endpoint-1 → §8.4 translation) behind the extended `provider.ts`. Pinned choices beyond the D-047 contract the task implements: (1) **Two failure surfaces, no re-wrapping** — an endpoint-1 transport failure re-throws the D-042 `TransportError` unchanged (task 105's `classifyTransportError` consumes the kind/status/`Retry-After` directly; wrapping into D-052's credential taxonomy would collapse the 429/5xx/auth distinctions §7.2 keeps apart), and an endpoint-1 parse failure throws the new island-local `SnapshotParseError` with `reason` (static English, feeding 105's `classifyParseFailure` verbatim), `httpStatus`, `sanitizedPayload` (the §7.4 hand-off: `sanitizeRawResponse(body, [account.secret])` — carried, never persisted here; storage is 086/103's), and `envelopeMessage` (a non-success envelope's `msg`, sanitized through the same function's raw-text path — dossier A2's "retained … as the diagnostic string"; a _missing_ code retains nothing, a malformed envelope's `msg` is noise). One failure meaning, therefore no `kind` discriminant or subclass split (D-052 needed two meanings; this needs one). (2) **Fail-soft is total on endpoints 2/3** — transport failures, parse violations, and caller aborts mid-cycle all degrade to a warn log; a cycle whose primary succeeded is a success (D-048 keeps `aborted` out of provider outcomes). Endpoint 2 is fetched every cycle and soft-parsed (`inCurrentPeriod`-true record per A9, else first `VALID`, `productName` only as the `planName` fallback); endpoint 3 is fetched every cycle and its body never parsed (D-047.6: it maps nothing in v1 — validating its envelope would produce a soft log and nothing else, i.e. dead consumption). No §7.4 payload attaches to soft failures: retention is tied to parse failures that produce no snapshot. (3) **The 099/100 boundary is a module boundary** — `mapping.ts` is a pure, never-throwing function over the validated containers, implementing the complete D-047 table now (099's done-condition requires validated → normalized); task 100 owns its refinement and contract-verifies every row against every fixture in that file without touching fetch code. (4) **Derivations never chain (§8.4's literal reading)** — the missing triple member derives from the two supplied; `percentUsed = 100·used/limit` only when `used` and `limit` were both _directly supplied_ (a derived `limit` does not qualify); the sole sanctioned chain is `percentRemaining = 100 − percentUsed` from a supplied _or_ derived percentage (dossier table). (5) **Wiring** — options add `apiBaseUrl` (default `https://api.z.ai`, the monitor/biz host — never the coding base), `logger` (a `Pick<Logger, 'warn'>` sink; absent means silent, the adapter creates no output sinks), and `clock` (stamps `collectedAt` at cycle end); `collectedAt` is stamped after the trio completes, the timestamp of the whole cycle per §7.1's wall-clock rule; `planName` blanks (trim-empty) count as absent so emitted snapshots always satisfy `findProviderSnapshotProblems`; the skip/collision/soft-failure logs carry static English plus payload enums (type/unit pairs) and D-042-scrubbed transport messages — and the skip reports additionally pass through task 102's sanitizer before logging (their raw-text path scrubs and caps), so every payload-derived string the cycle emits is secret-free by construction, with the D-025 logger's scrubbing as a second layer, not the only one. (6) **D-052's stub-message contract entry is superseded by this decision** — the loud stub and `SNAPSHOT_NOT_IMPLEMENTED_MESSAGE` are removed because 099 is the task D-052 named as the stub's owner; the test-only mock provider server gained exact-match `setPathBehavior`/`clearPathBehaviors` (additive; the global behavior API is unchanged) because a three-endpoint cycle cannot be routed by a single global behavior.

**Reasons.** The dossier fixes the requests, envelope rules, mapping tables, and per-endpoint policy; what it left to this task is the boundary representation. Re-throwing the transport error unchanged is forced by D-048's design (105 owns kind → outcome; every fact it needs lives on the error) and keeps the adapter free of §7.2 policy. The `sanitizedPayload`/`envelopeMessage` split follows the two consumers: §7.4 storage wants the whole body sanitized, A2 diagnostics want the envelope's own string — both must be secret-free by construction, which reusing task 102's sanitizer (raw-text path for the msg) guarantees without new scrub code. Total fail-soft on 2/3 follows the dossier's policy sentence ("Endpoints 2 and 3 fail soft") with no abort exception carved out — D-048's `cancelled` pseudo-outcome exists precisely so caller lifecycle is never misread as a provider outcome, and a primary-completed cycle is real collected data. The module split answers the task brief's explicit option ("if the mapping is substantial, split it as `mapping.ts` … 100 owning its refinement"): the D-047 table is substantial, and a pure module gives 100 a single file to deepen with contract tests while 099's fetch/orchestration code stays stable. The no-chaining derivation rule is §8.4's own text ("only when the required original fields are supplied") applied consistently; the one exception is the dossier's explicit table row. Trim-empty blanks as absent aligns the adapter's emission with the invariant checks that guard every persisted snapshot, so a whitespace-only `level` can never produce an invalid row downstream.

**Consequences.** Tasks 106/107/110 consume cycle failures exactly through the two surfaces (TransportError kind/status; SnapshotParseError reason/httpStatus plus the retained payload path of 086/103); task 100 refines `mapping.ts` and may extend its exported seam but must not move envelope validation out of `snapshot.ts` (strict/tolerant tier split is D-047.5). The metric keys, `invalidReason` strings, reason vocabulary, `SnapshotParseError` field set, the `apiBaseUrl` default, the logger/clock option names, and the fail-soft totality are contract: changing any requires a successor decision. A capture that falsifies a D-047 row (weekly entry shaped differently, absolute token values that are not credits, a real error envelope without `msg`) requires the D-047/D-049 successor process — new fixtures, a new dated dossier section — before this code may change. The mock-server per-path routing is test-support surface: future multi-endpoint provider suites (106's retry cycles) build on it.

## D-054 — Mutation-report rendering: one committed renderer, normalized status vocabulary, loud failure on the unknown (spec §4.4, §17.3)

**Date:** 2026-10-30 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§4.4](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#44-cicd-and-supply-chain-safeguards), [§17.3](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#173-required-test-coverage) · **Tasks:** [U-005](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-045

**Decision.** The rolling `mutation-report` issue body is rendered by a single committed script, `scripts/render-mutation-report.mjs`; the workflow's "Render report markdown" step is a thin `node scripts/render-mutation-report.mjs > /tmp/mutation-report.md` call, and the script doubles as the local verifier (first CLI argument overrides the default `reports/mutation/mutation.json` path, so any downloaded artifact re-renders by hand — the one-liner is documented in `docs/mutation-testing.md`). Status handling: (1) **Canonical vocabulary is the mutation-testing-schema `MutantStatus` enum as Stryker serializes it** — PascalCase `Killed`, `Survived`, `Timeout`, `NoCoverage`, `CompileError`, `RuntimeError`, `Ignored`; the exact lowercase spelling of each is accepted as a defensive alias, and **anything else aborts the render with a non-zero exit naming the status and file**. A Stryker vocabulary change must break visibly, never silently re-zero the report (the failure mode of issue #5's run 41054956364, whose inline renderer tallied PascalCase statuses against lowercase keys). The old script's camelCase keys (`timedOut`, `noCoverage`) are deliberately not aliases — no producer ever emitted them; accepting them would legitimize the bug's own vocabulary. (2) **Score semantics pinned to the documented formula** — detected = Killed + Timeout, total = every mutant in the JSON, score = detected/total at one decimal, per file and overall; a zero-mutant report renders `—` rather than dividing by zero. Error statuses (RuntimeError/CompileError) count in the denominator and as neither detected nor survived. (3) **Error-status visibility** — their counts are always in the summary line, and when non-zero an extra bullet lists `file (count)` pairs sorted by count descending, then file name (the reference run's 5 RuntimeErrors all sit in `src/services/polling-outcomes.ts`). (4) **Survived triage list order is pinned** — report-JSON file iteration order, mutant order within file, 200-row cap with an explicit overflow line (previous behavior, now actually reachable). (5) **Verification split** — the unit tests (`test/unit/render-mutation-report.spec.ts`) pin the format and every number over a synthetic all-statuses report (happy path, lowercase equivalence, alias acceptance, loud failure on unknown statuses including `toString`, cap, error-file ordering, zero-mutant edges) and run in `make check`; full-artifact verification against a real downloaded `mutation.json` is the manual pre-landing gate, not a committed fixture — a 3681-mutant artifact is generated output and would bloat the repository.

**Reasons.** The inline heredoc was the root enabler of the bug: untestable and unrunnable outside the workflow, it shipped with a case mismatch no local harness could catch, and the artifact numbers (85.6% = 3150/3681, 497 Survived, 29 NoCoverage, 5 RuntimeError) were only recoverable by re-deriving them from the JSON. Extracting one renderer gives the workflow, the unit tests, and hand verification the same code (the workflow's inline copy and a separate verifier script would drift or duplicate). PascalCase + lowercase aliases cover both real spellings the renderer may ever see without a vocabulary audit; the loud abort covers everything else, which silent tallies provably do not (the fallback `tally[m.status] = …` created unseen keys and read zero forever). The score formula matches `docs/mutation-testing.md`'s published semantics ("detected / total, detected = killed + timed out") and reproduces Stryker's own 85.6% verdict for the reference run, so no documentation meaning changes — only the numbers become true.

**Consequences.** Renderer format changes (bullet wording, table columns, cap size, ordering) are contract-visible in the issue body and must update the unit tests' expected markdown in the same commit. A future Stryker status (or a casing change beyond exact lowercase) fails the workflow's render step with the offending status named in the log instead of publishing wrong numbers; extending `STATUS_ALIASES` is a successor decision. If ignore comments ever reach the codebase and `Ignored > 0` in a report, whether ignored mutants belong in the score denominator (Stryker's own metrics exclude them; this renderer counts them per the documented formula) must be revisited in a successor decision. The workflow's artifact-upload and issue-upsert steps are unchanged; the end-to-end re-render lands with the next scheduled run or a manual dispatch after this reaches `master`.

## D-055 — Mutation-triage exclusions and the score's scoreable denominator: in-code Stryker ignores are deliberate artifacts, and the renderer adopts Stryker's own formula (spec §17.3)

**Date:** 2026-10-30 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§17.3](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#173-enforced-quality-thresholds) · **Tasks:** [U-006](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-045, D-054

**Decision.** Two rules settle how mutation-triage exclusions work and how the report scores them. (1) **Equivalent or intentionally unspecified mutants are excluded in code, next to the line, with `// Stryker disable next-line <Mutators>` comments carrying a short English reason** — the exclusion is a reviewed artifact that travels with the code, per `docs/mutation-testing.md`. Stryker's ignore granularity is one line per mutator name, so an exclusion necessarily also covers line-mates of an equivalent mutant (for example, a `ConditionalExpression` ignore on a line where one variant is equivalent and another killable); the reason must say so when it happens, and the killing tests for those behaviors stay in the suite so removing the directive re-arms them. Exclusions are reserved for mutants with no observable behavior difference (dead return values, flags re-asserted by a later freeze, normalization results invisible to the parser, error inputs the runtime cannot produce) — never for behaviors a test could pin, and thresholds are never lowered instead. (2) **The report renderer's mutation score switches to Stryker's own formula** — `score = (Killed + Timeout) / (Killed + Timeout + Survived + NoCoverage)`, per file and overall, replacing D-054's `detected / every-mutant` denominator: `Ignored` and the error statuses (`RuntimeError`, `CompileError`) leave the denominator (verified against the installed Stryker's `mutation-testing-metrics` `calculateMetrics`, where `mutationScore = totalDetected / totalValid` with `totalValid = detected + survived + noCoverage`). Both stay visible as counts — the summary line keeps the ignored and error tallies, error files keep their bullet, and the per-file table keeps the raw mutant total — so nothing becomes invisible, only the score stops disagreeing with the verdict line, which comes from Stryker's own threshold check.

**Reasons.** D-054 flagged this exact question as a successor decision the moment ignore comments first appear; U-006 is that moment (59 of the triaged run-41054956364 survivors are equivalents across `config-validation.ts`, `transport.ts`, `single-instance.ts`, and `registry.ts`). Keeping `Ignored` in the denominator after that would have made the issue's score strictly lower than Stryker's own — a self-inflicted repeat of issue #5's class of bug (numbers contradicting the verdict), and a permanent tax on honestly documenting equivalence. Matching Stryker is the self-consistent choice because the verdict, the break threshold, and the clear-text score the workflow logs all come from Stryker's formula; a diverging denominator could eventually flip the issue's optics red while Stryker stays green. In-code placement of the exclusions (over a config-level `excludedMutations` list) keeps every suppression one review-comment away from the code it suppresses, and the line-granularity cost is accepted knowingly: it is bounded, documented per directive, and recoverable — deleting a directive restores the mutants, and the suite's behavior pins then kill them again.

**Consequences.** The rolling issue's score line now reads `X% (D detected of S scoreable mutants …; ignored and error-status mutants are excluded, see D-055)`; `docs/mutation-testing.md`'s "How to read the report" section describes the scoreable denominator, and `test/unit/render-mutation-report.spec.ts` pins both the changed wording and an ignored-heavy fixture (50 killed + 50 survived + 30 ignored + 20 runtime errors ⇒ 50% of 100 scoreable, 150 total in the table). Stryker runs no longer generate the excluded mutants at all, so the raw totals shrink in future artifacts while the deliberate-exclusion inventory lives in the code. Adding a new `// Stryker disable` requires the same discipline as this task: a reasoned audit entry in the landing commit, tests for every line-mate behavior that stays killable, and no use of ignores as a substitute for a test that can actually be written. Whether equivalent-mutant exclusions should also be enumerated somewhere machine-readable (beyond Stryker's own JSON) stays open; nothing today consumes such a list.

## D-056 — The `sessions` and `meta` tables: SHA-256-hex session identity with §15.2's two expiry bounds CHECK-enforced, key/value service state, one migration for both (spec §11.2, §15.2)

**Date:** 2026-10-31 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§11.2](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#112-required-logical-tables), [§15.2](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#152-passwords-and-sessions), [§15.1](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#151-network-and-authentication-modes), [§11.1](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#111-database-settings), [§11.3](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#113-retention-and-cleanup) · **Tasks:** [087](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-021, D-027, D-031, D-032, D-034, D-039

**Decision.** `0007-sessions-meta` — the seventh entry of the canonical `MIGRATIONS` list (schema version 7, completing §11.2's table list) — creates both tables and one index as one STRICT `CREATE TABLE` × 2 plus one `CREATE INDEX` through `context.database` (no transactions inside; D-027), in a single entry because D-031's rule is one `NNNN-…` entry per task. Pinned interpretations: (1) **`sessions` column set exactly §11.2's row** — `token_hash TEXT PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL`, `created_at`/`last_seen_at`/`expires_at INTEGER NOT NULL`, nothing else. The digest is the identity: §15.2's lookup path is cookie token → SHA-256 → row, and no query references a second id (the D-036/D-039/D-046/D-051 no-second-identity rule). `sessions_token_hash_hex` pins the stored shape to exactly 64 lowercase hex characters — `createHash('sha256').digest('hex')`'s form — via the D-032 GLOB encoding (first character in class, no character outside, exact length) plus the NUL guard; the raw 256-bit token's wire forms (base64url's 43 mixed-case characters, base64, raw bytes into TEXT) cannot fit — under one recorded precondition: a lowercase-hex cookie encoding would make the raw token shape-identical to the digest (no SQL constraint can distinguish them), so the value-level digest-not-token guarantee rides on task 154's writer contract and the cookie's wire form stays non-hex (base64url), keeping the two shapes distinct. The task's done-condition — schema tests verify no raw session token column exists — is structural three ways: the exact four-column pin, the credential-fragment pin (`token_hash` is the only column whose name may carry token/cookie/secret/raw vocabulary; any other such column breaks the test — the accounts D-032 precedent), and the hex-shape CHECK; the digest-not-token provenance of the value remains the session layer's writer contract (task 154).
