**Date:** 2026-11-02 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§15.2](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#152-passwords-and-sessions), [§11.2](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#112-required-logical-tables), [§11.3](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#113-retention-and-cleanup), [§17.1](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#171-required-test-coverage) · **Tasks:** [155](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-056 (the `sessions` schema whose single effective-expiry column and `SessionSighting` refresh seam this verdict composes; the never-hex/base64url and formula single-siting pins it extends), D-058 (the facade whose sync contract, no-clock rule, and CHECKs-are-the-write-gate discipline the new functions inherit), D-123 (the task-154 creation module this extends, whose consequences recorded this exact composition), D-061 (the §11.3 cleanup that stays the only expired-row deleter), D-118 (task 144's `revokeAllSessions` — the already-landed password-change revocation the verdict side now agrees with), D-121 (the `RequestAuthenticator` seam the future wiring wraps this verdict behind), D-021 (the explicit-`now` clock seam), D-090 (the safe-integer fail-fast family the `now` guard follows)

**Decision.** Task 155 lands §15.2's expiry sentence — "Sessions expire after 7 days of inactivity and no later than 30 days after creation" — plus the revocation semantics ("Changing the password revokes all sessions", and logout), as the request-side half of `src/services/sessions.ts` (the module D-123 built), and pins five interpretations. (Correction trail: the task's review round — deepseek-v4.1-flash, one round, APPROVE with 4 P3, zero P0–P2 — folded two documentation corrections into this entry and the same commit, which had not landed when corrected (the D-123 precedent): the "unreachable between two calls on one synchronous connection" claim about the vanished-at-refresh arm was wrong — `quotameter passwd` revokes every session over its own separate connection while the server runs, so the arm is live cross-process, not defensive; and the half-open interval's lower endpoint was written as though the verdict enforced it — the verdict's test is the upper endpoint alone, the lower names the canonical row's birth, now pinned executably by a regressed-clock test. The round's other two P3s: the integration marker scan completed to the creation suite's full four-encodings parity, and a pre-existing task-144 window — revoke-before-write plus old-hash-until-reload — was recorded as a loose end for the login/reload tasks, not a defect of this commit.) (1) **Validity is half-open `[created_at, expires_at)`, and the verdict's test is the interval's upper endpoint alone**: a request at exactly `expires_at` is expired; at `expires_at - 1` it is valid. "Expires at T" makes T the first dead instant, §15.2's "no later than 30 days after creation" composes the same way (the expiry lands at `created + 30 d` at the latest, and a session alive AT that instant would be alive later than the rule allows), and it is the reading under which every accepted sighting refreshes to a strictly future expiry — the inclusive alternative would let a sighting at exactly `created + 30 d` rewrite `expires_at = now`, a refresh to an already-dead expiry. The interval's lower endpoint names the canonical row's birth, not a second verdict input: a wall reading before `created_at` is the regressed-clock case pin (2) records. The boundary's relationship to §11.3's cleanup is pinned as benign asymmetry: `deleteSessionsExpiredBefore` (strict `<`, D-056/D-061) deletes only rows dead before `now`, so a boundary-dead row survives until the next cleanup run — storage hygiene lag only; the verdict is the access gate. (2) **`authenticateSession({ repository, token, now })`** is the per-request composition D-123's consequences recorded — digest the presented wire token through the module's own `hashSessionToken` (the raw token never reaches storage), look the row up through `getSession`, judge `now < expires_at` (the row's single effective-expiry column already folds both bounds; no rule arithmetic runs at request time), and on the valid arm record the sighting: `touchSession` writes `last_seen_at = now` and `expires_at = effectiveSessionExpiry(created_at, now)` — the inactivity window slides to `now + 7 d`, the absolute cap never extends, and the write cannot violate the 087 CHECKs because it is the same single-sited formula they enforce. **Every valid sighting refreshes** — no threshold, no dedup; `last_seen_at` tracks the latest authenticated request exactly, and a regressed clock reading is trusted like every other wall stamp (D-021) and can only shrink the expiry, the fail-closed direction (pinned by the regressed-clock test: a sighting before `created_at` is accepted and refreshes to an earlier expiry). The verdict variants carry the evidence: `expired` names which bound fired (`rule: 'absolute'` when the row's own `expires_at` equals `created_at + SESSION_MAX_AGE_MS`, else `'inactivity'` — the canonical writers always produce exactly one of the two bounds, and the both-equal case of a last sighting exactly 23 days in is named `'absolute'`); `unknown` is the single fail-closed answer for every absent row, and a `touchSession` that reports the row gone downgrades to it — nothing can interleave between two calls on the server's own synchronous connection, but the passwd CLI's separate connection revokes while the server runs, so the arm is live cross-process and the composition must let a revocation beat an in-flight sighting, never lose to one. (3) **The verdict never deletes**: an `expired` row is left for §11.3's cleanup (task 091, D-061) — the verdict is read-plus-refresh, cleanup owns expired-row deletion, and a delete here would be a second writer for a job the startup/daily scheduler already does. (4) **Revocation is deletion, `unknown` the only aftermath**: no tombstones and no revoked-vs-unknown distinction — storage cannot tell a never-existed digest from a deleted one, and the consumer's 401 is identical. `revokeSession({ repository, token })` is the logout primitive: digest the token, delete the one row through the facade's `deleteSession`, answer whether one existed (logout is idempotent; the cookie clearing is 157's endpoint). (5) **No service-level revoke-all wrapper**: password-change revocation stays where task 144 landed it — `revokeAllSessions` in `src/cli/passwd.ts` over the facade's `deleteAllSessions` — and the future UI password-change endpoint composes the same facade call; a service function that only forwarded one facade call would add a second name, no logic (the contrast is `revokeSession`, which adds the digest transform the discipline needs). The module stays synchronous (D-058), logger-free (§15.4/§16 — the zero-console pin now covers the new functions), and D-021 throughout: a non-integer `now` fails fast with a field-naming `TypeError` before any storage call; repository failures propagate unchanged.

**Reasons.** §15.2 states both bounds as one sentence over two clocks (last activity, creation), and D-056 had already collapsed them into one stored column maintained at sighting time — so request-time enforcement could only ever be a comparison against that column, and the design freedom was the boundary's inclusivity, what a valid request writes, and what revocation leaves behind. The half-open reading is forced by composition: the inclusive alternative's day-30 sighting rewrites `expires_at = now` (a refresh that arrives dead), while half-open guarantees every accepted sighting strictly extends observed life; and the cleanup's strict-`<` (already D-056's pinned contract, not this task's to change) is only consistent-looking under the inclusive reading but harmless under either — the verdict gates access, cleanup reclaims rows, and one boundary-instant of lag between them costs nothing. Refreshing on every valid sighting follows the seam's own shape: task 088 built `touchSession` as the sighting recorder, D-056 named login the first sighting, and a dedup threshold would add policy the spec nowhere states. The `rule` field makes "both expiry rules enforced" observable rather than incidental — the tests can assert WHICH bound fired, which is exactly the done-condition's demand that the two rules be covered as rules, not as one undifferentiated rejection. And `unknown` as the only absence answer is fail-closure made boring: four storage-indistinguishable states collapse into one verdict, and no consumer can grow a leak by trying to tell them apart.

**Consequences.** Task 156 (rate limiting) and 157 (cookie flags) and the login/logout endpoints compose this module without touching `src/storage/` or its contract: the `RequestAuthenticator` wiring is one lambda over `authenticateSession(...).verdict === 'valid'` (the seam's docblock now names the primitive), the login endpoint calls `createSession` (D-123) and the logout endpoint `revokeSession`. The exported surface (`SessionVerdict`, `SessionExpiryRule`, `AuthenticateSessionOptions`, `authenticateSession`, `RevokeSessionOptions`, `revokeSession`, joining D-123's) is internal API under `src/`, not package surface; changing the verdict variant names or the `rule` vocabulary is a breaking change for the consuming endpoints and requires a successor decision. The done-condition ("fake-clock tests cover both expiry rules and revocation") is pinned executably in both suite halves: `test/unit/sessions.spec.ts` extends to 33 tests over a behavioral in-memory facade (the inactivity rule alone — idle past 7 d inside the 30 d bound with no sighting recorded; the absolute rule over a 5-day-old sighting; the half-open boundary pinned one ms apart for BOTH rules; the sliding refresh and never-extending cap with the exact `touchSession` arguments; the regressed-clock acceptance whose refresh shrinks the expiry; unknown tokens; the revocation-won-the-race downgrade; logout by digest, idempotent, sibling-sparing; password-change revocation through `deleteAllSessions`; the fail-fast guard proven storage-call-free by a read counter; failure propagation; the zero-console pin), and the new `test/integration/sessions-authentication.spec.ts` (6 tests) runs the same table over real migrated databases — a 29-day fake-clock walk sliding the window daily with the cap pinning from day 23, the day-30 rejection of a session seen one day ago (`rule: 'absolute'` — the distinguishing case), the 8-day-idle rejection with the row left in place (the never-deletes pin against the real table), the half-open boundary on the real schema with the accepted side's refresh landing, refresh writes passing the 087 CHECKs with the §15.4 whole-database marker scan repeated after refreshes, and both revocations through the facade (`revokeSession` and the exact `deleteAllSessions` call task 144 wired). `sessions.ts` measures 100% coverage on all four axes without joining the D-085 pinned critical-module keys; `src/services/README.md`, `src/storage/README.md`, and `CHANGELOG.md` carry the boundary, and `src/server/api/auth.ts` changes comments only. No public API, format, or event changes.

## D-125 — The §15.2 login rate limiting of task 156: a sliding half-open five-failure budget per opaque source key with doubling capped delays (delays, never rejections), success as the reset, behaviorally-exact bounded memory, and a logger-free timer-free primitive whose delays the endpoint sleeps on (spec §15.2, §15.4, §16, §17.1; task 156)

**Date:** 2026-11-02 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§15.2](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#152-passwords-and-sessions), [§15.4](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#154-secret-protection), [§16](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#16-logging-and-diagnostics), [§17.1](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#171-required-test-coverage) · **Tasks:** [156](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-122/D-123/D-124 (the sibling §15.2 primitives, the land-the-primitive-not-the-endpoint precedent this follows, and — D-124 — the half-open boundary discipline the window expiry borrows), D-121 (the §15.1 seam whose consequences pinned this task's placement: "task 156's limiter composes inside the same authenticator (or ahead of it inside the login route), never here"), D-113 (the error-envelope registry whose consequences promised this task a `RATE_LIMITED` code and an `@fastify/rate-limit` registration — the promise this entry supersedes: delays are not errors), D-059 (the §7.2 doubling-delay family the growth formula joins), D-021 (the explicit-`now` clock seam), D-090 (the safe-integer fail-fast family), D-066 (the closure-factory pattern for shared in-process state)

**Decision.** Task 156 lands §15.2's rate-limit sentence — "Rate-limit authentication to no more than five failed attempts per source address within 15 minutes, then apply increasing delays. Log failed attempts at `warn` without logging passwords." — as `src/services/login-rate-limit.ts`, the third §15.2 primitive of the future `AuthService` beside `password-hash.ts` and `sessions.ts`, and pins six interpretations. (1) **The window slides and expires half-open.** "Within 15 minutes" counts the failures in any 15-minute span, not an aligned fixed bucket — a fixed bucket lets five failures at one bucket's end and five at the next bucket's start pass as neighbors inside a single 15-minute span, which is exactly the burst the rule exists to slow. A failure exactly `LOGIN_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS` old is outside the window: the counted set is the half-open interval `(now − window, now]`, the same boundary discipline D-124 pinned for session expiry. (2) **Five failures are admitted undelayed; then delays, never rejections.** With `n` in-window failures the next attempt waits `0` while `n < 5`, else `LOGIN_RATE_LIMIT_BASE_DELAY_MS × 2^(n−5)` capped at `LOGIN_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_DELAY_MS` (1 s doubling to the 15-minute window length — the D-059 family at login scale, and a delay longer than the window would outlive the failures that caused it). §15.2 says "apply increasing delays", not "lock out": an over-budget attempt is answered slowly, never refused — a legitimate user who mistypes five times still logs in, later, while a serially attacking source's guessing rate collapses to the delay cadence (at saturation, one attempt per window; a concurrent burst can race the check-then-record window and land K attempts at one delay each — holding the cadence under concurrency is the endpoint's composition, see (4)). (3) **A successful login resets the source's budget** — deletion of the source's history, so the next failure counts from one. The budget exists to slow credential guessing; a verified password ends the guessing, and a counter that kept throttling a proven-legitimate source would serve no security purpose while taxing the one honest user the system has. (4) **The delay is computed from history, before verification.** §15.2 budgets _failed_ attempts, so an attempt cannot price itself before its outcome exists: the endpoint asks `delayBeforeAttempt(source, now)`, sleeps the answer (the timer is the endpoint's — a service-layer sleep would need fake-timer tests and risks event-loop blocking; the module owns no timers at all, which is what makes every rule a deterministic fake-clock table), verifies with `verifyPassword`, then reports through `recordAttempt(source, outcome, now)`. Concurrent attempts racing inside that check-then-record window can only under-delay a burst whose failures have not landed yet — the next attempt sees the full count — the honest ordering rather than a reserve-then-adjust protocol the spec nowhere demands; the endpoint that wants the cadence held under concurrency serializes per source (a consequence for the endpoint task, below). (5) **Memory is bounded with behaviorally exact counting.** Per source only the newest `LOGIN_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_RETAINED_FAILURES` timestamps are kept, and the retention trim sorts by stamp value before cutting, so the retained set is always the largest stamps by value whatever the clock did (an insertion-order trim would, after a regressed record, keep a small still-in-window stamp and drop a live larger one — under-counting; the review round's catch, fixed and pinned). The bound sits at the delay formula's saturation count — the smallest `n` whose raw delay reaches the cap (15 at the shipped constants, derived from them by test so the pin travels) — because in-window-ness is monotone in stamp value and every count at or above saturation answers the capped delay: the bounded count is exactly `min(k, bound)` of the unbounded history's `k`, and both sides of that `min` map to the same delay at and above saturation, so the bounded history answers identically to an unbounded one — under the same sweep — for every count and every clock reading (pinned against the raw formula for counts 0–100, plus a regressed-clock trim case). Map-wide a sweep at most once per window (checked on `recordAttempt`, the only writer) drops sources whose failures have all expired: the map never holds more than the sources active in roughly the last two windows. The sweep's deletion decision is identical to an unbounded history's would be (the largest stamp is always retained, so an all-expired retained set means every dropped stamp was expired no later), keeping the bounded and unbounded systems aligned; the deletion side is behaviorally invisible under a non-regressing clock — an entry whose failures have all expired answers zero and counts from zero at the next record whether deleted or retained — so that side's contract is memory, stated here and in the module docblock, while the keep side (entries with live failures survive) is pinned observably through what subsequent records count. State is in-memory only: §15.2 assigns no persistence to rate-limit state, a restart clears every budget, and restart rights are operator privileges, not attacker ones. (6) **No credentials, no logger, no clocks of its own — the endpoint-layer logging contract is documented, not implemented.** The module's inputs are an opaque source key (never parsed — the endpoint owns what "source address" means on the wire; distinct keys are simply distinct budgets), the outcome label, and an explicit `now` (D-021; a non-integer reading fails fast with a field-naming `TypeError` before any state change, the D-090 family, and a regressed wall reading is trusted — it can only widen the counted window, the fail-closed direction). It holds no logger: §15.2's "log failed attempts at `warn` without logging passwords" belongs to the endpoint layer that sees the attempt, and the contract is documented in the module header — one `warn` record per failed attempt carrying the source address and outcome only, never the candidate password, the stored hash, or any session token (§15.4; the future endpoint's marker-secret test owns that pin, and the zero-console pin holds the primitive's half executably: a module that cannot log cannot leak a credential through one). (Correction trail: the task's review round — deepseek-v4.1-flash, one round, APPROVE with 1 P2 / 4 P3, zero P0–P1 — folded five fixes into this entry and the same commit, which had not landed when corrected (the D-122/D-123 precedent): the value-sorted retention trim (the P3 the round's bounded-vs-unbounded simulation caught — an insertion-order trim under-counts after a regressed record; see (5)), the stale pre-156 story still living in `src/server/http.ts`, `src/server/README.md`, and `src/server/api/error.ts` — the P2, comment-only corrections naming the landed primitive and the unregistered dependency's non-owner — plus this entry's missing D-113 reference, an unbounded saturation-search loop a future constant change could have turned into a worker hang, and the "157+" endpoint-reference corrected to a plan-gap record below.)

**Reasons.** §15.2 fixes the numbers (five failures, 15 minutes, per source address) and the response shape (increasing delays) but leaves open the window mechanics, what "delays" means operationally, whether success resets, and where the state lives. The sliding window is forced by the "any 15-minute span" reading above; the half-open edge follows D-124's precedent for the identical boundary question. Delays-not-rejections is the spec's own word and the correct trade for a single-user self-hosted service: a lockout converts a mistype-prone owner into a locked-out owner (and, behind a proxy, a shared source address into a denial-of-service lever against the legitimate user), while delay throttling preserves eventual access at the attacker's expense. The doubling curve reuses the §7.2 house family rather than inventing linear growth: one extra constant (the base) with the cap already implied by the window, and the steeper curve reaches one-attempt-per-window within ten excess failures. Success-reset follows the budget's purpose rather than maximal strictness — the counter's job ends when the password is proven. The primitive-not-endpoint scope follows D-121's recorded consequences ("task 156's limiter composes inside the same authenticator (or ahead of it inside the login route), never here") and the D-122/D-123 precedent: no login endpoint exists to wire, and the §15.1 mode layer stays untouched. The bounded-retention design exists because an unbounded per-source timestamp list is a memory-exhaustion lever (a hostile source can fail arbitrarily often inside one window), and the saturation-count bound is the largest truncation that provably changes nothing — the exactness argument (monotone in-window-ness plus cap saturation) is simpler than any approximate scheme and testable against the raw formula. Returning delays as numbers rather than sleeping internally keeps the module synchronous, deterministic under fake clocks (the done-condition's demand), and honest about who owns the wire (the endpoint).

**Consequences.** The future login endpoint composes `createLoginRateLimiter()` — one instance for the whole login surface — as check → sleep → verify → record (serializing per source to hold the delay cadence under concurrency, per (4)), and owns the §15.2 `warn` logging contract documented in the module header plus its marker-secret test. **Plan gap (the D-122 precedent for recording it): no task in `plan/tasks.md` owns the HTTP login/logout endpoints** — 157 is cookie flags, 158 security headers, 159–163 the resource endpoints, 164 integration tests; the composition target this primitive and D-122's verifier/D-123's creation/D-124's verdict all wait on needs a task the main session should add. This entry also supersedes D-113's consequences sentence "Task 156 adds `RATE_LIMITED` … and maps `@fastify/rate-limit`'s error onto it": delays are not errors, no rate-limit error class is coming, and the registry's code set is untouched. The exported surface (`LOGIN_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_FAILURES`, `LOGIN_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS`, `LOGIN_RATE_LIMIT_BASE_DELAY_MS`, `LOGIN_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_DELAY_MS`, `LOGIN_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_RETAINED_FAILURES`, `LoginAttemptOutcome`, `LoginRateLimiter`, `createLoginRateLimiter`) is internal API under `src/`, not package surface; changing the delay curve, the window semantics, or the reset rule is a successor decision. A future constant change is safe while `LOGIN_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_RETAINED_FAILURES` stays at or above the saturation count the tests derive from the exported constants — the pin fails the suite otherwise (and the derivation loop is bounded, so an unreachable cap fails a test instead of hanging the worker). The `@fastify/rate-limit` dependency stays declared-but-unregistered with no owning task left: it counts requests rather than failed attempts and answers 429 rather than increasing delays, so it cannot express §15.2 — whether it stays declared (or is removed as dead weight) is the main session's maintenance call, recorded here; the task-146 pin that it is unregistered stays green. The done-condition ("rate-limit behavior is tested and failed logs contain no credentials") is pinned executably in `test/unit/login-rate-limit.spec.ts` (23 fake-clock tests): the budget (attempts 1–5 undelayed, the sixth onward delayed), the exact doubling sequence with the cap takeover, formula-identical answers for every count (the retention-exactness pin), the value-sorted trim under a regressed clock, the ±1 ms window edge, the partial slide, per-source isolation in both directions, the success reset (full, partial, unknown-source no-op), the pruning record, the sweep (both sides), the clock discipline (fail-fast before state changes, regressed clock fail-closed), and the zero-console pin. `src/services/login-rate-limit.ts` measures 100% coverage on all four axes without joining the D-085 pinned critical-module keys (the D-118/D-122/D-123 precedent); `src/services/README.md`, `src/server/api/auth.ts` (comments only), `src/services/sessions.ts` (comments only), `src/server/http.ts` (comments only), `src/server/README.md` (comments only), `src/server/api/error.ts` (comments only), `test/integration/server-http.spec.ts` (comments only), and `CHANGELOG.md` carry the boundary. No public API, format, or event changes.

## D-126 — The §15.2 session cookie attributes of task 157: `Secure` mirroring the client-facing protocol (transport facts, not the bind host, because the config contract has no public-URL field), leftmost-forwarded-proto precedence, `Max-Age` mirroring the row's effective expiry with the verdict as the gate, and a no-endpoint scope (spec §15.2, §15.1, §15.6, §6.2, §17.1; task 157)

**Date:** 2026-11-02 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§15.2](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#152-passwords-and-sessions), [§15.1](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#151-network-and-authentication-modes), [§15.6](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#156-operational-security), [§6.2](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#62-configuration-contract), [§17.1](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#171-required-test-coverage) · **Tasks:** [157](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-123 (the mint whose raw token this module's attributes serialize — "157 owns the flags" — and the base64url cookie-safety pin the wire round-trip re-asserts), D-124 (the verdict that stays the gate the cookie's `Max-Age` merely mirrors, and whose half-open reading the expired-input refusal inherits), D-125 (the plan-gap record this entry extends: the login/logout endpoints that compose this primitive still have no owning task), D-122 (the land-the-primitive-not-the-endpoint precedent, now four entries deep), D-121 (the §15.1 layer that already reads proxy indicators per request — value-blind, names only, deliberately complementary to this module's proto-value reading — and whose `PUBLIC_AUTH_ROUTE_CONFIG` the future login route uses), D-109 (the construction that registers `@fastify/cookie` for parsing and never enables trustProxy — the fact that makes `request.protocol === 'https'` a socket-derived, header-unforgeable `requestTls`), D-021 (the explicit-`now` clock seam), D-090 (the safe-integer fail-fast family the timestamp guards follow)

**Decision.** Task 157 lands §15.2's cookie sentence — "Use a random 256-bit session token in a cookie with `HttpOnly` and `SameSite=Strict`; set `Secure` for HTTPS based on the public URL/reverse-proxy configuration." — as `src/services/session-cookie.ts`, the fourth §15.2 primitive of the future `AuthService`, and pins five interpretations. (1) **The spec's "public URL/reverse-proxy configuration" resolves from the request's own transport facts, because the configuration contract defines no such field.** §6.2's schema covers `server` (host/port), `app`, `auth`, `logging`, providers, accounts — no public URL, no proxy settings — and D-121 already reads the reverse-proxy reality per request (indicator presence). The bind host therefore has **no vote** in the `Secure` decision: §15.6 terminates TLS at the reverse proxy (nginx/Caddy under `auth.mode: required`), the service itself carries no certificate configuration and never speaks TLS directly in any supported deployment, and a non-loopback bind is still plain HTTP — stamping `Secure` on an HTTP cookie would protect nothing (the token rides the same wire) while breaking the session bootstrap (a `Secure` cookie is neither stored nor sent over plain HTTP). `Secure` mirrors exactly one question: is the **client-facing leg** of the request HTTPS? — decided by `isClientFacingHttps(SessionCookieTransportFacts)`: the request's own TLS socket first (the directly observed fact, header-unforgeable because trustProxy is never enabled in D-109's construction), else the leftmost element of `X-Forwarded-Proto` (the de-facto header the documented proxies emit; proxies append, so the leftmost element names the originating leg, the same rule as `X-Forwarded-For`), else the leftmost RFC 7239 `Forwarded` entry's `proto` parameter (the standards-track fallback, case-insensitive name, quote-stripped value, **quote-aware splitting** — a quoted `for` value may carry `,` or `;`, RFC 7239 §5.2's own example, and neither may cut an entry off its `proto`), else HTTP — the leg the server itself saw. Whitespace is tolerated and casing normalized; an empty value is absent evidence (the next source stays consultable) while a non-empty one is read literally (`https` is HTTPS, anything else describes a non-HTTPS leg). Spoof analysis, the fail directions: a forged `X-Forwarded-Proto: https` on a direct plain-HTTP request can only make the attacker's **own** login cookie carry `Secure` (the browser then refuses to store it over HTTP — a self-inflicted lockout, never an exposure), and §15.1/D-121 already force the password on every request carrying a proxy indicator, so the header cannot slide past authentication; the mirror direction — a client prepending a forged `http` to an append-style proxy's list (`http, https`) — downgrades only the forger's **own** cookie, and the leftmost rule stays: an any-`https` alternative would mislabel genuine client-HTTP legs and break legitimate logins on HTTP-public deployments, while cross-scheme replay of a downgraded cookie is the deployment's own exposure (§15.6 recommends TLS-only publication), not a flag this module can heal; stripping the header behind a real proxy is the proxy's own misconfiguration, outside the server's trust boundary and invisible to any server-side rule. (2) **`HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict`, and the cookie's identity are unconditional constants**: §15.2's own words attach the first two to the cookie itself with no exception cell anywhere in §15; the spec names no cookie, so D-126 pins `quotameter_session` (`SESSION_COOKIE_NAME` — self-identifying, never a generic `session` that another loopback service could collide with) and `Path=/api` (`SESSION_COOKIE_PATH` — §13 mounts every endpoint under the prefix, so the cookie never rides a static-asset or SPA request, and the value passes through verbatim: base64url is RFC 6265 cookie-octet-safe, D-123's pin, re-asserted on the wire by the round-trip test). (3) **`Max-Age` mirrors the row's effective expiry at set time, and the server-side verdict stays the gate.** `sessionCookieAttributes({ transport, expiresAtMs, nowMs })` computes `ceil((expiresAt − now)/1000)` whole seconds — rounded **up** so the client cookie never dies before the row D-124's verdict judges (an early-dead cookie logs an owner out of a live session; a late one costs a single 401 from the verdict); the fresh login cookie carries `Max-Age=604800` (D-123's creation expiry at the 7-day inactivity bound). Re-issuing the cookie on a refreshed sighting — the same call over the refreshed record — is the endpoint's documented composition (it keeps cookie and row aligned forever), and an endpoint that never re-issues merely caps the cookie at 7 days: a re-login, never an out-of-bounds session (the row's own bounds are untouched). A persistent cookie (explicit `Max-Age`) over a browser-session cookie is chosen so the client credential cannot outlive the row by a browser's lifetime. (4) **The clear variant is the logout protocol**: `clearSessionCookieAttributes(transport)` — identical attribute set, `maxAge: 0` — because browsers match cookies by name and path, so the same `Path` (and the same attributes generally) is what makes `Max-Age=0` reliably delete the cookie that was set, `Secure` and all. (5) **Fail-fast and no wiring, by scope**: a non-integer epoch-ms input throws a `TypeError` naming the field (the D-090/D-123 family — §11.1 timestamps are integers, and a fractional value would otherwise serialize a silently wrong `Max-Age`); `nowMs >= expiresAtMs` throws — setting a session cookie for an already-expired session is a composition error (D-124's half-open verdict rejects its first use; the dead session gets its cookie cleared, not set). The module holds no logger (§15.4/§16 — nothing can log a token, executably pinned), no clock of its own (`now` explicit, D-021), and no fastify import (its `SessionCookieAttributes` maps 1:1 onto `@fastify/cookie`'s serialize options at the endpoint). Like D-122–D-125, no endpoint is built: the login/logout routes are the plan gap D-125 recorded, and the only code changes outside the new module and its tests are comments naming the landed primitive (`src/server/http.ts`, `src/server/api/auth.ts`, `src/services/sessions.ts`, both READMEs). (Correction trail: the task's review round — deepseek-v4.1-flash, one round, APPROVE with 1 P2 / 4 P3, zero P0–P1 — folded four resolutions into this entry and the same commit, which had not landed when corrected (the D-122/D-123/D-125 precedent): the P2 quote-aware RFC 7239 splitting (`for="a,b";proto=https` lost its `proto` to a plain comma split — fail-safe, no false `Secure`, but the wrong answer; now a quote-respecting splitter on both the entry and the parameter level, pinned by the §5.2-example tests), the forged-`http` downgrade direction now pinned explicitly above (kept leftmost with reasons, recorded), the mixed-scheme clear residual now recorded in the clear-variant pin below (the code declined — see Consequences), and the integration suite's brittle lone-string `set-cookie` representation pin relaxed to accept both shapes.)

**Reasons.** §15.2 fixes three cookie attributes and conditions the fourth on "the public URL/reverse-proxy configuration" — a phrase the configuration contract never materializes as a field, which forces the question this entry answers: what, concretely, is that configuration? The per-request reading follows from what exists: the schema's silence on one side, D-121's established per-request proxy reading on the other, and the deployment reality of §15.6 (TLS terminates at a proxy the service cannot see through except by its forwarded headers). The bind-host alternative was rejected on its own semantics: a non-loopback bind changes §15.1's password verdict precisely because it exposes plain HTTP — it does not make anything HTTPS, and tying `Secure` to it would break exactly the deployments that most need the session cookie to work while they configure TLS upstream. The leftmost-forwarded rule is the only one consistent with how the documented proxies append observations (the client-facing leg is the first hop's claim, the same convention as `X-Forwarded-For`), and the precedence order (socket > `X-Forwarded-Proto` > `Forwarded`) runs from the most directly observed to the most de-facto to the most standard. The `Max-Age` mirror with `ceil` keeps the client cookie from ever being the limiting factor of a session the server still judges valid — the verdict is the security boundary (D-124), the cookie merely fails to outlive it. The clear twin mirrors attributes because cookie deletion is name-and-path matching, not attribute matching. The primitive-not-endpoint scope is D-122's precedent verbatim: no login endpoint exists to wire, and the §15.1 mode layer stays untouched.

**Consequences.** The future login endpoint composes `createSession` (D-123) → `sessionCookieAttributes({ transport, expiresAtMs: session.expiresAt, nowMs })` → `reply.setCookie(SESSION_COOKIE_NAME, token, attributes)` — and the logout endpoint `revokeSession` (D-124) → `reply.setCookie(SESSION_COOKIE_NAME, '', clearSessionCookieAttributes(transport))` — with the transport facts resolved per request by the documented recipe (`request.protocol === 'https'` for the socket fact, Node's folded header values for the two forwarded ones); the endpoint task the plan gap still owes should also decide whether refreshed sightings re-issue the cookie (documented above as the alignment-preserving composition). The exported surface (`SESSION_COOKIE_NAME`, `SESSION_COOKIE_PATH`, `SessionCookieTransportFacts`, `isClientFacingHttps`, `SessionCookieAttributes`, `SessionCookieOptions`, `sessionCookieAttributes`, `clearSessionCookieAttributes`) is internal API under `src/`, not package surface; changing the cookie's name, path, or the `Secure` rule is a successor decision (a name change additionally invalidates every stored browser cookie). Adding a public-URL or proxy field to the configuration contract later (a `server.publicUrl`, say) would supersede interpretation (1) and should record how the field composes with the per-request facts. The done-condition ("cookie attributes are tested under HTTP and HTTPS/proxy setups") is pinned executably in both halves: `test/unit/session-cookie.spec.ts` (the pure matrix — plain HTTP, direct TLS incl. socket-over-headers precedence, `X-Forwarded-Proto` exact/case/whitespace/multi-hop-leftmost/empty/garbage, `Forwarded` proto incl. quoted/case/empty/lone-quote values, proto-less entries, and the quote-aware §5.2-example arms (`for="a,b"`, `for="a;proto=http"`, unbalanced quotes), XFP-over-`Forwarded` precedence both directions, the unconditional attribute pins across every transport, the exact/ceil `Max-Age` table with the 7-day schema-constant tie, the fail-fast guards, the frozen objects, the clear twin, the zero-console pin) and `test/integration/session-cookie.spec.ts` (the wire through the full task-146 construction and the real `@fastify/cookie`: probe routes composing the module exactly as the endpoint will, asserting the serialized `Set-Cookie` attribute set under plain-HTTP loopback, proxied HTTP, proxied HTTPS (`X-Forwarded-Proto` and `Forwarded`), multi-hop folded lists, direct TLS, the logout clear with and without `Secure`, and the value's verbatim round-trip back through `request.cookies`). Two of the round's P3s were declined with reasons: emitting **both** clear variants (with and without `Secure`) for mixed-scheme logout resilience is endpoint composition over this primitive (and the residual is client-side hygiene lag only — the revocation `revokeSession` deleted the row, the missed cookie answers 401 on any use; a TLS-only publication cannot produce the shape), and exporting a request-fact **resolver** would move the endpoint's own request→facts mapping into the services layer — the same seam discipline D-121 keeps (`classifyAuthMode` over facts, the guard over the request) holds here; both are recorded as endpoint-task guidance. `session-cookie.ts` measures 100% coverage on all four axes without joining the D-085 pinned critical-module keys (the D-118–D-125 precedent); `src/services/README.md` gains the module section, `src/server/README.md`, `src/server/http.ts`, `src/server/api/auth.ts`, and `src/services/sessions.ts` change comments only, and `CHANGELOG.md` carries the boundary. No public API, format, or event changes.

## D-127 — The §15.5 security headers of task 158: the exact-list helmet surface (a fail-closed `default-src 'none'` CSP with same-origin allowances, no inline/external sources, no nonces), nosniff and no-referrer, the API-only `no-store` hook on the §13 boundary, and the unlisted-defaults-disabled emission (spec §15.5, §14.1, §15.6, §17.1; task 158)

**Date:** 2026-11-02 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§15.5](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#155-headers-and-limits), [§14.1](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#141-ui-overview), [§15.6](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#156-operational-security), [§17.1](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#171-required-test-coverage) · **Tasks:** [158](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-109 (the §3 plugin split that made helmet configuration-owning — "registered by its owning task 158" — whose deferred registration this task now executes), D-120 (the root-scope Host guard whose registered-ahead-of-addHook position in the hook chain this layering was verified against), D-111 (the route-scoped health `no-store` this entry generalizes), D-113 (the §13 envelope whose `sendApiError` remains the error-path `no-store` guarantee, and whose router-level `frameworkErrors` arm is the one helmet-less response class), D-121 (the auth-mode guard whose 401/403 verdicts carry the set), D-125 (the §15.2 rate-limit primitive that keeps `@fastify/rate-limit` unregistered — the D-109 pin's other half, unchanged by this task)

**Decision.** Task 158 lands §15.5's header sentence — "Use a strict Content Security Policy without inline scripts or external sources, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, and `Cache-Control: no-store` for API responses." — as a `@fastify/helmet` registration plus one root-scope hook in the task-146 construction (`src/server/http.ts`), and pins five interpretations. (Correction trail: the task's review round — deepseek-v4.1-flash, one round, 0 P0/P1, 3 P2, 4 P3 — folded four corrections into this entry and the same commit, which had not landed when corrected (the D-124 precedent): the `/api` predicate now percent-decodes (P2-1, reproduced by the reviewer — raw `request.url` vs the router's decoded matching let `/%61pi/health` reach the API with no `Cache-Control`), the first draft's "ECharts uses CSSOM assignment, unaffected" claim was wrong and is replaced below by the tooltip/renderer constraint (P2-2), the upgrade "tripwire" is now the executable complete-allowlist pin rather than a named denylist (P2-3), and the `assetsInlineLimit`/`frozen` wordings were corrected (P3-2/P3-4). The round's P3-1 — setting the three headers inside `sendApiError` so the router-level `frameworkErrors` arm carries them too — was declined with reason: it would duplicate the CSP byte literal across modules (or import-cycle to avoid it) for a JSON error body no browser renders; the exception stays documented and pinned, and a shared-literal module is the successor path if it ever matters.) (1) **The CSP is fail-closed and byte-exact**: `default-src 'none'` with allowances only for what the built UI is — same-origin module scripts and hashed styles (`script-src`/`style-src 'self'`), same-origin images and locally bundled fonts (§14.1), and the same-origin API (`connect-src 'self'`) — while the directives CSP does not fold into `default-src` are pinned `'none'` (`base-uri`, `form-action`, `frame-ancestors`, and `object-src` explicitly beside them). No `'unsafe-inline'` or `'unsafe-eval'` anywhere (Vite emits referenced hashed files, never inline code, and the runtime-only Vue build needs no `eval`), no `data:` allowance (unlisted by the spec and unneeded — a future inline-asset build need amends this policy by successor decision, it does not silently widen), no nonce machinery (§15.5 demands no inline scripts at all, so there is nothing for a nonce to whitelist), and no `upgrade-insecure-requests` (the service is plain-HTTP-by-design on loopback; §15.6's TLS leg belongs to the proxy). The wire order is the directive object's insertion order; helmet serializes deterministically, and the suites pin the exact byte string. (2) **The emitted security-header surface is exactly §15.5's list**: every helmet default the spec does not name is disabled — `strictTransportSecurity` (TLS terminates at the §15.6 reverse proxy; the service never speaks TLS itself, and an app-set `max-age`/`includeSubDomains` would reach through a passing proxy into subdomains the operator never delegated to this app), `xFrameOptions` (framing policy lives once, inside the spec'd CSP, as `frame-ancestors 'none'` — not duplicated in the legacy header), `crossOriginEmbedderPolicy`/`crossOriginOpenerPolicy`/`crossOriginResourcePolicy`/`originAgentCluster`/`xDnsPrefetchControl`/`xPermittedCrossDomainPolicies` (cross-origin-isolation and metadata headers the spec does not list and a same-origin SPA does not need), and helmet's legacy-IE pair `xDownloadOptions`/`xXssProtection` (both still default-on in helmet 8.3 — discovered empirically and disabled with the rest). `nosniff` and `no-referrer` are configured explicitly so the values are single-sited in the construction, not inherited defaults. (3) **`Cache-Control: no-store` is the API-only rule, on the §13 path boundary**: a root-scope `onRequest` hook sets it for `/api` and `/api/…` (query stripped and percent-DECODED — the exact predicate the not-found handler's SPA-vs-envelope split uses, single-sited in `isApiRequestPath`; fastify's `request.url` is the raw wire path while the router matches the decoded one, so the decode is what puts `/%61pi/health` on the no-store side and keeps the bare `/%61pi` on the envelope arm; `/apiary` stays a UI deep link, and a malformed escape keeps the raw path because the router's `frameworkErrors` own that rejection), registered ahead of the Host guard so even a gate-rejected `/api` request carries it. Static responses keep `@fastify/static`'s own default (`public, max-age=0` — revalidate-always over `send`'s ETags): §15.5 fixes no static caching directive, and revalidation cannot serve a stale app shell after an upgrade. `sendApiError` KEEPS its own `no-store` (D-111's precedent generalized, not removed): the envelope is the error surface wherever it appears — non-API 404/403 arms and the router-level `frameworkErrors` included — and an error response is never cacheable; the health route's task-147 route-scoped header is gone, superseded by the hook. (4) **The layering was verified on the pinned runtime, not modeled**: helmet's `onRequest` hooks are added by a plugin registered AHEAD of the construction's `addHook` calls and run FIRST in the root chain — the Host guard's thrown 403s carry the full helmet set — so the only helmet-less response class is the router-level `frameworkErrors` (a malformed percent-escape is rejected during routing, before any hook), which still answers the §13 envelope with its `no-store`. Both facts are pinned executably so a fastify/helmet ordering change surfaces, not ships silently. (5) **The browser-level done-condition ("the UI still runs") is proven against the real server, not the preview**: the existing e2e suite drives `vite preview`, which never passes through the application server and cannot see these headers — so the new `test/e2e/csp-shell.spec.ts` boots the real `buildHttpServer` over the built UI (DIST_DIR-aware) and loads it in a real Chromium, asserting the header set on the main response and an empty `securitypolicyviolation`/console-error record. The "grow a CSP-violation check in the smoke spec" alternative was rejected for exactly that reason: a violation check against the preview server would assert nothing about the served policy.

**Reasons.** §15.5's sentence is a closed list, and the task's strictness reading follows its own words: "a strict Content Security Policy" fails closed (`default-src 'none'` — every fetch type without an explicit allowance is blocked, so a future feature breaks loudly until the policy is amended, not silently wide), "without inline scripts" bans the source expressions that would permit them (and with them the nonce machinery whose only purpose is to exempt inline scripts), and "or external sources" bans every non-`'self'` host. The exact-list surface follows the same discipline in the other direction: the spec's silence on HSTS is not permission to second-guess the §15.6 proxy operator, and silence on COOP/COEP/legacy headers is not a mandate either — a smaller, spec-anchored surface is easier to defend, to test byte-exactly, and to extend later by decision. The no-store split is forced by the spec's own qualifier ("for API responses"): a path-scoped hook is the one mechanism that covers every API response class — future 2xx endpoints included, guard verdicts, the catch-all — without touching the static side, which the spec leaves to the static plugin; and `sendApiError`'s guarantee must stay because the envelope legitimately appears outside `/api` (the API-only mode's frontend 404s, the SPA-containment 403s) and on the frameworkErrors path that bypasses hooks entirely. The layering facts were established empirically (three probe scripts on the pinned runtime) because fastify's hook-ordering between plugin-boot-added and directly-added hooks is not documented behavior a security task should guess on.

**Consequences.** The construction (`src/server/http.ts`) now registers helmet with the module-private `SECURITY_HEADERS_CONFIGURATION` and the `apiCacheControlHook`; the emitted surface on a normal response is exactly `content-security-policy`, `x-content-type-options`, `referrer-policy` (+ `cache-control` per the split, `public, max-age=0` static / `no-store` API) — pinned by exact value and by absence in `test/integration/security-headers.spec.ts` (API success/error/401-verdict/HEAD, static index/assets/CSS/deep-link, the `/api`-boundary edges `/api`, `/api?x=1`, `/apiary`, the percent-encoded spellings `/%61pi/health` and `/%61pi`, API-only mode, and the two layering facts), with the registration itself flipped in `test/integration/server-http.spec.ts` (helmet registered, `@fastify/rate-limit` still deliberately not, D-125). The browser proof lives in `test/e2e/csp-shell.spec.ts`, which requires a built UI (`make build` / DIST_DIR) and joins the Playwright leg of `make check-all`. **The policy binds the future UI implementation (165+)**: no inline `style=` attributes in markup and no library that styles through the style ATTRIBUTE (`style-src 'self'` blocks both; CSSOM assignment from script stays unaffected) — a constraint **ECharts' default configuration does not satisfy**: its HTML-rendered tooltips and its SVG renderer apply inline styles through the attribute (apache/echarts#19570, #19398; the review round's P2-2 corrected this entry's first draft, which had claimed ECharts only uses CSSOM), so tasks 175/176 must either configure `tooltip.renderMode: 'richText'` with the canvas renderer or take a successor decision adding `style-src-attr 'unsafe-inline'` (spec-compliant: §15.5 bans inline SCRIPTS only — the byte pins amend in their three single sites if so). Bundled assets must not become `data:` URIs: Vite's default `build.assetsInlineLimit` of 4096 inlines small assets exactly so, so this policy requires `assetsInlineLimit: 0` in `ui/vite.config.ts` (the review round's P3-2) — or, again, a decision adding `data:` to `img-src`/`font-src`. No service workers (`worker-src` falls back to `'none'`), no WebSocket upgrades to other origins (`connect-src 'self'`) — any of those needs is a successor decision amending the directive set and its byte pins. Nothing in the public npm-package contract changes (headers are additive server behavior over a not-yet-published package); §17.1's "CSP and security headers" test requirement is discharged by the named suites. A helmet major upgrade that grows a new default header will fail the pins first — the ten-name denylist AND the complete header-name allowlist the integration suite pins on a representative API response (the review round's P2-3: a denylist alone cannot catch a genuinely new default; the allowlist pin catches any header name that appears) — and its admission becomes a decision, not an accident.

## D-128 — The §13 accounts endpoints of task 159: the configuration store as an injected seam (keys live in `config.json`, never the database), the content-free constant key mask with closed serializer contracts, the storage-row-first create order with a compensating delete, §13's query-param spelling as the purge confirmation, D-052's kinds as the test-outcome vocabulary, and the raw-responses gate widening for the purge evidence count (spec §13, §8.2, §6.3, §15.4, §11.2; task 159)

**Date:** 2026-11-02 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§13](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#13-http-api), [§8.2](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#82-accounts), [§6.3](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#63-secret-storage-and-writes), [§15.4](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#154-secret-protection), [§11.2](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#112-required-logical-tables) · **Tasks:** [159](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-121 (the consumer-owned seam precedent — `RequestAuthenticator` defined where it is consumed, implemented by later wiring; this entry applies the same shape to the configuration half of account management), D-113 (the frozen error-code registry this task adds nothing to — endpoint refusals ride existing classes with stable `details.reason` values), D-111 (the closed-schema compiled-serializer leak guard, generalized from health to the whole accounts surface), D-061 (the §8.2 archive/purge split the DELETE route composes verbatim, including the idempotent `already-archived` outcome and the per-table purge evidence this entry's gate widening carries), D-058 (the storage facade the endpoints reuse — no SQL, no re-implementation), D-052 (the credential-check `kind` discriminant the test endpoint reads structurally), D-100 (the one-pattern-two-consumers export rule — `ID_PATTERN` now exported for the API schema), D-069 (the one-file gate-widening precedent), D-067 (the raw-response gate this entry widens once, with reasons), D-018 (the no-`removeAdditional` Ajv discipline re-asserted scope-locally)

**Decision.** Task 159 lands the five §13 accounts routes — list (masked), create (write-only key), update (label/enable/key), archive/purge (§8.2's split), and the provider connection test — as `src/server/api/accounts.ts`, an encapsulated plugin inside the `/api` scope that registers only when the construction passes the new optional `ApiRoutesOptions.accounts` (store seam, `QuotaRepository`, `ProviderRegistry`, clock), and pins seven interpretations. (1) **The configuration half is an injected seam, not a built service.** §6.3 fixes where account secrets live — the `0600` configuration file, never the database (a rule the §11.2 schema tests already pin mechanically) — and §6.4 fixes when they change (reload, without restart). No runtime configuration-mutation service exists (the composition root is empty; `ConfigService` is future work), so the endpoints define `AccountConfigStore` — `list`/`find`/`add`/`update`/`remove`/`secretOf` — at the consumer, exactly as D-121 defined `RequestAuthenticator` at the auth-mode guard: the routes are complete and fully tested against the seam (an in-memory double in the suite), and the production implementation — an atomic `writeConfigFile` read-modify-write over the validated configuration plus §6.4's change application — belongs to the composition task that owns the file and the database. `secretOf` is the seam's only secret surface: it exists for the connection test, resolves into the registry's branded `createAccountContext` (non-enumerable secret), and is never echoed, logged, or serialized. (2) **The key mask is a constant, content-free by construction.** §13 says "Return only a mask and a boolean indicating whether the key is configured"; a mask derived from key material (last-4, prefix) would put key bytes on the wire and leak length information, so `keyMask` is the fixed `'********'` beside `hasKey` — and the deeper guarantee is structural: every response serializes through closed TypeBox contracts (`additionalProperties: false`), so the compiled serializer emits exactly the declared keys and drops any other — a handler bug that returned the secret could not put it on the wire (D-111's health guard generalized). `apiKeyEnv` is deliberately not a request field: binding an account to an environment variable is an operator/configuration-file concern (§6.3), and an env-sourced account reports `keySource: 'environment'` and refuses key mutation with `FORBIDDEN`/`environment-key-read-only` — the read-only rule is key-scoped; label and enabled stay mutable. (3) **Create writes the storage row first and compensates.** `repository.insertAccount` is synchronous and a just-created row carries no history, so a failing configuration write has a total compensation (`deleteAccount`); the reverse order would leave a configured account whose every collection fails on the missing row. The id is client-supplied (validated against the §6.2 charset — the configuration contract's `ID_PATTERN`, now exported additively for the API schema, D-100's no-drift rule made executable by a test asserting the two schemas carry the same pattern) or generated (`acc-` + 16 hex), stable from creation either way. (4) **The purge's confirmation is §13's own query spelling.** The route table itself defines `?purgeHistory=true` as the explicit action, so the API requires exactly that boolean (`false` archives honestly; garbage fails VALIDATION) and the UI's confirmation dialog (task 170's deliverable) composes on top — the endpoint also carries D-061's per-table evidence counts in the purge response, so the confirmation flow sees exactly what the cascade removed. **Unknown account is a both-halves verdict** (the review round's P1, folded in): an entry without a row is first-class on this surface (GET lists it, PATCH renames it), so DELETE refuses 404 only when neither the store entry nor the storage row knows the id — an entry-only account archives by its entry removal alone and purges with the honest zero-evidence report, which also makes a failed post-purge entry cleanup retryable through the API (the retry's `managed` still resolves, so it reaches `store.remove` again and heals the ghost instead of stranding it behind a 404). (5) **The test endpoint answers 200 with D-052's vocabulary whenever the test RAN.** A failed credential is a successful test with a negative result, not a request error: `outcome: 'ok' | 'rejected' | 'unavailable'`, the `kind` discriminant read structurally off the thrown error (the field the adapter contract exposes for consumers that cannot import adapter types), the provider's sanitized-by-construction message on failure, and escalation to `INTERNAL` only for unclassifiable throwables (D-113's strict rule applied at the endpoint). A keyless account is `FORBIDDEN`/`no-key-configured` (§7.3's Not configured as the honest refusal); an unresolvable environment name is `unavailable` (§7.2's inconclusive class — the D-112 residual, service-side); the run is bounded by the transport's own §7.2 deadline, not a duplicate race. (6) **Strict body validation, scope-locally.** Fastify's shared Ajv carries `removeAdditional: true` — unknown body fields are silently stripped, so a create payload smuggling `apiKeyEnv` beside the declared fields would be accepted with the smuggled key ignored; §13's boundary rejects it. The plugin compiles its schemas through a scope-local Ajv with `removeAdditional: false` (D-018's discipline) while re-asserting the framework's `coerceTypes: 'array'` (the `?purgeHistory` boolean coercion), `useDefaults`, and `allErrors` — the rest of the API keeps the framework default until a construction-level decision changes it for everyone. (7) **The `raw_responses` gate widening is count-only.** D-061's purge evidence names every §11.2 history table, and one of them is `raw_responses` — the response schema's field carries the deleted-row COUNT (an integer produced by the storage-side `purgeAccount`), never a payload: no stored body, captured header, or size crosses the boundary. `test/unit/raw-response-gate.spec.ts` sanctions exactly `src/schemas/api/accounts.ts` (the D-069 one-file precedent), and §7.4's "never over HTTP" holds for every payload.

**Reasons.** The two-store reality is the spec's own: §6.2/§6.3 put id/providerId/label/enabled and the secret source in the configuration file, §8.2/§11.2 put lifecycle status and history in SQLite, and §6.4 makes the account list live-reloadable — so an accounts endpoint is necessarily a composition over both, and the only question this task could answer without building the composition root is where the configuration half's boundary sits. The D-121 precedent answers it: define the seam at the consumer, land the routes complete against it, and leave the filesystem/reload machinery to the layer that owns it — building a partial ConfigService here would either duplicate the atomic-write/reload layers (065/068's territory) or fork them. The constant mask follows from §15.4 read strictly ("never return API keys") plus the closed-serializer guarantee already proven for health: a derived mask is key material on the wire, and a constant is the only mask that cannot leak by construction. The storage-row-first order follows from the compensation calculus — the facade's synchronous insert makes the row trivially undoable before any history exists, while a configuration entry without a row is a polling-broken ghost. The purge-confirmation reading takes §13's route table as normative (the query parameter IS the explicit action the spec spells) and leaves the human-factors confirmation to the UI task the plan assigns it to. The 200-on-failed-credential shape keeps the §13 envelope for request errors and the body for domain results — the same layering §7.2 keeps between polling outcomes — and the structural `kind` read is the adapter contract's own cross-boundary vocabulary. The scope-local strict Ajv exists because the alternative (a construction-wide change) would alter every landed route's validation behavior from a task whose carve-out is the accounts surface — and because fastify's stripping default is exactly the §13 boundary violation (accepted-and-ignored unknown fields) the error envelope exists to answer. (Correction trail: the task's review round — glm-5.3#max after the deepseek primary timed out and kimi's quota window was spent; one round, REQUEST_CHANGES with 1 P1 / 4 P3 — folded three resolutions into this entry and the same commit, which had not landed when corrected: the P1 both-halves unknown verdict of interpretation (4) (the first draft decided "unknown" on the storage outcome alone, so a configuration-only account could not be deleted by the API that listed it, and a purge whose entry-cleanup failed left an API-unremovable ghost), a foreign-`kind` escalation pin in the test double's vocabulary (a classified-LOOKING `{kind: 'other'}` throw must reach `INTERNAL`, not the 200 shape — the structural reader's reject arm is now executable), and the create-race residual of interpretation (3), declined with reasons and documented at the create site: two truly concurrent same-id creates race the two-step duplicate pre-check and the loser answers INTERNAL over the driver's raw constraint error instead of the 400 duplicate class, but mapping it would message-match SQLite's constraint wording — a fragile contract D-058 keeps out of the facade — and the single-user §15.1 service has no second operator to hold the window open. The round's fourth P3 — flipping task 159's status in `plan/tasks.md` — is the main session's by the cycle's dual-mode rule, not a defect of this commit.)

**Consequences.** The composition task that owns the configuration file and the database implements `AccountConfigStore` over `loadConfigWithEnv` + `writeConfigFile` (+ §6.4's change application) and passes it through `ApiRoutesOptions.accounts`; until then the unwired construction answers the scope catch-all's 404 for `/api/accounts*` (pinned by a test against the plain task-146 construction). The exported surface (`ManagedAccountConfig`, `AccountConfigStore`, `AccountsRouteOptions`, `accountRoutes`, `accountView`, `mergeAccountViews` in `src/server/api/accounts.ts`; the schemas and `ACCOUNT_KEY_MASK` in `src/schemas/api/accounts.ts`; the now-exported `ID_PATTERN` in `src/schemas/config.ts`) is internal API under `src/`, not package surface; changing the seam's method set, the `details.reason` vocabulary, the response field names, or the mask constant is a successor decision (a mask change additionally ripples into the UI's presentation, task 171). The login/logout endpoints remain the D-125/D-126 plan gap: the authorization tests pin the §15.1 seam as it exists (the fail-closed default and the configured modes), and the composed seam-true arm proves the future `RequestAuthenticator` wiring composes with these routes unchanged. §7.2's auth-rejection suspension lift on a manual test is polling-service wiring (D-064's state is not reachable from this seam) — a loose end for the composition task beside the config-sync that mirrors configured accounts into storage rows (the merge already renders the pre-sync lag honestly: `status: 'active'`, null history facts). The done-condition ("each endpoint has contract, authorization, and error tests") is pinned executably: `test/unit/api-accounts-schema.spec.ts` (the closed-contract tables, the charset/`minProperties`/boolean rules, the outcome discriminated union, the no-drift id pin), `test/unit/api-accounts-view.spec.ts` (the pure merge matrix — field ownership, honest-gap views, archived retention, the no-secret-fields key-set pin, the fail-loud guard), and `test/integration/api-accounts.spec.ts` (51 tests over real migrated disposable databases through the real scope: per-endpoint contract shapes and §13 status codes; authorization — the fail-closed 401 across all five endpoints in `required` mode, the composed seam arm, §15.1's proxy 403, and the §15.3 mutation guards binding the new routes bodied and bodiless; errors — unknown provider, duplicate id by row and by store, malformed and smuggled bodies, the empty patch, blank keys, archived and env-key refusals, unknown ids on both DELETE arms, the malformed purge flag with nothing-happened evidence, the post-purge cleanup failure's honest aftermath and the healed ghost-entry retry, the entry-only archive and purge arms, the foreign-`kind` and unclassifiable provider failures' generic 500 with the cause logged and the key absent from the log; and the marker-secret discipline scanning every response body across create/list/patch/rotate/test/purge). `src/server/api/accounts.ts` measures ≥98% on all four coverage axes without joining the D-085 pinned critical-module keys; `src/server/README.md` gains the appended endpoint section, `src/schemas/README.md`'s module inventory stays accurate (the new `api/accounts.ts` follows the `api/` placement it documents), `CHANGELOG.md` carries the boundary, and `test/unit/raw-response-gate.spec.ts` records the count-only widening beside D-069's. No public API, format, or event changes — the HTTP surface is new, its contracts are the task's own deliverable.

## D-129 — Task 165's Vue 3 + Vite application foundation: the composition-root reading of "set up" beside the placeholder, the CSP-shaped build contract (assetsInlineLimit/emptyOutDir plus verify-build's shape checks), and the token seam handed to theme selection (spec §3, §14.1; task 165)

**Date:** 2026-11-02 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§3](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#3-technology-and-packaging), [§14.1](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#141-general-ui-requirements) · **Tasks:** [165](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-127 (the served CSP this task's build contract executes, whose "binds the future UI implementation (165+)" clause is discharged here), D-109 (the task-146 static serving this build output feeds — `ui/dist` or DIST_DIR), D-092 (the typecheck-all gate that already includes `ui/tsconfig.json`)

**Decision.** Task 165 reads "Set up Vue 3 and Vite" as the **application foundation**, not a visible surface: a test-scaffolding placeholder (`ui/`, landing with the e2e/component foundations) already built into dist, so the task's deliverable is what the later UI stages stand on, and nothing they own is built early. (1) **`ui/src/main.ts` is the single composition root** — `createApp(App).mount('#app')` plus the global stylesheet import, with documented seams: Vue Router and the shell layout plug in with 166, the `vue-i18n` English catalog with 167, theme selection with 168; no component owns application wiring, and no plugin is registered early. `src/App.vue` stays the minimal shell root carrying exactly the previous user-visible strings and testids (`Quotameter`, `app-status` + the "not implemented yet" line) — deliberately, so the task-036 ESLint raw-text exception, the e2e smoke/a11y assertions, and the CSP shell spec all keep testing the same contract across the rewrite. (2) **The production build is CSP-shaped twice over**, executing D-127's requirement that `ui/vite.config.ts` set `build.assetsInlineLimit: 0` (Vite's default 4096-byte limit inlines small assets as `data:` URIs, which `img-src`/`font-src 'self'` refuse) and adding `build.emptyOutDir: true` (DIST_DIR sits outside the Vite root, where Vite's guarded auto-clean refuses to act — without the explicit setting, stale hashed assets accumulate in the container volume and stay servable forever; both settings are pinned executably against the resolved config object by `test/component/vite-config.spec.ts`, which lives in the component project so `ui/tsconfig.json` stays the single project checking `ui/**` and its specs). On top of the configuration, `scripts/verify-build.mjs` grows from existence-checking to **shape-checking**: the emitted `index.html` must carry no inline `<script>` without `src`, no `<style>` block (self-closing included), no `style=` attribute (quoted or unquoted — a minifier emits the unquoted form), no inline event handler, no `javascript:` URI, and no `data:` URI; stylesheets must additionally carry no external `url()` reference; and the **JavaScript bundles are scanned for `data:` URIs too** — Vite's asset inlining lands JS-imported assets inside the JS chunk (`import img from './x.png'`), the exact regression `assetsInlineLimit: 0` exists to prevent, so a config edit or plugin that reintroduces inlining fails `make build` (every build, CI included) instead of surfacing as a browser violation only in `make check-all`'s csp-shell spec. The `data:` pattern is MIME-anchored (`data:image/…`, `data:font/…`, …) so attribute text or bundle strings merely starting with "data:" cannot false-positive. Fixing the script for this extension also fixed a **latent vacuous check**: `fs.promises.glob` returns an async iterable, so the original `matches.length === 0` compared `undefined` and could never fire — a build missing its JS/CSS bundles passed verification since the script landed; the materializing `globArray` helper removes it. (3) **The theme seam is token-shaped, not behavior-shaped**: `ui/src/assets/base.css` defines `--qm-*` custom properties on `:root` with a `prefers-color-scheme: dark` override block — the `system` half of §14.1's three modes — plus the local system font stack (§14.1's "bundle fonts and assets locally" is satisfied by not fetching any); components consume tokens, never raw colors, and 168 adds the explicit light/dark override hook and browser-storage persistence on top of these names (charts styling for both modes rides the same tokens in 175/176). (4) **The npm-package surface is untouched**: `package.json`'s `files` allowlist gains no `dist/` entry — §3's "the tarball includes the ready-to-serve `dist/` output" is task 184's manifest finalization, coordinated with `check-package`'s allowlist pins; nothing here pre-empts it. (Correction trail: the task's review round — deepseek-v4.1-flash, one round, APPROVE, 0 P0 / 0 P1 / 3 P2 / 5 P3 — folded five findings into this entry and the same commit, which had not landed when corrected (the D-124/D-127 precedent): the JS-bundle `data:` scan and the unquoted/self-closing style forms (P2-1/P2-2, both demonstrated by the reviewer as false negatives); the executable pin on the two vite settings (P2-3 — they have no observable effect while the UI references no sub-4 KiB asset, so nothing else in the tree could catch a deletion); the MIME anchoring that removes the "Data:"-text and `data-style=` false positives (P3-1); and the extra shapes — inline event handlers, `javascript:` URIs, external stylesheet `url()` (P3-2, partially adopted: the handler/URI/url() checks are cheap and noise-free in a Vite tree, while a broad external-`href` check was declined with reason — a plain `<a href="https://…">` link is a legal navigation CSP does not block, and §14.1's "do not call third-party domains" is a fetch rule; flagging anchors would break legitimate future content). Two further P3s were deferred rather than adopted: the `emptyOutDir` blast-radius guard (P3-3 — DIST_DIR is compose-hardcoded to a dedicated volume path; a README caution replaces code, and a misconfigured override deleting a non-dedicated directory stays the operator's own blast radius) and dark-mode contrast scanning (P3-4 — the axe e2e runs Chromium's light default; the tokens' manual ratios pass AA comfortably in both modes (muted 6.82 light / 7.67 dark) and the `colorScheme: 'dark'` a11y pass belongs to 168, which owns themes.)

**Reasons.** The scope reading follows the plan's own sequencing: 166–168 own the router, the string catalog, and the theme controls, so a foundation that built any of their surface would leave them rewriting it (the main session's "leave seams, don't implement" instruction is this entry's short form). Keeping the placeholder strings and testids identical across the rewrite keeps three e2e suites and one lint exception as change detectors for the mount contract instead of churning them into task 165's diff — the smallest blast radius a foundation rewrite can have. The double CSP shaping (configuration + verification) is defense in depth for D-127's binding: the vite settings prevent the known inlining behaviors at the source, while the verify-build shape checks catch the unknown ones (a plugin update that starts inlining, a config edit that re-enables the limit) at the earliest gate every build passes — and the browser-level proof stays where D-127 put it, on the real server. The verify-build extension is justified over e2e-only coverage because `make check` (the per-task gate) runs no build and no browser: without a build-time check, a CSP-incompatible build could land through a green `make check` and fail only at `check-all` — or worse, in production serving. `emptyOutDir: true` is safe in exactly the direction it acts: host/CI builds to `ui/dist` inside the root are cleaned by Vite's default anyway, and the DIST_DIR container path is a dedicated build-output directory owned by this configuration (compose.yaml's volume), never a user path.

**Consequences.** `ui/` now carries `README.md` (stack, build flow, DIST_DIR invariant, contributor CSP rules, layout, the strings/language rule), `src/assets/base.css` (tokens + document base), the rewritten `src/main.ts` and `src/App.vue`, and the hardened `ui/vite.config.ts`; `scripts/verify-build.mjs` keeps its success message's stable prefix and now answers "expected outputs present, CSP shape clean". The contract's own tests are `test/integration/verify-build-script.spec.ts` (the tz-verify-script pattern: real child processes over synthetic dist trees in temp dirs) — happy tree and a same-origin `url("/assets/…")` stylesheet exit 0; missing `index.html`, missing CSS bundle, inline script, style block (both forms), style attribute (both forms), event handler, `javascript:` URI, `data:` URI in HTML, in CSS, and in a JS bundle, and an external stylesheet `url()` each exit 1 with their message, the JS/CSS `data:` rows pinning the shape checks the vite settings should make unreachable (the regression net for when those settings regress) — plus `test/component/vite-config.spec.ts` pinning the two settings themselves against the resolved config. Done-condition evidence ("the app builds into the expected dist/ directory" and serves/renders from Fastify): `make build` emits hashed external bundles into DIST_DIR with verify green; the e2e suite runs green over that build — smoke (shell renders, title/heading/status assertions unchanged), a11y (h1 contract), and csp-shell (the real `buildHttpServer` construction: byte-exact §15.5 headers and zero `securitypolicyviolation`/console-error records on `/` and a deep link); the component mount suite passes unchanged, and the built CSS shows the tokens and the dark-mode block surviving the bundle. Known residuals, deliberate: the two App.vue strings remain raw until 167's catalog (the documented task-036 exception), the `fs.glob` ExperimentalWarning on verify-build's stderr is expected noise (the `node:sqlite` precedent), and prettier/eslint may still disagree over the long `<p>` line in `App.vue` (the gotchas.md ping-pong rule: prettier wins, the eslint warning stays).

## D-130 — The §13 status/providers/quota/settings endpoints of task 160: the §7.3-facts composition over 159's seams plus two §6.4-live readers, the D-077 reading of `/api/quota`, the registry-driven providers listing nesting the config's own schedule contract, the annotated settings view with restart-required **refused** in PUT (§13's "allowed for runtime modification" read literally), and `SettingsStore` as the third consumer-owned seam (spec §13, §7.2, §7.3, §8.4, §9.2, §6.2–§6.4, §14.5, §15.2, §15.4; task 160)

**Date:** 2026-11-02 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§13](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#13-http-api), [§7.2–§7.4](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#72-retry-and-error-behavior), [§8.4](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#84-normalized-snapshot-and-metric-model), [§9.2](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#92-configuration-and-validation), [§6.4](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#64-change-application), [§14.5](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#145-settings) · **Tasks:** [160](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-128 (the registration rule these plugins follow and the `AccountConfigStore` seam whose type `StatusRouteOptions` reuses verbatim — one store instance serves both route families), D-121 (the consumer-owned seam precedent — `SettingsStore` is its third application after `RequestAuthenticator` and `AccountConfigStore`), D-022 (the settings-validation boundary the PUT runs and whose `pendingPassword` hand-off this task discharges at the endpoint consumer: the plaintext reaches the store seam, hashing stays the composition/auth-service's), D-026 (the §6.4 classification whose vocabulary the PUT response reports and whose restart list the view marks), D-023 (the environment-source marking rendered as the view's `source: 'environment'` — the read-only annotation Stage 12/13 was instructed not to re-derive), D-070/D-114 (the §7.3 derivation and last-error selection composed verbatim, and the exact-occurrence secret redaction now mirrored server-side), D-077 (the last-valid-value query that defines `/api/quota`'s metric rows), D-111 (the closed-contract serializer guard, applied to every new response), D-113 (the frozen error registry — no new codes), D-100 (the shared-pattern rule — `PeakHoursConfigSchema` nested whole into the providers response, the `ID_PATTERN` precedent scaled to a node)

**Decision.** Task 160 lands the four §13 route families as three plugins (`src/server/api/status.ts` registering `GET /api/status` + `GET /api/quota`, `src/server/api/providers.ts`, `src/server/api/settings.ts`) behind D-128's optional-options rule, and pins six interpretations.
