(1) **The status family is composition, not derivation.** `deriveAccountStatus`/`readPollingRunEvidence` (task 111) and `getLatestValidMetricValues`/`getLatestSnapshot` (tasks 122/…) are consumed verbatim; the endpoint adds only the merge (the D-128 union of configuration entries and storage rows — archived accounts stay visible and derive `disabled`, their §8.2-retained history served by `/api/quota`), §7.2's last-error selection (six bounded outcome-filtered probes, the D-114 method), and two §6.4-live per-request seams — `pollingIntervalSeconds` and `suspensionOf` — because both inputs change under reload and a construction-time constant would freeze the freshness window; `suspensionOf` defaults to unsuspended at the composition exactly as D-070 recorded for the restart view. `configured` resolves through `AccountConfigStore.secretOf` (the connection test's own source of truth), and the resolved value additionally feeds an exact-occurrence redaction of the last-error message — §7.4's rule made server-side over D-048's sanitized-by-construction transport errors. (2) **`/api/quota` is task 122's reading of "latest successful snapshot":** header facts from the latest snapshot, metric rows from the last-valid-per-key query with per-row collection stamps (rows may come from different snapshots), the §7.3 status riding as freshness context, absence honest (`metrics: []`, null facts — §7.2's never-zero), and the both-halves 404 reserved for an account known to neither store nor storage; timestamps are epoch-ms integers — the landed D-128 accounts vocabulary — with §10's ISO-8601 sentence read as governing the §13 range _parameters_ (history/events `from`/`to`), the single-format reading recorded here so the surface never mixes clocks. The §8.4 `label` is **not** served: the storage row omits it (D-039) and no metric catalog exists on the provider contract — the §14.3 overview's label need is a provider-layer export decision left to a later task (`/api/providers` is its natural carrier), not an invented wire field. (3) **`/api/providers` is registry-driven:** the listing answers available types in registration order; a configuration entry naming an unregistered adapter is not listed (not an available type — the D-119 doctor case reports it), a registered provider without a configured schedule answers `peakHours: null` (§9.2's honest absence, never an invented schedule), and the response nests `PeakHoursConfigSchema` itself so the wire contract and the file contract cannot drift (D-100's one-pattern-two-consumers rule at node scale); `requestTimeoutSeconds` stays off the wire (§13 names types and schedules). (4) **The settings GET is annotated, not just valued:** every scalar carries `{ value, source, restartRequired }` — §14.5's restart and read-only markings as data (the restart set is §6.4's closed trio, drift-pinned against `RESTART_REQUIRED_FIELDS`; `source: 'environment'` is D-023's marking), `passwordConfigured` is the mask-and-boolean, `paths` is the read-only §14.5 display block, and no view object can express a secret (closed contracts; the accounts/providers sections are absent entirely — their own §13 surfaces own them, which also makes D-022's naive-GET-then-PUT secret-drop hazard structurally unexpressable here). (5) **PUT refuses the restart trio** — §13's "Update settings allowed for runtime modification" read literally: `server.host`/`server.port`/`auth.mode` answer FORBIDDEN `restart-required-field` with the file-plus-`quotameter restart` remedy (§6.4's own prescription for the UI), environment-overridden fields answer `environment-overridden-read-only` (§6.3; checked first because the environment wins over the file), and a supplied `auth.passwordHash` answers `password-hash-not-settable` (D-022's channel rule; a client-settable hash is a lockout footgun) — while validation runs through `validateSettings` → `parseConfig` (the loader's own rules; the body schema stays structural so the problems vocabulary stays single-sourced) and the response reports D-026's `applied`/`restartRequired`, where a non-empty restart list reveals a hand-edited pending change through the startup diff — never this request's doing, since this endpoint refuses to make one. (6) **`SettingsStore` is the third consumer-owned seam** (`read`/`apply`, defined in `src/server/api/settings.ts`): `apply` receives the validated merged configuration (omitted sections — including stored account secrets and provider schedules — survive, per D-022's merge semantics) plus the pending password for the composition to hash with §15.2's scrypt and to trigger §6.4's change application; session revocation on password change stays with the future auth service, as D-124/D-123 recorded.

**Reasons.** The task's only architectural question was where each half of the two-store reality lives: for the status family the answer is "nowhere new" — 159's seam already exposes exactly the configuration facts §7.3 needs, and the two live inputs get readers rather than constants because §6.4 makes their subjects reloadable (a pinned wire test moves the interval and watches the freshness window follow). The quota reading follows the main session's directive and §7.2's retention rule: the operator's question is "what is the last thing I know", which is the last valid value per metric, not the latest snapshot's possibly-invalid rows; serving archived accounts is §8.2's own retention semantics (a read is not a mutation — 159's archive refusals are all mutations). The providers registry-drive follows §8.1's extensibility contract: a type exists when an adapter is registered; joining the schedule from live configuration keeps §9.2's file-edited schedule honest on both sides (read-only on the wire, swapped by reload). The PUT refusal reading takes §13's route-table sentence as normative beside §6.4's taxonomy: the UI cannot restart the process (§6.4 says _show_ `quotameter restart` — a CLI), so an accepted server.port write would silently diverge from the running listener with no remedy but the same file edit the refusal prescribes; identifying the trio in GET (per the done-condition) and refusing it in PUT keeps both §13 sentences true without a second configuration channel. The `passwordHash` refusal closes the one direction D-022 left open at this boundary: the boundary accepts the hash for init/CLI file writes, but an API client setting an opaque hash it cannot verify is a lockout, and the boundary's own `pendingPassword` mechanism exists precisely so the plaintext is the only channel. `SettingsStore`'s shape (validated-config-in, outcome-out) mirrors what the composition already owns — the reloader's diff is the outcome vocabulary, the atomic write is D-101/D-108's machinery — so the seam adds no behavior, only the injection point.

**Consequences.** The composition task that owns the configuration file and the reloader implements `SettingsStore` (hashing `pendingPassword`, revoking sessions on password change per §15.2/D-124, applying §6.4 through `reload()`, and — the review round's write-side obligation, carried on the `apply` payload as `sources` — **excluding every `sources.fields` path from the file write**, because the configuration handed over is the environment-merged effective one and persisting it verbatim would bake `QUOTAMETER_*` values into `config.json`) and passes it plus the status readers through `ApiRoutesOptions.status`/`.providers`/`.settings`; until then the unwired construction answers the scope catch-all's 404 for all five paths (pinned per family). The exported surface (`StatusRouteOptions`, `statusRoutes`, `lastErrorOf`, `redactSecretOccurrences`, `statusAccountView`, `metricView` in `src/server/api/status.ts`; `ProvidersRouteOptions`, `providersRoutes` in `src/server/api/providers.ts`; `SettingsStore`, `SettingsSnapshot`, `SettingsApplyOutcome`, `SettingsRouteOptions`, `settingsRoutes`, `settingsViewOf`, `attemptedSettingsFields`, `blankAttemptedSettingsFields` in `src/server/api/settings.ts`; `strictValidatorCompiler` in `src/server/api/validation.ts`; the schemas in `src/schemas/api/{status,providers,settings}.ts`) is internal API under `src/`, not package surface; changing the seam method sets, the `details.reason` vocabulary (`environment-overridden-read-only`, `restart-required-field`, `password-hash-not-settable`, `invalid-settings`, `blank-value`), the response field names, or the annotated-view shape is a successor decision. The review round (deepseek-v4.1-flash, APPROVE, 4 P2 / 5 P3) was folded in before landing beside three of its smaller findings: the **blank-value refusal** (a supplied-but-blank-after-trim field is a client mistake through the request body — `VALIDATION`/`blank-value` — not D-022's prompt-skip "not supplied", which stays the right semantics for init/CLI; without the refusal a blank password "change" answered success while changing nothing), the **sources-on-apply payload** above, the shared `strictValidatorCompiler` construction (one D-128 site for the new plugins; the accounts module's own copy is frozen history that joins at its next owning change), the §7.4 **plan-name redaction** in `/api/quota` (provider-controlled data fields get the same exact-occurrence guard as error messages), and the one-clock-per-response hoist. Known residuals, recorded: the metric `label` gap for §14.3 (a provider-layer catalog export is the missing piece; `/api/providers` is its natural carrier when it lands); the last-error and plan-name redaction covers the account's currently-configured secret only — an archived account's removed entry leaves nothing resolvable to redact with, accepted because §7.2 transport messages are sanitized by construction (D-048) and the marker pins cover every reachable flow; the **accounts surface's `planName` shares the provider-text exposure** `/api/quota` now redacts — 159's frozen module, left to its owning change (the same standing note as its validator copy); `logging.level` is PUT-able (D-026 classifies it live) but its live application rides the composition's `setLevel` wiring, not this endpoint; and the §13 route table's `auth` family (login/logout/session) remains the D-125/D-126 plan gap. The done-condition ("secrets are excluded and restart-required settings are identified") is pinned executably: `test/unit/api-settings-schema.spec.ts` (the closed no-secret guard and the restart-flag no-drift row), `test/unit/api-settings-view.spec.ts` (the annotation matrix incl. environment marking and default fallbacks, the attempted-fields ≡ `ENV_OVERRIDES` row, and the blank-value table), `test/integration/api-settings.spec.ts` (the wire pins: restart flags on the wire, the three refusals with stable reasons, the blank-value refusal, the sources-on-apply payload, marker hash/key/password absent from every response body, the pending password reaching only the seam), beside the status/quota/providers suites' contract/authorization/error rows and their own marker pins (`[REDACTED]` rendering for the stored error and the plan name included).

## D-131 — Task 166's Vue Router and app shell: the four-route table with a catch-all overview redirect, lazy route components under the CSP build contract, the shell layout, and the bootstrap status line relocated into the overview view (spec §14; task 166)

**Date:** 2026-11-02 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§14](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#14-web-interface), [§14.1](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#141-general-ui-requirements) · **Tasks:** [166](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-129 (the composition root and shell seams this task fills in), D-127 (the served CSP the lazy-chunk output must keep satisfying), D-109 (the static serving + SPA fallback the router rides on)

**Decision.** (1) **The route table is exactly §14's four pages** — overview (`/`, name `overview`), account management (`/accounts`, §14.2), settings (`/settings`, §14.5), and login (`/login`, §14.6) — as named routes with **lazy-loaded components** (`() => import(...)`): code splitting keeps the initial shell light and, under D-127/D-129's build contract, every view is an external hashed chunk admitted by `script-src 'self'` — verified by the green csp-shell e2e over the rebuilt bundle. **The catch-all redirects to `/`**: §14 prescribes no not-found screen, so an unknown client path lands where the SPA fallback itself lands (§14.1) — the overview — rather than inventing an unspecified 404 surface (and its strings). (2) **`createAppRouter(history = createWebHistory())`** is the factory in `ui/src/router/index.ts`: the injectable history is the component-test seam (memory history, no browser location), and `main.ts` mounts **after `router.isReady()` resolves**, so a direct deep link paints the target view on the first render instead of an empty outlet — the client half of the done-condition's "direct navigation works". (3) **The shell layout**: `App.vue` is the persistent surface — site header (the `Quotameter` h1 and the primary nav) and the single `main` landmark carrying `RouterView`. The nav holds the three always-present sections (Overview, Accounts, Settings); **the login entry is auth-state dependent and deliberately absent** — task 180's seam, marked by comment in the layout, with the `/login` route already named so the future guard redirects by name. Views render `h2` headings, preserving the exactly-one-h1 a11y contract. (4) **The bootstrap status line moves from the shell into the overview view**: the `app-status` testid and its exact D-129 string are page content, not shell chrome — the smoke contract (asserted at `/`), the a11y h1 pin, and the csp-shell `/` + `/accounts` deep-link assertions all stay green byte-identical, and each content task (170+, 172–174, 179, 180) replaces its view wholesale without touching the shell. The other three views carry a uniform `data-testid="page-status"` placeholder ("Not implemented yet.") — the honest marker where content has not landed. (5) **The task-036 i18n exception is extended, not removed**: five fixed strings join the ignore list (the four section labels, reused as nav text and view headings, and the placeholder marker); task 167's catalog replaces them and re-tightens the rule. (6) Tooling facts recorded for the tree: `vue-router` lands as **devDependency `^5.4.0`** beside `vue` — both are build-time/bundled UI dependencies (the shipped package carries the built dist, task 184's manifest finalization; nothing runtime imports vue-router from `files/`); vue-router 5's **navigation chain settles across a macrotask hop**, so a DOM-driven push under happy-dom never resolves on microtask flushing alone — `test/component/app.spec.ts` drains with a short timer hop (`settleNavigation`), while the browser needs nothing (the e2e probe drives the same flows without waits); and `createMemoryHistory(base)`'s argument is a base, **not** an initial location (the queue starts at `""` → the root), so the specs push the initial route before mounting.

**Reasons.** The scope reading follows D-129's sequencing: 166 owns the routes and the shell they live in, and nothing the content tasks own is built early — the four views are placeholders with honest markers, per the plan's own task list (170+/172–174/179/180). The redirect-over-not-found choice keeps the URL surface to the four specified pages and avoids unspecified UI (and untracked strings) in a task whose strings are, by instruction, held minimal until 167's catalog. Relocating `app-status` into the overview view is the smallest change that keeps every e2e contract a change detector for the new shell instead of churning three specs into this diff — and it puts the status line where the content task will replace it, not in shared chrome someone would have to remember to remove. The devDependency placement mirrors `vue` exactly; the lockfile (host-installed, container volume synced via `make deps`) is the only dependency change.

**Consequences.** `ui/src/router/index.ts` (routes + factory), `ui/src/views/{Overview,Accounts,Settings,Login}View.vue` (placeholders), the rewritten `App.vue` and `main.ts`, the extended i18n ignore list in `eslint.config.ts`, and `ui/README.md`'s route table land together. Done-condition evidence: `test/component/router.spec.ts` (each path resolves to its named route; direct navigation reaches all four; unknown paths redirect to the overview — memory history), `test/component/app.spec.ts` (nav surface and its three-links-only shape, per-route view rendering via h2 + `page-status`, link-click navigation with the `aria-current` pin, the overview status placeholder at `/`), and the browser-level probe in `test/e2e/smoke.spec.ts` (deep link `/accounts` renders its view through the SPA fallback; a nav click switches to `/settings` client-side — a `window` sentinel proves no full reload) beside the existing csp-shell deep-link proof — all green over the rebuilt bundle with `make check` and the Playwright leg. The review round (deepseek-v4.1-flash, one round, APPROVE, 0 P0 / 0 P1 / 1 P2 / 4 P3) had all five findings accepted and folded into the same commit: the mount now happens on both `router.isReady()` arms (a rejected initial navigation — a lazy-chunk fetch error — still mounts the recoverable shell instead of a blank page), the e2e client-navigation probe gained its no-reload sentinel, the router spec pins that every page route stays a lazy importer (static imports would silently undo the external-chunk code splitting), the `aria-label="Primary"` i18n blind spot is recorded in the loose ends below, and the three stale documentation references (testing.md's exemption count, gotchas.md's `<p>`-warning location, package-layout.md's reserved rows) are updated. Loose ends handed forward: 167 moves the seven raw strings (six now + any it finds) into the catalog and re-tightens `no-raw-text` — the nav's `aria-label="Primary"` must reach the catalog too, and its completeness check must know `no-raw-text` reads text nodes only, so attribute strings are invisible to the lint (the review round's finding); 180 wires the auth guard behind the named `/login` route and adds the nav's auth-state entry; 168's theme hooks are untouched (the shell consumes `--qm-*` tokens only).

## D-132 — Task 167's vue-i18n English catalog: the typed nested-by-surface catalog module, the `createAppI18n` factory, the no-exceptions lint re-tightening, and the both-directions completeness spec covering `no-raw-text`'s attribute blind spot (spec §14.1, §4.1; task 167)

**Date:** 2026-11-03 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§14.1](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#141-general-ui-requirements), [§4.1](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#41-public-repository-and-language) · **Tasks:** [167](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-131 (the shell whose raw strings and extended lint exception this task retires, and whose recorded `aria-label` blind spot is closed executably here), D-129 (the composition-root seam `createAppI18n` plugs into, and the `app-status` string the catalog preserves byte-exactly), D-127 (the served CSP the runtime-only catalog lookup stays neutral to), D-092 (the typecheck-all gate that now also checks the i18n modules)

**Decision.** Task 167 lands §14.1's sentence — "The only shipped language is English, but all strings must live in the `en` locale catalog through `vue-i18n`; hardcoded strings in components are prohibited and checked by lint/tests." — as five interpretations. (Correction trail: the task's review round — deepseek-v4.1-flash, one round, APPROVE, 0 P0/P1, 3 P2/3 P3 — folded in before landing: the lint `attributes` option and the closed attribute list (P2-1, P3-3 — the first draft put attribute checking on the spec alone and its docs overpromised "any" attribute), the `fallbackLocale` assertion (P2-2), the removal of the dead `EnCatalog` export and the softened typing claim (P2-3), the empty-namespace guard (P3-1), and quote-aware comment stripping (P3-2) all entered this entry and the same commit.) (1) **The catalog is a typed TS module, not locale files**: `ui/src/i18n/en.ts` exports the `en` object `as const`; vue-i18n's SFC-block/locale-directory machinery is deliberately not adopted — a typed module keeps the tree free of a parallel message file format (the same reasoning that keeps `ui/tsconfig.json` the single checking project, U-030). Key-level `t()` typing (`DefineLocaleMessage` augmentation making a wrong key a compile error) was considered and deliberately not adopted: the both-directions spec already fails a wrong key at test time, and the augmentation is a self-contained option for a later task. The structure is **nested by surface with flat dot paths at the call sites**: `app` and `nav` own the shell chrome, each route page owns one namespace (`overview`, `accounts`, `settings`, `login`) holding its `title` and placeholder `status`, and identical values in different namespaces stay distinct keys — the contexts differ and may diverge (`nav.overview` labels a link, `overview.title` a heading). (2) **`createAppI18n()`** creates the instance with `legacy: false`, `locale: 'en'`, `fallbackLocale: 'en'`, messages inline; a factory, not a singleton, mirrors `createAppRouter` (D-131) so component tests install their own instance per mount, and it is registered beside the router in the D-129 composition root. The return type stays inferred: annotating it as the generic `I18n` widens `global` to the legacy/composition union and hides the `Composer` the tests pin. (3) **The lint exception is gone, and the rule sees attributes too**: `@intlify/vue-i18n/no-raw-text` runs with no text exemptions and with the rule's own `attributes` option — for every tag, a static literal in a text-bearing attribute (`aria-label`, `aria-description`, `aria-placeholder`, `aria-roledescription`, `aria-valuetext`, `alt`, `title`, `placeholder`, `label`, `abbr`; form values and ID references excluded as non-labels) is an error, while bound expressions (`:attr="t('…')"`) stay legal — D-131's blind spot closed at lint time. The lint contract `test/unit/vue-i18n-lint.spec.ts` pins all of it through the real ESLint binary: the former bootstrap spellings ("Quotameter", "Not implemented yet.") fail as raw text, a static `title="…"` fails, and a bound `:aria-label="t(…)"` passes (exactly one error in the fixture). The shell plus all four views render through `t()` with bytes identical to the pre-catalog literals — the smoke/a11y/csp-shell e2e contracts stay green unchanged. (4) **The completeness rule is both-directions, shape-aware, and attribute-aware** (`test/component/i18n-catalog.spec.ts`): it fails when a `t()` key used in `ui/src` is missing from the catalog; when a catalog key is referenced nowhere (dead keys die with their pages — no reserved namespaces, and an **empty namespace cannot smuggle one past**: the shape walk requires every namespace to carry at least one entry); when a `t()` argument is not a static string literal (a dynamic key would be invisible to both directions above); when a static literal sits in a user-facing attribute in a template (the test-side twin of the lint option, with a **no-drift pin** asserting the spec's list equals the ESLint rule's — one list changing alone fails); and when a bound attribute's expression is _exactly_ a string literal (`:title="'Save'"` — a static literal in disguise that the lint rule cannot see, being an expression). Source scans are **comment-aware and quote-aware**: block, line, and HTML comments are stripped by a small quote-tracking scanner (a plain `//.*$` regex would corrupt `https://…` inside strings and template attributes), so documentation mentions of `t(…)` cannot fake a usage or a dynamic — both stripper behaviors are pinned by helper tests — and the spec's guards were verified non-vacuous by scratch regressions: a static `aria-label`, a missing key, and a dead key each fail it with a locating message. (5) **`vue-i18n` is a devDependency mirroring `vue`/`vue-router`** (D-131's placement rule: the shipped tarball carries the prebuilt bundle, so UI framework deps are build-time only; §3 keeps runtime dependencies minimal), and the runtime it adds is CSP-neutral — message strings compile to an AST that is interpreted, never `eval`/`new Function` — pinned the strongest way available: the csp-shell e2e's zero-violation record over the rebuilt bundle.

**Reasons.** §14.1's sentence carries two obligations — strings live in the catalog, and the ban is "checked by lint/tests" — so the task's deliverable is the enforcement pair as much as the catalog: the re-tightened rule discharges the lint clause, the completeness spec the test clause, and the attribute scan exists precisely because the lint rule reads text nodes only (D-131 recorded that `aria-label` is invisible to it and required "a documented equivalent" — the scan is that equivalent, executable). Both-directions completeness because a catalog that may accumulate dead keys decays into archaeology within a task or two — the placeholder entries exist to be replaced, and an unused-key rule is what forces their deletion. Static-literal-only lookups because they are the premise that makes both directions computable by scan. The factory shape follows D-131's hermetic-test precedent, and the inferred return type follows vue-i18n's own generics: the useful type is the narrowed one. The devDependency placement and the typed-module catalog both follow the project's existing pins (D-131; U-030's single-project typing) rather than introducing new conventions mid-stream.

**Consequences.** `ui/src/i18n/{en.ts,index.ts}` land; `ui/src/main.ts` installs the factory; `App.vue` and the four views render exclusively through `t()` (twelve text nodes and the nav's `aria-label` binding); `eslint.config.ts` carries the exception-less rule with the `attributes` option; the two specs (`test/component/i18n-catalog.spec.ts`, the extended `test/unit/vue-i18n-lint.spec.ts`) pin the contract executably; `vue-i18n@^11.4.17` joins the devDependencies (the only dependency change — host-installed, container-synced through the lockfile). Documentation moved with the code: `ui/README.md`'s catalog section (structure, both-directions rule, the closed attribute list with the no-drift pin and the bound-literal rule, message-format escaping, and the one deliberate non-catalog string — the static `<title>` in `index.html`, a document-shell artifact outside Vue, not a component string), `docs/agents/testing.md`'s i18n rule (the exemptions are gone), and `docs/architecture/package-layout.md`'s UI table (`ui/src/i18n/` replaces the never-materialized `ui/src/locales/` reservation). Known residual, documented: the ESLint `vue/singleline-html-element-content-newline` warnings on the short `<p>` placeholder lines persist (the pre-existing Prettier/eslint-plugin-vue standoff, gotchas.md — do not "fix"). Convention handed to the later UI tasks (168 theme, 170+, 172–174, 179, 180): new keys go under the owning page's namespace (or `app`/`nav` for chrome) in the same commit as the consuming component; raw text nodes, static user-facing attribute literals, bound-literal disguises, and dynamic lookups are all build failures by lint or by the completeness spec; message-format specials (`{`, `}`, `@`, `|`) must be literal-escaped (`{'@'}`) in catalog values. Loose end recorded: key-level `t()` typing via `DefineLocaleMessage` augmentation remains available as a self-contained follow-up if compile-time key narrowing is ever wanted.

## D-133 — Task 168's theme selection: the `data-theme` attribute token override, the `quotameter.theme` browser-storage contract, the `createAppTheme` plugin with injectable storage/media seams, and the deferred per-mode a11y scans (spec §14.1; task 168)

**Date:** 2026-11-03 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§14.1](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#141-general-ui-requirements) · **Tasks:** [168](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-129 (the `--qm-*` token seam and the `prefers-color-scheme` block this task builds the override half onto, and the dark-mode a11y deferral this task owns), D-131 (the shell the theme control lands in), D-132 (the catalog discipline every new theme string follows), D-127 (the CSP the attribute-flip mechanism must stay neutral to)

**Decision.** Task 168 lands §14.1's sentence "Support `system`, `light`, and `dark` themes. Persist the choice in browser storage and style charts for both light and dark modes." as four parts. (1) **The mechanism is an attribute, not a class or a stylesheet swap**: the controller sets `data-theme="light"|"dark"` on the document element and **removes the attribute for `system`**, with `base.css` carrying the selector contract — the `:root, :root[data-theme='light']` block holds the light tokens, a `prefers-color-scheme: dark` block guarded by `:not([data-theme])` holds the dark tokens (so the media query governs exactly when no explicit mode is set), and a `:root[data-theme='dark']` block re-asserts them (the dark values are deliberately duplicated: CSS cannot share one declaration list between a media query and a selector, and the `light-dark()` function — the deduplication CSS offers — is unusable here because a custom property stores the unresolved token, so `getComputedStyle().getPropertyValue('--qm-…')` would hand the future charts a `light-dark(#fff, #17171b)` wrapper instead of a color; explicit duplication keeps every token chart-readable verbatim). The attribute selector outspecifies the media block's `:root`, so explicit `light` overrides an OS dark preference — the whole point of the explicit modes — and flipping the attribute re-cascades the tokens with **no reload and no inline style** (D-127 untouched: a data attribute and CSSOM-driven cascade, no `style=` anywhere; csp-shell stays green over the rebuilt bundle). `color-scheme: light|dark` rides the same three blocks so UA widgets (form controls, scrollbars) follow the mode; the `<meta name="color-scheme">` stays as the pre-CSS system default. (2) **The persistence contract**: browser `localStorage` under the key **`quotameter.theme`**, values exactly `system`/`light`/`dark`; an absent or invalid stored value reads as `system` (silently — the invalid value is never echoed or written back until the user picks a mode), and both directions of the storage exchange are best-effort-try/catch: browsers where `window.localStorage` access itself throws (all-cookies-blocked Safari) or where `setItem` fails (quota, private mode) still get a fully working theme for the session — the choice persists wherever the browser allows writing, and nowhere else is persistence possible; `no-console` is error-level in `ui/**`, so the failures are swallowed with a comment, not logged. The pre-paint flash for a stored explicit mode (page paints system-light until JS runs) is accepted: the only standard mitigation is an inline pre-render script, which D-127's no-inline CSP forbids by construction (no nonces), and a self-hosted tool's one-paint flash is the smaller cost than weakening the policy. (3) **`createAppTheme({storage?, media?})` is a Vue plugin** (`ui/src/theme.ts`): `install()` provides the controller and starts the two effects — the `watchEffect` mapping the preference onto the document attribute, and a `change` listener on the `prefers-color-scheme: dark` media seam feeding `resolvedTheme` (the computed that answers what is actually displayed: explicit modes verbatim, `system` resolved through the seam — the reactive hook the 175/176 charts subscribe to for re-renders). The seams mirror `createAppRouter(history)`/`createAppI18n()` (D-131/D-132): the composition root installs the real browser seams, component tests install `MemoryThemeStorage`/`FakeThemeMedia` per mount (`test/helpers/theme.ts`); `useTheme()` injects and throws loudly when the plugin is missing. The user-facing control is deliberately a **labeled `<select>` in the shell header** (not a cycling button): explicit state needs no cycle-order semantics to document, test, or explain to a screen reader, keyboard operation is native, and task 179's settings page reuses the same `useTheme()` seam with the same three-option shape under its own namespace. The four new strings live under `app.theme.*` in the catalog (D-132, same commit as the consuming component). (4) **D-129's deferred dark-mode a11y pass lands here**: `test/e2e/a11y.spec.ts` scans the shell with its tokens actually applied per mode — explicit `light` and explicit `dark` through the control (each `data-theme` state asserted before axe runs, so a broken handler cannot silently scan one light page twice), plus `system` under `emulateMedia({ colorScheme: 'dark' })` (D-129's recorded "axe e2e runs Chromium's light default" gap) — all clean against the existing wcag2a/2aa/21a/21aa/22aa tag set.

**Reasons.** The attribute-removal-means-system invariant makes the CSS the single authority: the `:not([data-theme])` guard expresses "media query only when unspecified" in the stylesheet itself, so the cascade cannot disagree with the controller (a stale `data-theme="system"` attribute would need a fourth CSS arm to stay honest — removing the attribute instead reuses the `:root` default). The plugin shape follows the landed composition-root pattern so `main.ts` reads as three sibling `app.use()` lines and every test seam is injectable rather than mocked. The select-over-button choice buys explicit state semantics at zero a11y cost — the cycling alternative needs its order explained somewhere (aria-label, docs) and hides the target mode until clicked, which is friction for exactly the low-vision users the AA work serves. The persistence fallbacks are the spec's own generosity boundary: §14.1 demands persistence, browsers may refuse storage, and the honest resolution is "session-scoped theme, no crash" rather than a broken shell. The e2e pins the done-condition where it is observable: computed `body` background flips live on select changes (the token cascade, not a class cosmetic, proven reload-free by a window sentinel), survives reload, follows emulated OS flips in system mode, and rejects invalid stored values without writing them back — plus the raw-token reads (the way the charts will read them, `getComputedStyle` on the document element) pinning a verbatim color per mode and the system-dark/explicit-dark agreement, and the per-mode axe scans closing D-129's recorded follow-up in the same commit that makes dark mode user-reachable.

**Consequences.** `ui/src/theme.ts` lands (`createAppTheme`, `useTheme`, `THEME_STORAGE_KEY = 'quotameter.theme'`, `isTheme`, the `ThemeStorage`/`ThemeMedia` seams — both with `add`/`removeEventListener` on the media side so `install()` can scope the listener to the app through `app.onUnmount` beside the stopped attribute effect); `base.css` carries the three-block selector contract with `color-scheme`; `App.vue` gains the labeled select and the flex header row; `main.ts` installs the plugin; `app.theme.{label,system,light,dark}` join the catalog. Tests: `test/helpers/theme.ts` (the in-memory fakes), `test/component/theme.spec.ts` (the controller matrix incl. disposal on unmount), the shell spec's control tests, `test/e2e/theme.spec.ts` (live restyle with the no-reload sentinel, raw-token chart-contract pins, OS emulation, storage round-trip and invalid-value fallback), and the per-mode a11y scans. Documentation: `ui/README.md`'s Theming section (mechanism, key, invalid-value rule, best-effort persistence, the token-only color rule for 175/176, the accepted first-paint flash), the `ui/src/theme.ts` row in `docs/architecture/package-layout.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` Unreleased. Hand-offs: task 179 reuses `useTheme()` for the settings surface (its keys under `settings.*`); tasks 175/176 read colors only through `getComputedStyle` token lookups and re-render on `resolvedTheme` — hardcoding a color in a chart or component is a regression against this decision.

## D-134 — Task 169's typed API client and error presentation: type-only schema imports (zero runtime coupling), the five-kind error taxonomy with catalog-only presentation (the envelope's message/details never render), trusted success casts, and the provide/inject client + `useApiCall` as the 170+ page contract (spec §13, §14, §15.3; task 169)

**Date:** 2026-11-03 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§13](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#13-http-api), [§14](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#14-web-interface), [§14.1](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#141-general-ui-requirements), [§15.3](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#153-csrf-dns-rebinding-and-host-validation), [§15.5](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#155-headers-and-limits) · **Tasks:** [169](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-113 (the §13 envelope and code registry the taxonomy consumes), D-117 (the §15.3 mutation-header contract the client attaches), D-128/D-130 (the endpoint contracts the client types from), D-131/D-132/D-133 (the factory+plugin composition-root pattern the client seam follows), D-127 (the CSP the same-origin relative base satisfies), D-132 (the catalog discipline the error strings follow)

**Decision.** Task 169 lands the UI's shared data layer as three modules plus one component, and pins six interpretations. (Correction trail: the task's review round — deepseek-v4.1-flash, one round, REQUEST_CHANGES with 1 P1 / 2 P2 / 3 P3 — caught the deadline/cancellation guard ending at the response headers (the P1 — the body read now runs inside the same armed guard), the `aborted`-recorded-as-error and the unguarded re-entry in `useApiCall` (both P2 — the policy and the re-entry token below), and three P3 test/wording gaps, all folded into this entry before landing; the `data-error-code` wording follows the reviewer's option (b) — `code` is recorded as the deliberate machine-readable channel rather than gated, which would need the runtime schema import this decision exists to avoid.) (1) **The schema coupling is compile-time only.** `ui/src/api/client.ts` takes every request/response type from `src/schemas/api/*` through `import type` — erased at build, so the browser bundle carries neither TypeBox nor the schemas nor anything server-side behind them, and the wire contract cannot drift from the UI's types without failing `vue-tsc`. Success bodies are **trusted casts**, not re-validated: the same-origin server serializes through the same closed schemas (D-111/D-128's serializer guard), a body that is not JSON at all is caught as the `unexpected` error kind, and a second Ajv/TypeBox validator in the browser would re-buy per payload what the contract already guarantees. The one runtime string that matters — §15.3's `X-Quotameter-Request` (D-117) — is the UI-local constant `API_MUTATION_HEADER`, **pinned against the server's `API_MUTATION_HEADER_NAME` by a component test** rather than imported at runtime (a runtime import of `src/server/api/security.ts` would drag the ApiError class and TypeBox into the bundle for one string). (2) **The error taxonomy is five kinds over one class**: `ApiClientError` with `kind ∈ {network, timeout, aborted, unexpected, rejected}` — `network` (fetch rejected; unreachable), `timeout` (the client's own deadline, default 15 s, overridable — §15.5 pins server timeouts only, and the client needs its own bound so a hung request cannot freeze a page), `aborted` (the caller's signal — a deliberate cancellation, never presented as a failure), `unexpected` (a response whose body is not the §13 envelope: an HTML error page, invalid JSON, a foreign JSON shape), and `rejected` (the envelope, any status — an envelope-shaped body classifies `rejected` even on a 2xx, the body says what it says). The deadline and the caller's signal are **composed manually onto one AbortController and stay armed through the whole exchange — headers AND body read** (a `fetch` resolves at headers; a stalled body after them is bounded, cancellable, and classified by who aborted — the review round's P1) so the taxonomy can tell who aborted, and a real `signal` reaches `fetch`; an already-aborted signal answers `aborted` without dispatching. (3) **Presentation is catalog-only — the envelope's `message`/`details` never render.** `ApiErrorNotice.vue` (an inline `role="alert"` region, `data-testid="api-error"`, `data-error-kind`/`data-error-code` for e2e) maps kind and envelope `code` onto `errors.*` catalog keys through explicit template branches (static `t()` literals — the D-132 both-directions rule forces the structure and keeps it total), with a fallback sentence for non-registry codes. The envelope payload rides the error object as `serverMessage`/`serverDetails` for programmatic use only: the client cannot vouch for what actually answered (a misrouted proxy or hostile same-origin responder controls those bytes), and §13's `code` is the stable machine-readable channel the presentation keys on instead — a hostile payload's whole reach is choosing which CATALOG sentence renders. `Error.message` is likewise a fixed per-kind sentence, so nothing response-derived can ride it into an accidental render or log. The envelope's **`code` is the one deliberate machine-readable channel** — §13's own stable-code property — surfaced (Vue-escaped, invisible to users) as the notice's `data-error-code` attribute for e2e and diagnostics; everything else the payload carried stays off the DOM. A marker test with a hostile envelope (internals-looking paths and key-shaped strings in `message`/`details`) pins the gate executably. (4) **The Vue seam is the D-131/D-132/D-133 shape**: `createApiClientPlugin()` installs (provide) the client in the composition root, `useApi()` injects with a loud throw when missing, and **`useApiCall(call)` is the per-request composable tasks 170+ consume** — `data`/`error`/`pending` refs, `execute()` re-running the thunk (retry, changed arguments), taxonomy errors caught into state, anything else rethrown so programming errors stay loud; two deliberate non-failures resolve `null` without touching `error` (the review round's P2 pair): a **caller cancellation** (`kind === 'aborted'` — a cancelled request is not a failure to present, and previously loaded data survives it) and a **superseded run** (an internal re-entry token — only the newest `execute()` may write state, so overlapping calls cannot have a stale result or a stale failure clobber the newest outcome). (5) **The done-condition's proof is the wiring itself**: every placeholder view carries the same three lines (`useApi()` → `useApiCall(() => api.health.get())` → render `ApiErrorNotice` on `error`) against the one §13 route that exists in every deployment, so "errors are handled consistently across pages" is executable (`test/component/api-error-wiring.spec.ts` mounts the shell at all four routes: failure renders the shared notice everywhere, success renders none) — and each content task replaces the probe with its real calls without touching the pattern. (6) **The task-180 seam is documented in place**: the notice's `UNAUTHENTICATED` branch is where the login redirect (the named `login` route) will hook, with the error's `code` field as the programmatic signal — no routing logic is built here. A `--qm-color-danger`/`--qm-color-danger-background` token pair joins all three theme blocks in `base.css` (WCAG-checked values, text carries the meaning beside the color — never color alone).

**Reasons.** §13 says the UI is the API's only consumer and §14 says every string is catalog-sourced; the design makes both structural. Type-only imports are the only shape that gives the UI real server types with zero bundle cost — a duplicated client-side contract would drift, and a runtime import would price one string at a TypeBox download (the bundle grew 1.6 kB total, the notice chunk included). The taxonomy names the layers a browser fetch actually has (transport, deadline, cancellation, body shape, envelope) because those are the layers a page can present differently — "unreachable" and "wrong format" and "refused" need different sentences, while the envelope's own prose adds nothing the code cannot say more stably (D-113's registry messages are leak-free, but the client's job is totality over what the network can deliver, including a responder that never read the spec). The 15 s default is far above every landed same-origin round trip and below human patience; §15.5's server-side timeouts do not bind the browser, and the manual abort composition (over `AbortSignal.any`) exists because the discrimination — who aborted — is the taxonomy's own requirement, and because the guard must span the two-phase fetch (headers, then body) without releasing either bound early. The catalog-only presentation subsumes §13's "Messages must not reveal secrets or internal filesystem paths" client-side: the invariant no longer depends on every server being the right server.

**Consequences.** `ui/src/api/{client,error,index}.ts` and `ui/src/components/ApiErrorNotice.vue` land; `main.ts` installs the plugin beside router/i18n/theme; `errors.*` join the catalog (all referenced by the notice's branches — the dead-key rule holds); the four views carry the canonical wiring; `test/helpers/api.ts` (FakeFetch, response builders) joins the theme-helper precedent. Tests: `test/component/api-client.spec.ts` (per-family round-trips, the §15.3 header matrix bodied and bodiless — DELETE and the bodiless POST test carry the header with NO content type, matching D-117's body-bound leg —, query serialization incl. a deliberate `purgeHistory=false`, the full taxonomy incl. the mid-body transport death, the stalled-body deadline and the mid-body caller abort, the already-aborted short-circuit, the timer/listener cleanup pin, the hostile-shape envelope-recognizer table, the header drift pin, the custom baseUrl incl. trailing-slash tolerance), `test/component/api-error-notice.spec.ts` (per-kind/per-code sentences table-driven off `API_ERROR_DEFINITIONS` with a registry↔catalog drift pin, the unknown-code fallback, the marker gates), `test/component/api-error-wiring.spec.ts` (the four-route consistency proof, the plugin seam, the `useApiCall` state machine incl. the aborted-is-not-an-error policy and the superseded-run pins), and the shell spec updated to install a healthy client. The e2e byte-pins (`app-status`/`page-status`) are untouched — the placeholder lines stay; under `vite preview` (no API behind it) the views honestly render the `unexpected` notice, against the application server none renders — recorded in `ui/README.md`. Hand-offs: tasks 161/162/180 add `history`/`events`/`peakHours`/`auth` families as methods on the client (same pattern, their own schemas); task 170+ consumes `useApi()`/`useApiCall()`/`ApiErrorNotice` exactly as the placeholder views demonstrate; task 180 intercepts `code === 'UNAUTHENTICATED'` at the notice's documented seam and may turn that branch into a redirect to the named `login` route; a §13 success body that fails a runtime shape assumption is a server-side contract break (the cast trusts D-111/D-128's serializers), not a client bug.
