## D-135 — Task 170's account selector and management UI: the selected-account store as a persisted id reconciled by consumers, inline confirmation panels (typed label for the purge, two-step for the archive), §8.2/§6.3 affordance gating, and no new design tokens (spec §14.2, §8.2, §14.1, §5.3, §6.3; task 170)

**Date:** 2026-11-03 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§14.2](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#142-account-management), [§8.2](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#82-accounts), [§14.1](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#141-general-ui-requirements), [§5.3](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#53-init-workflow), [§6.3](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#63-secret-storage-and-writes) · **Tasks:** [170](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-128 (the §13 accounts surface the page drives — the masked list, the write-only key bodies, the archive/purge split, the test-outcome vocabulary), D-134 (the page contract consumed verbatim: `useApi()`, one `useApiCall` per request, `ApiErrorNotice`, trusted success casts), D-131/D-132/D-133 (the factory+plugin composition-root pattern the selection store follows; the catalog discipline the `accounts.*` keys follow; the best-effort browser-storage stance the persistence copies), D-061 (archive is terminal, no reactivation — the archived-card affordance set and the archive confirm's wording), D-067 (purge evidence carried in the DELETE response — not surfaced further by this task), D-127 (the CSP the inline-confirm/no-dialog design and the token-only styling stay neutral to)

**Decision.** (Correction trail: the task's review round — deepseek-v4.1-flash, one round, REQUEST_CHANGES with 1 P1 / 2 P2 / 7 P3 — folded in before landing: the purge gate trims **both** sides (the P1 — a label with surrounding whitespace, creatable through this very UI and legal server-side, made the typed confirmation unsatisfiable and an archived such account unpurgeable from the UI; the create/rename sends now trim too, so labels this UI creates are canonical), the failed-load rule and the dismissal seam below (both P2), the archived-card wording (a P3 — the test button renders disabled, it is not removed), and four smaller fixes — the cancelled replace-key field clears, a successful key replacement clears the previous test verdict, three test gaps (failed-load storage pin, purge-from-archived, padded label), and the stale `ui/src/api/` layout row.) Task 170 lands §14.2's "account selector and management page" and pins seven interpretations. (1) **The selection store is a persisted id, reconciled by consumers.** `ui/src/account-selection.ts` is the D-131…D-134 factory+plugin+inject shape (not Pinia — §3 keeps runtime dependencies minimal and the `ui/src/stores/` reservation stays unused): `createAccountSelection({storage?})` provides `{selectedId, select}`, `useAccountSelection()` injects with the loud-throw remedy, and the choice persists best-effort under the `localStorage` key `quotameter.selected-account` — absent/empty reads as `null`, an explicit clear persists as the empty string, and both storage directions are try/catch (D-133's stance verbatim). The store validates nothing: a non-empty stored string is a candidate id read back verbatim, because which ids exist is list data the consumers already load — so **reconciliation is the documented consumer rule**: on every _completed_ list load, keep the stored id while it is listed, else select the first account, else `null` (the accounts page re-runs it on every load and reload; task 172's overview consumes the same composable against its own data and may add its own selector control on the same store). The completed-load guard matters: reconciling against the empty pre-load or failed-load state would wipe a stored choice the arriving list would have honored. A **route parameter was rejected** as the persistence carrier: §14/D-131 pin exactly four routes, a selection query would leak into every shareable URL and fight the stored choice, and browser storage is D-133's established precedent for cross-reload UI state. The shell nav stays as landed — §14.2's sentence puts the selector on the management page; an overview-side control is 172's call on the same store. (2) **Confirmation affordances are inline panels, not modal dialogs.** The purge (§8.2's separate explicit action, irreversible) requires **typing the account's exact label** — the confirm button stays disabled until `typed.trim() === account.label.trim()` (the review round's P1: both sides trim, so a padded label can never dead-end the gate), and the `purgeHistory: true` flag leaves the client only behind that match (the task-170 confirmation the §13 spelling was waiting for); the archive (terminal per D-061, but history-preserving) gets the lighter **two-step inline confirm** whose body states the terminal semantics. Both are plain DOM after their trigger buttons — keyboard-reachable by construction, no focus trap to build or test under the served CSP — and on open, focus moves to the safe control: the cancel button for archive, the typing gate for purge. The typed-label gate compares against the account's _label_, not id: labels are what the page shows the operator, ids are internal vocabulary; the gate is an explicitness proof, not addressing (the DELETE targets the selected id regardless). (3) **§8.2's lifecycle semantics gate the affordances to match the server, not to paper over it.** An archived account renders no rename, polling, replace-key, or archive controls at all (each would answer `FORBIDDEN`/`account-archived`) and renders the test button disabled — the archived notice states the retained-history state, and the purge stays available (the §8.2 follow-up over the retained history, offered on active and archived cards alike). The environment-sourced key (§6.3, `environment-key-read-only`) gets no replace-key form: the facts row names the source instead, so the read-only rule is stated, not discovered by refusal. The connection test disables without a configured key (`no-key-configured`) — a doomed round trip withheld, with the facts row already saying "Not set". (4) **Write-only keys are structural**: `type="password"` + `autocomplete="new-password"`, never prefilled (the replace form's field starts empty every time it opens), never echoed, and cleared after every submit attempt — success and failure alike; the rendered key state is the §13 constant mask verbatim, `hasKey`-gated. The create form omits `apiKey` from the POST body entirely when empty (§5.3's keyless account) and exposes no `id` field (the server generates; D-128) — and its blank-guards (label, whitespace-only key) refuse client-side with catalog'd field errors and **no request**, D-011's blank rule applied at the input boundary where the server's VALIDATION would be noise. (5) **The test result renders immediately and honestly**: the outcome sentence (explicit `t()` branches per §13 vocabulary — ok/rejected/unavailable) plus the provider's own §13 `message` in a `role="status"` region. The message is a schema-validated success body inside D-134's trusted-cast boundary (provider-authored sanitized English per D-052) — unlike the error envelope's prose, which never renders; only the provider-rejected outcome borrows the danger tint (§7.2 keeps "inconclusive" apart from "refused"), and the text carries the meaning either way. (6) **No new design tokens**: the 169 danger pair covers the destructive affordances (border/tint on the purge panel and the danger buttons), every state pairs text with color (§14.1 never-color-alone — the selector's archived marker and the polling/key facts are words), and the decorative dash between the test sentence and the provider detail is CSS `::before` content, keeping it out of the text nodes the raw-text rule governs. (7) **The page's data flow keeps one source of truth**: the view owns the two loads (accounts, providers) with one `useApiCall` each; every successful mutation emits and the view reloads the list once — the card never patches its props from mutation responses (the reloaded list is authoritative), and the card is keyed by account id so a selection switch is a fresh instance with no per-account state leaking across cards. (8) **A load failure is not an empty list, and a dismissed failure is gone** (the review round's P2 pair): `useApiCall` nulls its data on failure (D-134), so the view keeps its own last-successful list — a failed reload leaves the previous surface rendered beside the failure notice and a catalogued retry, the empty state renders only when a completed load answered zero accounts, and a failed initial load renders neither (the notice and retry replace an assertion the page cannot make); the add form's "no provider in this build" sentence likewise renders only for a successfully empty providers list, never for a failed load. And `useApiCall` gains `reset()` — clear `data`/`error`/`pending` and supersede any in-flight run (the re-entry token again) — the dismissal seam a confirmation panel uses on cancel/re-open, so a previous attempt's `role="alert"` cannot re-announce a failure that did not just happen; a successful key replacement also resets the connection-test verdict, which described the credential that no longer exists.

**Reasons.** The selection-store reading follows the spec's silence: §14.2 names "an account selector and management page" without a word on persistence or routing, and the two candidate mechanisms split on what they optimize — a route param makes the selection shareable (nobody shares "look at MY selected account") while storage makes it durable (exactly what a single-operator monitoring tool wants between visits), and D-133 had already chosen storage for the same class of state. Keeping the store id-only is the honest seam: a store that fetched its own account list would duplicate the page's load, race it, and still need the consumer's reconciliation when the two disagree — the rule lands once, in the consumers that hold the data. The typed-label purge over a modal confirm: §8.2 says "separate explicit action with confirmation" and §14.2 "explicit confirmation" — a typed match is the strongest explicitness affordance that needs no new vocabulary (the label is on screen, in the panel title's context), it is inherently keyboard-accessible, and it cannot be clicked through by muscle memory the way a confirm button can; the archive stops short of it because archive preserves the history (reversible in effect: the data survives) and D-061's terminality is about the lifecycle flag, not data loss. Inline panels over dialogs: the native `<dialog>`'s focus management is the one thing dialogs buy, and the two-step panels deliver the same keyboard path without it, under a CSP that forbids nothing here but a test stack (happy-dom) whose dialog support is unproven — less machinery, same guarantees. The affordance gating mirrors the server's own refusal vocabulary because the alternative is UI that offers actions it knows will be refused — each gated control would render an error notice as its only possible outcome, which is noise pretending to be functionality; stating the reason (archived notice, environment facts row) communicates the same fact without the round trip.

**Consequences.** `ui/src/account-selection.ts`, `ui/src/components/{AccountAddForm,AccountManageCard}.vue`, and the rewritten `ui/src/views/AccountsView.vue` land; `main.ts` installs the selection plugin; the `accounts.*` catalog namespace replaces the placeholder `status` entry (the both-directions completeness rule forced its death in the same commit); `ui/README.md` documents the page architecture, the action→API map, and the reconciliation seam for 172+. Tests: `test/component/account-selection.spec.ts` (persistence, null semantics, throwing storage both directions, plugin seam, default wiring) and `test/component/accounts-view.spec.ts` — the done-condition executable: a miniature accounts backend on the injectable fetch seam pins per action the exact method/URL/body (POST with and without key; PATCH bodies exactly one field; the bare archive DELETE URL with no query vs `?purgeHistory=true` only after the typed match; cancel paths dispatch nothing; focus lands on the safe controls; reconciliation on load/switch/purge/empty; the environment-key and archived affordance matrices; envelope/network failures through the shared notice; the write-only discipline — masked inputs, empty first paint, no key material in the rendered DOM). The shell specs updated for the real page (per-URL healthy bodies in `api-error-wiring.spec.ts`, the empty-state pin in `app.spec.ts`, the `accounts.status` catalog pin retired from `i18n-catalog.spec.ts`); e2e adds the per-theme axe scan of `/accounts` over its honest no-API degradation surface. **The csp-shell deep link moved to `/settings`**: task 170 made `/accounts` an API-loading page and that construction wires no accounts routes, so the §13 scope's honest 404 envelopes arrive as Chromium console noise unrelated to the policy the spec guards — restoring `/accounts` there is the composition task's seam (wire the API into the construction, or mount the page's chunk lazily there). Loose ends handed forward: 172 consumes `useAccountSelection()` with the same reconciliation rule against its own load; the §14.3 overview facts (plan name, last collection) are 172's, not the card's (management facts only); a formal masked-field test idiom (beyond the per-spec pins here) can be extracted when the second write-only field lands (179's password change); the `AccountMutationResult`'s purge evidence counts are carried but not rendered — a future toast/status surface is their natural home; and the rename of an account whose label collides with another's is allowed (labels are not unique server-side) — the typed purge gate stays unambiguous because it gates the _selected_ account's action, not addressing.

## D-136 — Task 171's masked write-only secret fields closed as a verify-and-close audit: the done-condition's "never returned to the browser" read as a three-link proof chain (wire scan, parsed-state scan, rendered-DOM pins), the real-surface bridge spec as the missing composition link, and the happy-dom environment container as the pattern's recorded boundary (spec §6.3, §14.2, §15.4; task 171)

**Date:** 2026-11-03 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§6.3](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#63-secret-storage-and-writes), [§14.2](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#142-account-management), [§15.4](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#154-secret-protection) · **Tasks:** [171](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-128 (the accounts surface's closed contracts and marker discipline — the server half of the proof map), D-130 (the settings/status families' own marker pins — the `passwordHash`-free settings GET; the providers listing carries no secret structurally, so it has no marker suite of its own), D-134 (the typed client whose fetch seam carries the new bridge, and whose type-only schema imports keep server code out of the browser bundle), D-135 (the task-170 UI affordance pins — the rendered-DOM link), D-111 (the closed-serializer guard every scanned body serializes through)

**Decision.** Task 171 lands as a verify-and-close audit with one closing test artifact, and pins two interpretations. **(1) The done-condition — "UI/API tests prove the key is never returned to the browser" — is read as a three-link proof chain, each link executable:** the _wire_ link (no response body the browser would receive contains key material — pinned server-side per route family since 159/160, and compositionally by the new bridge spec), the _parsed-state_ link (no client-resolved value — the state Vue components render from, an error's `serverMessage`/`serverDetails` included — contains key material), and the _rendered-DOM_ link (the components render no key material and the write-only affordances hold — 170's component pins: masked `type="password"` inputs with `autocomplete="new-password"` from first paint, never prefilled, cleared after every submit attempt — success and refusal alike —, the constant mask rendered verbatim). The audit found every link individually proven **except the composition**: no earlier test drove the real `/api` surface and inspected what the UI's own data layer receives — task 170's component fixtures are key-free by construction (a handler/serializer regression putting a key on the wire would fail no UI test), and 159/160's integration markers involve no UI-side consumer. **(2) The closing artifact is the real-surface bridge spec** (`test/integration/accounts-real-surface.spec.ts`): the real `createApiClient` (the exact object the accounts page installs, real §15.3 mutation headers, real body pipeline, the §13 error handler installed) runs a full §14.2 management session — providers+list loads, create with a marker key, replace key, connection test, rename, archive, and one honestly refused create for the error path — against the real route stack (real serializers, real guards, real migrated `node:sqlite` storage, real `ProviderRegistry` with a credential-capturing double) through a bridge that maps the client's fetch seam onto `app.inject` and captures every exchange verbatim, request and response alike. The session proves non-vacuously (every verb dispatched, every success status 2xx, the store holds the exact marker at create time and the rotated one after — anchored before the archive removes the entry — and the provider double saw the current key: the write path genuinely carried the secrets server-side) that no captured response body, no request URL, no client-resolved value (successes and the thrown error alike), and no log record contains either marker — over a NON-EMPTY sink (the refused create logs its cause server-side) — that the markers left the browser only through the two write channels (the create POST and the replace-key PATCH, never a GET or DELETE body), and that the mask `********` rides both the wire and the parsed display state (`hasKey`/`keyMask`/`keySource`, with the archived account's honest `none`/`false`/`null` triple).

**Reasons.** The three-link reading follows §6.3's own sentence ("neither the saved value nor the API response may reveal it" — the response is the wire link, the saved value's non-revelation is observable only through what the UI holds and renders) and §15.4's channel list (HTML and JavaScript bundles are the rendered and shipped forms; URLs, logs, and error messages are separate channels already pinned where they live). The bridge was placed in the integration project rather than as a component mount for a structural reason recorded here as the pattern's boundary: the component project's happy-dom environment container (Vitest 5's Vite-environment module graph) refuses to bundle the `node:*` built-ins the server side statically requires (`node:sqlite` most immediately — verified live with static, `@vite-ignore` dynamic, and transitive forms), so a happy-dom test cannot host the real route stack; a `// @vitest-environment happy-dom` pragma in the integration project would land in the same container. The DOM link therefore stays with the component suite, which composes with the bridge honestly: the components render nothing but the client's outputs, so parsed-state cleanliness plus the component render pins is the complete display claim. The settings password's write-only field (§14.5) is server-side already (D-130's `passwordConfigured`-only GET and the seam-hashed PUT) and its UI affordances are 179's — recorded as the task's loose end, not a gap of this one.

**Consequences.** `test/integration/accounts-real-surface.spec.ts` lands (the D-128 store double trimmed to the session's needs — duplicate-id `add` rejection and the `failNextAdd` failure hook included, per the seam contract —, the D-052 provider double as a context-capturing ok case owned by its registry factory, the deterministic-clock harness of the accounts suites, and the §13 error handler installed as the production construction does); `accounts-view.spec.ts` gains the two refused-submit clearing pins (the rejected create and a refused replace-key both leave the key input empty — the "cleared after every submit attempt" claim now executable on both outcomes); `ui/README.md` gains the write-only proof map under the accounts-page section and `src/server/README.md` a pointer beside the accounts endpoints, so the audit trail is readable where each half lives. The review round (deepseek-v4.1-flash, one round, APPROVE with 3 P2 / 7 P3) was folded in before landing: the create-path write anchor (the P2 — only the rotated marker was server-side-anchored before), the refused-submit component pins and the doc wording they back (the P2 pair), the three dropped client-resolved values bound and asserted (the rename's effect included), the URL scan's second marker, the error-path exchange (the refused create: INTERNAL envelope, the thrown error's payload, and the now-non-empty log scan), the registry-owned contexts array, and the D-130 reference corrected (providers is structurally key-free, not marker-pinned). The bridge pattern — a component's injectable fetch seam served by the real route stack over `app.inject` — is available for reuse when a future task wants real-surface composition proofs (the environment boundary above is its recorded constraint: it lives in node-environment projects). Changing the proof map's shape (deleting a marker suite, unwiring the bridge's guards) is a successor decision. No implementation changed: the audit found the accounts, settings, status/quota, and providers surfaces, the client, and the UI affordances all conforming; the commit is tests + docs.

## D-137 — Task 172's account overview cards: the §14.3 metric-label resolution as a provider-layer static catalog on `/api/providers` (optional `QuotaProvider.metricCatalog`, single-sourced from the adapter's identity table, raw-key fallback UI-side), the five-load page over the shared selection store, and per-field honest value rendering (absolute → percentage → Unknown, never zero) (spec §14.3, §14.6, §8.4, §7.2, §7.3, §14.1; task 172)

**Date:** 2026-11-03 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§14.3](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#143-account-overview), [§14.6](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#146-statuses-and-authentication-screens), [§8.4](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#84-normalized-snapshot-and-metric-model), [§7.2](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#72-retry-and-error-behavior), [§14.1](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#141-general-ui-requirements) · **Tasks:** [172](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-130 (the status/quota endpoints the page consumes verbatim, and the recorded loose end this decision resolves: "`/api/quota` carries metric keys but no labels — a provider-layer catalog export is needed; `/api/providers` is its natural carrier"), D-039 (the storage rows' deliberate `label` omission that created the gap), D-047/D-053 (the Z.ai recognition tables whose identities become the catalog — the single source), D-134 (the page contract: `useApi()`/`useApiCall`/`ApiErrorNotice`, trusted success casts), D-135 (the selection store and its reconciliation rule — the overview is the second consumer), D-132 (the catalog discipline the new `overview.*` keys follow), D-133 (the token-only color rule the new status tones follow), D-111/D-128 (the closed-contract guard the extended providers response serializes through)

**Decision.** Task 172 lands the §14.3 surface and resolves D-130's recorded label question. (Correction trail: the task's review round — deepseek-v4.1-flash, one round, 1 P1 / 2 P2 / 9 P3 — was folded in before landing: the status-row-absent P1 and the two P2s below reshaped the card's absence semantics and the quota target, eight of the nine P3s entered as written, and the one declined is noted in Consequences.) **(1) The label resolution: §14.3's "the quota type and label" is the §8.4 `label` — adapter-owned English data, so it is served, not forked UI-side.** `QuotaProvider` gains an **optional** `readonly metricCatalog?: readonly { metricKey; label }[]` (optional so the spec's §8.1 sketch pin and every existing test double stay valid; a present-but-malformed catalog — non-array, blank or whitespace-padded fields, duplicate keys — throws at `register` like the other wiring checks, ahead of the duplicate-id verdict so re-registering reports the shadowing), the Z.ai adapter exports `ZAI_METRIC_CATALOG` built **from the recognition identities themselves** (the mapping's own single source; the catalog cannot drift from what the adapter emits), and `GET /api/providers` serializes it as each provider's `metrics` array — always an array, empty when the adapter declares none (the honest "none declared", not a nullable the consumer must second-guess; the response object stays closed). The UI resolves `(providerId, metricKey) → label` with the **raw metric key as the documented fallback** — a stable adapter-defined identifier rendered verbatim when the provider declares no catalog or no entry for the key. A UI-side i18n mapping was rejected: it forks D-047 decision property, must grow per provider against §8.1's "adding a provider never rewrites … chart components", and still needs the key fallback; the server catalog is the same weight and serves the §14.4 charts (174+) too. Provider metric labels are **data** like provider names (the D-135 precedent — the accounts page renders `/api/providers` names), not chrome; §14.1's catalog rule governs UI-authored strings. **(2) The page is five loads over the shared selection store.** `accounts.list` (selector + identity), `providers.list` (names **and** the label catalog), `status.get` (the §7.3 rows), `settings.get` (exactly the configured display time zone — §14.1; a failed load degrades to the browser's zone beside its notice, never a blocked card and never a silent wrong zone), and `quota.get(selectedId)` re-run on every selection change; the selector is the store's second control and re-runs D-135's reconciliation rule verbatim. The quota target is **list-validated** (the review round's P2): the selected id dispatches only once a completed list load vouches for it — a stale stored id earns no flashing 404 — and a target switch **clears** the previous account's quota before the new load, so one account's values can never render as another's, while failed reloads keep last-good copies (the D-135 rule) beside per-load notices; the data-defining loads (accounts/status/quota) carry retries with distinct accessible names (the review round's P3), the two gracefully-degrading ones (providers, settings) render their notice alone. A status row that is **absent** — the §7.3 load still in flight or failed — renders its slots as the explicit `Unknown` (the review round's P1): "Never — no successful collection yet" and "None" state collection history only a loaded row vouches for, never a load the page could not complete. **(3) Per-field honest rendering: each of used/remaining/limit shows its absolute value with its explicit unit when present, else its percentage (`42%`, a different unit, labeled as such — §14.3's "used/remaining/limit **or** percentages"), else an explicit `Unknown` — never zero, never blank; a genuine zero renders as `0 credits`** (pinned with hostile zero-plausible fixtures: `used: null` beside `remaining: 0` renders `Unknown` and `0 credits` in one card). Percent-only metrics (`unit: 'PERCENT'`) render percentages only; invalid metrics render `invalidReason` and no value lines (§8.4 stores them without numeric values; the reset/window metadata may survive, D-010); an absent `resetsAt` omits the line (§14.3's own "if available"); each card shows its own `collectedAt` stamp because D-077 rows may come from different snapshots; and a snapshot with a stamp but zero recognized rows (the adapter's skip path) states its own fact — distinct from "no successful collection yet" (the review round's P2). **(4) The §14.6 statuses render as text + tone + shape** — `AccountStatusBadge` maps the eight tokens onto five tone groups (ok/pending/warn/error/neutral) with new `--qm-color-ok*`/`--qm-color-warn*`/`--qm-color-muted-background` tokens in all three theme blocks (D-133's token-only rule), a CSS-drawn shape marker per tone (filled circle, hollow circle, diamond, triangle, hollow square — no images, CSP-neutral), and the label as real text: the text is the signal, color and shape supplement it (§14.1). Label selection is an explicit script-level switch with static `t()` keys (a Record of keys would be a dynamic lookup the D-132 completeness scans cannot see).

**Reasons.** The label reading follows the spec's own vocabulary: §14.3 says "label", §8.4 defines `label` as an adapter-authored English display field, and §8.1's extensibility sentence makes the UI-side fork the wrong side to own it — the resolution puts the declaration where the identities already live (the recognition table) and exposes it through the endpoint D-130 itself nominated. The always-array wire shape keeps consumers free of null-handling for a field that is genuinely list-shaped. The five-load split mirrors what each §14.3 sentence needs (nothing loads twice, and the quota re-request is the only selection-keyed one), and clearing-on-switch is the only honest policy once values are per-account: the alternative — keeping the old account's numbers while the new ones load — renders one account's quota under another's identity. The absolute-then-percentage-then-Unknown ladder is §14.3's own "or" made per-field: a percentage is the same underlying fact in the provider's other unit, so it fills the field's slot honestly, while `Unknown` makes absence explicit — the never-zero discipline of §7.2/§8.4 extended from storage to display, with the genuine-zero pin guarding the opposite dishonesty (an absent value must not become `0`, and a real `0` must not become `Unknown`).

**Consequences.** Server-side: `metricCatalog` on `QuotaProvider` (+ registry validation, trim-checking like the id rule and ordered after the duplicate-id verdict), `ZAI_METRIC_CATALOG` in the Z.ai mapping module, `ProviderMetricViewSchema` + the `metrics` array on `ProviderViewSchema` (`src/schemas/api/providers.ts`), and one line in the providers route — an additive wire change to a landed §13 contract, recorded here per the public-contract rule and documented in the three READMEs. UI-side: `ui/src/format.ts` (pure `Intl` helpers — `formatEpochMs`/`formatRelative`/`formatQuotaNumber`/`windowHours`, the relative ladder seconds→years — the 174+ chart tasks reuse), `AccountOverviewCard.vue`, `AccountStatusBadge.vue`, `MetricCard.vue`, the rewritten `OverviewView.vue`, the `overview.*` catalog namespace (the placeholder `overview.status` line dies), and the new status-tone tokens in `base.css`. The relative-time phrases are computed when data arrives (no live ticker — a reload re-renders; recorded as acceptable under §14.3's "relative to current time"). Tests: `test/component/overview-view.spec.ts` (the §8.4 matrix — full, the hostile null/zero pair, percent-only, the mixed per-field percentage fallback, limit-only, invalid, no-snapshot vs zero-metric-snapshot, reset/window omissions — the eight-status table with exact labels and tones, label catalog + key fallback, selection/reconciliation/switch semantics incl. the no-stale-cross-account and stale-stored-id pins, the status-row-absent Unknown pin, and the failure surfaces per load with working distinctly-named retries) and `test/component/format.spec.ts` beside the server-side rows (`registry.spec.ts` catalog validation incl. the padding rows, `api-providers-schema.spec.ts` contract rows, `api-providers.spec.ts` serialization with and without a catalog, the provider's catalog≡identities pin); the shell specs updated for the real page (`app.spec.ts`'s overview pin, the wiring spec's content selector, the i18n spec's retired placeholder pin, `healthyApiBody` learning the three new routes); e2e: the smoke overview assertion becomes the honest no-API degradation (the D-134 `unexpected` notice, no fake empty state), a per-mode axe scan of `/` joins the a11y suite, and the csp-shell policy probe moved from `/` to `/login` — task 172 made the overview API-loading and that construction wires no data routes, so the honest 404 envelopes are console noise unrelated to the policy (the same move D-135 recorded for `/accounts`; restoring `/` is the composition task's seam). the remaining eight entered as written (the stale schema comment, the strengthened status table, the stale-selection test, the matrix rows, the registry padding/order hardening, the empty-error-message tail, the year bucket, the retry names); the one declined P3 is the component-suite axe scan of the populated surface — the a11y comment's overclaim was corrected instead, and adding an axe dependency to the happy-dom component project for one surface is weight the composition task's served-with-API e2e answers better. Loose ends handed forward: 173 owns the fuller empty/initial guidance (the one-line no-accounts, no-snapshot, and no-metrics notes are placeholders for it); 174 mounts the range controls between the account card and `[data-testid="overview-metrics"]`; a UI refresh affordance (a periodic or manual reload that would exercise keep-last-good quota reloads beyond the retry path) is 174's to add if its range switching wants it; the derived-fields marker (`derivedFields` rides the wire but is not yet surfaced — a derived value is a real §8.4 value) is available to 175's charts if tooltips want to distinguish.

## D-138 — Task 173's empty and initial states: the fresh-install state matrix as the done-condition's enumeration, the attention classifier mirroring §7.3's precedence (archived outermost), the blocked-vs-waiting no-snapshot split, and links only where the UI can act (spec §14.3, §14.6; task 173)

**Date:** 2026-11-03 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§14.3](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#143-account-overview), [§14.6](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#146-statuses-and-authentication-screens) · **Tasks:** [173](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-137 (the overview surface these states complete — the one-line `overview.empty.*` notes were its recorded placeholders for this task, and the identity card's facts feed the classifier), D-135 (the failed-load rule the matrix inherits verbatim: a failed load is never a fake empty state — every matrix cell asserts no `api-error` renders beside its guidance), D-134 (the pending/error/empty distinction the loading states keep), D-132 (the catalog discipline the new `overview.attention.*` keys follow, and the namespace rule that keeps the harmonized-but-distinct empty-state keys separate), D-128/D-130 (the wire facts the classifier reads — `hasKey`/`keySource` and the §7.3 rows incl. archived-derives-disabled), D-131 (the route/link vocabulary the CTAs reuse)

**Decision.** Task 173 lands the §14.3 "helpful empty states" and the §14.6 `Disabled`/`Not configured` guidance, and pins four readings. (Correction trail: the task's review round — deepseek-v4.1-flash, one round, REQUEST_CHANGES with 1 P1 / 1 P2 / 5 P3 — was folded in before landing. The **P1**: the first classifier keyed the keyless-environment branch on `!hasKey`, but `hasKey` on the §13 accounts surface is **declaration-level** — `ManagedAccountConfig.keyConfigured` says a source is configured (§6.3's exactly-one rule), and the status endpoint's own composition (`configured = keyConfigured && secretOf !== null`) proves the two levels are distinct — so an unresolved-`apiKeyEnv` account reads `hasKey: true` on the wire, the branch was unreachable, and the fixture asserting it was a wire-impossible shape. The fix: the classifier takes the §7.3 status row beside the account view and recognizes the declared-but-unresolved key by `keySource === 'environment' && statusRow.status === 'not-configured'`, with an absent row claiming nothing (no keyless notice beside an Unknown badge); the matrix fixtures now use the real wire shapes. The **P2**: the loading lines (initial and quota-pending) had never been behaviorally pinned — both now are. Three **P3s** entered: the e2e mock serves the real registered provider (an empty catalog is a degradation case, not a fresh-install state, and the README matrix now labels it so), the attention surface gained its own axe scan (the contrast pair no scanned page exercised), and a stale hand-off comment in `app.spec.ts` was updated. Two **P3s** declined with reasons recorded in Consequences: the partial-archive badge/notice window and the auth-rejected waiting sentence.) **(1) The done-condition is a matrix, and the matrix is the enumeration.** "Fresh install does not display a blank or broken page" is made executable as a cell set — fresh `init` without an account (empty accounts, no status rows), the declared-but-unresolved-`apiKeyEnv` account (with and without its status row), the schema-total sourceless keyless fallback, a disabled account, an archived account without and with retained history, a healthy keyed account before its first poll (incl. the pre-sync `createdAt: null` storage shape), and the registry-empty degradation cell — each pinned in `test/component/overview-view.spec.ts` against mocked backends asserting BOTH halves: the cell's surface renders AND no failure notice does (guidance that only appears beside an `api-error` would be the broken page in disguise). **(2) The attention precedence mirrors §7.3's own derivation order, with the UI lifecycle fact outermost:** `archived` → `disabled` → keyless — the pure classifier `accountAttentionOf` (`ui/src/account-attention.ts`, single-sourced for the notice component and the metrics region's wording) reads the §13 account view **and** its §7.3 status row. Archived outranks the `enabled: false`/`hasKey: false` its wire shape carries (the terminal lifecycle is the fuller story behind the `disabled` status §7.3 derives for it — D-130's archived-derives-disabled, explained rather than contradicted); disabled outranks keyless exactly as §7.3's rank 0a outranks 0b, so the notice can never disagree with the badge rendered from the same facts. The keyless branches read the two wire halves for what each is worth: `hasKey` is declaration-level, so the reachable `Not configured` shape — a declared-but-unresolved `apiKeyEnv` key — is recognized through the status row and gets the server-side remedy sentence and **no link** (§6.3 makes environment keys read-only through the API; nothing on the accounts page fixes it, and a dead CTA is not "actionable"); a status row that is absent vouches for nothing; the schema-total sourceless fallback (`hasKey: false` on an active account, which no current composition produces) links to the replace-key action. **(3) The no-snapshot wording is attention-aware.** 172's "values appear after the first successful poll" is a promise only a healthy account can keep — under a blocker the poll never runs, so the metrics region states "collection is not running for this account" and the actionable advice lives exactly once, in the notice above (the link is not repeated: one remedy, one affordance). A healthy pre-first-poll account keeps the waiting sentence beside its `Collecting` badge and `Never` line, unchanged. **(4) Guidance is actionable and harmonized:** every empty state names the next step; the next step is a `RouterLink` exactly where the UI can perform it (SPA navigation, same-origin, CSP-neutral — the D-131 vocabulary); the page-level no-accounts block upgrades to title + skip-the-key hint + link, its wording harmonized with the accounts page's own empty state (task 170) while the keys stay namespace-distinct per D-132. Loading states stay 172's shape (the initial-load and quota-loading lines, the `Unknown` status slots) — D-134's pending semantics already keep loading distinct from error and empty, and no new loading chrome is warranted; both lines are now behaviorally pinned.

**Reasons.** The matrix-first reading turns the done-condition from a vibe into a table each row of which fails a test when it regresses; asserting the absence of `api-error` in every cell is what makes "not broken" mean something (a page that renders guidance only because everything failed is the blank page with extra steps). Mirroring §7.3's precedence is the only ordering under which the notice and the badge — two surfaces rendered from the same wire facts — cannot tell different stories; inventing a UI-specific order (say, keyless before disabled) would have the notice contradict the badge on every disabled-and-keyless account. The link-where-actable rule follows from honesty: §14.3's "helpful" is the remedy being reachable, and a CTA that lands on a page with no fixing action (the read-only environment key) is a wrong instruction, not guidance. The blocked-vs-waiting split extends 172's own no-snapshot-vs-no-metrics discipline (two different facts, never conflated) by one axis: absence of data under a blocker and absence of data awaiting a poll are different facts too — 172's review-round P2 precedent applied to wording. Keeping the remedy link un-duplicated follows the same rule the §14.6 badge set: each surface states its own fact.

**Consequences.** UI-side: `ui/src/account-attention.ts` (the classifier over the account view + §7.3 row), `ui/src/components/AccountAttentionNotice.vue` (the notice: the sentence via an explicit static-key switch, the CTA a `RouterLink` rendered for the three UI-actionable kinds, token-only styling deliberately neutral — the badge beside it carries the tone), the upgraded `overview-empty` block (title/hint/link), the `noSnapshotText` branch in `OverviewView.vue`, and the catalog gains `overview.empty.{noAccountsTitle,noAccountsHint,cta,noSnapshotBlocked}` + `overview.attention.{archived,disabled,keylessEnvironment,keyless,cta}` while the placeholder `overview.empty.noAccounts` dies. Tests: the fresh-install matrix, the loading-line pins, and the classifier truth table (incl. the absent-row no-claim, the keySource discrimination, the sourceless fallback, and the §7.3 precedence pin) in `test/component/overview-view.spec.ts`, whose mounts now install a memory-history router (RouterLink); `test/e2e/a11y.spec.ts` gains the route-interception pattern — `page.route('**/api/**')` serving the fresh-install bodies over a shared `fulfillOverviewBody` helper — axe-scanning the real no-accounts surface and the attention surface (a disabled account) in both themes and proving the CTA a live SPA link; the technique (mocked-API e2e for data-backed states the preview server cannot produce) is recorded for 174+ reuse. `ui/README.md` documents the matrix and the precedence. **The declined findings, with reasons:** (a) the partial-archive window — a `store.remove` failure after the row is retired leaves `status: 'archived'` with the config entry still present, so the badge may briefly derive a non-`disabled` status beside the archived notice — is a server-side retryable partial state (D-128's post-destructive cleanup is retryable through the API), and the notice states the authoritative fact (the row IS retired; polling HAS stopped), so the classifier keys on the storage lifecycle and the residual is documented here and in the classifier's docblock instead of complicating the UI; (b) an `auth-rejected` account with no snapshot keeps the waiting sentence — extension beyond the task's four families (the §7.2/§7.3 failure states carry their own landed presentation: the badge plus the card's last-error line with its outcome class and message), recorded as a 180/174+ consideration rather than implemented here. Loose ends handed forward: 174's range controls mount between the identity card and the metrics region (D-137's seam, unchanged); §14.6's login-state presentation stays 180's (the `UNAUTHENTICATED` branch seam is D-134's; the empty-state wording here deliberately says nothing about authentication); a served-with-API e2e construction (the composition task) remains the way to axe-scan the fully populated surface.

## D-139 — Task 161's §13 history and events endpoints: the D-139 timestamp reconciliation (ISO-8601 request parameters, epoch-ms response fields), the out-of-retention arm as the 200-with-report, the kind-discriminated unified timeline, the margin-widened raw runs-evidence read, and the empty-point/bucket wire encoding (spec §12, §13, §11.3, §10; task 161)

**Date:** 2026-11-03 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§12](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#12-events-reset-detection-and-missing-data), [§13](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#13-http-api), [§11.3](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#113-retention-and-cleanup), [§10](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#10-time-and-time-zones) · **Tasks:** [161](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-130 (the quota surface's epoch-ms reading whose recorded loose end — "§10's ISO-8601 sentence governs the §13 range parameters" — this decision closes for the range-bearing routes), D-128 (the optional-options registration rule and the both-halves account verdict these routes follow), D-082 (the retention-aware reads and the three-outcome vocabulary the response states; its open API-layer choice is closed here), D-081/D-090 (the downsampling contract consumed verbatim — boundaries as data, budget bounds, effective resolution), D-075/D-080 (the gap detector and timeline indicators consumed verbatim over the run stamps), D-078 (the live reset detection the integration seeding drives), D-113 (the frozen error registry — no new codes), D-074 (the reset evidence served verbatim in `details`)

**Decision.** Task 161 lands the two range-bearing §13 routes as one plugin (`src/server/api/history.ts` registering `GET /api/history` + `GET /api/events`, contracts in `src/schemas/api/history.ts`) behind `ApiRoutesOptions.history`, and pins six interpretations. (Correction trail: the task's review round — the deepseek primary timed out; kimi/k3.1-pro, one round, REQUEST_CHANGES with 2 P1 / 1 P2 — folded in before landing, and all three findings entered this entry and the same commit: the empty margin read now recovers the nearest bounding runs through two bounded probes so a range inside a margin-outlasting outage still renders its full-range stopped region; the downsampler input is the VALID points only with invalid rows re-inserted as their own point entries and the empty-point merge flushed by the gap midpoint, so an invalid row inside a gap can no longer defeat the boundary cut or misplace the empty point; and the archived-storage-only readability gained its wire pin.) (1) **The timestamp reconciliation (the task's mandated decision, closing D-130's loose end):** §13's own sentence — "`from` and `to` are required ISO 8601 UTC values for history, events, and peak-hours" — governs the **request** parameters: ISO strings with a mandatory explicit offset or `Z`, parsed through the landed `epochMsFromIso` (§10's strict gate; offset-less strings are rejected as VALIDATION with `details.reason: 'invalid-timestamp'` and the offending `param`, `from > to` as `inverted-range`), while every **response** timestamp stays the epoch-ms integer of the landed vocabulary (D-128 accounts, D-130 status/quota) — the response echoes the requested and effective ranges as epoch-ms too, one format per direction, never a mixed clock inside one body. Task 162's `/api/peak-hours` inherits the rule as §13's third named consumer. (2) **The out-of-retention arm is the 200-with-report:** D-082 left "reject or explicitly truncate" open at the API layer; the closed reading is that both arms share one response contract — `range.outcome: 'truncated'` serves the clamped bounds with `retentionHorizon` = the effective lower edge, `rejected` answers the empty series/events with the horizon named and null effective bounds — because §13's own "state that in the response" describes a body report, and an error-envelope arm would force the UI to parse two shapes for one query. The retention window is read per request (`historyRetentionDays`, the `pollingIntervalSeconds` precedent: §6.4 classifies it live). (3) **The history wire encoding:** raw points are `kind: 'point'` entries (§8.4 values as honest nulls on invalid rows), an overfull series answers `kind: 'bucket'` entries (D-081's min/max/first/last preservation, the per-field extrema as nulls for uncovered fields, the bucket endpoints kind-less — only points-array entries carry the discriminator), and §12.2's "explicit empty point between gap edges" is a `kind: 'empty'` entry at the gap's interval midpoint, spliced after downsampling (empty points are markers, never aggregation members; the D-081 boundary cut keeps the bracketing entries at the gap's own edges). Series identity (`unit`/`limitType`) rides at the top from the newest in-range row — null when empty; an **unknown metric key is an empty series, never an error** (the vocabulary is adapter-owned and catalogued by `/api/providers`), and `maxPoints` defaults/bounds are the schema-layer literals §13 states, drift-pinned against the downsampler's constants (the schemas layer cannot import the services layer). (4) **The events timeline is one kind-discriminated array** — `reset` (the stored §12.1 events with the D-046/D-074 `details` evidence verbatim: metric data only, never secrets), `gap` (D-075's fields), `collection_error` (task 120's class-a indicator, the message passed the same §7.4 exact-occurrence redaction as the status surface's `lastError`), `stopped_service` (class-b) — ordered instant-ascending, then a frozen kind rank, then metric key; the optional `metric` filter narrows only the per-metric kinds (resets and gaps) — failed cycles and stopped regions are account-level facts — and without it the last-valid query's key set enumerates exactly the series that can hold gaps (a metric with valid points in range necessarily has a last valid row; completeness is structural). (5) **The runs-evidence read:** one margin-widened **raw** facade read (`EVIDENCE_MARGIN_MS = gapThresholdMs(3600) + 300_000` = the widest §12.2 silence judgment plus one worst-case cycle span) supplies both §12.2 halves: the interval timeline built from D-069's per-run `interval_seconds` stamps (collapsed to changes; equal stamps keep the first cadence so the detector's unique-stamp contract holds on degenerate data) and task 120's bounding records, which anchor the range-edge silences — without the left margin, a run straddling `range.from` would move a leading region's start to the range edge instead of the record's own end (pinned by test). The raw read is the sanctioned D-082 pattern for internal consumers: pre-horizon rows are cadence/anchor evidence only — the timeline module clamps regions to the range and filters markers, so nothing out-of-policy is served — and the margin's coverage argument (every in-range row's own run sits inside the read, so the detector's point-coverage tripwire cannot fire) is bounded by one cycle span around the edges. (6) **Downsampling boundaries arrive as data** (D-081's contract): the route reads the account's stored RESET events for the series and feeds their instants beside the gaps, so reset markers and gap edges survive aggregation by the landed rule, never by endpoint-side recomputation.

**Reasons.** The timestamp question had exactly two self-consistent answers (ISO both ways, or the split D-130 had already staked for the quota surface); the split wins because §13 names the ISO requirement **only** for the range parameters while every landed response field since D-128 is epoch-ms — flipping the response half now would fork the surface mid-family, and §14.4's chart axis consumes epoch-ms natively (the UI converts the two request params once per query). The 200-with-report follows the same single-shape logic: D-082's report was designed to be stated, and an HTTP error cannot carry a body the chart code can render beside its empty axes. The kind-discriminated encoding keeps the three history entry classes and four event classes structurally distinguishable — the §12.2 done-condition's own requirement for gaps-vs-errors, generalized — and the empty point as a distinct kind prevents conflating "no collection happened" with "collection returned an invalid reading" (§8.4's honesty rule at the series level). The raw runs-evidence read is the honest resolution of three needs no retention-aware wrapper can express (the detector's coverage tripwire wants every point's own run, the timeline's edge anchoring wants records beyond the range, and the retention seam's own policy is about what is SERVED) — the same reasoning D-082 recorded for 118/119's raw series reads, now with the margin argument written down.

**Consequences.** The composition task that owns the configuration file passes `ApiRoutesOptions.history` (store seam, repository, `historyRetentionDays` reader, clock); until then both paths answer the scope catch-all's 404 (pinned per route). The exported surface (`HistoryRouteOptions`, `historyRoutes`, `parseEpochMsParam`, `parseRequestedRange`, `intervalTimelineFromRuns`, `historyPointInput`, `historyPointView`, `historyBucketView`, `emptyPointView`, `mergeEmptyPoints`, `rangeReportOf`, the events view builders, `sortEventItems`, `EVIDENCE_MARGIN_MS` in `src/server/api/history.ts`; the schemas and kind/budget/outcome constants in `src/schemas/api/history.ts`) is internal API under `src/`, not package surface; changing the wire kinds, the range-report fields, the `details.reason` vocabulary (`invalid-timestamp`+`param`, `inverted-range`), or the timeline order is a successor decision. Known residuals, recorded: the evidence-margin read bounds the range-edge cadence/anchor divergence by the margin itself (a boundary row whose run predates the horizon by more than one cycle span is approximated by the earliest in-policy run's cadence — the D-082 boundary-divergence class, unreachable without a horizon-adjacent interval change); `resolutionMs` is fractional by construction (the widest allocated slice width) and the contract declares `number`, not integer; the heavy integration seeds carry explicit timeouts (D-094's family — measured 39 s for 1501 ceremony-wrapped cycle writes, reseeded as one repository transaction for the bulk case) while the boundary tests keep the full `persistCollectionCycle` path; and the UI client additions (174+'s job) consume the schema types type-only, exactly as D-134 recorded — `healthyApiBody` gains its history/events arms when the pages land, not here. The done-condition ("response contracts covered end-to-end against SQLite") is pinned by `test/unit/api-history-schema.spec.ts` (closed contracts, kind unions, the query grammar, the no-drift rows), `test/unit/api-history-view.spec.ts` (the pure compositions incl. the margin-derivation pin and the redaction table), `test/integration/api-history.spec.ts` (23 tests) and `test/integration/api-events.spec.ts` (21 tests) — both over migrated disposable SQLite through the real `/api` scope, seeding through the live write path (`persistCollectionCycle` + task 118's `detectCycleResetEvents`) so the served resets are the pipeline's own output.
