## D-140 — Task U-040's composition root: the raw-file read-modify-write behind both stores, the minimal settings write, the storage component with its lazy repository facade, and the manual-test-observing provider wrapper (spec §5.6, §6.2–§6.4, §7.2, §13, §15.2; task U-040)

**Date:** 2026-11-03 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§5.6](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#56-process-lifecycle-backups-and-upgrades), [§6.2](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#62-configuration-contract), [§6.3](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#63-secret-storage-and-writes), [§6.4](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#64-runtime-settings-changes), [§7.2](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#72-retry-and-error-behavior), [§13](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#13-http-api), [§15.2](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#152-passwords-and-sessions) · **Tasks:** [U-040](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-121 (the auth projection `HttpServerOptions.auth` this composition maps 1:1 as its docblock promised, and the consumer-owned-seam precedent), D-128 (the `AccountConfigStore` seam implemented here over `loadConfigWithEnv` + atomic `writeConfigFile` + §6.4, and the pre-sync config-sync gap closed here), D-130 (the `SettingsStore` seam with its `sources.fields` write-side obligation and the `pendingPassword` hashing hand-off discharged here), D-139 (the history options — store seam, repository, `historyRetentionDays` reader, clock — passed exactly as its consequences recorded), D-017 (the lock-first ordering that forces the storage component's start-time open), D-064 (the suspension state machine the holder wraps), D-124 (the password-change session revocation), D-026 (the §6.4 vocabulary the stores report through the reloader), D-021 (the one shared clock), D-061 (archive terminality in the config-sync), D-102/D-052 (the adapter-importing privilege and the credential-check `kind` the observation reads)

**Decision.** Task U-040 lands the production composition as a new module, `src/server/composition.ts`, that task 060's `buildComponents()` (now async — internal API; `runServer` awaits it inside its try, so §6.2's refuse-to-start reports and exits 1 unchanged) delegates to, and pins eight interpretations. (Correction trail: the task's review round — deepseek-v4.1-flash, one round, REQUEST_CHANGES with 1 P1 / 6 P2 / 4 P3 — folded in before landing: the keyless-account invariant relaxation (the P1, interpretation (8) below), the storage stop's retry-preserving close, the `attempted` write-candidate payload, the key-change release wiring, the env-resolved keys in the logger's startup secret list, a direct store-level test suite, a reserved port for the listener-binding test, and four smaller pins/wordings; two P3s were declined with reasons — the Consequences record them.) (1) **The startup sequence is eager where reading secrets is concerned, lazy where touching shared state is concerned.** `composeApplication()` resolves the §6.1 directories, runs `enforceConfigPermissions` EAGERLY — before `loadConfigWithEnv` reads the file, because a secret-bearing file the §6.3 permissions have not vetted must not be parsed (the landed `createPermissionsCheck` component stays unused: as a component it would run after the load it exists to precede) — then loads and refuses on problems, and only then builds the shared clock (D-021, one instance), the redacting logger (§16 level from the configuration, the startup accounts' RESOLVED keys — file values and `apiKeyEnv` reads alike — pre-registered as known secret values, §15.4 defense-in-depth; keys added at runtime rely on the route contracts' structural no-leak guards, the recorded residual), the reloader (D-026), the suspension holder, and the registry. The components are the §5.6 order `[single-instance-lock, storage, http-listener]`: the data directory is created by the LOCK's start (D-017), so storage opens, migrates (`runStartupMigrations` with backups per §11.4), and builds its repository inside its own component — and because route registration is eager while the repository is a start-time fact, the routes receive a **lazy facade** (a Proxy over the holder) that resolves the real repository on first use and answers a clear wiring error before the app has started; requests only flow after every component started. A storage-start failure closes the connection it opened, and `stop` clears the holder only after its checkpoint-and-close release actually ran — a throwing checkpoint stays retryable (U-018's contract), never a silently leaked handle. (2) **The HTTP seam is `HttpServerOptions.routes`** — `Omit<ApiRoutesOptions, 'auth'>` spread beside the construction-derived `auth` object, so D-121's projection gains its promised producer and the five families wire as five members; absent members keep the no-half-wired rule verbatim (the landed per-family 404 pins run against the bare construction and stay green). (3) **Both stores own one serialized file owner, and the write base is the RAW file JSON.** `src/server/config-stores.ts`'s `ConfigFileOwner` serializes every mutation of both stores (accounts and settings edit the same file; interleaved read-modify-writes would clobber each other's section) with the reloader's own queue shape. Each mutation re-reads the file (`readFile` + `parseJson`; ENOENT reads `{}` — the env-only mode's sanctioned sub-minimal file is RMW-able and a first write starts from `{}`), mutates only its own section, validates the candidate through `parseConfigWithEnv(candidate, env)` — the exact reload pipeline, so a mutation that would break the effective configuration is refused value-free BEFORE any byte is written — writes atomically (`writeConfigFile`, D-016), and applies §6.4 through the composition-wrapped reload; a rejected reload rejects the store call (the endpoint answers INTERNAL, the incumbent stays effective per §6.2; the file may be ahead of memory, the honest residual of a concurrent hand-break). The raw-JSON base is the point: the effective configuration is the environment-merged, defaults-materialized view — persisting it verbatim would bake `QUOTAMETER_*` values into the file (D-130's hazard) and materialize sections the operator left minimal. (4) **The settings write writes only what the request attempted.** The `apply` payload gains `attempted` — the body-supplied field set, carried beside `sources` exactly as D-130's own review round carried the write-side obligation (the endpoint computes it already; `api-settings.spec.ts` pins the carry). The candidate takes from `change.config` exactly the mutable scalars in `attempted` (a change validated against an older snapshot cannot revert a field a concurrent request already applied — the review round's stale-base revert), never a `sources.fields` path (the obligation, applied defensively even though the endpoint refuses those attempts), and `auth.passwordHash` only from a fresh `hashPassword(pendingPassword)` computed outside the serialized mutation — the effective hash is never copied back, so a concurrent `quotameter passwd` write survives a settings PUT. A password change revokes every session through `deleteAllSessions` once the write and its reload both succeeded (§15.2/D-124): the revocation rides the accepted reload, so a rejected reload leaves the incumbent hash effective and its sessions coherent with it — the coherent pairing on both arms. (5) **The config-sync runs at storage start and rides the reload.** Configured accounts are mirrored into rows (missing rows inserted with the shared clock's stamp, label drift copied into the row's denormalized mirror through `updateAccountDetails`, archived rows never touched — D-061's terminal archive; rows without entries keep their §8.2 history), and the stores' injected reload re-runs the sync whenever `applied` includes `'accounts'` — the composition never hands the stores a bare `reloader.reload()`, so the mirror cannot lag a write. (6) **The §7.2 suspension holder is a services module and BOTH release conditions are fed.** `src/services/account-suspensions.ts` holds per-account D-064 state over the landed transitions (nothing re-implemented) and owns the identity vocabulary (`keyIdentityOfSecret`, the sha256 of the resolved secret — one site so the two observations compare like with like). The manual-test half: the composition registers each adapter wrapped by `observingManualTests()` (`src/server/providers.ts` — the module the layout already reserves for adapter composition); the wrapper applies D-064's unconditional release-on-request BEFORE the attempt, feeds `applyCycleOutcome('auth_error', keyIdentity)` on a structurally-read `credentials-rejected` rejection, rethrows everything unchanged, and delegates `fetchSnapshot` unobserved (polled cycles feed the machine through the polling engine when it joins — observing both holders would double-feed it). The key-change half (the review round's P2): the composition-wrapped reload reports every configured account's current key identity whenever `applied` includes `'accounts'` — `applyKeyIdentity` releases an episode that began under a different key, idempotently otherwise (D-064's own design for per-observation reporting), so a key rotation through `PATCH /api/accounts/:id` clears `Auth rejected` with no polling engine in the composition; an unresolvable source (unset `apiKeyEnv`, the §5.3 keyless skip) reports a distinct per-source identity, because "the key changed to something else" releases either way. When the polling engine's composition task lands it becomes the holding side for polled cycles; this holder stays the composition's seam for manual tests, key observations, and status reads so the two cannot disagree. (7) **Deliberately unwired, as residuals:** SIGHUP → `reload()` (process-signal wiring belongs to the D-024 readiness seam's task; the CLI's `reload` command already refuses to signal an invalid file, and until the wiring lands its SIGHUP is a no-op), the sessions-backed `isAuthenticated` (the login endpoints are the D-125/D-126 plan gap; the §15.1 layer stays fail-closed — under `required` mode everything but health answers 401), and the graceful-drain/polling components (no in-flight work exists to drain until the engine lands). (8) **A configured account may be keyless (relaxing D-014/D-018's strict §6.3 reading — the review round's P1).** The cross-field rule "exactly one of apiKey or apiKeyEnv must be set" made `POST /api/accounts` without a key answer 500 through the production store: the landed D-128 endpoint contract makes `apiKey` optional precisely because §5.3 step 3's skip path lands in the web UI ("The user may skip adding a key and add it later in the UI"), the UI's add form omits blank keys, and D-138's attention classifier already handles the sourceless configured account — the invariant contradicted the spec's own named flow, and the composition is the first construction that surfaces the collision (both landed accounts suites run against store doubles). §6.3's "exactly one may be set" governs the ALTERNATIVE (never both sources at once) — that arm stays; the presence duty is dropped, and the keyless configured account displays §7.3's `Not configured` (§7.3 already lists it as a separate state). `init`'s no-key flow (which does not persist a keyless initial account) keeps its behavior; its comment's "invalid configuration" rationale is now stale and belongs to the CLI's owner to reword — `src/cli/**` is outside this task's carve-out.

**Reasons.** The task's architectural questions were where the file-owning discipline lives, what it writes, and how eager registration meets start-time facts. The raw-JSON RMW answers all three file questions at once: it is the only base that can neither bake environment values (D-130's obligation, by construction rather than by subtraction) nor materialize defaults, it validates through the same pipeline that will judge the reload (no second validator to drift), and it keeps the file's own shape for everything the mutation does not own — which is also why the settings write is diff-based rather than verbatim-minus-env: the stricter rule subsumes the obligation and protects the un-asked-for sections (including the stored hash) for free. The lock-first storage open is not a preference: D-017's lock creates the data directory, so an eager open would fail on a fresh install and would race a second process's migrations; the lazy facade is the minimal bridge, and its before-start throw is the fail-fast wiring signal. Observation rides the provider rather than the routes because the route families are landed contracts and the composition root is the one layer allowed to compose adapters — and because the wrapper sees exactly the signal the accounts endpoint classifies (the same D-052 `kind`), so the wire's vocabulary stays the single authority. The suspension holder lives in `services` (it composes a services state machine and consumes no server types), keeping `services → server` import-free as the layout requires.

**Consequences.** `buildComponents()` returns the composed service: the previously-404 families answer on a real server, which tasks 174+ (charts against a real server) and 183 (acceptance) implicitly required, and a keyless `POST /api/accounts` answers its landed 201 contract (the invariant relaxation also updates `test/unit/config.spec.ts` and `test/unit/config-validation.spec.ts`, `docs/architecture/decision-overview.md`, and `docs/config-schema.md`; `src/cli/init-account.ts`'s no-key comment is now stale — the CLI owner's rewording, outside this task's carve-out). `HttpServerOptions.routes` is the composition-root seam for future families (task 162's peak-hours wires the same way); the exported surface (`composeApplication`, `ComposeApplicationOptions`, `ComposedApplication` in `src/server/composition.ts`; `createConfigFileOwner`, `createConfigFileAccountStore`, `createConfigFileSettingsStore` and their option types in `src/server/config-stores.ts`; `createAccountSuspensions`, `keyIdentityOfSecret` in `src/services/account-suspensions.ts`; `observingManualTests` in `src/server/providers.ts`) is internal API under `src/`, not package surface. The done-condition ("an integration test through the production construction, not test doubles, against a temp config + SQLite, and the previously-404 routes answering") is pinned by `test/integration/composition.spec.ts`: the full construction over temp directories with only the provider adapter doubled (the external boundary the no-network guard requires tests to own) — every family answering, the config-sync across two lifecycles (also proving the lock releases on stop), create/update/archive and settings PUTs persisting through the real file with the §15.4 marker never on the wire or in a log line, environment-owned fields never baked (the file stays `logging`-less under `QUOTAMETER_LOGGING_LEVEL`), the env-resolved key marked and covered, the keyless §5.3 skip path answering 201 and reading `not-configured`, the scrypt hash stored and the pre-inserted session revoked, a password-less PUT leaving the stored hash byte-identical, the §7.2 `auth-rejected` → lifted sequence over `/api/status` plus the key-rotation release, and both §6.2 refusals — beside the store-level matrix in `test/integration/config-stores.spec.ts` (absent-file base, malformed/non-object refusal, duplicate id, unknown ids, refuse-before-write with byte-identical file, reload-rejection propagation, `apiKeyEnv` resolution arms, concurrent-mutation serialization, the attempted-only and env-skipping settings writes, the non-object-section refusal), the unit pins `test/unit/account-suspensions.spec.ts` (incl. the key-change release) and `test/unit/server-providers.spec.ts` (incl. the suspended-then-inconclusive release), and the updated `server-main.spec.ts` bootstrap pins (the §5.6 names/order; the no-configuration refusal; the default-assembly run over a reserved port). Two review P3s declined, with reasons: the mutation queue stays a local twin of the reloader's inline serialization (extracting a shared primitive would touch `src/config/reload.ts`, a D-085 coverage-pinned critical module, for eight duplicated lines — the twins are pinned behaviorally by the serialization tests on both sides), and `readRawConfig` keeps direct `node:fs` access (the owner's tests are integration-by-convention over real files, per testing.md's "SQLite/config work — integration"; a `ConfigReadFilesystem`-style seam would serve no test this suite needs that real files do not). Known residuals, recorded: a hand-edited file change concurrent with an API mutation is last-writer-wins per section (the single-operator §15.1 service, D-128's accepted-concurrency precedent); a settings PUT against a file whose non-owned fields drifted from the effective configuration (a hand edit plus no reload) writes the PUT's fields over the fresh file read, preserving the hand edit elsewhere; and runtime-added keys are covered by the route contracts' closed serializers rather than the logger's startup secret list. SIGHUP wiring, the login endpoints' `isAuthenticated`, and the polling engine remain the named successors' scope.

## D-141 — Task U-042's init-side password collection: the environment-by-name non-interactive channel (`--password-env`), the loopback-optional/non-loopback-required interactive pair over passwd's shared flow, the fresh-run-only offer, and the hash (never the `pendingPassword` channel) submitted through the boundary (spec §5.3 step 4, §15.2, §15.1, §15.4; task U-042)

**Date:** 2026-11-03 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§5.3](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#53-init-workflow), [§15.2](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#152-passwords-and-sessions), [§15.1](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#151-network-and-authentication-modes), [§15.4](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#154-secret-protection) · **Tasks:** [U-042](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-101 (the pending tolerance this task builds on, whose "at which point the pending state simply stops being produced" vision this entry scopes), D-118 (the `passwd` contract whose `askNewPassword`, `MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH` boundary, hash-submission convention, and no-value-flag reasoning are consumed verbatim; its consequences named this exact `--password-env` additive change), D-122 (the verification primitive behind the stored hash), D-100 (the `--yes` layer the flag joins), D-022 (the settings boundary the hash travels through), D-011 (blank-env-value uniformity)

**Decision.** Task U-042 makes `init` the second §15.2 password setter on fresh runs, in both modes, and pins five interpretations. (Correction trail: the task's review round — deepseek-v4.1-flash, one round, REQUEST_CHANGES with 1 P1 / 1 P2 / 5 P3 — folded into this entry and the same commit, which had not landed when corrected (the D-119/D-122 precedent). The P1 is the revocation below; the P2/P3 fixes are the renamed non-loopback note test, the type-exhaustive outcome mappings (a narrowing overload on `askNewPassword` that removes `skipped` from `passwd`'s view, and the spelled-out `closed`/`interrupted` cases in `askInitPassword`), the untrimmed-marker and exact 11/12-character boundary pins, and the two added file-marker assertions; one P3 — extracting the shared name-validation of `--password-env`/`--api-key-env` into a helper — was declined with reasons in the commit body: the checks' messages are flag-specific prose (the remedy nouns differ), so a parameterized extractor would trade twenty lines of straight-line duplication for a message-assembly indirection, and both channels' rule sets are already pinned executably against each other.) (1) **The non-interactive channel is the environment, by name** — the new `--password-env <variable>` value option of `init --yes`, mirroring `--api-key-env` check for check (the account schema's exported name pattern, the reserved `QUOTAMETER_` prefix refusal, own-property set-ness with blank counting as unset per D-011) plus the §15.2 minimum checked on the raw untrimmed value; there is deliberately no `--password <value>` flag (§15.4's process-listing rule, the same reasoning that keeps `--api-key` out of init and a `--password` out of `passwd` — D-118's consequences named this exact additive shape), and no problem ever contains the argument or the value (the argument may be a mistyped password). The password rides `buildYesAnswers`' result beside the answers — never inside `InitAnswers` — so the plaintext's only journey is prompt-or-env to the hashing call, exactly the confinement `passwd.ts`'s docblock promises. (2) **The interactive pair is `passwd`'s own flow behind additive options, and the bind host chooses its mode**: `askNewPassword` (D-118) gains `{ prompt?, skippable? }` and a `skipped` outcome (the exactly-empty first answer in skippable mode — a whitespace-only answer stays an answer and fails the shared length check; secrets are never trimmed), and the new `src/cli/init-password.ts` asks one muted pair after the §5.3 step-3 questions and before the account's connection test: loopback binds (the §15.1 default) ask optionally with Enter keeping none — completing init without a password leaves `auth` exactly as §15.1 ships it, `mode: 'auto'` with no `passwordHash`, the task's done-condition read against §15.1's two-mode vocabulary — while non-loopback binds ask required-shaped per §5.3 step 4 ("require a password before starting the service"): the prompt names the requirement, the empty answer is the too-short complaint like any other (the mandatory-timezone precedent — a required question offers no skip), and three rejected pairs cancel the run with nothing written. Closed or interrupted input at the pair cancels through the handler's uniform `input closed before the password was answered` failure (D-044's no-separate-interrupt rendering); cancellation semantics match every other question (D-099). (3) **The offer is fresh-run-only, and storing a password revokes what a surviving database holds** (the review round's P1). Re-runs collect no password in either mode — D-101's re-run surface stays exactly its four settings questions — because changing an existing password is `quotameter passwd`'s contract (D-118's fail-secure revoke-before-write ordering is the machinery such a change requires, and init re-runs would have to duplicate it), and a password-pending re-run keeps the `passwd` remedy D-101 pinned; `--password-env` against an existing configuration is therefore one clear problem naming the passwd command, mirroring the account flags' fresh-only rule. But "fresh" is fresh about the **configuration file** only: the data directory may still hold a database whose sessions were minted under a previous installation's password (a deleted configuration — init's own invalid-file remedy says "remove the file, then run init again" — or a re-pointed `QUOTAMETER_CONFIG_DIR`), so a run that stores a hash first revokes those sessions through `passwd`'s own exported `revokeAllSessions` in its fail-secure order (after the stale-detection guard, before the write; a failed revocation aborts with nothing stored, and a revoked count renders beside the write trailer — fresh machines read absence silently). The D-101 pending write itself stays reachable exactly where it was designed to be: `--yes` without `--password-env` on a non-loopback bind (the deliberate init-now, passwd-later journey — §15.1 binds starting, not existing), so the tolerance and its tests survive collection landing. (4) **The hash, not the `pendingPassword` channel, is what init submits**: the handler hashes through the new `InitDeps.hash` seam (production `hashPassword`, D-118's encoding; D-122's verifier reads it back) and `assembleInitConfig` submits `auth: { passwordHash }` through `validateSettings` — `passwd`'s exact convention, one validation pass over the complete post-hashing state — while the §15.2 minimum stays enforced at the collection layer (the shared pair flow for interactive input, the flag check for the environment value), which is where D-118 enforces it too. D-101's anticipated `auth.password`/`pendingPassword` hand-off (its consequences paragraph) is thus executed with a different, smaller mechanism: the channel remains the future UI settings endpoint's, and init never handles a plaintext inside any validation layer. (5) **The fresh summary reports password state only**: a `Password:` row (`set (only a scrypt hash is stored)` / `none` — the Account row's state-words discipline), with the §5.3 step-4 requirement note suppressed when a password was set (a stored hash satisfies the requirement, the persist display's own rule).

**Reasons.** Every gap closed toward the smallest surface that keeps one implementation per concern. The env-by-name channel is forced by §5.4-adjacent §15.4 reasoning already recorded twice (D-100 for the key, D-118 for `passwd`'s flag refusal) — a non-interactive init must still be able to set the password §5.3 step 4 can require, and the environment is the only channel that never lands in a process listing or shell history. Reusing `askNewPassword` (rather than a second pair flow in `init-password.ts`) eliminates the drift surface between the two commands that set passwords — the bounded attempts, the pair restart, the muted echo, and the closed/interrupted distinction stay one implementation, with `passwd`'s no-options call shape provably unchanged (pinned, and type-narrowed: the no-options overload returns a union without `skipped`). The required-when-non-loopback reading follows §5.3 step 4's own words plus D-101's "pending state simply stops being produced" expectation for the flow that now has a channel — the interactive human typing at the prompt is exactly who "require" addresses — while the `--yes` absence-tolerance keeps D-101's landed journey intact rather than hard-failing automation the spec never says to refuse (§15.1's refusal binds the service start, and the pending write's remedy prints). Fresh-run-only collection keeps the _interactive change_ flow in exactly one place (`passwd`, with its owner resolution, revocation, and reload advisory), while the revocation of a surviving database — the review round's P1, correcting the first version's "a fresh run has no database" premise, which was true by assumption and not by construction — reuses `passwd`'s probe and order verbatim, so the security control has one implementation and init only decides _when_ it applies: exactly when it stores a hash, the one moment the credential changes under this command. The hash-submission convention avoids a second validation vocabulary: the boundary already re-validates the merged configuration, the hash is schema-opaque, and the plaintext never needs to enter a layer whose job is validating configuration shape.

**Consequences.** `quotameter passwd` remains the change/completion command (its D-118 contract untouched); a future UI password-set path (159+'s settings endpoints) reuses `hashPassword` and this same hash-submission convention, and may use `validateSettings`' `pendingPassword` channel as D-022 designed it — init no longer precludes it. `INIT_VALUE_OPTIONS` and the dispatch table grow `password-env` together (the lockstep test already enforces it), so the stray-without-`--yes` guard covers the flag automatically; the fresh-run summary's new `Password:` row is pinned byte-shape alongside the Account row, and adding any future password-adjacent row is a coordinated renderer+test change. Fresh-run piped-automation scripts gain one answer line (Enter skips on loopback; a pair on non-loopback) — the breaking edge is pinned by every updated suite rather than documented around, and every launcher/handler harness in the init suites now redirects `QUOTAMETER_DATA_DIR` beside the config dir (a password-writing run revokes surviving sessions, so no test may touch a shared default). The exported surface (`LOOPBACK_PASSWORD_PROMPT`, `REQUIRED_PASSWORD_PROMPT`, `InitPasswordOutcome`, `InitPasswordDeps`, `askInitPassword` in `init-password.ts`; `AskPasswordOptions`, `RequiredPasswordOutcome`, and the `skipped` outcome on `askNewPassword` in `passwd.ts`; `InitDeps.hash`/`InitDeps.revokeSessions`; `YesInput.password`; `assembleInitConfig`'s fourth parameter) is internal API under `src/`, not package surface; making the interactive pair optional on non-loopback binds, adding a skip escape to the required mode, or offering password change on re-runs each requires a successor decision (the last one brings D-118's full revocation machinery with it). The done-condition is pinned executably at every level: the marker password (`unit-password-marker-42`, `integration-password-marker-42`, `pty-password-marker-42`, `yes-integration-password-42`) is asserted absent from every stdout/stderr line and from the written configuration in unit handler runs, piped real-launcher runs, PTY typed and whole-block-paste runs, and the `--yes` environment runs — while the file positively stores a `scrypt$`-shaped `auth.passwordHash` — and the optional half (skip → `auth: { mode: 'auto' }`, no hash; the hash seam never called) is pinned at the handler, the real launcher, and the `--yes` layer, completing §15.1's default-state requirement in the strongest form available: the written bytes. The P1 revocation is pinned at the handler (the none/revoked/failed arms over the seam) and end-to-end in `test/integration/cli-init-idempotent.spec.ts` (a real migrated database with two live sessions, a fresh configuration directory, a collected password — the sessions gone, the hash stored, the marker absent, the revoked line rendered).

## D-142 — Task 162's §13 peak-hours endpoint: the D-139 timestamp reconciliation inherited (superseding D-073's interim `toUtcIso` note), retention as the inherited 200-with-report over the effective range, the nullable-facts no-schedule arm beside the computing empty-windows arm, the span-cap VALIDATION, and the D-140 composition wiring (spec §9.3, §13, §11.3, §10; task 162)

**Date:** 2026-11-04 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§9.3](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#93-schedule-calculation-and-display), [§13](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#13-http-api), [§11.3](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#113-retention-and-cleanup), [§10](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#10-time-and-time-zones) · **Tasks:** [162](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-139 (the timestamp reconciliation this route inherits as §13's third named consumer, plus the range parsing/report and the 200-with-report consumed verbatim), D-073/D-079 (the timeline contract this route serves — partition, half-open bounds, local-time rendering, `MAX_QUERY_SPAN_DAYS`; D-073's consequences named the ISO-serialization alternative this entry supersedes), D-140 (the `HttpServerOptions.routes` composition seam this task wires, exactly as its consequences recorded), D-128 (the optional-options registration rule and the both-halves account verdict), D-082 (the pure `boundHistoryRange` the route reuses without a storage read), D-130 (the live schedules reader precedent), D-113 (the frozen error registry — no new codes), D-097 (the time-suite manifest the new specs join)

**Decision.** Task 162 lands `GET /api/peak-hours?accountId&from&to` as `src/server/api/peak-hours.ts` inside the `/api` scope behind `ApiRoutesOptions.peakHours` (contracts in `src/schemas/api/peak-hours.ts`), and pins six interpretations. (Correction trail: the task's review round — deepseek-v4.1-flash, one round, APPROVE with 1 P2 / 1 P3, both folded in before landing — sharpened interpretation (5): the bare span catch had misclassified a narrow range at the ECMAScript epoch ceiling (where the zone conversion itself cannot represent the +offset reading) as `range-too-wide`; a truthful pre-check with its own `range-unsupported` reason now guards the representable band before any computation, the catch's reachability argument includes it, and the ceiling range is pinned by test. The P3 — a test comment naming a five-digit year over a six-digit fixture — is fixed in place.) (1) **The response is the timeline verbatim, and the D-139 timestamp reconciliation applies in both directions** — D-073's consequences paragraph had anticipated "epoch milliseconds → ISO 8601 `Z` via `toUtcIso` at its boundary"; D-139's later rule (epoch-ms responses, §13 names the ISO requirement only for the request parameters) wins for the third named consumer, and the interval boundaries serve as epoch-ms integers beside D-073's own `yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm` local-time strings — which are §9.3's separate output requirement ("local time in the schedule time zone"), not timestamps, so the one-format-per-direction rule is not mixed by them. The wire entries are the calculator's union members field-for-field (`kind`-discriminated `peak` with `windowId`/`name`/`multiplier`, `off-peak` with the schedule's rate; `intervalViews` is a typed copy, not a projection), the response echoes the resolved `providerId` (the configured entry wins, a storage-only row supplies it for archived accounts — §8.2's retained timelines stay computable) and the schedule facts `timezone`/`offPeakMultiplier` derived through the calculator's own two functions (`resolveTimeZone`, the `CONFIG_DEFAULTS` fallback), drift-pinned by test. (2) **Range and account parameters are the family's, reused not forked:** `parseRequestedRange` and `rangeReportOf` from `src/server/api/history.ts` (the `invalid-timestamp`+`param`, `inverted-range`, and NOT_FOUND arms are D-139's/D-128's own), and the both-halves account verdict is re-derived locally only because the route needs both halves' data (the entry's `providerId` beside the row's), not just the verdict. (3) **Retention is inherited, over the effective range:** §13's range/retention sentence names peak-hours, so the D-139 200-with-report applies — `boundHistoryRange` (the pure D-082 bound, no storage read — the timeline is computed, not stored) clamps `from` to the horizon, the intervals partition `[effectiveFrom, effectiveTo)`, and `rejected` answers empty intervals with the horizon named; the schedule facts still echo in the rejected arm because they are configuration, not range output — the retention and no-schedule arms are orthogonal. (4) **The no-schedule arm is the nullable pair, and empty windows is NOT it:** an account whose provider has no `providers.<id>` entry answers `timezone: null`/`offPeakMultiplier: null` with empty intervals (§9.2's "never invent a schedule"; the same fact `/api/providers` states as `peakHours: null` — a boolean beside the nullables would say it twice), while a configured schedule with an empty `windows` array computes normally — the whole range one off-peak interval at the schedule's zone and rate, §9.2's own unverified-schedule shape; the §14 UI's "Peak-hours schedule is not configured" message reads `/api/providers`, which serves `windows` (this route serves intervals). (5) **The span cap is the service's, surfaced as VALIDATION beside a representability pre-check:** retention never clamps `to` (D-082), so a far-future end can exceed D-073's `MAX_QUERY_SPAN_DAYS` (3660 local days); the route maps the calculator's throw to VALIDATION with `details.reason: 'range-too-wide'` and `maxDays` — the bound single-sited in the service (a route-side pre-check would re-derive the zone-day arithmetic). The mapping's reachability is documented in place: `from`/`to` are pre-validated finite and ordered, the zone is config-validated IANA (§9.2 gates the live reader), and — the review round's P2 — `requireRepresentableRange` pre-rejects the epoch-ceiling neighborhood (±8.64e15 ms minus a two-day headroom that covers the zone offset, the guard day, and the `24:00` next-midnight resolution) with the truthful `range-unsupported` reason, so a request whose instants no zone conversion can render is never misreported as too wide, and the span cap is the only throw the catch can see. (6) **The wiring point is D-140's `routes` seam, exactly as its consequences recorded:** `composeApplication()` passes `peakHours: { store, repository, schedules, historyRetentionDays, now }` beside the history block — the same store/repository instances, the same live `providers` reader the providers endpoint reads, the shared retention reader and clock — so the endpoint answers in the production construction (the previously-404 last row of §13's table).

**Reasons.** Every open question the task found had a family precedent that made a fork expensive: the timestamp direction (D-139 had already staked the split and named this route its third consumer — flipping the response half for one route would fork the surface mid-family, and §14's highlighting consumes the local-time strings verbatim beside the epoch-ms axis), the retention arm (§13's own sentence names peak-hours; D-139 had closed D-082's open choice as the 200-with-report, and a computed timeline is served over the same effective range the stored series are, so nothing older than retention is queryable through any of the three routes), the error vocabulary (D-113 frozen; the `range-too-wide` reason is a `details` value in the D-139 pattern, not a new code), and the registration (D-128's optional-options rule, D-140's pre-built seam). The no-schedule/empty-windows split follows §9.2's own text: the "not configured" message belongs to the empty-`windows` shape, which only `/api/providers` can express on the wire — serving `windows` here too would duplicate the providers surface into the range route; the nullable facts encode "nothing is computable" (no zone exists) without a second discriminator. The facts-from-the-same-functions rule (drift-pinned) keeps the echo and the computed intervals from ever disagreeing, including in the rejected arm where no timeline exists to copy from.

**Consequences.** §13's route table is complete: every named path answers through the production construction, and the composition family walk pins it. The exported surface (`PeakHoursRouteOptions`, `peakHoursRoutes`, `resolveSchedule`, `ScheduleFacts`, `scheduleFactsOf`, `intervalViews` in `src/server/api/peak-hours.ts`; the schemas and `PEAK_HOURS_INTERVAL_KINDS`/`LOCAL_TIME_PATTERN` in `src/schemas/api/peak-hours.ts`) is internal API under `src/`, not package surface; changing the interval wire shape, the null-facts encoding, the `range-too-wide`/`range-unsupported` reasons, or the empty-windows computation is a successor decision. The three peak-hours-named specs join `test/unit/time-suite-manifest.spec.ts`'s pinned list (the `test:time` substring filter selects them by name — the D-097 convention that time/peak-hours specs are named after their modules), so CI's §17.1 matrix runs the endpoint's DST proof under all nine `TZ` cells; the suites are `TZ`-invariant by pinned-literal epochs (verified under `Asia/Kathmandu` locally). The done-condition ("server-generated intervals match the configured timezone/DST tests") is pinned three ways: the unit view suite wraps the task-114/115 matrix timelines (New York's 23/25-hour days, Havana's midnight gap with the shifted-boundary local times — where the honest rendering of a clipped stretch ending at a shifted instant is the shifted wall time, not the configured one, D-073's truthful-rendering rule —, Lord Howe's 30-minute and Chatham's quarter-hour gaps, Kolkata's half-hour offset with range clipping, the §9.1 production week) in the served envelope and validates through the compiled response schema before deep-equality; the integration suite serves the same classes through the real `/api` scope over migrated SQLite; and the composition spec proves the production construction serves the configured §9.1 schedule's intervals. OpenAPI (task 163) generates from the same schemas; the UI chart consumer (174+) reads the local-time strings verbatim and never calculates windows independently (§9.3).

## D-143 — Task U-043's resolution of the `@fastify/rate-limit` dependency: removed — §15.2's failed-attempt budget is the services-layer primitive (D-125), no spec sentence asks for a generic per-request 429 limiter (§15.5's limits are the body size and the timeouts), and §3's own minimal-runtime-dependencies instruction settles the tie (spec §3, §15.5, §15.2, §13; task U-043)

**Date:** 2026-11-04 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§3](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#3-technology-and-packaging), [§15.5](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#155-headers-and-limits), [§15.2](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#152-passwords-and-sessions), [§13](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#13-http-api) · **Tasks:** [U-043](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-109 (the §3 plugin split that declared the dependency for a then-imagined HTTP-layer task 156 and pinned its deferred registration), D-125 (the services-layer primitive that superseded that plan, recorded the package's inexpressibility, and left the dependency's fate as the main session's maintenance call — the call this entry answers), D-127 (the task-158 construction pin that asserted the unregistered state this entry retires), D-113 (the error-envelope registry whose promised `RATE_LIMITED` code D-125 already retired — the second landed contract a registration would contradict)

**Decision.** Task U-043 removes `@fastify/rate-limit` from `dependencies` (lockfile regenerated host-side with npm 11.9.0 via `npm install --package-lock-only`, container volume re-synced by the stamp-file `npm ci`; the diff is deletions-only — the package entry plus the one dependency it orphaned, `ip-address`; its other three transitives — `@lukeed/ms`, `fastify-plugin`, `toad-cache` — remain, still required by `fastify` and the other plugins) and pins the fate executably: the construction suite's D-109/D-127 registration test keeps its `hasPlugin('@fastify/rate-limit') === false` assertion (the accidental-registration guard) and gains the declaration pin — `package.json` at the repo root carries no `@fastify/rate-limit` in any shipped dependency field (`dependencies`, `optionalDependencies`, `peerDependencies`) — so re-adding the package fails `make check` until the decision trail is updated (scratch-verified in both directions: the pin fails on a re-added line; a `src/` import of the uninstalled package would already fail typecheck). **The register branch was examined first and rejected scope-by-scope, from the spec text rather than convenience.** (a) _The login scope_ — the one place the spec rate-limits anything (§15.2) — is D-125's, and the package cannot express it: §15.2 budgets **failed** attempts and demands **increasing delays** ("then apply increasing delays" — delays, never rejections), while the plugin counts requests and answers 429s; and behind the §15.6 reverse proxy, where `trustProxy` is never enabled (D-109's construction, D-126's socket-fact reasoning), `request.ip` stays socket-derived, so every client shares the proxy's address — a per-IP 429 limiter there is the shared-source denial-of-service lever against the legitimate user that D-125's delays-not-rejections choice explicitly rejected. (b) _A general API scope_ has no spec sentence asking for it: §15.5 — the section the task cites — is titled "Headers and limits" but enumerates the limits it means (the 64 KiB request-body limit and the connection/request timeouts); §13 defines no 429 for any endpoint; the spec's abuse answers are §15.1's auth modes, §15.3's Host/Origin validation, §15.6's TLS proxy/firewall/SSH-tunneling publication — plus the §15.2 login budget. A registered limiter would enforce a rule nobody wrote. (c) _Any registration_ would contradict the landed error contract twice over: the plugin's rejections are native 429 errors that need either the `RATE_LIMITED` registry code D-125 explicitly retired ("delays are not errors, no rate-limit error class is coming") or no code at all — and a codeless native 429 is a foreign status D-113's strict classifier projects to INTERNAL 500, worse than nothing. **The §3 row is a knowing deviation, recorded as such**: §3's technology table heads its column "Required implementation" and names `@fastify/rate-limit` in the HTTP-server row, so removing the package departs from the row's letter — and this entry departs anyway, because the same section's closing paragraph commands "keep runtime dependencies minimal", and the behavior the row was named for — back when task 156 was imagined as an HTTP-layer concern — is owned by `src/services/login-rate-limit.ts` (D-125); an unregistered, unimported runtime dependency of a package that ships to end users (`quotameter` publishes `dependencies`) is pure supply-chain surface — audit noise, install weight, Dependabot churn — with zero behavior, the "dead weight" D-125 flagged. The spec and the manifest now disagree on this one row, deliberately; a future spec revision should drop the entry so they agree again.

**Reasons.** The task's done-condition demanded a deliberate answer to "which scope a per-request limiter actually protects", and the honest answer is none: every candidate scope either contradicts a landed decision (login), lacks a spec sentence (everything else), or breaks the error contract (any). Removal is not the convenient branch — it touches the published dependency set — but it is the branch the spec's own minimal-dependencies instruction supports against the row's letter: the single rate-limiting requirement anywhere in the specification is §15.2's, it is discharged by the D-125 primitive, and §3's minimal-dependencies instruction makes the unused package a net cost. Keeping it "in case" would leave the D-109/D-127 pin asserting a permanent non-use invariant over a dependency that ships in every installation — a decision the package manager re-asks on every audit and every Dependabot run, which is exactly the fate a recorded decision should settle once.

**Consequences.** D-125's "open maintenance question" is answered and D-127's unregistered-pin comment updated: `src/server/http.ts` (docblock), `src/server/README.md`, and `src/services/README.md` now state the removal where they stated the deferral; the construction suite (`test/integration/server-http.spec.ts`) pins the new state. Re-adding the package for a future per-request limiting need is a successor decision that must register it with an explicit justified scope (answering this entry's (a)–(c) against the then-current spec text) and amend the declaration pin, the registration pin's comment, and this entry's references. No code imports the package (verified by grep and by typecheck passing against an uninstalling `npm ci`), no plugin registers it (the kept pin), and nothing in the public npm-package contract changes — the dependency set of a not-yet-published package, with `check:package`'s tarball allowlist unaffected by a dependency removal. The spec's §3 row stands as written and now disagrees with the manifest on this one entry — the deliberate, recorded deviation above; a future spec revision should drop the row so they agree again. `CHANGELOG.md` carries the boundary.

## D-144 — Task 163's OpenAPI publication: the schemas-as-single-source over a literal route inventory, the booted-scope drift guard in the unit project, OpenAPI 3.1.0/2020-12 at `docs/openapi.json`, and error statuses derived from the registry (spec §13, §18; task 163)

**Date:** 2026-11-04 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§13](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#13-http-api), [§18](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#18-documentation-deliverables) · **Tasks:** [163](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-113 (the error registry the document's error responses derive from — code → status + default message + the closed envelope schema, so the vocabulary cannot fork), D-128/D-130/D-139/D-142 (the wire contracts the document projects), D-117 (the §15.3 mutation header documented as a required parameter on exactly the state-changing methods, named from the owning constant), D-126 (the session-cookie name imported from `SESSION_COOKIE_NAME` for the security scheme), D-015 (the `generate-schema.mjs` generation precedent this task scales from one document to the API surface), D-093 (the drift-guard spirit — a structural spec failing `make check` on inventory drift), D-111 (the schemas-layer home whose exports are the single source of truth)

**Decision.** Task 163 publishes the API description as `docs/openapi.json` (presented by `docs/api.md`), generated by `npm run openapi:generate` / `make openapi` from two modules following the D-015 pattern: `scripts/openapi-document.mjs` — the builder, pure data, no filesystem — and `scripts/generate-openapi.mjs`, the `OPENAPI_DIR`-aware writer (default `docs` on the host, `/var/lib/quotameter/openapi` in the container; `make openapi` generates into the volume and streams the file back, the uid-invariant `make schema` recipe). Five interpretations are pinned. (Correction trail: the task's review round — deepseek-v4.1-flash, one round, APPROVE with 5 P2 / 7 P3 — is folded into this entry, which had not landed when corrected — the house precedent. Ten findings were accepted and fixed in the same commit: `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` joined the body-carrying mutations' code sets, the exact-description registry enforcement and the base-set derivations below, the `Required<ApiRoutesOptions>` future-family pin, the defaulted-property publication rule below, the release-checklist regeneration step (`docs/release.md` — `info.version` reads `package.json`, so a version bump without regeneration fails the freshness arm), the root-security pins, the `\\S` pattern on the documented mutation-header value, `STATE_CHANGING_METHODS` imported instead of duplicated, the duplicate-`(method, path)` build rejection, and the builder's own unit spec for the rejection arms. One P3 idea was declined with reasons in the commit body: `$ref`-deduplicating the error envelope — inline embedding was the deliberate choice, the reassembly comparison pins direct objects, and duplication in a generated artifact costs nothing semantically.) (1) **The schemas are the single source of truth; the route inventory is literal and guarded.** Runtime route introspection was examined and rejected as the generator's base: fastify 5 exposes no public route table (`fastify.routes`/`router` are gone; `findRoute` returns no schemas), and — decisively — route options carry none of the operation metadata an API reference exists to publish (summaries, tags, per-route error codes, publicness). So the builder holds a hand-maintained inventory of exactly those facts, while every SCHEMA in the document is wired by importing the actual `src/schemas/api/*` exports through jiti — the embedded request/response/parameter schemas are the JSON projections of the validation contracts by identity, §13's "generate OpenAPI from the same schema definitions used for request validation" read literally — and the error responses, the mutation-header name and method set, and the cookie name are likewise imported from their owning modules (the registry, `API_MUTATION_HEADER_NAME`, `STATE_CHANGING_METHODS`, `SESSION_COOKIE_NAME`). The inventory's drift risk is closed executably (interpretation 3), the same shape as D-093's coverage-map guard. (2) **The artifact is OpenAPI 3.1.0 with the draft-2020-12 dialect**, because TypeBox emits 2020-12 JSON Schema and 3.1 schema objects ARE 2020-12 — the projections embed verbatim, with no `nullable` re-writing and no second schema language to drift (3.0 would force a translation layer over exactly the contracts the routes compile); placement is `docs/openapi.json` because §18 lists the deliverable as documentation (the npm-package publication of the reference stays task 192's carve-out — the artifact and generator only). `info.version` tracks `package.json`'s version, so releases restamp the document by regeneration — and `docs/release.md`'s checklist names that regeneration step, because the freshness arm fails CI on a bump that skips it. (3) **The drift guard boots the real scope in the unit project.** `test/unit/openapi-published.spec.ts` registers the production `apiRoutes` on a bare fastify instance whose injected seams THROW if called — plugin bodies only wire routes at registration, proven by the guard booting green — collects every route through the `onRoute` hook (the one public introspection surface that still exposes method/prefixed-url/`schema`/`config` on the pinned runtime), and fails on: a stale artifact (committed ≠ builder), an undocumented route, a documented-but-missing route (fastify's auto HEAD twins and the `/api/*` catch-all are excluded by named rule — a transport artifact and an error handler, not operations — with a structural pin that both still exist so the exclusions cannot swallow a restructure), a schema mismatch (the document's path/query parameters are re-assembled and deep-compared against the documented equivalent of the live routes' `params`/`querystring` schemas; `requestBody` and success responses likewise — a route re-wired to a different contract fails even when method and path still match), a publicness mismatch (the live `route.config.auth === 'public'` set vs the document's `security: []` overrides — health is the one, §13), a mutation-header mismatch (§15.3's `STATE_CHANGING_METHODS` exactly), a non-serializer response that is not an EXACT registry entry (description, status, and the closed `ApiErrorBodySchema` body — an invented or mis-mapped description fails), a missing construction-guaranteed base code (VALIDATION/INTERNAL/FORBIDDEN everywhere, UNAUTHENTICATED everywhere but the public route), or a missing root security requirement (the global `sessionCookie` scheme over D-126's constant — without this pin, deleting the root requirement while keeping the per-operation overrides would publish an effectively unauthenticated reference that passed every other arm). The wired families satisfy `Required<Omit<ApiRoutesOptions, 'auth'>>` — the future-family pin: a new optional family (U-041's auth routes) left unwired in the guard fails typecheck there, so it can never be silently invisible to every arm. The builder's own rejection arms (duplicate `operationId`, duplicate `(method, path)` — which would silently overwrite — unknown registry code, two codes on one status) are driven by `test/unit/openapi-document.spec.ts` over injected inventories (`buildOpenApiDocument(operations)` defaults to the committed one for production callers). All four guard drift directions were proven live on scratch mutations of the artifact (a phantom path, a deleted path, a mutated body schema, a dropped security override — each failing with its arm's own message), then restored. (4) **Error responses are inventory-listed registry codes, not per-route guesses.** Each inventory entry names its codes; the builder maps them through the registry (unknown code → build-time throw; status collisions → build-time throw) with the registry's default leak-free message as the description, and the base sets encode what the construction guarantees scope-wide: VALIDATION and INTERNAL everywhere, UNAUTHENTICATED everywhere but health (the §15.1 guard, opted out by route config), FORBIDDEN everywhere (the §15.3 Host/Origin/header guards run for every route in the scope), NOT_FOUND where the handler throws it, PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE and UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE on the body-carrying mutations (§15.5's 64 KiB body limit, and D-117's content-type leg binding body-carrying requests — the bodiless DELETE and connection test deliberately document neither: a body is not part of their contract, and both limit and content-type rules travel with one; a client that sends a body anyway still meets the envelope, which the §15.3 documentation states generally). (5) **Parameters are exploded, not blobbed**: each params/querystring object schema becomes one OpenAPI parameter per property, carrying the TypeBox property node's projection (constraints and descriptions included) and `required` membership — so tooling shows real per-parameter validation, and the reassembly comparison of interpretation 3 is the exact inverse of the explosion. One publication rule refines `required`: **a property that declares a `default` is documented optional**, because the validator compiles with `useDefaults: true` and materializes it when omitted — the wire truth (pinned end-to-end by the history suite's default-budget test) that the TypeBox `required` list overstates for `maxPoints`. The rule lives in the builder and is mirrored by the guard's `documentedEquivalent`, so the pair is checked against each other on every `make check`; the root cause (the schema property not being `Type.Optional`) is a `src/schemas/api/history.ts` change outside this task's carve-out, recorded here for its owning successor — when it lands, the rule becomes a no-op for that property and nothing else changes.

**Reasons.** §13 demands the description come from the same definitions the server validates through, but an OpenAPI document is more than schemas — it is operation metadata no runtime artifact carries, so SOME hand-maintained surface is unavoidable; the design choice is whether that surface can lie. The literal inventory plus the booted-scope guard makes every lie fail `make check`: adding a route without documenting it, removing one and leaving the documentation, re-wiring a contract, or changing the security model all break a named assertion (proven on the four scratch arms), which is the D-093 property transplanted to the API surface. Deriving error statuses from the registry rather than duplicating `{status, description}` pairs keeps D-113's one-vocabulary rule intact through the publication boundary — a new error class joins the document by joining the registry, never by editing JSON. The unit-project placement of the guard is deliberate: the boot touches no sockets and no SQLite (the seams throw, the handlers never run), so the guard is fast and hermetic while still executing the production plugin registrations — and it must run in `make check`, not an integration lane, to be the gate the task asks for. The freshness arm makes hand-edits of the artifact pointless (the committed file must byte-match the builder), which is why the guard's other arms compare the committed document against live truth rather than trusting the builder as an intermediary. Reading the committed file with `node:fs` instead of the sibling spec's typed JSON import is a measured deviation: at ~290 KB (34× the config schema) the inferred literal type would tax every typecheck for zero benefit, since the guard compares parsed data, never the inferred shape.

**Consequences.** Every future §13 route change (U-041's auth endpoints above all) must update `scripts/openapi-document.mjs` and regenerate in the same commit — the undocumented-route arm and the `Required<ApiRoutesOptions>` typecheck pin enforce it mechanically; the auth family will also want a `sessionCookie`-bearing login flow description and possibly a new security-scheme note, a successor's ordinary inventory work. A new error class (D-113's coordinated path) appears in the document by adding the code to the registry and the affected inventory lists. Schema changes require only regeneration (`make openapi`) — the freshness arm catches forgetfulness, and releases must regenerate after the version bump (`docs/release.md` names the step). Task 192 (Stage 14) decides how the reference reaches the npm package (`files` entry, bundled viewer, or repository link) without re-deciding anything here; the document's `info.version` will follow the release version automatically. The exported surface (`buildOpenApiDocument` in `scripts/openapi-document.mjs`, typed for consumers by `scripts/openapi-document.d.mts`) is generator surface, not package surface; the `.d.mts` declares the one export the drift guard consumes. Known residuals, recorded: the inventory's operation prose (summaries/descriptions) and its per-route HANDLER-thrown classes (which of NOT_FOUND/415/413 a route answers) are inventory-trusted judgment — the guard proves the documented set is registry-exact and construction-guaranteed-complete, but cannot execute handlers to prove semantic completeness (that is task 164's integration lane); the `maxPoints` `Type.Optional` schema-side fix (interpretation 5's root cause) belongs to a successor; and `servers` is the same-origin relative form (`/`), deferring any absolute-URL example to the deployment documentation that owns host/port facts (§15.6).

## D-145 — Task 164's cross-endpoint sweep suites: the production composition as the test harness (D-140's construction driven by `fastify.inject`, only the provider adapter doubled), the coverage-matrix boundary that leaves per-route domain contracts to the per-family suites, and the interpretation calls the sweeps surfaced (§7.4's exact-occurrence marker, the schedule-dependent span cap, the U-041 404 boundary) (spec §13, §15, §17.1; task 164)

**Date:** 2026-11-04 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§13](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#13-http-api), [§15](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#15-security), [§17.1](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#171-required-test-coverage) · **Tasks:** [164](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-140 (the composition root whose `composeApplication()` is the harness — "an integration test through the production construction, not test doubles, against a temp config + SQLite" is this suite's shape, generalized), D-121 (the §15.1 guard whose fail-closed `isAuthenticated`-absent arm the sweeps pin across every endpoint as it behaves today), D-113/D-115/D-117/D-120 (the error registry and the three §15.3 guards whose binding the sweeps prove per-route, not per-catch-all), D-127 (the §15.5 header set, asserted with the same byte literal `security-headers.spec.ts` pins), D-128 (the mask/boolean contract pinned positively), D-139/D-142 (the range grammar arms the error sweep rides), D-134 (the D-113/D-121 UNAUTHENTICATED notice seam U-041 will activate), D-094/D-087 (the timeout discipline for the lifecycle-bearing tests), D-097 (the naming rule that keeps the sweeps outside the `test:time` filter vocabulary)

**Decision.** Task 164 lands the §17.1 "API" row's cross-endpoint half as four sweep specs plus one shared harness, and pins four interpretations. (1) **The harness is the production composition** — `startComposedApi`/`withComposedApi` in the new `test/helpers/composedApi.ts` wrap `composeApplication()` over fresh temp directories (config written through the atomic `writeConfigFile`, permissions enforced by the composition itself, the §5.6 lifecycle driven through `QuotameterApp`), so every sweep request traverses the real `/api` scope, the real guards, the real config file, and a real migrated SQLite database; the only double is the provider adapter (the external boundary the no-network guard requires tests to own, registered through the production `observingManualTests` wrapper — the composition.spec precedent verbatim). The alternative — bare `buildHttpServer` options with hand-built route blocks, the per-family shape — was rejected for this suite's purpose: the per-family suites already own that construction's coverage per route, the unique cross-endpoint value is proving the §15 defenses and the §13 envelope bind the routes AS `runServer` WIRES THEM (all families at once, the real stores, the real auth projection), and the composition choice satisfies §17.1's "every endpoint through `fastify.inject` using a real temporary `node:sqlite` database" by construction. Lifecycles are shared per describe (`beforeAll`/`afterAll`, explicit hook timeouts) for READ-ONLY requests only — guard rejections mutate nothing — while every mutating test (the contract sweep's five happy-path mutations, the secrets sweep's key rotation and env-key arms) owns its dedicated lifecycle, so no test can read state another test wrote; the property is executable (the suites pass under `--sequence.shuffle`), and a dedicated lifecycle exists besides where a different auth cell demands one. (2) **The coverage-matrix boundary is deliberate** — the sweeps close what no per-family suite pins (guards × every real route across families; §15.1 × every endpoint through the production construction — peak-hours had NO §15.1 pin; §15.5 headers on the endpoints' success and error responses; the 64 KiB limit on real routes incl. the at-boundary cell; one envelope-conformity table over every reachable class; the multi-marker secret sweep with stored-state positive controls) and leave to the per-family suites: per-route domain contracts (downsampling, retention/DST timelines, §7.3 derivation, purge evidence, settings refusals), INTERNAL escalation via store doubles (unreachable through a healthy production composition by design), the full §15.1 bind×mode cell matrix and startup refusals (api-auth-mode, bare construction), guard verdict byte-pins and header-value edge cases, the raw-wire Host arms (absolute form/duplicate/missing — inject cannot express them), and composition store/sync/suspension behaviors (composition.spec). (3) **The auth surface covered is §15.1 as it behaves today**: `auth.mode: 'required'` + a configured hash answers the D-113/D-121 UNAUTHENTICATED envelope on every protected endpoint — the composition passes no `isAuthenticated` (the login endpoints are U-041's to build), so nothing can satisfy the demand and the fail-closed arm IS the contract this task can pin; the hash is a marker-shaped placeholder (the guard reads presence only; verification meets a password at the login endpoint), and the pin's header comment names U-041 as the successor that will re-pin the authenticated arm. The unbuilt `/api/auth/login`, `/api/auth/logout`, and `/api/auth/session` are pinned at today's boundary — the catch-all 404 envelope, with the POSTs needing the full §15.3 client shape to reach it (the guards bind unbuilt paths too). (4) **The interpretation calls the sweeps surfaced, recorded**: (a) §7.4's server-side redaction is EXACT-OCCURRENCE over the account's resolved key inside provider-sourced stored text — an arbitrary error message is not redacted (it is the §13 "last error" data the spec requires on the wire), so the marker method embeds the key in the stored plan name and error message and asserts the `[REDACTED]` rendering on every endpoint that serves the stored text (`/api/quota`, `/api/events`, `/api/status`), beside the never-on-the-wire scans (the accounts surface's `planName` is excluded — null by construction today; see Consequences); (b) the peak-hours span cap (D-142's `range-too-wide`) is reachable only with a CONFIGURED schedule — the no-schedule arm computes nothing and answers 200 — and only through a far-FUTURE `to` (retention clamps `from`, never `to`, D-082): a sweep that misses either fact asserts a 200 where it expects a 400; (c) the body-limit boundary: a body of EXACTLY 64 KiB passes the transport and is judged by the schema (the sweeps prove a padded unknown field answers VALIDATION, not 413), and the over-bound 413 case must carry the full legitimate mutation headers because the §15.3 guards run ahead of the body parser — a headerless oversized body answers 403, never 413 (the D-117 ordering, now pinned on a real route).

**Reasons.** The task's done-condition ("schemas, auth, validation, error envelopes, secret masking, and CSRF defenses are covered") was already 90% covered, spread across thirteen per-family suites — each pinning its own route's contract against store doubles and its own slice of the guard tables against the catch-all. Re-proving any of that would be duplication; the genuine gaps were all CROSS-endpoint: no suite proves the guards bind EVERY real route (only the accounts and settings families had per-route guard pins), no suite proves the §15.1 verdicts through the production construction (where the fail-closed seam is the composition's deliberate design), peak-hours had no auth pin at all, the §15.5 header set was pinned on health/404/401 but not the resource endpoints' successes, the 413 class had never been produced by a real route, and no single marker sweep covered every echoing endpoint with positive controls proving non-vacuity. The composition harness answers all of them with one construction, and its cost is one real lifecycle per describe (~0.4 s measured — migrations on temp SQLite), well inside the D-094 timeout discipline: the two tests that compose an extra lifecycle in-test measure ~0.34 s clean and carry explicit 10 s timeouts; the shared hooks carry 30–60 s. Naming: the `api-sweep-*` prefix keeps the files outside the `test:time` substring filter's vocabulary (D-097's documented blind spot — a spec named after a time/peak-hours module would silently join the TZ matrix's nine-fold cost).

**Consequences.** The exported surface is test-only (`test/helpers/composedApi.ts`: `startComposedApi`, `withComposedApi`, the assertion helpers, the cycle seeders, `paddedJsonOfExactLength`; four `test/integration/api-sweep-*.spec.ts` files, 51 tests total) — no `src/` change, no public API change; future sweep-style suites (U-041's endpoint contract tests, 183's acceptance) reuse the harness rather than re-deriving the composition lifecycle. U-041 inherits three recorded obligations: re-pin the authenticated arm (its `isAuthenticated` wiring flips the required-mode sweep's 401 expectation — the suites' header comments name it), the login route's public-config exemption (D-121's `PUBLIC_AUTH_ROUTE_CONFIG`), and the marker-secret test D-125/D-126 documented for the login endpoint. Two exclusions the sweep records for its successors: the accounts surface's `planName` field is `null` by construction in this composition (no `src/` writer populates the row's `plan_name` column today; when the polling composition lands one, the §7.4 exact-occurrence redaction must join it there as it already does on `/api/quota` and `/api/status` — otherwise the embedded-key scan extends to a failing pin), and the harness MIRRORS the composition's `startupSecrets` registration into its injected logger (capturing records in a sink requires injecting one, which bypasses the production arm — the mirror is documented in the helper and D-140's own branch stays exercised only by production runs; a logger-construction seam in `composeApplication` would remove the mirror and is noted as a maintenance option). Known residual, recorded: the sweeps share lifecycles across read-only tests for runtime economy (order independence holds — verified under `--sequence.shuffle`, and every mutating test owns its lifecycle), so an isolation-minded debug run still has the per-family suites' per-test property. `CHANGELOG.md` carries the boundary; `plan/tasks.md` untouched (the main session's flip, per the cycle's dual-mode rule). (Correction trail: the task's review round — deepseek-v4.1-flash, one round, REQUEST_CHANGES with 0 P0/P1, 7 P2, 3 P3 — folded in before landing: the mutating tests moved off the shared lifecycles (the P2 order-dependence — the suites now pass under `--sequence.shuffle`, the property their docblocks had claimed), the §15.1/Host inventories gained the three mutation routes and the public-health Host arm, the §15.5 header matrix gained the five mutation successes and the 414 class (the helper's docblock now names `security-headers.spec.ts` as the owner of the complete header-name allowlist tripwire), the key-rotation marker gained its own lifecycle with an entry-specific positive control (the file-wide assertion had been satisfiable by another test's data), the harness mirrors the startup-secret registration and the log scan gained its non-empty positive control, the headerless-oversized-body 403 pin landed (the ordering D-145 had claimed in prose), the accounts-`planName` exclusion and the marker-inventory wording were corrected, and the helper learned to clean up its temp directory when composition fails. One P2 resolution recorded rather than implemented: seeding the accounts row's `plan_name` to prove the §7.4 redaction on `/api/accounts` would fail today — `accountView` serves the column unredacted, D-130's own residual class — so the sweep documents the exclusion and the product fix (redact `planName` in `accountView`, mirroring `/api/quota`) belongs to the endpoint's owner, reported to the main session.)

## D-146 — Task U-041's login/logout endpoints: D-125's composition order held by per-source mutual exclusion over `request.ip` with the slept delay clamped to the transport's socket bound, the delays invisible on the wire, D-126's refreshed-sighting open point resolved as no-re-issue behind the unchanged `(request) => boolean` seam, login's 401 as the registry-default `UNAUTHENTICATED`, and logout session-bound and idempotent (spec §13, §15.2, §15.1, §14.6, §15.4; task U-041)

**Date:** 2026-11-04 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§15.2](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#152-passwords-and-sessions), [§13](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#13-http-api), [§15.1](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#151-network-and-authentication-modes), [§14.6](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#146-statuses-and-authentication-screens), [§15.4](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#154-secret-protection) · **Tasks:** [U-041](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-122/D-123/D-124 (the §15.2 primitives the login handler composes verbatim — verify, mint, verdict/revocation — whose consequences each named this endpoint), D-125 (the budget's composition order and the per-source serialization this task executes, plus the endpoint-owned `warn` contract), D-126 (the cookie attribute twins and the refreshed-sighting open point resolved below), D-109 (the connection-timeout bound the delay clamp answers to), D-121 (the §15.1 seam consumed unchanged and the `PUBLIC_AUTH_ROUTE_CONFIG` opt-out login takes), D-113 (the frozen error registry the 401 rides), D-134 (the UI notice branch whose `UNAUTHENTICATED` signal the wire now proves), D-140 (the composition root wired with the sessions-backed `isAuthenticated` it had recorded as unwired), D-144 (the OpenAPI drift guard whose `Required<ApiRoutesOptions>` pin mechanically forced this task's inventory update)

**Decision.** Task U-041 lands the plan gap D-125/D-126 recorded — `src/server/api/auth-routes.ts` registers `POST /api/auth/login` and `POST /api/auth/logout` inside the `/api` scope behind `ApiRoutesOptions.authRoutes` (the D-128 optional-options rule; absent, both paths answer the catch-all 404), with the wire contracts in `src/schemas/api/auth.ts`, and pins seven interpretations. (Correction trail: the task's review round — deepseek-v4.1-flash, one round, REQUEST_CHANGES with 2 P1 / 2 P2 / 3 P3 — folded in before landing (the D-119/D-122 precedent). The P1s reshaped interpretation (1): the first design queued same-source attempts on a promise chain, which made the per-connection hold UNBOUNDED (queue wait plus the delay — a queued request could idle past the construction's socket-inactivity bound from the waiting position alone) and left the queue an unbounded memory lever over the public endpoint, and the delay timer was referenced, holding the process open past §5.6's bounded shutdown after the listener closed. The resolution — per-source mutual exclusion plus a transport-safe clamp on the slept delay plus an unref'd timer — is recorded in (1) and (2) below. The P2s hardened the tests (the marker scan now covers the ATTEMPTED candidate, the warn record's key set is pinned exactly, and the registry-default 401 message is asserted); the P3s corrected the passwordless-proxy docblock claim, the published "every non-health operation" wording, and a member count.) (1) **Login's composition is D-125's documented order, held under concurrency by per-source MUTUAL EXCLUSION.** One attempt runs `delayBeforeAttempt(source, now)` → sleep-if-delayed → `verifyPassword` → `recordAttempt`, and at most one attempt per source is in that section at any moment: a same-source request arriving while another is in flight is answered immediately with the same 401 class under `details.reason: 'source-busy'` — without verifying anything and without recording anything (no guess evaluated, no budget consumed, the wire shape stays a failed login, and its own single credential-free `warn` with `outcome: 'source-busy'` is the operator's flood signal). This is the cadence hold D-125's consequences assigned the endpoint ("serializing per source") in its strictest form: the check-then-record window D-125 warned about is structurally impossible when the second attempt cannot enter, the processed-attempt rate is at or below the serialized ideal, and the busy map holds at most one entry per active source — neither a queue nor memory can grow with hostile traffic. (2) **The slept delay is clamped below the transport's socket-inactivity bound, and the timer never holds the process open.** D-125's curve reaches 512 s at the thirteenth in-window failure and caps at the 15-minute window, while the construction destroys an idle socket after `HTTP_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT_MS` (300 s — D-109's own docblock: the bound "must comfortably exceed the longest legitimate silent handler", and a login inside its delay is exactly that): an unclamped sleep would be answered by a connection reset, not the slow answer §15.2 demands. The endpoint therefore sleeps `min(delay, MAX_LOGIN_DELAY_SLEEP_MS)` — 240 s, comfortably inside the bound with the scrypt to follow, pinned against it by a unit relation test so the two constants cannot drift apart — a clamp that only binds where D-125's curve exceeds it (every spec-level delay, 1 s doubling through 256 s, sleeps unchanged), keeps the delays increasing (§15.2's own word), stays inside D-125's window-length cap rationale, and tightens the throttle fail-closed; the budget's arithmetic is untouched. The default sleep unrefs its `setTimeout` (pinned by a `hasRef()` probe): `runServer` drains the event loop instead of exiting, so a referenced timer would linger up to the full clamp past §5.6's bounded shutdown — unref'd, the closed server's loop drains while the sleeping handler simply never completes its response (its socket was force-destroyed by the bounded close anyway). (3) **The source key is `request.ip`** — socket-derived and header-unforgeable because `trustProxy` is never enabled (D-109), opaque per D-125; behind §15.6's reverse proxy every client shares the proxy's address, the shared-source reality whose lockout lever D-125's delays-never-rejections choice already rejected — the busy arm is the same trade again: a flooded shared source answers fast non-verifying 401s while its processed cadence stays throttled, never a lockout. (4) **Failed attempts answer the registry-default `UNAUTHENTICATED` 401 with `details.reason: 'invalid-credentials'`** — the code the D-134 notice branch intercepts (the wrong-password 401 and the mode guard's demand share the class deliberately: both mean "present credentials"), the registry's own message rides it (no override, keeping the D-144 document's registry-derived descriptions exact), and §15.2's logging sentence executes as exactly one credential-free `warn` (`{ source, outcome: 'failure' }`, the key set pinned exactly) — never the candidate password, the stored hash, or any token. A passwordless configuration takes the same arm: `verifyPassword(undefined, …)` is `false` by D-122's totality guard — the reachable shape is `auto` + direct loopback (every passwordless remote shape refuses at startup; a proxied passwordless request against a PROTECTED route answers the §15.1 layer's 403 before any handler), while login itself, being public, deliberately takes the 401. (5) **Logout is session-bound, bodiless, and idempotent.** No public opt-out (under `required` a cookieless or dead-cookie logout answers 401 before the handler — the never-issued clear costs one dead client cookie until its `Max-Age`, D-126's documented hygiene lag; under `auto` it is always reachable), only the §15.3 mutation header (the bodiless D-117 rule), `revokeSession` + `clearSessionCookieAttributes` verbatim, and `{ revoked }` — the honest distinction between "a row was deleted" and "nothing to delete" — with the clear twin sent either way.
