(6) **D-126's refreshed-sighting open point is resolved as NO re-issue.** The §15.1 seam stays D-121's `(request) => boolean`; the wiring is D-124's predicted one-lambda composition as a named factory (`createSessionAuthenticator({ repository, now })`, in the route module so the composition root stays a one-line call; a missing or empty cookie answers `false` without a storage read), which cannot see the reply — so every valid sighting refreshes the ROW (D-124's `touchSession`) while the COOKIE keeps its mint-time `Max-Age` (7 days): an active owner re-logs-in at most weekly, the orphaned row self-expires within the 30-day cap, and the verdict stays the sole security boundary. The alignment-preserving alternative (the seam seeing `reply`, or an onSend re-issue hook) is the named successor path if the UX ever demands it. (7) **The success bodies are minimal and epoch-ms, and the stored hash is a live thunk.** Login 200 `{ session: { expiresAt } }` (the row's effective expiry — the integer the cookie's `Max-Age` mirrors, the D-139/D-142 one-format-per-direction rule), logout 200 `{ revoked }`, both handlers adding the family's per-route `no-store`; a login while already holding a session mints a fresh one (the old row is inert and self-expires), no implicit re-login revocation; `passwordHash(): string | undefined` is read per attempt — §6.4/D-026 classify it live, so a `passwd` run or a settings PUT applies to the next login without a restart, the same per-request-thunk shape the §15.1 guard's `passwordConfigured` takes, implemented by the composition over the reloader's effective configuration.

**Reasons.** Every open point had a landed constraint that made one answer the composition of record rather than a new choice: the budget's order and its "delays, never rejections" wire-invisibility are D-125's own text; the exclusion and the clamp are the two colliding invariants reconciled — D-125's curve against D-109's documented socket bound (an unclamped sleep is a reset, a queued sleep is a reset, and neither is the slow answer the spec demands) — with the busy arm chosen over a bounded queue because one in-flight attempt plus fast non-verifying 401s preserves everything D-125 wanted (eventual access, throttled cadence, no lockout) while making the per-connection hold a provable constant; the unref'd timer follows §5.6's drain-don't-exit rule directly. The 401's registry-default message follows from D-144's exact-description enforcement (an override would publish a description the document cannot derive); the passwordless 401 is D-122's totality guard executing as designed; logout's session-boundness follows from D-121's opt-out being a route's own declaration (logout has no credential-free reason to exist — its entire purpose is the session) while its idempotence is D-124's `unknown`-only aftermath; and the no-re-issue resolution keeps the seam D-121 staked and D-124 predicted, trading a weekly re-login for the smallest wiring surface — the re-issue alternative would widen the §15.1 seam's signature (a public-contract change) or add a second cookie-writing path, both disproportionate to a UX nicety the single-user deployment tolerates. The `request.ip` source key needs no new trust decision: the construction already refuses `trustProxy`, so the address is the socket's own fact.

**Consequences.** The four §15.2 primitives are composed end to end: the composition root (D-140) wires `createSessionAuthenticator` over the lazy repository and the shared clock — closing the deliberately-unwired seam its module header recorded — beside the `authRoutes` block, so a `required`-mode production deployment authenticates from the first start (pinned through the real construction: login → protected 200 → logout → 401). The D-144 drift guard update was mechanically forced exactly as its consequences named: both operations joined `scripts/openapi-document.mjs` (login public with the body-carrying mutations' 413/415 set and `UNAUTHENTICATED` beside the public base; logout session-bound and bodiless), the `auth` tag landed, `docs/openapi.json` regenerated, and the guard's `Required<Omit<ApiRoutesOptions, 'auth'>>` boot wires the new family to refusing seams. `GET /api/auth/session` (§13's third auth row) stays unwired: task 180's UI consumer owns its design, and this module's registration seam is where it joins. The unwired construction's behavior is unchanged (the fail-closed default `isAuthenticated` still answers false), so no existing suite needed adjustment. The exported surface (`AuthRouteOptions`, `authRoutes`, `createSessionAuthenticator`, `sessionCookieTransportOf`, `MAX_LOGIN_DELAY_SLEEP_MS`, `defaultSleep` in `src/server/api/auth-routes.ts`; the three schemas and their Static types in `src/schemas/api/auth.ts`) is internal API under `src/`, not package surface; changing the login/logout bodies, the delay's wire-invisibility, the clamp/exclusion semantics, the no-re-issue resolution, or the seam factory's contract requires a successor decision. The done-condition is pinned executably three ways: `test/unit/auth-routes.spec.ts` (the authenticator's arms — missing/empty-cookie storage-call-freedom, verdict mapping, the exact refresh write — the D-126 transport resolution, the clamp-to-connection-bound relation, and the unref'd-timer probe), `test/integration/auth-routes.spec.ts` (the exact cookie attributes on both HTTP and proxied-HTTPS legs, digest-only storage with the whole-database raw-token scan, the credential-free single `warn` with its key set pinned and BOTH markers (the correct password and the attempted candidate) absent from every body and log line, the registry-default 401 message, every §13/§15.3 error arm incl. the construction-limit 413, the live-hash flip, the full §15.1 matrix with the `UNAUTHENTICATED` code as the D-134 signal, the no-re-issue pin — the row slides while no `Set-Cookie` appears, and the fake-clock budget: five undelayed failures, the doubling sequence, the transport-safe clamp, the over-budget success that still logs in after paying its delay, the half-open window release, the success reset, per-source isolation, and the exclusion proof — a gated sleep parks the in-flight attempt while a same-source newcomer answers `source-busy` without sleeping, verifying, or recording, the post-release delay proving the budget state), and `test/integration/composition-auth.spec.ts` (the production-construction proof over temp config + SQLite). A UI password-change flow, the settings-PUT revocation's interaction with live sessions beyond D-124's semantics, and any `Retry-After`-style politeness channel all remain their owning tasks' calls.

## D-147 — Task 174's rolling-range controls: the retention source and strict-excess disabling semantics, the no-zone boundary rule (D-068 mirrored client-side), the radio group with per-option text explanations, page-local range state, and the history/events client arms the page wires range-keyed (spec §14.4, §14.1, §10, §13, §11.3; task 174)

**Date:** 2026-11-04 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§14.4](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#144-history-charts), [§14.1](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#141-general-ui-requirements), [§10](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#10-time-and-time-zones), [§13](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#13-http-api), [§11.3](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#113-retention-and-cleanup) · **Tasks:** [174](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-139 (the history/events wire grammar the client arms consume — ISO-with-offset request boundaries, epoch-ms responses, the 200-with-report that stays the server-side authority; its consequences named these UI additions 174's job and `healthyApiBody`'s new arms), D-068 (the server-side rolling-range pin this task mirrors client-side: the closed five-id vocabulary, the exact absolute-duration bounds), D-134 (the typed client whose pattern the two new families follow, and the UI-local-constant-pinned-by-test precedent the vocabulary reuses), D-137 (the seam between the identity card and the metrics region, the first quota metric vocabulary, and the refresh affordance handed to 174), D-138 (the empty-state interplay — the range control renders whenever an account is selected, data or not), D-133 (the token-only color rule the control follows; UA radios theme through `color-scheme`), D-132 (the static-key catalog discipline the option labels follow), D-130 (the settings view that exposes retention as an annotated scalar)

**Decision.** Task 174 lands the §14.4 range filters on the overview and pins six interpretations. (Correction trail: the task's review round — deepseek-v4.1-flash, one round, REQUEST_CHANGES with 1 P1 / 8 P3 — was folded in before landing: the **P1** — the a11y suite's route-interception cells answered the newly-wired `/api/events` load with the 404 envelope, deterministically failing the attention cell's no-`api-error` assertion under `make check-all`'s e2e leg — was fixed by standing healthy history/events bodies in `fulfillOverviewBody` (the same helpers the component suites use); the exhaustive-`never` label arm, the fallback's polite live-region announcement, the healthy-per-route catch-alls in the stale component fixtures, the retention-7 axe-scanned e2e cell, and the load-count wording entered with the same round, and its two accepted trade-offs are recorded in Consequences.) (1) **The retention source and disabling semantics.** Retention is the settings view the page already loads for its display time zone — §13's annotated `app.historyRetentionDays.value`, read per page load — not a new endpoint and not the range report (the report is per-request output, wrong-shaped for pre-flight affordance gating). A range is disabled when its exact duration **strictly exceeds** the retention (`durationMs > retentionDays × 86 400 000`): §14.4's own word is "exceed", so an exactly-equal range stays selectable — the equality cell that keeps the §14.4 default (7 days) selectable at §11.3's accepted minimum (7 days); the other equality cells (14d under 14, 30d under 30) follow the same rule. While retention is **unknown** (`null`: the settings load is pending or has failed) nothing is disabled — an unknown fact asserts nothing, the disabling is a pre-flight affordance convenience, and the server's own D-139 range report (`truncated`/`rejected`) remains the authority on what is actually queryable. A selection that becomes disabled once retention arrives (the late-settings window, or a future live retention reduction) reverts to the §14.4 default via a watcher — always selectable by the equality rule above, never a silently out-of-policy request the server would truncate. (2) **No zone anchors a boundary — the task brief's open question, closed by reading §10/§14.4/D-068 together.** §10 defines "last N hours/days" as a rolling interval ending now with explicit `from`/`to` bounds; D-068 pinned the server-side reading as pure absolute-duration epoch-ms arithmetic with **no calendar or DST wall-clock component**; §14.4's display-zone sentences are all axis/tick/tooltip presentation. So the client computes `to = now`, `from = now − duration` (D-068's closed interval) with **no time-zone input at all** — the configured display zone never participates in a request (§10: presentation only) — and serializes through `toISOString()`, which always emits ISO-8601 UTC with the explicit `Z` designator D-139's request grammar (the server's strict `epochMsFromIso` offset gate) requires. The bounds are recomputed **on every dispatch** (a rolling range ends "now": a range switch or refresh re-anchors, a stale pair is a lie about the window). (3) **The control is a radio group, and the explanation is per-option real text.** `HistoryRangeControls.vue` renders a fieldset + legend with five native radios sharing one `name`: keyboard support is native (Tab reaches the group, arrows move the selection — no script handles keys, the semantics do), and each disabled option carries its sentence ("Exceeds the {days}-day history retention", the configured retention named) **inside its own label** — §14.4's "explain why" met as text beside the disabled state, §14.1's never-color-alone rule met structurally (the disabled attribute and the sentence are the signal; color and italic styling only supplement). A `<select>` was rejected: disabled options in a closed list cannot carry per-option explanations, which the done-condition demands. (4) **The range's state is page-local.** A `ref` in `OverviewView` defaulting to `7d` — no persistence, no store: §14.4 names no persistence for the range, and unlike the account id (cross-page identity, D-135's store) it is a query parameter of one page's history surface. (5) **The vocabulary is UI-local and drift-pinned.** `ui/src/history-range.ts` redeclares the five ids, their exact durations, the default, **and the id union itself** — nothing crosses from `src/**` at all: the layout contract (pinned by `test/unit/package-layout.spec.ts`) keeps ui imports of server code to type-only `src/schemas/**`, and this vocabulary lives in `src/util/rolling-ranges.ts` (off-limits to this task besides, and runtime-importable never). The drift is closed executably in BOTH directions by `test/component/history-range.spec.ts`: the runtime arrays compare entry-for-entry, and each side's ids assign to the other's union type (`readonly HistoryRangeId[] ← ROLLING_RANGE_IDS` and the mirror) — a server-side id the UI does not know, or a UI id the server rejects, fails compile or runtime — the `API_MUTATION_HEADER` precedent (D-134) applied to a union plus a table. (6) **The client arms and the page wiring.** `api.history.get({accountId, metric, from, to, maxPoints?})` and `api.events.list({accountId, from, to, metric?})` join the client with type-only schema imports (D-139's recorded shape), and the page wires **both** range-keyed loads now so 175/176 inherit them: the account-level §12.2 timeline keys on the validated target × the range; the metric series additionally keys on the **first quota metric key** (the wiring proof — per-metric charts are 175; no snapshot ⇒ no metric vocabulary ⇒ no series request, while the timeline still loads because it states account-level facts). Nothing renders from the payloads in 174 — the chart region's loading/empty states belong to 175/176 — but failures render the shared notice with distinctly-named retries (the D-137 pattern), and a **refresh** beside the control re-runs quota + history + events with fresh bounds: the affordance D-137's consequences explicitly handed to 174 ("if its range switching wants it" — it does: without it the rolling window goes stale as the page sits open), discharging that loose end.

**Reasons.** Every open question had a landed precedent that made a fork expensive. The retention source: the page's settings load already carries the annotated scalar, so a second surface would duplicate §13 for one number. The strict-excess comparison: §14.4's own verb, with the equality cell that matters for the default — 7d under §11.3's minimum, where disabling it would leave no honest §14.4 window at all. The no-zone boundary: D-068 had already settled the arithmetic server-side, and mirroring it client-side (drift-pinned) is cheaper and more honest than re-deriving a zone-anchored boundary §10 never asked for — the display zone's only §14.4 roles are axis ticks and tooltip text, both 175's. The radio group: the done-condition's "disabled options explain why" is only satisfiable per-option in an open list; the theme select's precedent (D-133) covers explicit-state controls without explanations. Page-local state: nothing in §14.4 asks the range to survive navigation, and a persisted range would need exactly the reconciliation machinery D-135 built for a fact (account existence) the range does not have. Both loads wired now: D-139's consequences said the client additions land "when the pages land" — this page IS their consumer — and the split trigger keys (target+range for the timeline, target+metric+range for the series) make each load re-run on exactly its own dependencies, so a selection switch resets the series while the new quota loads and dispatches once its metric vocabulary arrives, without duplicate timeline dispatches.

**Consequences.** UI-side: `ui/src/history-range.ts`, `ui/src/components/HistoryRangeControls.vue`, the client's `history`/`events` families, the two range-keyed loads + retention watcher + refresh in `OverviewView.vue`, and the `overview.range.*` + `overview.{retryHistory,retryEvents}` catalog keys. Tests: `test/component/history-range.spec.ts` (drift pins, the retention matrix incl. equality, exact ISO spans across a DST transition), `test/component/history-range-controls.spec.ts` (structure/keyboard semantics, the enabled/disabled × explanation matrix, unknown retention, selection round-trip, disabled inertness, theme-independence smoke incl. a no-hardcoded-color source scan), the extended `test/component/overview-view.spec.ts` (seam placement, the default 7-day dispatch round-trip in D-139's grammar incl. the no-`maxPoints` pin, the no-metric rule, range-switch re-dispatch with disabled inertness, the late-retention fallback via the backend's gated settings answer, selection-switch re-dispatch, both failure arms with recoveries, the refresh re-anchoring), the client round-trips in `test/component/api-client.spec.ts` (percent-encoded ISO colons pinned), and `test/helpers/api.ts`'s `healthyApiBody` grows the history/events arms with a retention-parameterized `healthySettingsBody` — exactly the consequence D-139 recorded; `test/e2e/a11y.spec.ts` serves the range-keyed loads through the same helpers and gains the retention-7 cell — the disabled surface with its reason texts axe-scanned in both themes. Hand-offs: 175 renders the series (one chart per metric — extend the history load from the single first-key proof to per-metric calls, reusing the same trigger shape), 176 renders the timeline strip from the already-wired events load, and both inherit the fresh-bounds rule; the range report's `truncated`/`rejected` outcomes are not surfaced in 174 (the pre-flight disabling makes `rejected` unreachable from this page — the window always ends at `now`, assuming the browser clock is within the retention of the server's, the sane-deployment premise §10's NTP discipline carries — and a truncation notice belongs to the chart region 175 owns); a per-metric `maxPoints` need rides the existing client parameter. Known residuals, recorded: (a) if the operator lowers retention below a selected range between page loads, the first request after reload may be truncated by the server before the settings load lands — the honest-but-unannotated window the report already names, closed visually by 175's outcome surfacing if it wants it; (b) an exactly-equal selection (7/7, 14/14, 30/30) can come back `truncated` by a sub-tolerance sliver — the server anchors the retention horizon to its own clock while the client's `from` is anchored to the browser's (the review round's finding; 175's outcome surfacing should treat a sub-tolerance clamp as not truncated, or threshold it); and (c) the refresh's direct series reload can be superseded when the refreshed quota's first metric key changed (the vocabulary watcher re-dispatches on the new key) — the `useApiCall` re-entry token makes the superseded request harmless (only the newest run writes state), and the rare duplicate is accepted rather than conditioning the refresh path on a key comparison.

## D-148 — Task 175's ECharts metric charts: the modular runtime seam with the canvas/richText CSP constraint (D-127), the pure one-unit option builder, the bucket first/last minimal render, the D-147 sliver threshold, and the per-metric card architecture (spec §14.4, §14.1, §13, §3, §8.4; task 175)

**Date:** 2026-11-04 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§14.4](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#144-history-charts), [§14.1](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#141-general-ui-requirements), [§13](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#13-http-api), [§3](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#3-technology-and-packaging), [§8.4](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#84-normalized-snapshot-and-metric-model) · **Tasks:** [175](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-127 (the CSP constraint that fixed the renderer and tooltip modes before any choice was open), D-133 (the token-only color rule and `resolvedTheme` restyle mechanism the charts consume), D-139 (the history wire grammar — kinds, epoch-ms fields, the range report — the adapter consumes), D-081 (the bucket semantics the minimal render honors), D-147 (the per-metric load hand-off and the equality-cell sliver residual this entry closes), D-134 (the `useApiCall` per-request pattern each chart card follows), D-132 (the catalog discipline every chart string follows), D-137 (the metric-label resolution the chart headings reuse), D-135 (the keep-last-good rule the refresh path follows)

**Decision.** Task 175 lands §14.4's per-metric charts as one `MetricHistoryChart.vue` card per quota metric below the overview's metric cards, and pins six interpretations. (Correction trail: the task's review round — deepseek-v4.1-flash, one round, REQUEST_CHANGES with 1 P1 / 3 P2 / 6 P3 — was folded in before landing, the D-124/D-127 precedent. Accepted and fixed in the same commit: the charts grid's `24rem` floor overflowed §14.1's 360 px viewport (the P1 — now `minmax(min(100%, 24rem), 1fr)` beside a narrow-viewport e2e cell); a failed refresh nulled `useApiCall`'s `data` and wiped the chart its own comments promised to keep (the P2 — the card now holds a last-good response cleared on identity/range changes, and the failure notice renders beside the kept chart); `echarts` sat in `dependencies` while every other browser library is a devDependency whose bundle ships prebuilt (the P2 — moved to `devDependencies`, the `vue`/`vue-i18n`/`vue-router` precedent D-132 recorded); the chart image's accessible name omitted the metric, leaving several same-prefixed images indistinguishable (the P2 — the summary templates carry `{metric}`); plus the P3s — the stale overview README architecture section, the dead `CHART_TOKEN_NAMES` (now consumed by the e2e chart-contract cell's completeness arm), the all-null series rendering unlabeled blank axes (now a stated "no valid values" state), the missing refresh-failure/multi-metric-refresh tests, and the non-exhaustive unit ladder (now the `never`-guarded switch). Two P3 notes were declined with reasons recorded in Consequences: the attribute-ordered theme test and the merge-based option update.) (1) **The dependency and its import strategy are spec-fixed, the renderer CSP-fixed.** `echarts` 6.1.0 joins `devDependencies` (host-installed with npm 11.9.0: `npm install echarts`, then moved with `npm install --save-dev echarts@6.1.0` after the review round; lockfile regenerated, the container volume re-synced by the stamp-file `npm ci` — Vite bundles it into `ui/dist` like `vue` itself, no server code imports it, and the shipped tarball carries the prebuilt bundle), and spec §3's own table row — "Apache ECharts, **modular imports**" — is executed literally: `ui/src/charts/runtime.ts` is the only module that imports the library (`echarts/core` + `LineChart`/`GridComponent`/`TooltipComponent`/`LegendComponent`/`CanvasRenderer`, one `use([...])` registration), so the bundle carries the tree-shaken pieces and every other chart module stays library-free and pure. The renderer is **canvas with `tooltip.renderMode: 'richText'`** — not a free choice: D-127's CSP analysis recorded that ECharts' SVG renderer and HTML tooltips style through the `style=` ATTRIBUTE (apache/echarts#19570, #19398), which `style-src 'self'` blocks, and named exactly this pairing as the no-amendment path. (2) **Unit segregation is structural, not checked.** The pure `buildMetricChartOption` (`ui/src/charts/series.ts`) takes exactly one view mode (`absolute`/`percent`) and one unit label and emits exactly ONE y-axis with the two-series used/remaining pair — there is no input shape that could place incompatible units on one axis, so the done-condition ("incompatible units never share a value axis") holds by construction and is pinned executably (a single non-array `yAxis`, both series' data provably drawn from one field family with the other family's values present-but-unused in the fixtures). The percent/absolute toggle renders ONLY where the series data carries both families (`seriesAvailability` scans the samples; a view exists only where values do — the unit field alone does not suffice); a percentage-only metric never gains a toggle and renders on its bounded 0–100 `%` axis (§14.4: "do not use separate axes for incompatible units … do not infer token counts"), an absolute-only metric stays absolute, and the default where both exist is absolute (§14.3's own ladder). The two series are distinguishable with color OFF the table: legend names in text, the used line solid, the remaining line dashed (§14.1). (3) **All three D-139 wire kinds render, minimally and honestly.** Points map verbatim (an invalid row's value nulls stay null — never zero, §8.4); a §12.2 `empty` entry maps to an all-null sample that breaks the line (`connectNulls: false`) — the gap-edge elaboration (hatched regions, the timeline strip) is task 176's; a `bucket` entry maps to its `first` at `fromEpochMs` and `last` at `toEpochMs` — D-081's first/last are real observed point references, so no value is invented, and a one-member bucket renders one sample. The bucket render is deliberate minimalism on the honest branch: the default 7-day window at the default 300 s cadence is ~2016 points over the 1500 default budget, so bucketed responses are the COMMON case and ignoring `kind: 'bucket'` would blank the default view; the per-field extrema stay on the wire items for 176 to render as bands on the same samples (the adapter's extension point). (4) **The D-147 residual is closed by a 60-second threshold.** `rangeNoticeOf(report)` keeps a `truncated` range report quiet while `effectiveFrom − requestedFrom ≤ TRUNCATION_NOTICE_MS` (60 000 ms — far above disciplined-clock skew, far below anything visible on any §14.4 window, strict excess at the boundary), surfaces a notice naming the retained window's start beyond it, and states `rejected` (a server clock beyond the whole retention ahead of the browser's — pathological, but stated rather than rendered as an empty chart). Each chart reads ITS OWN response's report; the per-metric notices are the honest per-card rendering of per-request facts. (5) **The per-metric card architecture executes D-147's hand-off.** The page's single first-key history load is replaced by `chartTargets` (the validated target × every quota metric key) rendering one `MetricHistoryChart` per key, keyed `` `${accountId}\u0000${metricKey}` `` (a selection switch is a fresh card set — no per-account state leaks); each card owns its `useApiCall` with bounds recomputed per dispatch (D-147's fresh-bounds rule) and re-runs on its identity/range props; the page-level refresh bumps a `refreshToken` the cards watch WITHOUT resetting — the card keeps its own last-successful response (`displayData = data ?? lastGood`, the page's `lastQuota` pattern), so a failed refresh renders its notice BESIDE the previous chart and a successful one replaces it, D-135's keep-last-good rule — while an identity/range change clears the kept copy with the query identity (one window's response must never render for another). The account-level §12.2 timeline load stays exactly as 174 wired it (176's consumer). The page-level history retry dies with its load; each card carries its own retry whose accessible name embeds the metric label (D-137's distinct-name rule), and `overview.retryHistory` leaves the catalog with it. (6) **Theme and testing seams.** Chart colors come only through `chartTokensOf` over the runtime's `readToken` — `getComputedStyle` `--qm-*` lookups — with two dedicated tokens (`--qm-chart-used`, `--qm-chart-remaining`) added to all three theme blocks of `base.css` (WCAG AA per mode; everything else reuses the shell's tokens), and the option computed reads `theme.resolvedTheme` so a mode flip re-reads the cascade and re-`setOption`s live — the exact mechanism D-133 recorded. The ECharts runtime itself is an injectable `ChartRuntime` (`useChartRuntime()`, the theme-storage/api-fetch precedent): production installs the DOM runtime; component tests inject a recording fake because ECharts cannot boot under happy-dom at all (zrender measures text through a real canvas 2d context) — every option the card builds is asserted through the fake's recorded `setOption` calls while the TOKEN reader stays the production `cssTokenReader` over live inline custom properties, so the color plumbing is tested for real. This is the deliberate test boundary: rendering correctness belongs to the mature library; the option pipeline — the part this repository owns — is fully tested without it.

**Reasons.** Every constraint was already staked by a landed record, which made the remaining choices narrow. The import strategy and renderer carry spec and CSP citations respectively — §3's row says "modular imports" and D-127 named canvas+richText as the no-successor path, so the only decision left was recording the execution. The one-unit builder answers the done-condition's own grammar: "never share" is a structural property, best held by an API that cannot express sharing, and the builder's purity keeps the whole §14.4 semantics (modes, availability, window bounds, formatters, tokens) testable without any library present. The bucket question was forced by arithmetic, not taste: at the default cadence the default range arrives bucketed, so 175 had to render buckets or ship a blank default view — first/last is the unique render that uses only D-081's guaranteed references and leaves the extrema untouched for 176. The sliver threshold answers D-147's recorded hand-off ("treat a sub-tolerance clamp as not truncated, or threshold it") with the only number that is simultaneously above NTP-disciplined skew and below perceptibility on a 24-hour-minimum window. The card-per-metric split follows the component-per-key Vue idiom (the accounts card's precedent) and moves each series' failure/retry/loading states to exactly where its data renders, shrinking the page; the refresh-token compromise keeps D-135's keep-last-good rule for the refresh path without weakening the reset discipline for genuine context switches.

**Consequences.** UI-side: `ui/src/charts/{runtime,tokens,series}.ts`, `ui/src/components/MetricHistoryChart.vue`, the `chartTargets`/`historyRefreshToken` wiring and the charts region in `OverviewView.vue`, the `overview.chart.*` catalog namespace (`regionTitle`, `loading`, `empty`, `noValidValues`, `rejected`, `truncatedNotice`, `retry`, `viewLabel`, `viewAbsolute`, `viewPercent`, `seriesUsed`, `seriesRemaining`, `summaryAbsolute`, `summaryPercent`) beside the removed `overview.retryHistory`, the `--qm-chart-*` tokens in `base.css`, and `formatChartDate` in `ui/src/format.ts` (the compact zone-formatted date the tooltips and axis labels render through — task 177 owns tick PLACEMENT and keeps consuming it). Tests: `test/component/chart-series.spec.ts` (the pure adapter: kind mapping incl. bucket first/last and the 1-member dedup, wire-order preservation, the availability matrix, `resolveViewMode` incl. the percentage-only pin, `rangeNoticeOf` incl. the strict-excess boundary, and the option builder — unit segregation, the 0–100 percent axis, null gaps, the requested-bounds window, the tooltip/axis formatters, token wiring, symbol density, animation-off/richText), `test/component/metric-history-chart.spec.ts` (mounted over the injected runtime: the D-139 dispatch grammar, the toggle's axis switch, both no-toggle arms, the states incl. the no-valid-values arm, the failure + named retry with recovery, the refresh keep-last-good pair — success keeps the instance, failure keeps the chart beside the notice, the kept-copy clearing on a range switch —, the live theme restyle, the dispose/recreate lifecycle, the aria summary), the updated `test/component/overview-view.spec.ts` (per-metric dispatch, the charts seam ordering, the refresh's +1-per-metric incl. the two-metric cell), `test/component/format.spec.ts`'s `formatChartDate` cells, the extended `test/e2e/theme.spec.ts` chart-contract cell (the new tokens' verbatim per-mode values, system-dark agreement, and the `CHART_TOKEN_NAMES` completeness arm — every chart token resolves in both modes), and the new narrow-viewport cell in `test/e2e/a11y.spec.ts` (the populated overview at 360 px gains no horizontal overflow). The a11y e2e cells are untouched otherwise by design: their healthy history bodies are empty series, so the cards render their empty states and ECharts never boots there. Hand-offs: 176 renders the timeline strip from the page-level events load and may extend `chartSamplesOf`/the option with the bucket extrema bands, reset markers, gap hatching, and the error strip on the same samples; 177 replaces the x-axis tick placement (hour/day boundaries in the display zone, DST-aware) while keeping `formatChartDate`; 178's synchronized cursor/zoom owns the option-update discipline (today's `notMerge` replace resets ECharts' own interaction state — legend series toggles — a documented trade for never letting stale configuration survive an update); a per-metric `maxPoints` need rides the existing client parameter (still deliberately omitted — §13's server-side default). The two declined review notes, with reasons: the requested attribute-ordered theme test (apply tokens only after `setTheme`) cannot run under happy-dom — component tests carry no stylesheet cascade, so the inline custom properties ARE the cascade seam, and the attribute→cascade half is already pinned by the theme suites; and the merge-based `setOption` update for state preservation — deferred to 178 with the comment in place, because no interaction state exists to preserve until that task lands its cursor/zoom. Known residual, recorded: ECharts' own rendering is untested in this repository's suites (the injected-seam boundary above) — a real-browser visual check joins the suite only if a future task needs pixel-level guarantees; and the two new tokens exist precisely so charts never borrow the status tones' semantics — reusing them for non-chart purposes would be a decision, not a convenience.

## D-149 — Task 176's chart annotations: the source-verified ECharts encoding (custom-series decal hatching, silent marks + the single axis-tooltip channel), the §12.2 account-vs-metric mapping, the never-color-alone scheme, and the peak-hours client arm (spec §14.4, §12.2, §9.3, §14.1; task 176)

**Date:** 2026-11-04 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§14.4](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#144-history-charts), [§12.2](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#122-collection-gaps-and-errors), [§9.3](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#93-schedule-calculation-and-display), [§14.1](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#141-general-ui-requirements) · **Tasks:** [176](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-148 (the chart architecture extended: the pure builder, the recording-runtime test boundary, the canvas+richText CSP constraint), D-147 (the range-keyed events load that is 176's events source, the fresh-bounds rule whose millisecond edge-drives the clamping below), D-142/D-139 (the peak-hours and events wire shapes consumed verbatim — epoch-ms intervals with `kind: 'peak'|'off-peak'`, the four event kinds), D-081 (the bucket semantics the annotations align with), D-133 (the token-only color rule; four new `--qm-chart-*` tokens), D-134 (the typed client's type-only import pattern the `peakHours` arm follows), D-127 (the CSP that keeps the renderer and tooltip mode fixed), D-132 (the catalog discipline every annotation string follows)

**Decision.** Task 176 renders the §14.4/§12.2 annotation vocabulary on task 175's per-metric charts and pins six interpretations, every ECharts-behavior claim verified against the 6.1.0 source in `node_modules` before a line was written. (Correction trail: the task's review round — deepseek-v4.1-flash, one round, REQUEST_CHANGES with 3 P1 / 1 P2 / 4 P3 — was folded in before landing, the D-148 precedent; the reviewer independently booted a headless ECharts model to prove three behaviors the option had wrong, and all three fixes entered this entry and the same commit: the strip's axes now bind to the strip's grid with an explicit `gridIndex: 1` (every axis otherwise attaches to grid 0 — the strip rendered inside the main plot, the P1); the axis-tooltip formatter renders value lines for the two LINE series only (`silent` does NOT keep the bands custom series out of the axis tooltip's collection — its datum joined the params and rendered an epoch-ms span as a quota value, the P1); and the band tint is `fillOpacity`, never element `opacity` (zrender's element-level opacity fades fill, stroke, AND the decal together — the stopped region's hatch and border rendered at 8% alpha, effectively invisible, the P1). The same round's P2 — the y-axis label truncation the entry claimed but the code did not carry — landed as `axisLabel.width`/`overflow: 'truncate'`; its P3s landed as the served-bounds tooltip times (a window-clamped band no longer mixes clamped display times with verbatim schedule times — `PeakBand` carries the served `start`/`end` beside the clamped `from`/`to`), the grid-geometry `LABEL_HEIGHT` de-double-count, count-first plural-neutral annotation wordings (`attempts: 3`, `1 quota resets` → `quota resets: 1`-style phrasing), the removed unused `width()` api seam, and the new pins for all of the above. One P3 was declined with reasons in Consequences: rendering the CLAMPED bounds in the display-zone tooltip line was proposed for consistency with what is drawn — but the two lines would then disagree about the same interval (the schedule line is the server's verbatim rendering of the SERVED bounds), so both lines state the served interval and the clamp is visible geometry, not a fact.) (1) **The hatching primitive is the custom series, not markArea — a source fact, not a preference.** ECharts' decal→canvas-pattern conversion runs only over raw series (`ecModel.eachRawSeries` in `lib/visual/decal.js`); the marker components (markArea/markLine) never pass through that stage, so an `itemStyle.decal` on a markArea silently does not render. `CustomView` converts `style.decal` itself (`createOrUpdatePatternFromDecal`), so **one silent custom series** (`z: 0`, `clip: true`, a hidden 0..1 y-axis of its own) draws every band kind as full-height rects on the main grid: peak windows tinted with a solid border, the off-peak complement unfilled with a dashed border, gaps transparent-filled with a 45° hatch and dashed border (beside 175's line break — §14.4's "line breaks AND hatched regions"), stopped regions tinted with the counter-angle hatch, a solid border, and an on-band "Service stopped" text label when the band is wide enough to hold it (64 px — a width threshold evaluated in the pure `renderItem`, which unit tests drive against a stubbed api). Reset instants are vertical `markLine`s on the used series — `symbol: ['none','none']`, dashed, the on-line "Reset" label at the top — one per reset; failed cycles are a `scatter` series on a **second, lower grid** (§14.4's "lower timeline strip"), one marker per cycle with a distinct symbol per §11.2 outcome (auth=diamond, rate_limited=triangle, network=circle, timeout=rect, server=roundRect, parse=pin — the exhaustive `never`-guarded switch). The runtime's modular registration grows `ScatterChart`, `CustomChart`, `MarkLineComponent` (same package, no new dependency). The strip renders only when a failed cycle exists in range, and the strip's axes bind to it with an explicit `gridIndex: 1` (ECharts' default attaches every axis to grid 0 — the review round's probe caught the omission) while the strip's grid and the main grid share **fixed left/right insets with no `containLabel`** (the main y-axis labels truncate inside the fixed margin), so the two plots align by construction; when the strip exists, its x-axis owns the date labels (the main x-axis hides its own — no stacked duplicate) and the strip's series joins the legend by name ("Failed collections"), which is at once its text label and a toggle. (2) **All tooltips flow through the ONE axis-trigger richText channel; every mark is `silent`.** The tooltip source was read before this choice: with a global `trigger: 'axis'`, the item-tooltip path resolves its trigger through the cascade `[item model → mark/series model → coordSys → global]` and per-series/per-mark `tooltip.trigger` overrides exist in the types — but the axis-pointer flow dispatches on every grid mousemove and its `_showAxisTooltip` replaces an already-shown item tooltip (per-series trigger overrides are documented-unsupported for the axis direction, "not support any more", `modelHelper.js`), so a per-element tooltip over a band is a race the axis channel always wins. The single formatter therefore states, for the hovered instant: the date and the two line series' values (175's behavior, unchanged — the value lines render for exactly the `Used`/`Remaining` series names, because the silent bands series still joins the axis tooltip's collection and its span datum is not a quota), the **covering schedule band** — §14.4's demanded content: the window name, the rate multiplier, and times in BOTH the display zone (`formatChartDate`) and the schedule zone (the server's own D-073 `localStart`/`localEnd` strings verbatim plus the zone name — §9.3's browser-never-calculates rule) —, the covering gap/stopped region with its humanized duration (`formatChartDuration`, new in `ui/src/format.ts`), and the **resets inside the snapped sample interval** `(previous.at, snapped.at]` (a reset is an instant between samples; the interval that contains it is the tooltip row it belongs to — a binary search over the samples the formatter closes over). The strip's markers carry their prebuilt lines on the datum (`params.data.tooltipLines`: outcome word from the existing `overview.error.outcome.*` vocabulary, attempts, HTTP status, retry-after, the sanitized message verbatim), and the formatter branches on the series name. The CSP constraint is untouched: everything renders on the canvas through richText. (3) **The §12.2 account-vs-metric mapping is D-139's own split made visual.** Resets and gaps carry `metricKey` — per-metric facts, filtered to their metric's chart; failed cycles and stopped regions are account-level (the events route's optional `metric` filter narrows only the per-metric kinds) and render **identically on every metric chart of the account** — a cycle that failed collected nothing for any metric. The events source is the page's already-wired account-level load (D-147's design: one request for all cards); the mapping (`annotationsOf`, `peakBandsOf`, `scheduleZoneOf` in the new pure `ui/src/charts/annotations.ts`) clamps every band to the card's own window and drops the emptied ones — the page's loads and each card's history load bound their own `Date.now()` (D-147's fresh-bounds rule), so the edges can differ by milliseconds and nothing may draw outside the axes; a null response, the §9.2 no-schedule arm (`timezone: null`, empty intervals), or a rejected range maps to no bands — the browser never invents a schedule. (4) **Never color alone (§14.1), by construction at every element.** The two lines: legend text + solid-vs-dashed (175). Peak vs off-peak: fill presence + border style + the tooltip's own words. Gap vs stopped: hatch direction (45° vs −45°) + border style + the stopped band's on-band label. Resets: a vertical line + the on-line text label. Failed cycles: six distinct shapes + the tooltip's outcome word + the legend name. The aria summary appends the annotation counts as text ("— in range: 1 quota resets, 2 failed collections" — count-first phrasing, grammatical at any count) through the `overview.chart.summaryMarks`/`marks*` keys. Four new tokens (`--qm-chart-peak`, `-reset`, `-gap`, `-stopped`) join all three `base.css` blocks and `CHART_TOKEN_NAMES` (the e2e completeness arm covers them); the error markers reuse `--qm-color-danger` (the shell's error tone — the semantic match), the off-peak border reuses `--qm-color-muted`; the live restyle is D-148's mechanism unchanged (component tests pin a band color flipping with the mode). (5) **The peak-hours client arm and the page wiring.** `api.peakHours.get({accountId, from, to})` joins the typed client with type-only schema imports (D-134's pattern, D-139's ISO-request grammar); the page wires it as the third range-keyed load beside the timeline — target- and range-keyed, fresh bounds per dispatch, re-run by the refresh, with its own distinctly-named retry (`overview.retryPeakHours`) — and both annotation loads now keep **last-good copies** cleared on identity/range change (D-135's rule, the cards' own `lastGood` precedent: a failed refresh keeps the previous annotations rendering beside the kept charts), passed to every card as `events`/`peaks` props. The peak response's own range report is deliberately not surfaced a second time: each card's history response already states the window's truncation/rejection (D-148's per-card notices), and the bands are clamped to that card's window regardless. (6) **The geometry change is uniform.** The builder now always emits `grid`/`xAxis`/`yAxis` as arrays (length 1 without annotations — the 175 shape modulo the array), with explicit `xAxisIndex`/`yAxisIndex` on every series; the fixed `left: 60` replaces 175's `containLabel` (the y-axis labels truncate inside the margin via `axisLabel.width`/`overflow`), because two `containLabel` grids reserve different label widths and their plots would misalign by exactly the main y-label width.

**Reasons.** The two hard constraints were ECharts' actual behavior and the spec's own words, and the source reading settled both before design froze. The decal finding forced the custom series (a markArea "hatch" would have shipped a spec violation silently — nothing in the test stack can see pixels), and the tooltip-race finding killed the per-element-tooltip design the marker types seem to invite: a tooltip that appears for one mousemove and is replaced by the axis tooltip on the next is worse than no tooltip, and the single channel composes ALL the facts of the hovered instant (values + band + region + resets) into one box, which is also exactly the §14.4 letter ("a tooltip showing interval name, time in both the display and schedule time zones, and the configured rate multiplier" — an instant-scoped demand, not an element-scoped one). The account-level consistency answers the task's open question from D-139's own semantics — the wire already declares which kinds are metric-filterable, so the chart mirrors the wire. The fixed-inset alignment beats `containLabel` because it is the only deterministic way to make two grids share an x-range; the cost (truncated y labels at extreme magnitudes) is bounded by the tooltip always stating exact values. The page-owned loads (one events + one peaks request for all N charts, vs N per-metric requests) follow D-147's recorded design that 176 consumes the timeline load it wired.

**Consequences.** UI-side: `ui/src/charts/annotations.ts` (the pure §12.2/§9.3 mapping), the extended `ui/src/charts/{series,tokens,runtime}.ts` (the annotation series, four tokens + `danger`, the three new modular registrations), `ui/src/components/MetricHistoryChart.vue` (the `events`/`peaks` props, the annotation computeds, the aria counts), `OverviewView.vue` (the peak-hours load, the last-good pair, the retry), `ui/src/api/client.ts` (the `peakHours` family), `ui/src/i18n/en.ts` (`overview.chart.*` annotation keys + `overview.retryPeakHours`), `formatChartDuration` in `ui/src/format.ts`, and the four tokens in `base.css`. Tests: the extended `test/component/chart-series.spec.ts` (the mapping table — per-metric/account-level filtering, clamping, degenerate drops; the served-band mapping incl. no-schedule/rejected/null; six-distinct symbols; the markLine/band/strip structure incl. hatch rotations and the strip's grid alignment; the single-channel tooltip's §14.4 peak content, both-zone times, gap/stopped durations, the reset interval rule, and the strip's prebuilt lines; the `renderItem` element against a stubbed api incl. the label-width threshold and the degenerate width), the extended `test/component/metric-history-chart.spec.ts` (the props flow into `setOption` — this metric's reset only, the peak pair, the strip + legend name; the aria counts; a band token flipping with the theme; the null-prop 175 shape; the no-schedule arm), `test/component/overview-view.spec.ts` (the peak load's grammar, re-dispatch on range/account, the failure + named retry, the refresh's +1), the `peakHours.get` round-trip in `test/component/api-client.spec.ts`, `formatChartDuration` cells in `test/component/format.spec.ts`, the four verbatim token pins in `test/e2e/theme.spec.ts`, and `test/helpers/api.ts`'s `healthyPeakHoursBody` (the no-schedule default) with its `healthyApiBody` route. Hand-offs: 177 owns tick placement on BOTH x-axes (it already consumes `formatChartDate`); 178's cursor/zoom must respect the two-grid layout (an `axisPointer` `link` across the grids is its natural tool) and reconsiders the `notMerge` trade D-148 recorded; a future bucket-extrema band rendering (D-081's served extrema) would join the same custom series as another band kind. Known residuals, recorded: ECharts' actual painting stays outside the test stack (D-148's boundary — the decal/hatch relies on CustomView's own conversion, source-verified but not pixel-verified); the strip markers' hover relies on the axis channel's scatter participation (the standard axis-trigger behavior for scatter series); and the band tint/hatch contrast pairs are chosen against the two theme backgrounds but carry no automated contrast gate (the §14.1 AA duty sits on the text tokens, which the annotations reuse for every label).

## D-150 — Task 177's configured-timezone axis ticks: the `customValues` delivery (source-verified), the boundary-walk algorithm (instant-space hours, wall-space days/months), the density ladder over the measured canvas, and the DST zone-name disambiguation (spec §14.4, §10; task 177)

**Date:** 2026-11-04 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§14.4](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#144-history-charts), [§10](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#10-time-and-time-zones) · **Tasks:** [177](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-148 (the chart architecture this extends: the numeric epoch-ms axis was built with tick placement left to 177, the pure-builder seam, the recording-runtime test boundary), D-149 (the strip whose x-axis shares the same ticks and whose fixed insets keep both grids aligned), D-147 (the requested-bounds window every ladder walks; the range arms that never anchor to a zone), D-068 (the server-side zone discipline mirrored: no machine-local paths), D-021 (the explicit-zone, injectable-time canonical style the client engine mirrors), D-079 (the ambiguous-DST assertion discipline the resolver follows), D-133 (the axis label colors, unchanged token wiring), D-132 (no new catalog keys — tick labels are `Intl` dates like `formatChartDate`, not catalog text)

**Decision.** Task 177 places the §14.4 metric charts' x-axis ticks on local hour/day/month boundaries of the CONFIGURED display zone and pins six interpretations. (Correction trail: the task's review round — deepseek-v4.1-flash, one round, REQUEST_CHANGES with 2 P2 / 4 P3, every finding independently reproduced by the reviewer (a 16-zone × 5-span sweep, a headless ECharts 6.1.0 SSR render, and a Vue 3.5.44 self-trigger probe) — was folded in before landing, the D-148/D-149 precedent: the **P2s** — the DST disambiguation was adjacency-local, leaving both ticks of a wall hour duplicated by a fall-back LONGER than one hour (Antarctica/Troll's two-hour shift repeats 01:00 and 02:00) indistinguishable (now a global per-wall-reading count over the whole ladder suffixes every duplicated tick), and the component's creation-time width measure was dead code (an effect does not re-run on its own write — Vue 3.5; the measure now precedes the option read, the observer reads the host's `clientWidth`, and the seam is pinned by a controllable-ResizeObserver test) — plus the P3s: the resize now writes the width only when the chosen ladder step changes (drag-resize fired the whole `notMerge` option rebuild per frame), the day/month walks dedupe equal consecutive instants (a skipped calendar day — Pacific/Apia has no 2011-12-30 — resolved to the same instant as its successor), the pre-177 zone-formatter cell now asserts a real tick instead of riding the off-tick fallback, and the two stale `format.ts` docblocks were reworded to the post-177 roles.) (1) **Delivery through `customValues`, verified against the 6.1.0 source before design froze.** ECharts' value axis computes its own ticks on a uniform epoch-ms ladder anchored at interval multiples (`intervalScaleNiceTicks` in `lib/scale/helper.js`) — a ladder that can hold neither a +05:45 zone's :15 phase nor an offset shift mid-window, which is exactly why §14.4 demands the numeric axis with a custom formatter. ECharts 6's `axisLabel.customValues`/`axisTick.customValues` (`(number | string | Date)[]`) ARE the tick set when present (`createAxisLabels`/`createAxisTicks` in `lib/coord/axisTickLabelBuilder.js` parse→extent-filter→dedup→sort them; the per-tick label still flows through the axis formatter; `fixMinMaxLabelShow` declines to drop end labels for custom sets) — so the pure engine's instants are handed to BOTH the main and the strip x-axis as `customValues`, with `axisTick` carried too (without it the tick MARKS would stay on ECharts' ladder while the labels moved). (2) **The engine (`ui/src/charts/ticks.ts`, the D-148 pure-helper pattern) walks the zone's actual boundaries, never a uniform ladder.** Hour granularity walks INSTANT space — from the first boundary at/after `from`, each next boundary is `t + 1 h` probed and, when the probe lands mid-hour (a sub-hour offset shift), snapped to the next aligned wall hour — so the epoch distances follow the zone's real offsets: 3 600 000 ms across New York's transitions, 5 400 000 ms across Lord Howe's ±30-minute shifts (its spring day has no wall 02:00 at all; the walk emits 01:00 then 03:00), and a fall-back's duplicated wall hour emits twice one real hour apart. Day and month granularity walk WALL space (local midnights / month starts over epoch-day and calendar-month indices, so a 7-day step keeps one weekday); a wall→epoch resolver built on the two-probe offset iteration handles the ambiguous (returns a genuine occurrence, the D-079 discipline — no ladder relies on which) and the SKIPPED reading (returns the boundary's actual first instant: Havana's 2026-03-08 midnight does not exist, the day starts at 01:00, and its tick still reads "Mar 8" while the neighboring midnight gaps run 24 h then 23 h). All arithmetic is `Intl.DateTimeFormat` with an explicit `timeZone` plus `Date.UTC` calendar math — no machine-local path (the D-021 discipline mirrored client-side; the suites pin zones explicitly and were verified green under four hostile process `TZ` values). (3) **Density is a ladder over the MEASURED canvas width.** Steps 1/2/3/6/12 h → 1/2/7/14 d → 1/3/6 mo are tried finest-first against per-kind minimum label gaps (72/64/64 px, derived from the longest label shape at ECharts' 12 px axis font: "12 AM EDT" ≈ 54 px); §14.1's 360 px viewport is the unmeasured floor, and the component re-fits on container resize by feeding its `ResizeObserver` reads into the option computed (a bare `resize()` only stretches already-placed labels). Sub-hour spans — not §14.4 shapes (the D-147 ranges start at 24 h) — render their 0–1 contained boundaries; no sub-hour granularity is invented (§14.4 names hour/day boundaries only). (4) **Labels per granularity, with the DST disambiguation.** Hour ticks render time-only ("2 PM"), day ticks "Nov 4", month ticks "Nov 2026" (the year always — a month-step axis spans months), through four new cached `Intl` formatters in `ui/src/format.ts`; the tooltip keeps its full `formatChartDate` header. A tick whose wall reading equals the previous tick's (the duplicated hour of a 25-hour day) or whose zone offset differs from the previous tick's renders with the zone's short name — so New York's 2026-11-01 reads "1 AM EDT" then "1 AM EST", never two indistinguishable "1 AM"s. (5) **The zone's source of truth is unchanged**: the page's settings-load-derived `timeZone` (browser-zone fallback on a failed load) that 175/176 already pass into every chart card as a prop; the engine receives it through the option builder's existing `timeZone` input — no new plumbing, and the DISPLAY zone still never touches request boundaries (D-147). (6) **Both x-axes share the SAME instants by construction**: one `chartTicks(window, zone, plotWidth)` call feeds the main axis and the strip axis (D-149's fixed insets keep the grids pixel-aligned; the shared values keep the labels instants-aligned), inside the same half-open `[from, to)` window (the right edge never renders a clipped label).

**Reasons.** §14.4's own sentence names the constraint ("ECharts' time axis uses local time or UTC only") and prescribes the numeric epoch-ms axis with an `Intl.DateTimeFormat` formatter — but a formatter alone moves only the TEXT; placement needed ECharts' explicit-tick facility, and `customValues` is the one the shipped source actually honors on value axes (the alternative — a `time` axis — is what the spec just excluded, and category axes would corrupt the data encoding). The walk split (instants for hours, walls for days/months) follows where each granularity's ambiguity lives: hour boundaries are what transitions duplicate or skip, so walking instants with probe-and-snap follows the zone's real offsets by construction; day/month boundaries are calendar facts whose skipped readings (Havana) resolve once per boundary, so wall arithmetic with the two-probe resolver is both exact and cheap. The zone-suffix rule answers the done-condition directly: a 25-hour day's duplicated hour is only honest if the two ticks are distinguishable, and the offsets are the honest difference. The density ladder (estimate-then-walk) keeps selection cheap and the walk exact — the estimate only picks a rung; DST day ±1 tick never moves a boundary. The width seam rides the card's existing `ResizeObserver` rather than a new one — one observer, one lifecycle.

**Consequences.** UI-side: `ui/src/charts/ticks.ts` (the pure engine: `chartTicks`, `chooseTickStep`, the exported `TICK_STEPS` ladder), the four tick-label formatters in `ui/src/format.ts` (`formatChartTime`, `formatChartZoneTime`, `formatChartDay`, `formatChartMonth` — one cache map per kind), `series.ts`'s `MetricChartOptionInput.widthPx` + `DEFAULT_CHART_WIDTH_PX` and the `customValues` wiring on `ChartXAxisOption`'s `axisLabel`/`axisTick` (both axes), and `MetricHistoryChart.vue`'s measured `chartWidth` ref fed from the host at chart creation and from the `ResizeObserver`. Tests: the new `test/component/chart-ticks.spec.ts` (the granularity table incl. the 14-day rung's precedence, the UTC and Kathmandu hour walks, the four DST-day proofs on pinned literal epochs — NY 2026-03-08 (23 ticks, no "2 AM", "3 AM EDT", 23 h midnights), NY 2026-11-01 (25 ticks, "1 AM EDT"/"1 AM EST", 25 h midnights), Lord Howe's both 2026 transitions (90-minute boundary gaps, the skipped wall 02:00) — the day walks (Havana's skipped midnight, 7-day epoch-day anchoring oracle), the month walks (calendar labels, 3-month quarter anchoring), and the degenerate spans), `chart-series.spec.ts`'s builder cells (customValues on both axes incl. the strip shape, the label map with its full-date fallback, the width coarsening, the 360 px floor), `metric-history-chart.spec.ts`'s mounted cells (every tick locally aligned in a +05:45 zone and inside the half-open window; the axes' instants identical), and `format.spec.ts`'s four formatter cells; `TZ`-independence verified by running the four suites green (123/123) under `TZ=America/New_York`, `Asia/Kathmandu`, `Pacific/Kiritimati`, and `Australia/Lord_Howe`. Hand-offs: 178's cursor/zoom work inherits zone-aligned ticks for free (the `axisPointer` follows data/axis values, not tick ladders) but its `link` across the two grids should keep both axes' `customValues` identical as this task leaves them; a future retained-precision zoom (sub-hour spans) will need a sub-hour rung — the ladder is additive and this entry deliberately stops at the hour (§14.4's vocabulary). Known residual: ECharts' painting of the labels stays outside the test stack (D-148's recorded boundary — the option pipeline is asserted, the canvas rendering belongs to the library; the label-gap constants are derived from font metrics, not measured per theme).

## D-152 — The release workflow's publish pipeline: the shared npm ≥ 11 pin for OIDC trusted publishing, the green-CI check-run gate, the artifact-critical in-job gates, and the task-184 boundary (spec §4.4; task U-029)

**Date:** 2026-11-04 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§4.4](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#44-cicd-and-supply-chain-safeguards) · **Tasks:** [U-029](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-008 (the release channel this pipeline makes deliverable), D-045 (the CI shape whose green run the gate consumes), D-009's packaging note and D-015's schema publication (the allowlist the check step validates)

**Decision.** U-029 fixes the three defects that made `.github/workflows/release.yml` unable to deliver a publish, and pins the pipeline shape. (1) **The npm mechanism is an explicit `npm install -g npm@11.9.0` step** — the same pin and mechanism as ci.yml's bump and the Dockerfile, not a setup-node option (setup-node has no npm-version input; the alternatives were an unpinned `npm@latest` or riding a Node line that bundles npm 11, both worse than the house pin). Tokenless OIDC trusted publishing requires npm ≥ 11.5; Node 22's bundled npm 10 cannot do it, so the previous workflow failed at the first tag by construction. The three pins (Dockerfile, ci.yml, release.yml) are held identical **mechanically** by `test/unit/release-workflow.spec.ts`, which extracts all three and fails `make check` on any drift — the executable form of the "keep the pin in sync" comments. (2) **The gate set is two-layered.** In-job, the publish pipeline runs only the artifact-critical gates — tag/version match, the coverage-gated test suite (`test:ci`, the same run CI's test job and `make check` use), the web UI build (`build:ui`) plus `verify:build`, and the tarball allowlist check (`check:package`) — before `npm pkg delete private` and `npm publish --provenance --access public`. The rest of CI (static checks, E2E, the timezone matrix, install containers, unsupported-Node) is deliberately NOT duplicated in the release job; instead a **green-CI gate** first verifies the tagged commit is on `master` (`gh api .../compare/master...{sha}` must report `identical` or `behind` — a green check run on an unmerged PR-head commit does not qualify) and then queries the tagged commit's check runs via `gh api .../commits/{sha}/check-runs`, refusing to publish unless the latest check run named `CI` (the required gate protecting `master`, task 004) completed successfully — the mechanical enforcement of D-008's "every release requires a green CI run on the tagged commit" and of the documented tags-point-at-green-`master`-commits rule, which the checklist could only state. A tag pushed while CI is still running, pointing at a commit that never ran CI, at a red commit, or off `master` is refused with an explanation. (3) **The task-184 boundary is resolved by ordering, not by manifest edits**: the workflow builds the UI _before_ `check:package` and publish, so the tarball check validates built artifacts from the moment task 184 (Stage 14) adds `ui/dist` to the `files` allowlist and `scripts/check-package.mjs`'s ALLOWED — no further workflow change needed. Until then a real publish still fails at the last step for two 184-owned manifest facts (no `repository` field — npm refuses `--provenance` without one — and no `ui/dist` in `files`); both are stated in `docs/release.md` rather than patched here, per the task's boundary discipline. The structural invariants (bump presence and placement, the pin sync, build-before-check ordering, the test gate, check-before-publish, `--provenance`, `id-token: write`, the trigger shape, and the absence of any npm token/secret) are pinned by `test/unit/release-workflow.spec.ts` — a line scanner in the `tz-verify-script.spec.ts` pattern (no YAML dependency; loud throws on shape drift) — so workflow drift fails `make check`; actionlint stays the documented manual lint step (gotchas.md), not a test-suite dependency.

**Reasons.** The defect report named the mechanism choice ("setup-node's npm override or an explicit install step"); the house answer is the explicit install, because the pin already exists in two places with a sync rule and a third copy under the same rule is cheaper and more auditable than a new mechanism. The gate split answers "which gates are release-relevant": everything that certifies the artifact being shipped runs in-job (a tag whose own pipeline is red must never publish, whatever CI said about the commit), while everything that certifies the commit is delegated to the green-CI gate — re-running the full matrix at tag time would double the release latency for near-zero signal, and skipping the CI check entirely would leave D-008's precondition to human discipline. The build-before-check ordering is the only part of the 184 dependency the workflow can own today, and it is exactly the part that would otherwise silently ship a UI-less tarball after 184 lands.

**Consequences.** `.github/workflows/release.yml`'s publish job is: checkout → setup-node 22 (npm cache) → `npm ci` → npm bump → tag/version match → green-CI gate (`GH_TOKEN: github.token`; the workflow's permissions are `contents: read`, `checks: read` for the gate's API reads, and `id-token: write` for the publish) → `test:ci` → `build:ui` → `verify:build` → `check:package` → `npm pkg delete private` → `npm publish --provenance --access public`. `docs/release.md` describes this pipeline step by step (including the gate's refusal modes and the 184 dependency) and drops its stale mutation-in-CI mention (D-045). Task 184 lands the manifest facts and extends `scripts/check-package.mjs`'s exact-match ALLOWED with matching for the packed `ui/dist/**` entries (npm lists each built file, not a directory); the workflow's step order then needs no change. Task 186's "tarball already contains dist/" verification runs against that state. Renaming the `CI` gate job, moving it out of ci.yml, retiring the master-ancestry compare, or renaming the release job's steps requires updating the guard spec in the same change; a future npm major bump edits the three pins together and no spec constant (the spec compares the files to each other and asserts ≥ 11.5.0 by tuple, pinning no literal).

## D-153 — Task 178's synchronized cursor and zoom: the source-verified ECharts `connect` group (value-carried `updateAxisPointer`, percent-based `dataZoom` under a stable id), the page-owned shared window with its empty-group/late-joiner rules, the D-148-deferred merge-based `setOption`, and the declined in-chart `axisPointer.link` (spec §14.4, §14.1; task 178)

**Date:** 2026-11-04 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§14.4](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#144-history-charts), [§14.1](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#141-general-ui-requirements) · **Tasks:** [178](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-148 (the chart architecture extended: the runtime seam, the requested-bounds window every chart of a page shares — the property the percent relay stands on —, and the deferred merge-based update this entry owns), D-149 (the two-grid strip layout the zoom must carry along; the `axisPointer` link it suggested, evaluated and declined below), D-150 (the tick ladder the zoom span re-walks; the hour floor that bounds the zoom's `minValueSpan`; the sub-hour rungs this entry deliberately does not add), D-147 (the range radios that stay the load authority — a zoom never re-queries; the refresh re-anchor that resets the zoom), D-133 (the token-only color rule the new axisPointer label follows), D-134 (the recording-runtime seam pattern the sync wiring is proven through), D-127 (the CSP the connect relay is neutral to — actions and canvas painting, no DOM styling), D-132 (the catalog discipline the three new affordance strings follow)

**Decision.** Task 178 lands §14.4's "Synchronized cursor and zoom across charts on the same page" and pins six interpretations, every ECharts-behavior claim verified against the 6.1.0 source in `node_modules` before design froze. (Correction trail: the task's review round — kimi as the first fallback (the primary deepseek-v4.1-flash timed out with no report), one round, REQUEST_CHANGES with 1 P1 / 2 P2 — was folded in before landing, the D-148/D-149 precedent: the **P1** — the announcement live region's text was a computed over the live zoom window, so a polite screen reader re-announced on EVERY wheel tick inside one zoom (the sentence is now snapshotted at the transition; pinned by a no-re-announce cell that zooms again inside the same window) — and the two **P2s**: the resize re-fit gate compared the ladder over the FULL window span while the option walks the ZOOM span (a resize while zoomed kept the stale tick density; the gate now reads the active tick window, pinned by an isolation cell whose width pair holds the full-window step while moving the zoom step — plot 284 → 447: 2-day/2-day but 12-hour → 6-hour), and the e2e cell proved only the source chart's own event (a broken relay would have passed it; the cell now also asserts the second chart's canvas bitmap CHANGES — negative-checked by building with the group join removed, which fails the cell).) (1) **The mechanism is ECharts' `connect` registry, driven through the runtime seam.** `echarts/core` exports `connect(groupId)`; instances carry a `group` property; `enableConnect` (lib/core/echarts.js) relays every registered action's event between the group's instances when the group is registered (loop-guarded by the CONNECT_STATUS_PENDING handshake, so relays cannot ping-pong). The runtime's `createChart(element, {syncGroup})` sets `chart.group` and registers the group — the ONLY echarts knowledge added to the seam, everything else rides the option. The cursor path is the registry's own designed one: the hover dispatches the `updateAxisPointer` action; its handler (`axisTrigger`) returns a payload carrying `axesInfo[{axisDim, axisIndex, value}]` plus a sample `seriesIndex`/`dataIndex`; the relayed action re-triggers the receiving chart BY VALUE (its own tooltip rendered through its own richText channel — the internal `showTip` carries `escapeConnect: true`, the library's own loop break, and the canvas+richText pair stays CSP-neutral). The zoom path is the same registry relaying the batched, percent-based `dataZoom` action (`roams.js` dispatches `{type:'dataZoom', batch:[{dataZoomId, start, end}]}`), matched on the receiving chart through `findEffectedDataZooms` BY ID — so the builder declares one inside dataZoom under the STABLE id `qm-chart-x-zoom` on every chart, and percent semantics name identical instants everywhere because every chart's x-extent is the same requested-bounds window (D-148; AxisProxy's percent base is "series data + axis.min/max"). (2) **The zoom lives INSIDE the loaded range and inside D-150's ladder vocabulary.** One inside dataZoom over BOTH x-axes (the strip rides the window; `xAxisIndex: [0]`/`[0,1]` as the strip exists), `filterMode: 'weakFilter'` (a band or strip marker straddling the zoom edge stays, clipped by the grid — the honest retention of an annotation that partially spans the inspected window), `zoomOnMouseWheel: 'shift'` (a wheel over a chart must not trap the page's scroll — §14.1 "suitable for continuous use"), and `minValueSpan: 3_600_000` — the hour floor of D-150's tick ladder, so a zoomed window never renders unlabeled axes; sub-hour rungs stay D-150's recorded follow-up, deliberately not added here. The zoom re-queries nothing: D-147's radios and the refresh stay the load authority, and a zoom's span never escapes the requested bounds (percent of the fixed extent). The TICK LADDER re-densifies with the zoom: the card feeds its own `dataZoom` events into the option builder, which walks the zoom span for ticks (`MetricChartOptionInput.zoom`) while the axes' `min`/`max` STAY the requested bounds — the percent base the relay's arithmetic depends on; ECharts renders the customValues that fall inside the live extent (D-150's verified filter), so the two facts compose. (3) **The shared state is page-owned and identity-honest.** `ui/src/charts/sync.ts` (echarts-free, the D-148 pure-helper pattern with Vue refs, the theme plugin's precedent) holds what the page renders: `zoomed` (the reset affordance) and `zoomWindow` (the announcement's instants), derived from the cards' reports (each card normalizes its own `dataZoom` events — a user gesture on one chart and the group's relay onto the others both fire there, in both the batched and the flat event shape, with a 0.001% full-range epsilon). The identity rules: an EMPTY GROUP FORGETS (a range or account switch rebuilds every card — the next window's charts start unzoomed; one window's percent never applies to another window's instants, D-135's no-staleness rule), a LATE JOINER ADOPTS the live window (a card whose own data lands last attaches after its first option and receives the current percent as a dispatch — the group stays aligned by construction), and RESET dispatches to every live handle directly (deterministic and observable at the seam, never relayed through one chart). A refresh re-anchors the rolling window, so a zoomed card resets its own zoom (the old percent would name different instants); an unzoomed card reports nothing — a fresh mount's null report must not wipe a window the other cards still hold. (4) **D-148's deferred merge-based `setOption` follow-through lands as `replaceMerge` over the count-varying families.** Updates call `setOption(option, {replaceMerge: ['series','xAxis','yAxis','grid']})`: those four families fully replace (annotation series and strip axes appear and disappear with the events/peaks props — no stale component survives, the guarantee the old `notMerge` bought), everything else merges, so ECharts' own interaction state — the dataZoom window this task adds, a legend series toggle — persists across data, view, theme, and tick updates instead of being wiped by a full replace. Stable ids on every grid, axis, and series make the merge matching index-independent (the y-axis indices shift when bands appear or disappear; ids cannot), and the rebuilt option never declares `dataZoom.start/end`, so the live range survives every update (merge keeps absent keys). (5) **§14.1 surfaces.** A keyboard-operable native "Reset zoom" button in the charts header renders exactly while a zoom is live (an honest state, never dead chrome); a polite `role="status"` live region announces the TRANSITIONS only (the applied window's instants through `formatChartDate` in the display zone, or the reset sentence) — one sentence per transition, never per wheel tick, the range-fallback notice's pattern. The cursor's on-axis label gains a formatter and token colors: ECharts' default renders the raw epoch-ms scale value (`scale.getLabel`, not the axis formatter) in its built-in theme colors — both fixed in the same option (`axisPointer.label.formatter` through the zone, colors through the tooltip tokens, D-133). Three catalog keys under `overview.chart.*`. (6) **The in-chart `axisPointer.link` D-149 suggested is DECLINED, with the source-found reason recorded.** A linked target axis processes with `noSnap` (axisTrigger's link pass), so linking the strip's x-axis to the main's would make the strip's NEAREST marker join every main-grid hover's tooltip params — unbounded by distance, stating a failure at instants that had none — and the interval gating that would bound it (the resets' (previous, snapped] rule) breaks roughly half of all direct marker hovers (the snap lands on the line series, not the marker). The cross-chart relay — the actual §14.4 sentence — never needed the link: the relayed `axesInfo` targets the same axis index on every chart (main hovers sync main plots, strip hovers sync strips), and the two grids' pointer lines stay individually honest. Declining costs only the within-chart pointer co-movement, recorded here as the residual.

**Reasons.** The connect registry is the only cross-instance mechanism the library ships, and the source reading settled both halves of its fitness before design froze: the `updateAxisPointer` payload carries the hovered VALUE (so receiving charts align by instant, not pixel — the charts have different widths and y-scales), and the `dataZoom` payload is percent-based over an extent every chart shares by D-148's own construction (so one shared id suffices to keep every chart's window identical). The alternatives were worse on the same evidence: a manual pixel relay needs per-target `convertToPixel` and its own loop-guarding for no gain, and a slider zoom adds chrome §14.4 never asked for. The page-owned coordinator exists because the registry cannot answer the page's questions — whether a zoom is live (the affordance) and which instants it covers (the announcement) are app state, and the identity rules (forget on empty, adopt on join, reset on re-anchor) are the app's honesty rules, not the library's. The merge follow-through was forced by this task's own feature: a `notMerge` update would wipe the user's zoom on every theme flip, tick refit, or late-arriving annotation — the exact interaction state this task exists to keep; `replaceMerge` over the four count-varying families preserves the old guarantee (no stale component) while the state survives. The `minValueSpan` floor is D-150's own boundary made executable: the ladder stops at the hour, so the zoom must too, until a future task adds the sub-hour rungs D-150 already scoped.

**Consequences.** UI-side: `ui/src/charts/sync.ts` (the coordinator: `createChartSync`, `zoomPercentOf`, the `ChartSync`/`ChartZoomPercent`/`ChartZoomWindow`/`ChartZoomReport` shapes), the extended `ui/src/charts/runtime.ts` (`connect` + `DataZoomInsideComponent` + an explicit `AxisPointerComponent` beside the transitive pull, `createChart(element, {syncGroup})`, and the `ChartHandle` growth: `on`/`off` over one event name, `dispatchAction` over one action, with the batched-and-flat `ChartDataZoomEvent` and the `replaceMerge`-carrying setOption opts), the extended `ui/src/charts/series.ts` (`CHART_X_ZOOM_ID`, `MIN_ZOOM_SPAN_MS`, the `dataZoom`/`axisPointer` option members, the `zoom` tick-window input, and the stable ids on grids/axes/series), `MetricHistoryChart.vue` (the `sync` prop, the attach-after-first-option/detach-on-release lifecycle, the zoom→ticks feedback, the guarded identity/refresh resets, the merge-mode update), `OverviewView.vue` (the coordinator, the reset button, the announcement live region), and the three `overview.chart.{resetZoom,zoomApplied,zoomReset}` catalog keys.
