## D-156 — Task 179's settings page: the browser-own IANA search vocabulary with the canonical-twin match, the always-rendered password section with its twice-stated revocation consequence, the annotations consumed verbatim from the served contract, and the minimal attempted writes (spec §14.5, §6.4, §6.2, §9.2, §14.1, §7.1, §11.3, §15.2; task 179)

**Date:** 2026-11-05 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§14.5](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#145-settings), [§6.4](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#64-change-application), [§6.2](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#62-configuration-contract), [§9.2](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#92-configuration-and-validation), [§14.1](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#141-general-ui-requirements), [§7.1](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#71-polling), [§11.3](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#113-retention-and-cleanup), [§15.2](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#152-passwords-and-sessions) · **Tasks:** [179](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-130 (the annotated settings endpoints the page renders from — the `source`/`restartRequired` markings, the `attempted`-only write semantics, and the restart-trio refusal the page mirrors by offering no control), D-140 (the composition that serves the endpoints and applies the minimal writes), D-134 (the page contract: `useApi()`/`useApiCall`/`ApiErrorNotice`, the UI-local-constant-pinned-by-test precedent), D-133 (the theme controller the page's row reuses, keys under `settings.*`), D-135/D-136 (the failed-load rule and the write-only field discipline), D-124/D-126 (the password change's revocation consequence), D-118/D-141 (the password-settle channels — the UI rides `auth.password`, never a hash), D-132 (the catalog discipline the `settings.*` namespace follows), D-147 (the retention the range controls read — the interplay stated in the field's hint), D-023 (the standing no-precedence-re-derivation rule the annotations consume)

**Decision.** Task 179 lands the §14.5 page as one view plus three section components and pins six interpretations. (Correction trail: the task's review round — deepseek-v4.1-flash, one round, REQUEST_CHANGES with 1 P1 / 2 P2 / 8 P3 — was folded in before landing, the D-148/D-149 precedent. The P1: the password section's configured line now flips with its own success (`passwordConfigured || changed`) — a stale "No password is set." beside the revocation notice contradicted the change the operator just made, and the form does not trigger the parent's reload (the change revoked the session; the fact is known locally). The P2s: the client guards now validate **only the fields the request will send** — a served zone the browser's `Intl` disputes (ICU skew against the server's Node, an environment-supplied zone this engine does not know) no longer blocks an unrelated save or points at a disabled input — and the claimed test arms landed for real (the inclusive boundary accepts 60/3600 and 7/3650, the exactly-12 password beside the 11 refusal, the whitespace-only D-011 refusal, and the `restartRequired: false` marker direction — the annotations are consumed, never assumed). Of the P3s, seven were accepted (the × rate prefix moved into a catalog message, the picked-suggestion stale-error clearing, the pending-restart notice surviving a client-refused submit, the password input disabled while pending, the dead exports `parseWholeInteger`/`LogLevelChoice` made private/removed, the README theme-keys sentence aligned with `settings.theme.*`, and a 360 px overflow e2e cell beside the a11y cell) and one was declined with reasons (ARIA combobox semantics for the suggestion list — full combobox keyboard handling goes beyond the project's native-controls stance and the suggestion buttons are operable as-is; the loading line stays a plain `<p>` matching every other page's loading line — the a11y follow-up pass is the right owner). One pre-existing nuance the round noted is handed forward rather than fixed: `test/helpers/api.ts`'s `healthySettingsBody` serves `restartRequired: false` for the trio — a shape the real endpoint cannot produce — but `test/helpers/**` is outside this task's carve-out.) (1) **The time-zone search vocabulary is the browser's own IANA list, client-side.** §13 defines no zone-list endpoint and the task's carve-out freezes `src/**`, so the list is `Intl.supportedValuesOf('timeZone')` behind a try/catch seam (an engine without it degrades to free text — the input's validity never depends on the list), and the search is a case-insensitive substring filter (capped at eight, collapsed on an exact pick), **plus a canonical-twin match**: engines list CLDR-canonical names, so a fully typed tzdb primary (`Asia/Kolkata`, `Asia/Kathmandu`) surfaces its listed twin (`Asia/Calcutta`, `Asia/Katmandu`) through `resolvedOptions().timeZone` equivalence — found live during testing (this Node's list has no `Asia/Kolkata`) and pinned by test over the real list. §5.3's explicit-choice rule holds client-side: a blank or non-IANA zone is a field error and no request, never a silent default, and validity mirrors the server's own check (leading `+`/`-` offset identifiers rejected before the `Intl` probe — drift-pinned over a shared probe set; both spellings save). A partial modern alias still matches nothing — the vocabulary is the engine's, and that limit is documented rather than papered over with a UI-side alias table that would drift. (2) **The password section renders in both auth modes with the consequence stated twice.** §14.5 says "in modes that use a password", and `auto` uses one exactly on the §15.1 remote paths — hiding the section in `auto` would strand the operator who set a password (via `init`/`passwd`) with no UI way to change it, so the section always renders with the configured/not-set state line; the D-124/D-126 consequence (a change revokes every session, including the current one) rides the pre-submit hint and the success notice, the §15.2 minimum is guarded client-side on the raw untrimmed value, and the field follows D-136's write-only discipline — masked, never prefilled, cleared after every dispatched attempt (a client-guard refusal keeps the typed value, the accounts form's rule: the operator is mid-edit, not mid-attempt). The password PUT deliberately renders only its revocation outcome; its `restartRequired` list (pending hand-edited file state) is not surfaced there — the dominant fact of that response is the revocation, and the pending-restart notice has one implementation, on the settings save where the operator who hand-edited the file actually lands. (3) **The annotations are consumed, never derived.** Every control's editability and every marker comes from the served `source`/`restartRequired` flags: `source: 'environment'` disables the control and renders §6.3's read-only annotation; `restartRequired` renders §6.4's marker ("restart required") and the remedy line (`quotameter restart`, §6.4's own words) — the restart trio renders no edit controls at all, mirroring D-130's PUT refusal structurally (a control the endpoint would refuse is noise pretending to be functionality). The PUT outcome's `restartRequired` array — D-130's pending-file state, never the request's doing — renders as the pending-restart notice, its field paths mapped through static-literal `t()` lookups. (4) **`logging.level` renders though §14.5 does not name it.** The served contract's fourth live-editable annotated scalar (D-130: "`app` and `logging` are the runtime-modifiable scalars") — hiding an editable served setting would be the dishonest surface; §14.5's enumeration is the page's minimum, not its ceiling. (5) **The writes are minimal by construction.** The PUT body carries exactly the fields whose drafts differ from the served values — D-130/D-140's `attempted` semantics made the client's job: an unchanged value sent anyway is a wasted write against a possibly newer file, and the save button itself refuses the no-change request (§13's `minProperties: 1` never met). (6) **§14.5's "account management/connection tests" is the landed `/accounts` page** (§14.2, D-135): the settings page duplicates nothing — the sentence enumerates the settings surface of the web UI as a whole, and the shell nav already links the management page from every page.

**Reasons.** Every open question had a landed constraint that made one answer the composition of record. The zone list: §13's route table is closed (task 163 publishes it), the task freezes server code, and the browser's list is the same resolver the UI formats every date through — a served list would re-buy, per page load, what `Intl` already guarantees, and the twin match closes the one real gap the browser vocabulary has (CLDR-canonical naming) without inventing a parallel alias table. The password-mode reading follows §15.1's own text about `auto`: the mode "uses" a password conditionally, and a UI surface that disappears under `auto` breaks the §15.2 change channel for exactly the deployment that most needs it (remote exposure). The annotations rule is D-023's standing instruction applied once more — the page that re-derives precedence re-derives it wrong eventually. The minimal-write rule is D-140's own write-side discipline mirrored client-side: the store persists only attempted fields, so the client attempts only changed fields. The `logging.level` call is the honest-surface principle: §14.5's "Expose … " list is read as the page's required minimum beside a served contract that names four live scalars, and the page ships what the contract owns.

**Consequences.** UI-side: `ui/src/views/SettingsView.vue` (the loads, the read-only facts and paths, the theme row on the shared controller), `ui/src/components/SettingsGeneralForm.vue`, `SettingsPasswordForm.vue`, `SettingsScheduleSection.vue`, the pure `ui/src/timezones.ts` and `ui/src/settings-fields.ts` (the UI-local ranges/enum/minimum, drift-pinned against `AppConfigSchema`'s bounds, `LOG_LEVELS`, and `MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH` — no runtime import of server code), and the `settings.*` catalog namespace replacing the placeholder `status` key. The §9.2 schedule renders in its own zone with days/times/multipliers verbatim; `peakHours: null` and `windows: []` both render the spec's exact not-configured sentence, and the registry-empty build states that honestly. Tests: `test/component/settings-view.spec.ts` (the editability matrix, the validation arms with no-dispatch pins, the PUT grammar incl. the suggestion-pick and canonical-twin flows and the pending-restart notice, the password matrix incl. the 11/12 boundary and the write-only pins, the schedule matrix, and the theme cross-control agreement at the shell level) and `test/component/timezones.spec.ts` (the server-agreement probes, the engine-list facts incl. the pinned-ICU `Asia/Calcutta` naming, the filter table incl. the twin and the partial-alias limit). E2E: the per-theme axe scan of the populated page through route interception, and the csp-shell deep link moves to `/login` — the settings page is API-loading now and that construction wires no data routes (the D-135 `/accounts` precedent; task 180 inherits the displacement when the login page gains loads). Hand-offs: task 180's session-aware UI will meet a password change whose current session is revoked — the success notice already says so; a future zone-list endpoint (if ever wanted) supersedes interpretation (1) and should retire the twin match with it. Known residual, recorded: the engine-list assertions pin this container's ICU naming (`Asia/Calcutta`); an ICU bump that renames the zone updates the pin, the same trade the D-097 TZ matrix makes with its zone facts.

## D-157 — The CI supply-chain pins: the Node runtime archive verified against repository-pinned SHA-256 constants (not a run-time SHASUMS fetch), and the Dependabot `dependencies` label resolved by creating the metadata, not by weakening the config (spec §4.4; task U-033)

**Date:** 2026-11-04 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§4.4](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#44-cicd-and-supply-chain-safeguards) · **Tasks:** [U-033](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-045 (the CI shape whose `install` job is hardened), D-152 (the U-029 guard pattern this task extends and the pin-sync discipline it borrows), U-004 (the missing-label failure class the Dependabot half repeats)

**Decision.** U-033 closes the two verified supply-chain gaps and pins their mechanisms. (Correction trail: the task's review round — deepseek-v4.1-flash, one round, APPROVE with 0 P0 / 0 P1 / 2 P2 / 5 P3, the digests and the live label re-verified by the reviewer — was folded in before landing, the D-154/D-155 precedent. Both P2s and all five P3s were accepted: the guard had pinned the verification line's PRESENCE, not its fail-closed execution — a `#`-prefixed, `|| true`-suffixed, `set +e`-softened, or `continue-on-error: true`-shielded line all passed while disabling the check — so the download, verification, and extraction lines are now pinned as EXACT shapes (a softened line fails), and the version-consistency set gained the install job's `node -v` expectation, the unsupported-node error grep, the step NAME's embedded version, and `package.json`'s `engines.node`; plus the extraction is tied to the exact verified path, the documented repair command gained `--repo yepbro/quotameter`, and a wrong D-054 citation was corrected to U-004.) (1) **The Node archive is verified against SHA-256 constants pinned in the workflow, in repository history.** The `install` job's download step now carries the two official `SHASUMS256.txt` digests for `node-v22.13.0-linux-<arch>.tar.xz` (source `https://nodejs.org/dist/v22.13.0/SHASUMS256.txt`, retrieved 2026-11-04, archives re-downloaded and verified to match before pinning), selects one by a `case` arm, and checks the downloaded file with `echo "<digest>  /tmp/node.tar.xz" | sha256sum -c -` AFTER the download and BEFORE the `tar -xJf` extraction (GNU `sha256sum` wants two spaces; GitHub's default `bash -e -o pipefail` fails the step on mismatch; `sha256sum` is coreutils, Priority: required, present in all three base images). The alternative — fetching `SHASUMS256.txt` from the same CDN at run time — is rejected as security theater: an attacker who can tamper with the archive can tamper with the checksum file served beside it, so the run-time fetch verifies the mirror against itself and stops nothing. The repository is the root of trust precisely because branch protection makes its history the one domain a compromised mirror cannot rewrite — the same reasoning as the SHA-pinned actions (docs/agents/workflow.md). The step also gains a `version=22.13.0` variable (URL, digests' source, and the symlink source all read it; the bump procedure edits one line plus two digests and is written out in the step's comment) and a fail-closed `*)` arm so an unknown architecture exits with a clear message instead of downloading an empty-arch URL. (2) **The Dependabot label is resolved by creating the metadata, not by weakening the config.** The `dependencies` label — assigned by both dependabot.yml update blocks, absent from the repository (verified: `gh label list` showed only the GitHub defaults plus U-004's `mutation-report`) — was created live once: `gh label create dependencies --repo yepbro/quotameter --description "Dependency updates (Dependabot)" --color 0366d6` (exit 0, verified present afterwards; repository metadata, not a push). The two alternatives are rejected on structure: an in-workflow bootstrap cannot work for Dependabot — U-004's bootstrap succeeds because the mutation workflow consumes its label in the same run after creating it, while no workflow of ours runs before Dependabot opens its PRs (a GitHub-managed service); bolting the bootstrap onto ci.yml would grant `issues: write` to the most-exposed workflow in the repository (it runs on every fork PR, where the token is read-only anyway and the step would silently no-op) — a least-privilege regression for no real coverage. Removing `labels:` from dependabot.yml is rejected because Dependabot's default label set for these ecosystems also references `dependencies`, so removal does not remove the dependency on the label existing — it only makes the reference implicit and the failure less discoverable. The repair one-liner is documented in the dependabot.yml header and docs/agents/workflow.md. (3) **The guard pin set.** The new `test/unit/ci-workflow.spec.ts` (the U-029 line-scanner pattern over ci.yml: no YAML dependency, loud throws, actionlint owns the block shape) pins: the download/verify/extract lines as EXACT shapes in verify-after-download-before-extract order (the extraction reads the exact path the digest verified), with `set +e` and `continue-on-error: true` banned from the step so the check is fail-closed, not decorative; the two digest literals bound to their architecture arms (a swap or one-character corruption fails); the fail-closed arm; the version consistency across ci.yml and the manifest — the install step's `version=` and step name, the test matrix's `'22.13.0'` declared-minimum entry, the timezone job's `node-version: 22.13.0` ICU-oracle pin, the install job's `test "$(node -v)" = "v22.13.0"` expectation, the unsupported-node job's `grep -F "22.13.0"` error grep, the documented SHASUMS source URL (derived from the spec's `PINNED_VERSION`, so a bump cannot leave it stale), and `package.json`'s `engines.node` — so ANY bump must edit the spec's `PINNED_VERSION` and `PINNED_DIGESTS` in the same change (the D-155 deliberate-update discipline); and the dependabot half — both update blocks keep declaring `dependencies`, and the `gh label create dependencies` repair stays documented. The hermetic suite cannot verify live repository metadata (and must not try); the text pin keeps the declaration deliberate and the repair discoverable.

**Reasons.** The P1-3 defect is a classic verify-the-artifact gap: the workflow already paid the trust cost of SHA-pinning its actions but downloaded the runtime itself blind, and the runtime is the more critical artifact — everything the install smoke tests prove is proven about bytes an attacker could have chosen. Pinning the constants in the repository is the only placement where verification crosses a trust boundary; every alternative that keeps the digest on the same host as the archive verifies nothing. The version-consistency pins exist because a digest without its version is meaningless: a future bump that changes the version but keeps the old digests would fail closed at run time (mismatch) but loudly and only in CI — the guard moves that failure to `make check` and forces the editor through the documented procedure. The label resolution follows the failure class, not the symptom: the U-004 evidence (a validation run failing `could not add label: 'mutation-report' not found`) established that label assignment requires pre-existing metadata, so the durable fix is metadata plus a documented repair, not a config retreat that leaves the same missing reference in Dependabot's defaults.

**Consequences.** A compromised Node mirror can no longer inject the runtime the install smoke tests run on without also breaking the digest check; a supply-chain incident upstream of `nodejs.org` becomes a loud CI failure naming the mismatch. Bumping the pinned Node version is a documented procedure in the workflow's comment (the step's `version=` and name, the two digests, the next step's `node -v` literal, the unsupported-node grep literal, `package.json`'s `engines.node`, then the spec's pinned version and digest literals) that `make check` enforces mechanically; editing any pinned line — digests, `version=`, the exact download/verify/extract shapes, the fail-closed arm, the dependabot label declaration, or the repair comment — requires updating the guard in the same change. The `dependencies` label is repository state, not repository content: forks and any future label deletion re-break Dependabot labeling until the documented one-liner is run — the same accepted residual U-004 carries for `mutation-report`. `docs/agents/workflow.md`'s Dependabot section and `docs/agents/gotchas.md`'s CI notes now carry both truths. Renaming the `install` job's Node-archive step requires updating the guard's scanner regex in the same change.

## D-159 — Task 180's login/logout UI: the mode-agnostic tri-state session cache (no boot probe, `GET /api/auth/session` stays unwired), the client-boundary `onUnauthenticated` interception superseding D-134's notice-branch seam, the open-redirect-guarded destination preservation, and the post-sign-out document reload (spec §14.6, §15.1, §15.2; task 180)

**Date:** 2026-11-05 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§14.6](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#146-statuses-and-authentication-screens), [§15.1](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#151-network-and-authentication-modes), [§15.2](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#152-passwords-and-sessions), [§14.1](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#141-general-ui-requirements), [§15.4](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#154-secret-protection) · **Tasks:** [180](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-146 (the login/logout endpoints this UI consumes — the wire arms, the invisible budget delays with the 240 s clamp, the idempotent `{revoked}` logout — whose consequences explicitly left `GET /api/auth/session` to this task's consumer), D-134 (the client/page contract and the `UNAUTHENTICATED` notice branch whose predicted seam this entry moves to the client boundary), D-121 (the §15.1 mode semantics the tri-state mirrors without mode knowledge), D-123/D-124/D-126 (the mint/verdict/cookie construction that makes the cookie the session's only client-visible truth), D-117 (the §15.3 bodiless mutation shape logout carries), D-131/D-132/D-133/D-135 (the factory+plugin+inject pattern and the catalog discipline the new modules follow), D-136 (the write-only secret-field discipline the password form follows), D-156 (the settings-page interplay — a password change revokes the session and that page's notice says so; and the predicted csp-shell `/login` displacement this task's load-free design voids), D-138 (the route-interception e2e technique the login suite reuses)

**Decision.** Task 180 lands §14.6's authentication screens — the `/login` password form (`ui/src/views/LoginView.vue`), the shell-header sign-out control (`ui/src/App.vue`), and the session layer that routes them (`ui/src/session.ts`, new) — and pins six interpretations. (Correction trail: the task's review round — deepseek-v4.1-flash, one round, REQUEST_CHANGES with 2 P2 / 6 P3 — was folded in before landing (the D-146/D-156 precedent; the resume session's round was the task's first, the predecessor draft never reached one). The P2s are now interpretations, not patches: (2)'s login-arm exemption (a rejected candidate is a statement about the candidate, not the session — in the passwordless `auto`-loopback deployment every login 401s, and letting one flip the state would brick SPA navigation until a reload, while the guard blocks the very loads that would disprove the state for a valid-cookie visitor who mistypes) and (3)'s string-location bounce (vue-router parses query and hash out of string locations but silently drops them from a `{ path }` object, so a preserved destination carrying either lost them). Of the P3s, five were accepted — the at-dispatch password clear (the candidate never lingers through the possibly minutes-long pending window), the sign-out control hidden on the login route (an authenticated visitor never sits there), the shell's failed-sign-out notice cleared on the next completed navigation, the `loginReturnTarget` hardening (any backslash rejected — browsers normalize `\` to `/`, the `//` escape's twin — and the login self-check made case-insensitive and trailing-slash tolerant), and the test waits raised to the 30 s house budget — and one was declined with reasons: the stale in-flight 401 that re-demotes a freshly signed-in session is real but unfixable without also breaking the legitimate demotion (a password change revokes sessions; the next protected load's 401 MUST re-demote an `authenticated` state — no client-side generation can tell the two apart), the bounced user lands on the login page where a resubmit recovers immediately, and the window requires an in-flight request that outlives a human login; recorded as the known residual.) (1) **The session model is a tri-state, in-memory, wire-signal cache — and the UI never learns the §15.1 mode.** `createSession()`/`useSession()` (the D-131…D-135 factory+plugin+inject shape) hold `'unknown' | 'authenticated' | 'unauthenticated'`: `unknown` is the honest start (no signal this SPA lifetime) and renders protected pages optimistically — in `auto` + loopback, §15.1's default, no 401 ever arrives, nothing forces `/login`, and the login page stays reachable by URL, exactly §14.6/§15.1's semantics for the mode that requires no password; `unauthenticated` is what the wire's §13 `UNAUTHENTICATED` envelope answers set; `signOut()` resets to `unknown`, deliberately not `unauthenticated` (under `auto`-loopback the overview keeps working after a sign-out — the next wire answer, not the store, says which world it is). Nothing persists: the cookie is the session's only truth (§15.2/D-126), a reload honestly restarts at `unknown`, and the store is a reactive cache of what the wire last said. **No boot probe exists**: D-146 left `GET /api/auth/session` to "task 180's UI consumer", but this task's carve-out froze `src/**` (a sibling storage task owns it — the endpoint cannot land here), and the stronger reason is that the tri-state needs no probe — the cookie rides every request, so the first protected load discovers the truth with no extra round trip, and the only mode-fact surface (`/api/settings`) is itself protected under `required`: a probe cannot serve the visitor the login page exists for. §14.6's "provide a login page when the active authentication mode requires a password" is satisfied by the wire-driven redirect — the deployment that requires a password proves it on every protected load. The session row stays §13's unwired future work, recorded here as the successor seam. (2) **The interception point is the client's classification boundary, superseding D-134's notice-branch prediction.** `ApiClientOptions.onUnauthenticated` fires whenever a response classifies as the §13 envelope with `code === 'UNAUTHENTICATED'` — whatever session-bearing family dispatched it, whatever page presents or drops the error — so an error whose notice never mounts still flips the session; the composition root wires it to `markUnauthenticated()` and the error still throws exactly as without the hook. **The login arm alone opts out** (`RequestSpec.reportUnauthenticated: false`): a rejected candidate is a statement about the candidate, not about the browser's session — without the exemption, the passwordless `auto`-loopback deployment (where every attempt 401s) would brick SPA navigation off one curious submit, and a valid-cookie visitor's mistype would demote a state the guard then prevents the proving loads from ever disproving. `ApiErrorNotice`'s `UNAUTHENTICATED` branch (D-134's documented seam) remains the _presentation_ such an answer keeps while the session layer's redirect takes the page away. (3) **Redirect mechanics preserve the destination and validate it.** `installSessionRouting(router, session)` — the composition root's one call, before the initial navigation — installs a `beforeEach` guard (an authenticated visit to `/login` bounces to the preserved destination as a STRING location — vue-router parses query and hash out of string locations but silently drops them from a `{ path }` object, and a preserved destination may carry either; an unauthenticated navigation to a protected target answers `/login?redirect=<fullPath>` with no API round trip and no flash of the protected page) plus a reactive watcher on the state (a flip while a protected page is already rendered navigates the same way; never from the login route itself — a protected page's late 401 can land while the form is up and must not re-navigate onto it; the form's own 401s never reach the signal at all under (2)'s exemption). `loginReturnTarget(redirect)` treats the `redirect` query as attacker-influenceable like any URL input: only a same-origin SPA path passes (leading `/`, no `//` protocol-relative open-redirect escape, no backslash anywhere — browsers normalize `\` to `/`, the same escape's twin — nothing resolving onto the login route itself in any casing or trailing-slash form, else the guard's bounce would loop), everything else collapses to `/`; unknown paths pass verbatim because the catch-all sends them to `/` anyway (§14 prescribes no not-found screen). (4) **The login form is mode-agnostic, load-free, and waits §15.2's delays out.** Zero fetch on mount — the §14.6 page must render before any credential exists, the property the csp-shell e2e cells stand on (D-156's predicted displacement of the `/login` deep link therefore did not materialize, by design). The password field is write-only (D-136): masked, `autocomplete="current-password"`, never prefilled, cleared AT DISPATCH (the body is built synchronously, so the attempted candidate never lingers in the field through the possibly minutes-long pending window), sent verbatim and never trimmed — §15.2's 12-character minimum binds whoever _sets_ a password (`init`/`passwd`/the settings page), never the verifier; the only client-side guard is the blank check. Failures are catalog sentences selected by the envelope's `details.reason` (D-134's discipline — the payload never renders): `invalid-credentials` and `source-busy` (D-146's two distinguishable arms) get their own sentences, an absent/unknown/hostile reason gets the generic failure, never a guess. Because the budget's delays are invisible on the wire (D-146: delays, never rejections), the form states the behavior up front (an always-visible hint) and the request carries its own deadline — `LOGIN_TIMEOUT_MS` = 250 s, above the endpoint's 240 s `MAX_LOGIN_DELAY_SLEEP_MS` and below the construction's 300 s socket-inactivity bound, pinned by constants test (UI-local, no runtime server import — D-134's rule): racing the 15 s client default would abort before the honest verdict and goad a retry that pays a doubled delay — the client working against §15.2's own mechanism. (5) **Sign-out ends in a document reload, not a router push.** A successful logout resets the store and `window.location.assign('/')`: a router push to `/` would be deduped by vue-router when the current route already is `/` (no remount, no fresh loads, and under `required` no 401 to drive the redirect — the defect the e2e invalidation proof caught in the first draft), while the reload restarts the SPA honestly at `unknown` and the next wire answers decide the world — under `required` the fresh overview load's 401 redirects to `/login?redirect=/`; under `auto`-loopback the overview simply renders — mode-correct routing without mode knowledge, and every in-memory artifact of the authenticated session dies with the document. A 401 logout answer (a dead cookie under `required`) presents nothing: the hook fires and the watcher navigates — a notice would talk over the redirect; every other failure (the service unreachable mid-sign-out) rides the shared `ApiErrorNotice` in the shell, cleared on the next completed navigation (the shell persists across routes — the notice belongs to the sign-out interaction, and a retry re-presents a condition that still holds). The control is visible unless the wire said `unauthenticated` or the current route is the login page (an authenticated visitor never sits there — the guard bounces them — so on that page the control is noise about an unproven session); there is no login nav entry (§14.6 asks for a page — the redirect and the URL reach it; the three-section nav is pinned by the shell spec). (6) **The settings interplay is D-156's recorded seam executing**: a password change revokes every session including the current one, that page's success notice already says so, and this task's layer needs nothing more — the next protected load's 401 drives the login redirect with the destination preserved.

**Reasons.** The mode question forced the architecture: §14.6 conditions the login page on the active mode, but every mode-fact the wire exposes is itself protected in the mode where the answer matters — so any boot-probe design either leaks protection or cannot serve its user, while the cookie-plus-401 design needs no new endpoint, no new round trip, and degrades honestly (the `unknown` state never guesses; `auto`-loopback simply never redirects). The client-boundary interception over the notice branch is the stronger version of D-134's own hand-off: the notice mounts only on pages that present the error, but the session flip must follow the signal wherever it arrives — including loads whose failures are presented elsewhere or dropped; the notice keeps its sentence, so presentation loses nothing. The destination validation is the standard open-redirect calculus for an attacker-influenceable query parameter, with the `/login`-self-collapse added because the guard's authenticated-bounce would otherwise loop. The 250 s deadline sits between the two landed constants it must respect — D-146's clamp (the honest answer never arrives later) and D-109's socket bound (the connection never dies first) — and pinning the relation by test keeps the three from drifting apart silently. The post-sign-out reload is forced by vue-router's same-route dedup, and it composes with the in-memory-session design instead of fighting it: the reload IS the honest "back to knowing nothing", already the documented semantics of the store.

**Consequences.** The exported surface (`SessionState`, `SessionController`, `createSession`, `useSession`, `loginReturnTarget`, `createSessionGuard`, `installSessionRouting` in `ui/src/session.ts`; `LOGIN_TIMEOUT_MS`, `ApiClientOptions.onUnauthenticated`, `ApiClient.auth` in the client; `LOGIN_ROUTE_NAME` in the router) is internal UI API; changing the tri-state's meaning, the hook's contract, the destination-validation rules, or the post-sign-out reload semantics is a successor decision. `GET /api/auth/session` remains §13's unwired row — a future server-side task that lands it should treat this entry's no-probe rationale as the baseline it supersedes (a served session/mode fact could, for instance, make the sign-out control's visibility exact instead of wire-derived, or pre-seed the state on deep links before the first protected load answers). The login page's zero-fetch property is load-bearing for the csp-shell e2e construction (no data routes wired there) and must survive future changes to the page. Under `vite preview` (no API) the login form renders with zero requests — the honest degradation — and the shell's other pages keep their `unexpected` notices. The done-condition ("protected pages redirect appropriately and logout invalidates the session") is pinned executably: `test/component/session.spec.ts` (the store, the destination table incl. the open-redirect arms, the guard matrix, the reactive redirect incl. the stay-on-login and guard-holds cells), `test/component/login-view.spec.ts` (the zero-fetch first paint, the blank guard, the exact §15.3 wire shape, the destination round trip incl. the unsafe collapse, the write-only pins, the D-146 arm matrix incl. hostile/absent reasons and retry clearing, the shared-notice arms, the pending locks), `test/component/api-client.spec.ts` (the auth round trips bodied/bodiless, the per-request deadline override proof, the `LOGIN_TIMEOUT_MS` relation pin, the hook's firing matrix and its no-behavior-change pin), `test/component/app.spec.ts` (the control, the logout wire pin, the document-reload routing), the updated shell/wiring/settings-view mounts, and `test/e2e/login.spec.ts` (the 401 → `/login?redirect` → sign-in → destination round trip with the destination's real content rendered, both failure arms' distinct sentences, and the sign-out invalidation — the next protected load redirects) beside the per-theme axe scans of the form. `ui/README.md` gains the section; `CHANGELOG.md` carries the boundary. No public API, format, or event changes — the HTTP surface is D-146's, unchanged.

## D-160 — The systemd availability predicate: marker-gated verification (absent, present-but-inert, live), patterns-never-exit-codes classification, and the CI test jobs' systemd-less environment pin (spec §5.1, §5.2, §5.3, §5.5; orchestrator task t-ci-systemd)

**Date:** 2026-11-05 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§5.1](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#51-supported-environment), [§5.2](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#52-cli-commands), [§5.3](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#53-init-workflow), [§5.5](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#55-doctor) · **Tasks:** — (one-off orchestrator task, no plan entry) · **References:** D-103 (the "the CI images ship no systemd" test-environment premise this entry re-establishes and re-scopes), D-106 (the route matrix consuming the probe — its semantics are unchanged; only the capability facts feeding it are classified more honestly), D-105/D-108/D-110/D-114/D-116 (the surfaces whose capability seams widen), D-157 (the CI supply-chain pins this entry's runner pin joins)

**Decision.** `probeServiceCapabilities` (src/cli/service-setup.ts) classifies the machine into four classes. (1) **Absent** — `/run/systemd/system` missing → `caps(false, false)` with **no process spawned**: the marker stays the cheap gate, so the development container, plain Docker containers, and the CI test runners (below) probe deterministically and spawn-free, exactly as before. (2) **Present-but-inert** — the marker exists but `systemctl is-system-running` answers with systemd's own inertness diagnostics (the bus-connect failure, in **both of systemd's wording generations** — ≤256's `Failed to connect to bus: …` and ≥257's `Failed to connect to {system,user} scope bus via local transport: …`, the review round's live-verified catch on a systemd-259 host), or a spawn failure of the binary itself (`spawn systemctl …` — Node's own message shape, every errno alike) → `caps(false, false)`: the **same graceful §5.3/§5.2 fallbacks as absent** ("systemd is not available on this machine…", manual-run/completion steps), never raw systemctl errors. Real-world members: chroots and zones with the host's `/run` visible, WSL without systemd, stripped container images that keep the marker but not the client, and any machine whose bus is dead while the marker lives. (3) **Live system manager, unreachable user manager** — the system probe answered; `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` is unset/empty/inherited, its `systemd` entry is missing, or `systemctl --user is-active default.target` answers inert → `caps(true, false)` — the existing class (cron, ssh without a session), now verified rather than assumed from filesystem facts alone (a stale runtime directory no longer routes into `--user` commands that can only fail with bus errors). (4) **Live** — both probes answered → `caps(true, true)`. Three pinned interpretations: **exit codes are never classifiers** — `is-system-running` exits 1 for a live-but-degraded system and `is-active` exits 3/4 for inactive/unknown units, so a manager answering with a non-success state is still a manager; only the inertness patterns (and the spawn-failure shape) are, matched case-insensitively against the single captured stderr line, and the classifier is deliberately conservative in the live direction (misreading a live manager as absent costs the manual steps; misreading an inert machine as live reproduces exactly the raw-error class this predicate exists to route away from). **`userManager` implies `systemd`** — a user instance cannot outlive its system manager, so `caps(false, true)` is no longer a producible probe result (the route matrix already treated it as systemd-absent; D-106's semantics are untouched). **The probe is async and bounded** — a claimed manager is verified with a real query under a 10 s race (`PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS`, injectable as `CapabilitySeams.probeTimeoutMs`, timer unref'd); a query that cannot answer within the bound classifies its scope not-answering — a wedged bus delays no CLI invocation past the bound and is never misread as live (the losing subprocess is left to D-Bus's own reply timeout; no kill handle crosses the seam). Every `probeCapabilities` seam (`init`, `service install`, `start`/`stop`/`restart`, `status`, `logs`, `doctor` — eight awaited call sites) widens to `CapabilityProbe = () => ServiceCapabilities | Promise<ServiceCapabilities>`, so existing synchronous test injections compile unchanged. The probe commands are read-only and pinned (`['systemctl', 'is-system-running']`, `['systemctl', '--user', 'is-active', 'default.target']`), injected through `CapabilitySeams.probeCommand` (production default `spawnServiceCommand`); a marker-less machine never calls it. **The CI environment half**: GitHub's `ubuntu-latest` moved to the 26.04 image during the announced October 19–November 19, 2026 migration window (this repository's runners flipped between the green 2026-10-29 runs and the red 2026-11-01 runs), whose job sessions run a **live** systemd — evidence from the failing runs: `systemctl --user enable --now` accepted real jobs (`Job for quotameter.service failed because the control process exited with error code`), `stop` of an unloaded unit exited 0, system verbs hit polkit denials, `timedatectl` answered. There, the real-launcher tests cannot stay honest: the owner's home comes from `/etc/passwd` (env `HOME` does not redirect it), so `quotameter service install` through the launcher really writes `~/.config/systemd/user/quotameter.service` and enables it — which the in-process default-seam `init` tests then did, contaminating every later owner-resolving test (doctor's `[pass] user unit is current`, status exit 1, control exit 0 — the cross-test contamination visible in the logs). The `test` job (ci.yml) and the full-suite `mutation` job (mutation.yml) are therefore pinned to `runs-on: ubuntu-24.04` — the systemd-less image class the whole suite was designed around (D-103's premise, quoted in ~ ten suite docblocks) and GitHub's own published mitigation for the migration — with workflow comments stating that re-pointing them at a newer image requires re-working those premises first.

**Reasons.** The orchestrator's brief asked for the inert-class hardening; the run-log forensics showed the new runners are the _live_ class, not the inert one — both facts had to be answered. The predicate change is justified independent of any runner: a mounted-but-dead `/run/systemd/system` is a real machine shape (chroots, WSL1, marker-inheriting containers), and §5.3's "if systemd is unavailable … provide exact manual-run instructions" reads on the _manager's availability_, not on the marker file's existence — a machine whose manager cannot answer any command is exactly the "unavailable" the fallbacks were designed for, and routing it into live-systemd paths produces the raw `System has not been booted with systemd` errors the graceful arms exist to prevent. Exit-code-based classification was rejected on systemd's own semantics (degraded ≠ absent); stderr-pattern classification is stable because the matched strings are systemd's own diagnostics, not human-formatted tables. The runner pin is justified over alternatives: making the real-launcher suites live-systemd-honest is not achievable without either accepting real service installs into the runner's passwd home during tests (unacceptable side effects — exactly the observed contamination) or deleting/weakening the §5.2/§5.3 outcome pins; running the whole job in a `container:` is a larger plumbing change (Playwright browsers, caches) than the one-line image pin; and `ubuntu-24.04` is the exact environment class the suite's documented premise names. The in-process suites keep their existing "production default seams" tests unchanged — their premise (systemd-less test environments) is true again under the pin — and the two init unit suites that never meant to exercise service setup at all now inject the systemd-less capability answer with forbidden command/write seams (the `forbiddenPrompter` precedent), making them hermetic on any host.

**Consequences.** The exported additions (`SYSTEM_PROBE_COMMAND`, `USER_PROBE_COMMAND`, `managerAnswered`, `CapabilityProbe`, `PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS` in service-setup.ts) and the widened `probeCapabilities` seams are internal CLI API: changing the class taxonomy, the inertness pattern set, or the probe commands is a successor decision. `probeServiceCapabilities` returning a Promise is a breaking change for any direct synchronous consumer (none exist outside the eight awaited call sites and the tests updated in the same commit). The CI pin's own consequence: `ubuntu-24.04` will itself be retired eventually — the workflow comments and this entry name the re-working that a newer image requires (hermetic re-design of the real-launcher service suites). Message strings are unchanged: the graceful arms render the same §5.3/§5.2 texts the suites pin, so no public CLI contract moved. Evidence: `test/unit/cli-service-setup.spec.ts`'s rewritten probe block (marker absent ⇒ no spawn; both bus-failure wordings plus the not-booted diagnostic and the spawn-failure shape ⇒ `caps(false,false)` with the user probe never running; the timeout race ⇒ the not-answering class; a degraded-but-live system probe ⇒ `caps(true,false)`; a non-success user-probe state ⇒ `caps(true,true)`; the live/live matrix with both probe commands pinned exactly; the own-property `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` discipline retained), the hermeticity seams in `test/unit/cli-init.spec.ts` / `test/unit/cli-init-yes.spec.ts`, the unchanged "production default seams" suites passing under the restored premise, and the real-launcher integration suites green in the systemd-less container. The review round (deepseek-v4.1-flash, one round, REQUEST_CHANGES with 1 P1 / 2 P2 / 4 P3 considered) was folded in before landing: the P1 (the ≥257 scope-bus wording) and both P2s (the probe timeout; the missing wording/user-state test arms) are now interpretations above, three P3s were fixed (the spawn-failure pattern replacing the `/enoent/i` free-text match, the "fail loudly" comment accuracy, the call-site count), one P3 was declined with reasons (moving the probe behind cheap gates — declined to preserve the entry-evaluated seam-const coverage pattern and because a live machine pays at most two one-digit-millisecond read-only queries that the marker gate already skips entirely on systemd-less machines), and one P3 (the stale `docs/mutation-testing.md` runner mention) was fixed in the same commit. The final CI proof lands on the orchestrator's push to the pinned jobs.

## D-161 — The runtime-verify script's gate pinning: behavioral ordering proof through a module-less-runtime simulation, canonical comparator parity through third consumption of the shared boundary matrix, and the `verify:runtime` npm-script wiring (spec §5.1, §17.2; task U-036)

**Date:** 2026-11-05 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§5.1](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#51-supported-environment), [§17.2](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#172-installationpackage-tests) · **Tasks:** [U-036](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-098 (the launcher's gate this script mirrors and the plain-JS duplication precedent this entry extends), D-155 (the extract-and-execute guard discipline whose "text pins only where execution cannot reach" rule shapes the test), D-157 (the exact-shape wiring pins), U-032 (the evadable-text-pin lesson the ordering proof answers)

**Decision.** U-036's three verified findings were filed against the pre-task-129 tree: the restructure that landed as `2eb8b3c` had already moved the script's `node:sqlite` load behind the version gate (dynamic `await import`) and rewritten its local comparator to the canonical prefix ordering — what remained was that **nothing pinned either property and no test exercised the script at all**. This entry pins them. (1) **The gate-before-import ordering is proven behaviorally, by simulating the module-less runtime.** The unsupported path's simulation seam is the data-URL `--import` preload of `test/integration/cli-bin-version-gate.spec.ts` (redefining the non-writable-but-configurable `process.versions.node` before the module evaluates) extended with one mechanism: the preload also calls `module.register()` on a resolve hook that throws for the specifier `node:sqlite`. On a runtime that _has_ the module — every runtime the suite can actually run on — a static import succeeds and no fake-version test can see the ordering defect; under the hook, the module is unresolvable exactly as on a below-minimum Node, and the discrimination is total: the correctly gated script prints its actionable refusal (`quotameter requires Node.js >= 22.13.0 (found <v>)` plus the `make shell` remedy) and exits 1 with the hook never firing (the dynamic import is never initiated past a rejecting gate), while a hoisted static import dies on the hook before any module body runs — no message, wrong stderr (verified live on the pinned 22.13.0 container for all three behaviors before the suite was written). The same hook proves the supported path's non-vacuity: with the module blocked, the real runtime fails on the blocked import rather than printing a hollow success line. Text pins remain only for the shapes execution cannot reach — the ESM resolve hook intercepts neither `createRequire` requires nor `process.getBuiltinModule` lookups (both verified live under the hook to bypass it) — so the source is pinned to carry exactly one `await import('node:sqlite')` occurrence (the post-gate probe; a second, e.g. a pre-gate swallowed copy, is the defect class) and no static-import spelling, no `createRequire`, no `getBuiltinModule`. (2) **The comparison-rules question closes as canonical parity pinned deliberately, not as reuse.** The script cannot import `src/util/version.ts` (it runs under plain `node` — no jiti, no build step, exactly like the launcher), and extracting a shared plain-JS comparator module for `bin/quotameter.mjs` and the script is rejected because the launcher must keep working from the bin/-only pre-packaging tarball its docblock contracts. Instead the script's copy becomes the **third consumer of the shared boundary matrix** in `test/helpers/nodeVersionGate.ts` (`VERSION_GATE_CASES`): every pass/reject/invalid case is faked into a real child process running the real script, asserting exit code, the message, and the success line — so the canonical rules, the launcher's copy, and the script's copy cannot drift apart silently, and adding a boundary case stays a one-place edit (the helper's docblock now names all three consumers). The matrix also gained a four-segment arm (`22.13.0.1` → invalid: the canonical parse rejects it loudly, the plain-JS copies fail closed). **The derivation and the patch segment are pinned where the matrix alone cannot reach** (the review round's P2, verified by the reviewer: against the real manifest — whose patch is `0` — a major.minor-only comparator passes all eighteen matrix cases, and so would a hardcoded minimum): fixture packages prove the gate follows a raised declaration at the patch level (`>=22.13.5` rejects a faked `22.13.4` naming `22.13.5`, accepts `22.13.5`), a raised minor (`>=22.14.0` rejects `22.13.0`), and a relaxed one (`>=20.0.0` accepts `22.13.0`) — the launcher suite's fixture pattern. The broken-manifest fail-closed branch is covered by the same pattern across its full width: JSON `null`, an empty object, a non-`>=X.Y.Z` range, unparseable JSON, and **no package.json at all** (the script's read/parse catch arm) — every shape reaching the `fix the manifest` message, never a TypeError. (3) **The wiring**: `"verify:runtime": "node scripts/verify-runtime.mjs"` beside `verify:build` in the manifest's scripts (the sibling-consistency the finding asked for), the `make verify-runtime` target rewired from the direct `node` invocation to `npm run verify:runtime` (the shape `make build` already uses for `verify:build`), and both pinned exactly by test — the script entry's value, and the Makefile recipe line. (4) **The exit discipline is the launcher's** (the review round's P2-1, accepted): every refusing arm sets `process.exitCode = 1` and returns from an `async main()` whose if/else chain places the SQLite probe only after the last gate arm — `bin/quotameter.mjs`'s own pipe-flush discipline, adopted once the restructure removed the fall-through risk that had justified the script's earlier `process.exit(1)` calls (an `exitCode`-style conversion of the old linear tail alone would have run the probe on rejected runtimes — the defect itself; the reviewer demonstrated live that an immediate `process.exit` truncates pipe-buffered stderr beyond 64 KiB, and the launcher's documented discipline avoids the hazard class entirely rather than arguing size bounds).

**Reasons.** The ordering pin's design follows D-155's hardening rule in reverse: where U-032 demonstrated that text-only pins are evadable and moved to execution, this suite keeps execution as the primary proof and retains text pins only for the `createRequire`/`getBuiltinModule` sidesteps the resolve hook structurally cannot see. The hook simulation was chosen over the alternatives because it is the only one that exercises the real defect precondition (the module's absence) without a second Node installation: `--no-experimental-sqlite`-style flags do not exist for a module that needs no flag on this runtime, and spawning an actually-old Node is impossible inside the pinned 22.13 container. The parity-via-matrix choice over a shared module preserves the launcher's tarball property at the cost of a second plain-JS comparison copy (the third implementation beside the canonical rules and the launcher's) — the cost the matrix already exists to police (D-098's precedent for two, extended to three by consumption rather than by refactor). The derivation fixtures exist because a matrix driven by the real manifest is structurally blind to patch-level ordering (the minimum's own patch is `0`) and to the derivation itself — the reviewer proved both blindnesses by mutation before the fixtures were written. The Makefile rewire is cosmetic for users (same target, same behavior) but makes the npm script the single invocation path, so the wiring pin has one truth to guard.

**Consequences.** Re-hoisting the sqlite import (static import, bare side-effect import, a duplicate dynamic import, or a `createRequire`/`getBuiltinModule` sidestep) fails `make check` with a message naming the defect class; relaxing the gate's message or exit semantics fails the matrix arms; drifting the script's comparator from the canonical rules fails the shared matrix in this suite just as it already fails in the launcher's and the unit suite (patch-level drift included, via the `>=22.13.5` fixture); hardcoding the minimum instead of deriving it from `engines.node` fails the raised/relaxed fixtures; changing the npm script's value, deleting it, or reverting the Makefile recipe fails the wiring pins; an unreadable or unparseable manifest reaches the actionable refusal, never a stack trace. Known residual, accepted: the hook simulates module _unresolvability_, not a module that resolves but fails at instantiation — a hypothetical runtime with a present-but-broken `node:sqlite` above the minimum line is out of scope (the gate's contract is the declared minimum, and such a runtime fails the probe's own error path loudly). The review round (deepseek-v4.1-flash, one round, synchronous, verdict APPROVE with 0 P0 / 0 P1 / 3 P2 / 2 P3) was folded in before landing: P2-1 (the false "POSIX pipe writes are synchronous" justification for `process.exit(1)` — replaced by the launcher's `exitCode` discipline with the restructure), P2-2 (the matrix's structural blindness to patch ordering and derivation — closed by the fixture arms), P2-3 (the unreadable-manifest branch claimed covered but never executed — the no-file and malformed-JSON fixtures), P3-1's `getBuiltinModule` ban and P3-2's copy corrections were accepted too; the one declined suggestion was P3-1's marker-file variant of the non-initiation proof (a hook that also touches a file, proving the import was never initiated even if a future script swallowed the import's error) — declined because the single-occurrence, API-ban, and static-shape pins close that class at the source, while the gate-first property itself is asserted directly by exit code and message regardless of the hook. Evidence: `test/integration/runtime-verify-script.spec.ts` (twelve tests: real-runtime success, faked pass matrix, faked reject matrix with the actionable message, invalid matrix fail-closed incl. the four-segment arm, module-less-runtime gate proof, blocked-import non-vacuity, source pins incl. the single-occurrence and sidestep bans, wiring pins, broken-manifest fixtures incl. no-file and malformed JSON, and the three derivation fixtures), all green in `make check` beside the existing gate suites (the launcher and unit suites re-ran green with the extended matrix); `make verify-runtime` green through the npm script.

## D-162 — The CI test jobs' systemd-less class now comes from the job container, not the runner image (D-160's successor)

**Date:** 2026-11-05 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** §17.1 · **Task:** orchestrator service fix (CI-red follow-through)

**Decision.** D-160 pinned the CI and mutation test jobs to `ubuntu-24.04` on the belief that the 24.04 image still provided the systemd-less class D-103's seam design assumes. Two pushed runs disproved the premise: every hosted image — 24.04 included — now ships a live user systemd, and beyond the outcome pins, earlier tests in a job wrote real user units into the runner's passwd-home (`HOME` does not redirect the passwd-derived owner), contaminating every later owner-resolving arm. The corrective mechanism is the job container: `test` runs `container: node:${{ matrix.node }}` and `mutation` runs `container: node:22.13.0` — a fresh, root-HOME, systemd-less environment per job, immune to image migrations and cross-test state. The `setup-node` steps go (the image is the runtime); the matrix's Node coverage is unchanged (the image tag carries it).

**Reasons.** The container restores the exact environment class the suite was designed around, deterministically and permanently, instead of chasing image labels through GitHub's migration windows; the repository already uses job containers for the install matrix, so the pattern is established. The alternative — making every default-seam arm inject its environment seams — abandons the arms' purpose (proving the production defaults resolve) and would not fix the integration real-launcher suites, which cannot inject at all.

**Consequences.** The unit default-seam arms pin `probeCapabilities` to the absent class where their outcome expectations require it (the immediately preceding service commit): the pinned arms and the container now agree by construction, and the real probe's live behavior stays the integration suite's territory. The npm cache the setup-node steps provided is gone (`npm ci` per job, slower but hermetic). A longer-term live-systemd-safe test isolation remains open follow-up territory if hosted containers ever change shape again.

## D-163 — The landing-gate load-flake class retired: the last default-timeout launcher cell pins the house 30 s, and process-orchestration marker waits size from the same rig census (spec §17.1; task U-044)

**Date:** 2026-11-05 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§17.1](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#171-required-test-coverage) · **Tasks:** [U-044](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-087, D-094, D-017, D-086

**Decision.** The three sites that tripped the 2026-11-04/05 full-run waves (each green in every isolated run; each occurrence costing a full landing-verdict re-run) are pinned, each by the verdict D-087's criterion dictates — a wait with a phase assumption gets a deterministic handshake, a slow-but-deterministic wait gets a sized timeout: (1) **`test/integration/cli-doctor.spec.ts`'s "pins the --raw option surface in --help"** — the D-094 census family's last default-timeout member — declares `{ timeout: 30_000 }` through the installed Vitest 5 options-object form, the house value the U-039 real-launcher suites pin for the identical single-boot `jiti/register` shape (the suite's five doctor-running siblings keep their heavier 60 s pins; there is nothing to synchronize — one spawn, await close, assert stdout). (2) **`test/integration/single-instance.spec.ts`'s real-process scenarios keep their causal U-001/U-002 file handshakes and gain sized deadlines**: `waitForFile`'s default 10 s → `MARKER_WAIT_TIMEOUT_MS = 20_000`; the describe's `CHILD_TIMEOUT` 20 s → 45 s; the two U-017 arms keep their 60 s pins (re-margined against measurement, not raised); `test/helpers/singleInstanceRunner.ts`'s `blockUntil` park bound 15 s → 25 s — it must outlast one in-pool boot of the sibling the orchestration waits for (a child that gives up while the now-patient parent still waits is the same incoherence) _and_ strictly exceed the spec-side 20 s marker-wait ceiling, because the child's park clock starts at its own marker write while the parent's wait for the next marker starts only after observing it and spawning the sibling (the review round's P3-1), while staying finite as the anti-leak bound for parked children. The markers are phase-deterministic, verified in the module: `saw-stale` is the breaker's _pre-guard_ inspection probe (`acquireLock` inspects after `publishLock`'s guard was released, which is what lets the holder publish while the breaker stalls), and `guard-waiting` is the third starter's first and only reachable `isAlive` call — the lock path is vacant while the breaker parks, so the contention-inspection probe is unreachable and `acquireGuard`'s holder poll is provably the first — so D-087's handshake criterion does not apply: the waits were merely under-sized, not phase-ambiguous. The pre-existing `guardTimeoutMs: 20_000` orchestration bounds bound only post-boot phases (the breaker's finish after `resume`, measured ~1–2 s) and stay. (3) **`test/integration/server-main.spec.ts`'s real-signal tests** (the task text names two suites; this third site tripped identically in the same waves and joins the scope per the retire-the-class spirit — recorded in the commit body): `waitForFile`'s default 10 s → 20 s (`signals-ready` _is_ the U-001 handshake — deterministic phase, slow boot) and the describe's `CHILD_TIMEOUT` 20 s → 30 s.

**Reasons.** The sizing census is D-094's method unchanged (six busy-loop hogs across the container's 8 cores, full coverage `make check` under them, ≈3× the measured worst — never a guess): a marker wait's latency is one full runner boot (`jiti/register` transpiling the `runServer` graph before the child can write anything), measured 1.8–2.2 s ambient and isolated-rig and worst ≈5.5 s in-pool under the rig (pool load ~14–17 — the U-039 regime), corroborated by the three-boot U-017 arms' whole-test 13.9–17.4 s across the rig runs there; 20 s holds ≈3.6× that worst. Whole-test rig worsts size the pins: 3.6–5.8 s single-boot cells (SIGTERM/SIGINT/`--help`) → 30 s ≈ 5× (the family's regime worst stays U-039's 5.9 s); 8.8–11.1 s two-boot real-process tests → 45 s ≈ 4× (the hot-pool sample, not the cool 5.8/6.2 s one — the worst sample sizes the pin); 13.9–17.4 s U-017 arms → the landed 60 s ≈ 3.4×, kept because both observed flakes were the inner 10 s waits, never the pin (the pin sizes from the measured whole-test worst, not the sum of the inner wait ceilings — waits are failure ceilings, not budgets; only a pathological chain of just-under-ceiling boots could make the test timeout pre-empt a marker wait's own message, the review round's P3-3 stance). Plain `node -e` boots (cli-doctor's `withLiveLock` readiness loop) measured 25–35 ms ambient — two orders below their 5 s bound even inflated — and stay under the census bar. No handshake was rewritten: every wait already synchronizes on a causally-written marker file, so the honest fix was the missing wall-time margin, exactly D-094's "the test simply needs more wall time" verdict for waits that own their phase.

**Consequences.** `docs/agents/gotchas.md`'s D-094 census note now records the process-orchestration marker-wait class (a `vi.waitFor` around a child boot is a boot-time assertion in disguise) beside the retired cli-doctor cell, with the standing rule: new marker waits size at authoring time from the same rig census, and the runner-side park bounds track the spec-side wait ceilings. Stability evidence at the final values: two full `make check` runs under the rig (4338 tests; the three target suites 100% green in both — one run fully green, the other's single failure an unrelated `cli-service-logs.spec.ts` backpressure-chunking cell under the rig, recorded for the main session as follow-up material, not fixed here per the U-039 scope precedent) and two full ambient runs fully green; the measurement run (pre-change values, load ~16.6) and one intermediate-value rig run were green as well. No `src/**` file, assertion, spawn, or environment changed — timeouts and docblocks only, the measurements recorded beside each constant. A generator or suite that grows its boots past the census re-measures, per D-094's standing rule.

## D-164 — Task 181's responsive-accessibility verification: the audit matrix and its three fixes (the designed focus ring, Escape dismissal with focus restoration, the suggestion list's ARIA-1.2-legal linkage), the coverage boundary against 182, and the recorded residuals (spec §14.1, §17.1; task 181)

**Date:** 2026-11-05 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§14.1](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#141-general-ui-requirements), [§17.1](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#171-required-test-coverage) · **Tasks:** [181](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-133 (the token system every contrast pair reads through, and the per-mode scan precedent), D-156 (the declined combobox P3 this task owned the follow-up of, and the native-controls stance the suggestion linkage keeps), D-135 (the panels' focus-IN discipline this entry completes with focus-BACK), D-138 (the route-interception e2e technique every new axe cell reuses), D-148/D-149/D-150/D-153 (the chart surface the new annotation-bearing scan renders), D-127 (the CSP every fix stays neutral to — stylesheet rules and DOM focus only)

**Decision.** Task 181 is a verify-and-fix pass over the whole landed UI, and its audit is recorded as a matrix — screens × themes × widths × workflows — with every gap closed by a fix or a recorded residual. (Correction trail: the task's review round — deepseek-v4.1-flash, one round, REQUEST_CHANGES with 1 P1 / 2 P2 / 5 P3, the reviewer live-probing Chromium to confirm the P1 — was folded in before landing: the **P1** (a keyboard suggestion pick unmounts the picked button and dropped focus to the body — `pickZone` now refocuses the field after the DOM settles, pinned in both suites), the **P2s** (a successful rename/replace-key now restores focus to the opener — the success path had the same body-drop as the pre-fix cancel path — and Escape during a pending mutation is ignored: the dispatched request owns its panel until it settles, because resetting the call mid-flight suppresses the outcome while the request still applies; a removed account now hands focus to the accounts selector from the parent after the reload settles, the card being gone), and the P3s (IME composition guards on every Escape handler — a composing user cancels the composition, not the panel; the suggestion list's ring room on all four sides; the annotated-charts fixture made contract-faithful — time-ascending events and schedule-zone local times; the write-only-at-dispatch login pin made real by a delayed response and an in-pending-window assertion; the chart aria summary now pinned over all four annotation counts; the docs' overcounts and overclaims corrected) all entered this entry and the same commit. **The fixes, three:** (1) **A designed focus indicator** — one global `:focus-visible` rule in `base.css` (a 2 px `--qm-color-foreground` outline, offset 2 px), replacing the per-widget UA defaults focus visibility had been leaning on (nothing removed the UA outline, so WCAG 2.4.7 passed by default — but the indicator was undesigned and unpinned); the rule is token-only, resolves in all three modes, and is CSP-neutral; the keyboard spec pins it behaviorally through a computed `outlineStyle` read on a Tab-focused nav link (execution over text pins, D-155's rule). (2) **Panel dismissal** — the accounts card's four inline surfaces (rename form, replace-key form, archive confirm, purge confirm) close on Escape and return focus to their opener button after the DOM settles (`nextTick` then focus — the opener re-renders with the panel's closing, so the plain template ref re-populates); task 170 moved focus IN on open (the archive confirm deliberately onto the safe control) and this entry completes the contract with focus BACK on dismissal, mouse-cancel included. (3) **The time-zone suggestion list's keyboard semantics** — D-156's declined P3, explicitly handed to "the a11y follow-up pass": the field keeps the native-controls stance (real focusable buttons, no `aria-activedescendant`, no roving tabindex — ArrowDown hands focus to the first suggestion, Tab/Enter stay the platform's) and gains the ARIA-1.2-legal linkage: `aria-describedby` to the static search hint (the affordance is announced before anything is typed), `aria-autocomplete="list"`, and `aria-controls` rendered **only while the list exists** (a dangling id reference is an axe `aria-valid-attr-value` violation — found by the scan itself); `aria-expanded` on a plain `<input type="text">` is **prohibited by ARIA 1.2** (the scan's `aria-allowed-attr` finding) and stays with the full combobox contract the project declined — an interpretation of §14.1's "support keyboard navigation" as native-keyboard operability plus legal linkage, not full ARIA widget roles. Escape reverts the edit to the served value from either the field or a suggestion button (collapsing the list, clearing a stale field error — the reverted value is the served one the guards never judge). **The coverage boundary against task 182:** this task's proofs are e2e/axe-level (the browser is where WCAG contrast and keyboard semantics are observable) plus component arms for the changed Vue logic in the existing suites (`accounts-view.spec.ts`, `settings-view.spec.ts` — no new component-test infrastructure; 182 owns that build-out). **The recorded residuals:** the chart zoom-in gesture is pointer-only — the chart is a `role="img"` text alternative over data fully available as text (the metric cards, the aria summary with its annotation counts), the zoom **reset** is a keyboard-operable button, and ECharts ships no keyboard dataZoom (building one would be a feature, not a fix); per-page system-mode axe scans stay justified by the theme spec's raw-token pins (explicit dark and system-dark compute the identical cascade by the pinned duplication); a skip link stays unnecessary at the shell's size (one header row — recorded, not dismissed silently).

**Reasons.** The audit found the token palette already AA-clean (every `--qm-*` pair hand-computed ≥ 5.9:1 text / ≥ 6:1 non-text in both modes — the D-133 discipline doing its work), so the fixes went where behavior was genuinely missing: focus visibility was real but unowned, dismissal was one-sided, and the suggestion list was keyboard-operable but neither linked nor escapable. The three fixes each ride existing seams — the token system (no new colors), the existing cancel functions (Escape is one more caller), the native button list (no new widgets) — which is why they could land inside a verification task. The axe-found ARIA interpretations (dangling `aria-controls`, prohibited `aria-expanded`) are recorded here rather than in the commit alone because they bind future fields: any input-with-suggestions surface inherits the same shape (describe the affordance, control only what exists, stay off the combobox contract's prohibited attributes).

**Consequences.** UI-side: the `:focus-visible` rule in `base.css`, the Escape/focus-restoration handlers and opener refs in `AccountManageCard.vue`, the linkage/keyboard seams and one catalog key (`settings.general.timezoneSuggestions`) in `SettingsGeneralForm.vue` (whose suggestion list also gains horizontal padding so the scroll container cannot clip the focus ring). Tests: `test/e2e/keyboard.spec.ts` (five cells: shell Tab/Enter/theme-select-arrows with the focus-ring pin, the keyboard-only login round trip, the radio-group range switch proven by the re-dispatched history window span, the panels' open/dismiss/restore contract, the suggestion ArrowDown/Enter/Escape flows), six cells' worth of coverage changes in `test/e2e/a11y.spec.ts` (five new tests: the charts region with the full annotation vocabulary — a points-bearing dual-view series under a reset, gap, failed cycle, stopped region, and windows-bearing peak schedule, with a live ECharts canvas booted inside the scanned host; the populated accounts page with the purge panel open; the login failure surface; and 360 px cells for the accounts and login pages, completing the four-page matrix), and the component arms above. `ui/README.md` gains the "Accessibility and responsive behavior" section; `CHANGELOG.md` Unreleased carries the entry. Hand-off: task 182's component build-out covers the same fixes at mount level if it wants deeper arms; a future keyboard zoom for charts (or a skip link, should the header grow) supersedes the recorded residuals with their own evidence.
