## D-165 — Task 182's UI component-test build-out: the gap-inventory boundary (what D-164 left e2e-only stays there), the closed interpolation-seam tables for the localized-strings half, and no product changes

**Date:** 2026-11-05 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§17.1](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#171-required-test-coverage) · **Tasks:** [182](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-164 (the coverage boundary this task inherited — its hand-off named this build-out), D-134 (the injectable fetch seam every new arm rides), D-135 (the canonical-label discipline whose create/rename halves gain their pins here), D-137/D-138 (the §8.4 matrix and the initial-states enumeration the new arms complete), D-147 (the fallback announcement now pinned), D-133 (the theme controller whose default seams gain pins), D-132 (the catalog discipline the interpolation half extends), D-136 (the happy-dom boundary that keeps the real-surface bridge out of the component project)

**Decision.** Task 182 lands as a coverage-gap closure over the suites tasks 169–181 built, and pins three boundaries. (1) **The inventory, not a rewrite, sets the scope.** The existing suites are extensive (~560 arms across 23 specs: every §14.2 action, the §8.4 matrix, the D-138 fresh-install matrix, the D-147 control matrix, the full chart pipeline, the login/session arms, the catalog's both-directions key completeness); the task's six list items each had genuine residue and nothing more was invented — the closed gaps are: the add-form's provider-select reconciliation (a NEW component suite — the watch is the form's own behavior and the page loads providers exactly once per mount, so the reload arms are only drivable in isolation), D-135's create/rename label trims (only the purge gate's trim was pinned), the card's identity-line cells (the exact mask line, "Not set", Active/Archived), the §8.4 enum vocabularies completed through the frozen `LIMIT_TYPES`/`METRIC_UNITS` lists (DAILY, the OTHER fallback arm, TOKENS, and percent as the unit of absolute values had never rendered), the non-integral rolling window and the null-reason invalid metric, the theme controller's default composition-root seams (window.localStorage, the `prefers-color-scheme` query, the locked-down-storage in-memory fallback), D-147's auto-fallback live-region announcement (rendered on fallback, retired by the next manual pick), the accounts/settings initial loading lines (D-138 had pinned the overview's only), and the shell sign-out's pending lock (re-labeled control, no re-entry dispatch). (2) **The localized-strings half closes the interpolation seam, not just key existence.** Beside the existing both-directions key scans, every `{placeholder}` a catalog message carries must be supplied at EVERY `t('key', …)` call site — per site, not as a union, because one complete site does not vouch for a second, incomplete one (the incomplete site renders literal braces on screen whatever its siblings pass): a static harvest of param names (shorthand, `name:`, and balanced-block parsing; a call shape the harvest cannot parse fails the suite loudly — the dynamic-key rule's param-side twin), with exactly two sanctioned non-literal shapes (same-file `const` param objects, resolved from the nearest declaration preceding the call site — the `stamps` object today — and spread members resolved one level into them) and one closed allow-list: the chart-template keys, rendered raw because `MetricHistoryChart` hands the catalog values to the chart builder's own `interpolate` (`series.ts`) whose composed outputs are already behaviorally pinned in the chart suites — the table pins each entry's placeholder-name set so a catalog rename fails with a named key. Both directions hold: no unsupplied placeholder (a drifted one renders literal braces on screen today), no dead supplied name. A whole-catalog render-through complements the static scans: paramless keys render their value verbatim through the real composer (an accidental plural `|`, linked-message `@`, or unbalanced brace compiles to something else and fails), parameterized keys render synthetic per-name markers with no residual braces. Lethality was proven on three scratch mutations — a renamed placeholder, a drifted seam-table entry, a plural bar in a paramless value — each caught, each reverted. (3) **No `ui/**` seam and no product change.** Every gap was provable through the standing fixtures (the per-suite fake backends, 181's `stallNext`, a settings gate mirroring the overview backend's, descriptor-level window seams for the theme defaults); D-164's e2e-only residuals (computed focus-ring pixels, real canvas bitmaps, real keyboard focus, axe scans, per-mode token colors) and D-136's integration-only bridge stay where they are.

**Reasons.** §17.1's component-test leg names six surfaces; the honest reading of "add UI component tests" against a tree that already carries 169–181's arms is the inventory: each list item's residue closed executably, nothing duplicated at a second level. The provider-select watch is the one behavior whose own level is the component (the page cannot re-deliver the providers prop mid-mount), so the suite split is honest rather than a style choice. The vocabulary tables are driven by the model's frozen enums — not cherry-picked literals — so a future `LIMIT_TYPES` member fails the table until it gains its sentence, the same closed-vocabulary discipline the wire contracts carry. The interpolation rules follow D-132's own logic to its next step: key existence was proven both ways, but a key with a drifted placeholder "exists" and still renders broken text; the failure mode lives only at the seam between message and params, so that is where the pin sits, with the two non-literal shapes source-resolved (not ignored — a silently skipped shape would hollow the rule) and the chart-builder seam named in a closed table rather than blanket-excluded. The render-through pin adds the compile dimension no static scan can see: vue-i18n messages are programs, and `|`/`@`/brace syntax errors surface only when the composer runs.

**Consequences.** `test/component/account-add-form.spec.ts` lands (4 arms); `accounts-view.spec.ts` (+4: the loading line over `stallNext`, the identity-line cells, the create/rename trim sends), `overview-view.spec.ts` (+5: both enum tables, the non-integral window, the null-reason invalid metric, the fallback announcement), `settings-view.spec.ts` (+1: the loading line, over a `settingsGate` added to the suite's own backend fixture — the overview backend's precedent), `app.spec.ts` (+1: the sign-out pending lock, 30 s house timeout), `theme.spec.ts` (+3: the default storage read, the matchMedia query pin with a live preference flip, the locked-down-storage fallback), and `i18n-catalog.spec.ts` (+3: placeholder supply both directions, the closed chart-template table, the whole-catalog render-through) — 580 component tests green, ~21 new arms, all hermetic (no network, no provider; the guard active in the project). Editing a catalog placeholder, adding a parameterized key, changing the chart strings object's membership, or relaxing the provider-select watch requires updating the corresponding pin in the same change; a new non-literal param shape (a computed object, a cross-file import) fails the harvest loudly and must either be restructured to a static literal or extend `collectSuppliedParams` consciously. `CHANGELOG.md` Unreleased carries the entry. Known residuals, deliberately not chased: happy-dom's `localStorage`/`matchMedia` descriptors are assumed redefinable (asserted in-test, so an environment change fails the arm's own premise check, not a mystery), and the component-level coverage percentages of `ui/**` remain unmeasured by design (the coverage gates own `src/**`; the UI's proof layer is behavioral).

## D-166 — Task 183's acceptance suite: the served-construction harness (real composition + real adapter over the loopback mock), the `staticRoot` seam, and the deterministic-marker world shapes (spec §14, §17.1; task 183)

**Date:** 2026-11-05 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§14](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#14-web-interface), [§17.1](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#171-required-test-coverage) · **Tasks:** [183](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-140 (the composition root whose construction the harness assembles, and the `port` seam precedent `staticRoot` mirrors), D-134/D-138 (the route-interception e2e technique the preview suites keep — the acceptance suite is the served-construction half, not a replacement), D-085 (the coverage gates that made the production seam's test mandatory), D-145 (the composedApi harness whose world-per-suite model this adapts to Playwright), D-139 (the range grammar the marker windows ride), D-075/D-080 (the gap/stopped derivations the seeded worlds are shaped around)

**Decision.** The §17.1 acceptance scenarios ("against the built package and mock provider in CI") run against the **production Vite build served by the real server construction**: `test/e2e/helpers/acceptance.ts` starts, per spec file, one `composeApplication()` assembled `QuotameterApp` on an ephemeral loopback port over fresh temp config/data directories, registers the **real `ZaiCodingPlanProvider`** with its documented base-URL test seams pointed at the task-026 loopback mock provider server, and serves the built UI through a new `ComposeApplicationOptions.staticRoot` pass-through (`process.env.DIST_DIR ?? resolveUiDistDir()` — the container volume or CI's `ui/dist`; default behavior unchanged, the `port` seam's exact pattern: "the composition's test seam for what the configuration schema cannot express"). Three pinned interpretations. (1) **Real clock, `Date.now()`-anchored seeding** — §7.3 statuses derive against the server's clock while the browser's rolling ranges and relative times anchor on its own; a fixed clock (the sweep harness's choice) would fight one of the two, so every seeded timestamp is relative to the real now, with each age placed far from its boundary (5 min Fresh vs a 15-minute threshold; 40 min Stale; failures 3 min ago whose §7.3 ranks preempt age entirely). (2) **The marker world is shaped for exact counts** — the chart-markers scenario asserts the aria summary's counts precisely, so its silences are each either far under or far over the three-interval threshold: a 5-minute reset pair, the failed cycle 5 minutes after it (no silence), then one 60-minute gap to the closing success — exactly one reset, one gap, one failed collection, and exactly two stopped periods (the leading range-start→first-run region is inherent to any finite history, not noise to eliminate). (3) **The peak-schedule proof is split at the recorded boundary** — the served intervals (captured from the wire the page itself fired) prove the construction delivers the configured schedule; the interval→band mapping and the painted band stay pinned at the component level (D-149's seam), because the chart tooltip is `renderMode: 'richText'` — painted into the canvas, with no DOM text to assert — and the chart-sync suite's bitmap technique observes painting changes, not band content.

**Reasons.** The task's done-condition names three facts the preview-server suites structurally cannot provide: the built bundle served by the production listener (not `vite preview`), a real API behind every load (the honest empty states, real data surfaces — the degradation surfaces the a11y suite scanned were task 172's recorded stopgap), and a provider boundary that is real code (the credential check's loopback round trip) rather than `page.route` interception. The composition root is the only construction that provides all three without forks, and its existing injection seams (`providers`, `port`, `logger`) left exactly one gap — the static root, hard-resolved to `ui/dist` inside the listener; overriding it at the listener would mean re-building the HTTP component outside the composition, defeating "the real server construction". In-worker composition keeps the harness vitest-free (the Playwright runner cannot import `test/helpers/isolation.ts`'s vitest dependency, so the harness owns its temp lifecycle) and per-file serial mode gives each spec file one `beforeAll` world on one worker (the a11y file deliberately starts a second, password-mode world for its login scan), while distinct temp directories, ephemeral ports, and per-instance single-instance locks keep parallel spec files isolated — the D-145 model, adapted. The auth scenario uses the real §15.2 path (a scrypt hash in the config file, the real login endpoint, the real session cookie) and spends exactly one failed attempt of §15.2's five-per-15-minute budget, keeping the run clear of the limiter's delays.

**Consequences.** `test/e2e/acceptance/` (nine specs, 23 scenarios: empty state, account creation/key masking + connection test, all eight statuses, range disabling, chart markers, themes, responsive 360 px/1280 px, login/logout, a11y smoke over the populated surfaces) runs on the unchanged `npm run test:e2e` CI path beside the untouched preview suites — `make test-e2e`/CI build the UI first, so the harness's static root always exists. `src/server/composition.ts` gains the `staticRoot` option (pinned by a new composition test: the overridden directory's `index.html` serves at `/` and the SPA fallback), and future served-construction e2e needs no further production seams. The marker-count pins mean a change to the gap/stopped derivation (or the aria vocabulary) fails the chart-markers scenario by name — reshaping that world is part of such a change, not a bug; the seeded worlds deliberately use the real catalog's metric keys (`mcp-monthly`, `tokens-5h`) so labels resolve through `/api/providers`. The preview suites keep their role: fast shell/CSP/theme-token/degradation pins without a server; new acceptance scenarios join `test/e2e/acceptance/` rather than converting the old ones. Known residual, recorded: the harness's browser is Chromium in the e2e project only, so the a11y smoke stays Chromium-scoped exactly like the existing axe suite.

## D-167 — The `cli-service-logs` backpressure cell's chunk boundaries are handshake-driven: signal-created chunks with write-callback markers replace the coalescing flood, and the held gate is proven causally (spec §17.1; task U-047)

**Date:** 2026-11-05 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§17.1](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#171-required-test-coverage) · **Tasks:** [U-047](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-087 (the verdict criterion — a wait with a phase assumption gets a deterministic handshake), D-094 (the rig census/sizing method), D-163 (the recorded deferral: deadline sizing deliberately left this cell alone because its failure is a chunk-coalescing timing assumption), D-116 (the `runJournalctlPassthrough` contract the cell pins), D-017/D-086 (the U-001/U-002 readiness-marker pattern this design generalizes from signal-delivery windows to stream chunk boundaries)

**Decision.** `test/unit/cli-service-logs.spec.ts`'s "gates forwarding on the sink until it drains (backpressure)" cell no longer depends on when the OS pipe coalesces a child's writes into the reader's `data` events. The previous shape flooded 200 lines (~1.6 KB) in a tight loop and then had to observe a **second** `data` event for its re-pause proof; under parallel-worktree load the flood arrived as one read, nothing was left after the first drain, and the internal 5 s wait threw — the mechanism behind all three recorded full-run trips (U-039's rig run 3, reported at ~5.4 s into a 15 s pin — the internal wait's deadline, not the per-test timer; U-044's final-value rig run, recorded out-of-scope in D-163; task 181's landing `make check-all`, green in 57/57 isolated re-runs). Pinned mechanism, the U-001/U-002 pattern applied to chunking: the child installs `SIGUSR2`/`SIGTERM` handlers **before** its first write — the `PID:<pid>` announcement doubles as the readiness marker, so signalling after reading it is safe — writes `CHUNK<n>` only when signalled, and creates the marker file `wrote-<n>` **from the write callback**, which Node fires only after the bytes reached the OS pipe: the marker therefore proves the chunk pending on the reader's side (a plain post-write marker would only prove the write call returned, leaving the bytes possibly still in the child's socket buffer). `SIGTERM` writes `FINAL` and exits 0 from its own write callback; the child stays alive on a `setInterval` until then, so the runner's exit-resume (`child.once('exit') → stdout.resume()`, D-116) cannot fire during the gated phases. The test's four phases, each causal: (1) the announcement — the pid line is the only write so far, so exactly one forwarded call is assertable and the gate provably closed on it; (2) **the gate holds against proven pending data** — after `SIGUSR2` and the `wrote-1` marker, a further `data` event requires `resume()`, which requires either the drain listener (held only by the test) or child exit (possible only via the test's signal); the review round's P2-2 kept a bounded settle window as the OBSERVATION of that causality rather than replacing it — the window cannot flake the true path (a holding pause means no event can exist) while the marker guarantees a pause-less runner must forward inside it (the bytes are already in the pipe when the window opens: loop-turn lateness, not a race); (3) the re-pause — calling the captured drain listener with the chunk provably in the pipe guarantees the `data` event, hence the re-pause and the REPLACED `once('drain')` listener, pinned by the review round's P3-2 as the real emitter would hold it: a tracked set that `once('drain')` adds to and `removeListener('drain')` deletes from, asserted to hold exactly the new listener after the re-pause (a runner stacking a second listener without removing the first leaves both in the set and fails) — the poll is a causal wait whose 5 s bound only bounds failure reporting (D-087/D-163's distinction); exactly two forwarded calls and the exact `PID…CHUNK1` prefix are assertable; (4) the release — the sink mocked accepting plus the second drain resume forwarding, a further signalled chunk flows ungated, and the resolved outcome plus the joined forwarded calls reconstruct the whole stream byte-exactly (`PID…CHUNK1…CHUNK2…FINAL`) — content, not write counts, because the ungated phase may still coalesce reads (the pipe preserves order, not boundaries). Gate semantics are pinned exactly as before — genuinely held until the sink drains — and strengthened where the old cell could only observe luck: the held gate is now proven against data known to sit in the pipe, the exact per-phase forwarded content is pinned, and a failing assertion cannot leak the child (the review round's P2-1: the child's first action is writing a pid file — the leak guard, distinct from the announcement readiness marker — which the cleanup reads and SIGKILLs even when phase 1's wait expired without a forwarded announcement; after a settled outcome the kill is skipped, the child having exited and its pid being recyclable; ESRCH is the already-exited answer, any other kill failure reported after cleanup unless a test failure outranks it — and the `once`/`removeListener` spies delegate non-drain events to the real methods, the review round's P3-3, so nothing else in the worker loses a listener during the cell).

**Reasons.** D-087's criterion: a timing assumption is fixed by synchronizing the phase, never by enlarging a deadline — U-044 sized the cell's timeouts and explicitly recorded the chunk-coalescing race as this task's material. The handshake makes every chunk's existence a consequence of the test's own signal, so "how many reads does the pipe deliver" stops being an environmental variable: while gated, exactly the announcement exists; after each signal, exactly one more chunk exists. The one non-obvious choice is the write-callback marker over a simpler post-write marker: only the callback orders the marker after the bytes are in the kernel pipe, which is what makes both the gate-holds proof (the silence guards real pending data) and the re-pause guarantee (resume must produce a `data` event) airtight. No production seam was needed: the runner's existing contract (raw forward, pause-on-false, `once('drain')` replacement, exit-resume, signal registration) plus child-side signals and marker files carry the whole protocol — preferred per the task's clarification over widening `runJournalctlPassthrough` behavior. Dropping the fixed 5 s exit timer is a side effect of the signal-driven exit, not a goal: the cell went from ~5.3 s (structurally at the mercy of its 15 s pin under any slowdown) to 0.12–0.19 s under the rig, re-margining the pin to ≈90× the measured worst without touching it.

**Consequences.** The standing rule lands in `docs/agents/gotchas.md` beside the D-094 census: a test that depends on how a child's writes coalesce into reads gets an explicit chunk-boundary handshake (signal-created chunks, write-callback markers, an announcement line that orders signalling after handler installation) — never OS-read luck; the retire-list drops the backpressure entry. The suite's file-top docblock and the cell's comment record the mechanism with its causality arguments. No `src/**` file, exported surface, spawn, or environment changed — `runJournalctlPassthrough` and its coverage are untouched. Stability evidence at the final tree (the U-039/U-044 method: six busy-loop hogs pinned to cores 0–5 of the worktree container's 8, launched from the worktree's own docktree project): the suite green in 10/10 targeted runs under the rig (junit per-cell 0.120–0.172 s) and 5/5 at ambient load (0.137–0.145 s), one full green `make check` under the rig (4371 tests, 0 failures, coverage thresholds met), and one full ambient `make check` at the commit tree. A future cell that needs chunk-boundary control over a runner-spawned child reuses the same protocol (the child source is self-contained in the cell); a runner change to its drain/pause discipline (say, debounced resume) must revisit the cell's phase-3 poll, which is the only observation coupled to the replacement-listener implementation detail.

## D-168 — D-157 landed ahead of its implementation (its draft text leaked into task 180's commit): U-033 re-run implements it verbatim, and the live `dependencies` label is verified already present (task U-033)

**Date:** 2026-11-06 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§4.4](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#44-cicd-and-supply-chain-safeguards) · **Tasks:** [U-033](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-157 (the complete design this entry executes, unchanged), D-159 (task 180's commit `1d381ff` — a resume of an uncommitted draft that unintentionally carried D-157's text), U-004 (the failure class the label half resolves)

**Decision.** D-157's entry landed in `master` on 2026-11-05 inside task 180's commit (`1d381ff`) while U-033's actual implementation — the workflow edit, the guard spec, the docs — was lost with a dead session; the entry was published as Accepted with a correction trail describing an implementation and a review round that never landed. Entries are immutable, so the record is repaired forward, not edited: this task implements D-157 verbatim (mechanism and documentation placement unchanged — the entry itself remains the design record), with five deltas worth pinning. (1) **The live label creation D-157 describes was executed by the dead session before it died** — verified present now (`gh label list` shows `dependencies  Dependency updates (Dependabot)  #0366d6`, matching D-157's command, description, and color exactly); it was not re-created. (2) **The review round D-157's correction trail describes belongs to the lost implementation**; the landed implementation's own review round — kimi as the first fallback (`kimi-code/k3.1-pro`; the primary deepseek-v4.1-flash timed out with no report), one round, APPROVE with 0 P0 / 0 P1 / 4 P2, all four findings accepted and fixed in the same commit — is recorded here and in the landing commit. (3) **The digests were re-sourced and re-verified for this landing** (2026-11-06: both archives downloaded from nodejs.org and hashed against `SHASUMS256.txt`) rather than trusted from the 2026-11-04 retrieval the entry records — the pin's own discipline applied to the anomaly. (4) **D-157's shell claim is corrected**: the runner's default shell for `run:` is `bash -e {0}`, not `bash -e -o pipefail` (pipefail requires an explicit `shell: bash`) — the checksum check fails closed under both settings because the verify pipeline adopts `sha256sum`'s non-zero exit and `-e` aborts (verified on a corrupted archive under both interpreters; the exact-shape and `set +e` bans carry the fail-closed property either way). (5) **D-157's removal rationale is corrected**: per the Dependabot options reference, a label listed under `labels:` that is missing from the repository is silently ignored, while Dependabot's DEFAULT labels (including `dependencies`) are auto-created — so removing `labels:` would not leave the implicit missing-label failure D-157 argued; the explicit declaration is kept on the corrected grounds that it pins the exact label set (one shared `dependencies`, not the defaults' `dependencies` plus per-ecosystem labels) and keeps it repository-governed. The same review round's remaining two findings — the bump-procedure comment now lists every edit site (the test matrix's declared-minimum entry and the timezone job's pin were missing) and the guard pins the matrix comment's version literal — extend D-157's pin set without contradicting it.

**Consequences.** D-157's text now describes real repository state from this commit on, with deltas (4) and (5) superseding its shell and removal-rationale claims (a future deviation remains a new decision referencing it). The process residual for the cycle: a dying session's uncommitted `DECISIONS.md` draft can be swept into an unrelated task's commit — a resumed session must diff the working tree against the resumed task's scope before committing (the check that would have caught this leak).

## D-169 — The `collection_runs` data-completeness closures: the §8.4 transport-evidence status D-069 named, the `raw_responses.content_type` wiring D-051's column always implied, and the abandon hook that keeps a thrown wrapper's cycle-start stamp out of the next run row (spec §11.2, §7.2, §7.4, §8.4; task U-035)

**Date:** 2026-11-06 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§11.2](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#112-required-logical-tables), [§7.2](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#72-retry-and-error-behavior), [§7.4](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#74-sanitized-raw-responses), [§8.4](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#84-normalized-snapshot-and-metric-model) · **Tasks:** [U-035](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-010, D-021, D-034, D-041, D-042, D-048, D-051, D-053, D-059, D-066, D-069

**Decision.** The three data-completeness gaps deepseek-v4.1-flash's review round found (P3-1/P3-2/P3-3, with qwen3.8-flash converging on the third) are each closed as a populate-or-fix, decided from §11.2's own column contracts: (1) **A successful run now records `http_status`** — §11.2 lists the column with no outcome scoping, D-034 pinned it "absent when no response arrived", D-048's classifier retains a status "whenever a response arrived", and on success a response did arrive (2xx by D-042's delivery gate). The wiring is the §8.4-surface successor decision D-069's consequences explicitly reserved: `ProviderSnapshot` gains an optional `httpStatus` (transport evidence beyond §8.4's stated shape — §8.4 says "equivalent to", and an optional additive field keeps equivalence for every consumer), validated at the D-010 boundary as an integer in `[100, 599]` (mirroring `collection_runs_http_status_range`), stamped by the Z.ai adapter from endpoint 1's delivered response (the metrics-originating exchange, D-047 — soft endpoints 2/3 are context, never cycle evidence), and retained by the settle seam through `classifySuccess`'s already-existing optional `httpStatus` parameter — the rail D-048 built, which no caller had fed until now. An adapter that stamps nothing stores NULL — the recorded absent-when-no-response rule, now reachable rather than constant; an out-of-range stamp is a §8.4 violation and lands as the seam's existing invalid-snapshot `parse_error` narrowing, never a crash. (2) **`raw_responses.content_type` is populated from the delivered header** — D-051 recorded the column as "the header value verbatim or absent" and created it because §11.2's row lists it, but no wire ever carried a value (the persist seam hardcoded NULL). `SnapshotParseError` gains the observed `Content-Type` as an optional trailing field, sanitized through D-041's raw-text path before it rides the error (a credential echoed inside a media-type parameter stores `[REDACTED]`, never the key — D-042's retained-server-string discipline applied to the stored column, refining "verbatim" exactly the way §15.4 refines every retained provider string; a real media type passes verbatim). The persist seam's structural narrowing admits the field as absent, blank-as-absent (a whitespace-only media type is no media type — stricter than the column's own CHECK, which rejects only the empty string), or a non-empty string — anything else is not a recognized parse failure and fails fast, the `httpStatus` precedent. (3) **A thrown retry wrapper can no longer leak its cycle-start stamp into the next run row** — D-059's wrapper throws only on programming mistakes (a broken sleep seam, an invalid random roll), and that path never reaches `settleCycle`, so the recorder's `??=` stamp survived into the next cycle's first attempt: the next row's `started_at` — D-069's "real reading at the cycle's first attempt" — could name a cycle up to an hour earlier (past a `Retry-After` deferral or a suspension cadence), misstating every §12.2 span built on it. `PollingAccount` gains an optional `abandonCycle()` hook; the engine's wrapper-throw containment invokes it, a throwing hook is simply one more programming mistake on that already-contained path (the flight's outer catch makes the same plain-interval fallback — no separate containment branch, which would only add an equivalent mutant), and the recorder's implementation drops the stamp. Rejected alternative: re-stamping on a fresh abort-signal identity — the engine's fresh-per-flight controller is undocumented discipline that the persist suites' own harnesses already violate (they pass a fresh signal per attempt), and the leak is a lifecycle fact the engine knows directly; the explicit hook says exactly that. A wiring that never calls the hook reproduces the old semantics (pinned by test as the seam an unwired engine leaves); settle keeps clearing first-thing, so a throwing settle needs no abandonment.

**Reasons.** All three arbiter readings come from §11.2's own row lists plus the decisions that created the columns: D-034's "absent when no response arrived" and D-051's "header value verbatim or absent" each describe when the column is NULL — a constant NULL on the majority path (success) or on every row (content_type) is a dead column, not a domain state, and both reviews' findings plus D-069's recorded gap name exactly that. The populate choices reuse existing rails end to end: `classifySuccess`'s parameter, the adapter's `secrets` list, D-041's sanitizer, and the structural hand-off the persist seam already narrows — no migration (the columns and their CHECKs already admit every populated value), no API/UI surface change (the §13 routes serve storage records, not `ProviderSnapshot`; the UI imports nothing from `src/schemas/metrics` at all). The fix choice for the stamp leak follows the house's explicit-seam precedent (D-020's tracker, D-059's broken-seam containment) over an identity heuristic: the engine is the only party that knows a cycle died unsettled, and the optional hook keeps every existing `PollingAccount` construction valid while the recorder (which owns the cell) makes the guarantee load-bearing — the composition spread `{ accountId, keyIdentity, …createCycleRecorder(…) }` D-069 recorded picks the member up with no composition-root change.

**Consequences.** `collection_runs.http_status` is 200 on every Z.ai success row from this commit on (and NULL for non-stamping adapters, a state only constructible in tests today); `doctor --raw` headers read the real content type instead of the permanent "unknown content type" (no CLI change — `renderRawDiagnostics` already renders the column). The §8.4 model change is additive and backward-compatible, but `ProviderSnapshot.httpStatus` and the `SnapshotParseError.contentType`/`PollingAccount.abandonCycle` members are now contract: removing or re-typing any of them requires a successor decision. Coverage: the boundary validation arms (`test/unit/metrics.spec.ts`), the persist seam's narrowing and both evidence wires plus the abandon/bleed pins (`test/unit/polling-persist.spec.ts`, `test/integration/polling-persist.spec.ts` against a real migrated database), the engine's abandon invocation, throwing-hook containment, and hook-free operation (`test/unit/polling-scheduler.spec.ts`, whose broken-backoff seam discriminates by delay value — the loop's hang-threshold wake wins the first `sleep` call, so call order cannot identify the backoff), and the adapter's stamping, content-type carry, and §15.4 scrub through real sockets (`test/integration/zai-coding-plan-snapshot.spec.ts`). `src/storage/README.md` (both columns' rows and pinned-interpretation bullets) and `src/services/README.md` (the recorder's closures and the scheduler's account seam) document the populated semantics; D-069's recorded success-`http_status` gap is closed by this entry, the successor its consequences named.

## D-170 — The repo-root `favicon.png` is removed as unreferenced residue rather than adopted as the UI icon (task U-037)

**Date:** 2026-11-06 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§4.1](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#41-public-repository-and-language), [§18](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#18-documentation-deliverables) · **Tasks:** [U-037](plan/tasks.md)

**Decision.** The ~1.3 MB `favicon.png` at the repository root, added alone by the exploratory commit `3d33e83` ("favicon", 2026-10-29), is deleted (`git rm`), not wired into the product. Verification before the decision: a whole-tree grep finds no reference outside the U-037 task text itself; `ui/index.html` declares no icon link; `ui/public/` does not exist and `ui/vite.config.ts` sets no `publicDir`, so the file was never copied into a build; the server's static serving mounts only the built UI (`@fastify/static` over `staticRoot` = `ui/dist` with the SPA fallback), so the file was never served; and it is outside the package manifest's `files` allowlist and `scripts/check-package.mjs`'s `ALLOWED`, so it never shipped in the tarball.

**Reasons.** The external review round flagged the file as committed-but-unreferenced residue, and the code confirms it: every path a favicon could legitimately serve through (the Vite public dir, an explicit `<link>` in `ui/index.html`, or the packaged tarball) is absent. Adopting it instead would be a UI/product decision (which icon, what weight budget — 1.3 MB is unfit for a browser asset regardless), out of scope for a documentation-truth task and unforced by any spec §18 deliverable: the spec's documentation list names no icon.

**Consequences.** The working tree loses a 1.3 MB binary with no build, serve, package, or test surface (the checks stay green unchanged). A future UI icon is a new, deliberate change: it belongs in `ui/public/` (Vite copies it into `ui/dist`) plus the `<link>` in `ui/index.html`, and must respect §3's minimal-tarball constraints; nothing in this entry opposes it. The documentation-truth pass that decided this (U-037) records its per-file verdicts in its commit body.

## D-171 — The three cross-module seams the external review round exposed, now pinned: the clock zone-validation memo is module-bounded, the peak-hours interval objects are frozen at construction, and the closed-vs-half-open range seam is documented as deliberate and pinned cross-module (spec §10, §9.3, §13; task U-038)

**Date:** 2026-11-06 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§10](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#10-time-and-time-zones), [§9.3](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#93-schedule-calculation-and-display), [§13](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#13-http-api) · **Tasks:** [U-038](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-021, D-068, D-073, D-081, D-082

**Decision.** The three unpinned seams qwen3.8-flash's decision-literate pass surfaced are each verified against the code first and closed as fix-or-document: (1) **`clock.ts`'s `zoneChecks` memo is bounded by the module, not by its callers.** D-021's memoization premise covered determinism and per-call `Intl` cost; the module's own growth note — "cache keys are zone names from validated configuration, so the map stays small in practice" — was a property of today's callers, not of the module (exactly the unstated-premise class this task pins). The verified production domain is indeed config-only: every key arrives via `resolveTimeZone(schedule.timezone)` (the calculator and the `/api/peak-hours` route), `resolveTimeZone(app.timezone)` (`service-status` formatting), branded-zone re-validation inside `zonedDateTime`, `peak-hours-dst`, and the `resolveLocalInstantLuxon` compat resolver, or doctor's display-zone check — all config-borne, and every path except doctor's deliberate defense-in-depth arm (total over any string by design, so it can judge a zone the twin rejected) passes the configuration twin's validation (`isValidTimeZoneName`, D-014 item 8) before the clock gate is consulted. But the domain is not provably finite, so a documented growth contract would have been false twice over: `isValidTimeZone` is exported and nothing structural prevents a future caller passing untrusted strings (failures are cached too, each distinct string a permanent entry), and V8's `Intl` accepts case-mangled spellings of valid names (`aSia/singapore` — acceptance the clock suite already pins), so even the success-key space has no finite bound a contract could honestly state. The fix: exported `ZONE_CHECK_MEMO_CAPACITY = 1024`; once the map holds that many distinct names, further names are computed per call and answered uncached — memoization stays transparent, and bounded growth becomes a module property. Sizing: over the tzdb's ≈600 names including backward links (≈350 primaries plus ≈250 links; the engine's `Intl.supportedValuesOf('timeZone')` list carries only ≈420 of them — canonical names plus listed aliases), so a legitimate workload that validates every tzdb name through the gate stays fully cached; both floors are pinned executably (the engine-list relation catches tzdb growth past the capacity over time, and a ≥600 relation pins the with-links rationale today), and worst-case memory is kilobyte-scale. The bound is a memory contract, not a security control — adversarial cache-thrashing (a hostile caller pre-filling the memo so later names recompute) is a documented non-goal: no untrusted input reaches the gate, and the degradation is performance-only. (2) **Peak-hours interval objects are frozen at construction** (D-073's successor for the value shape): D-073 froze the timeline and its intervals array, but the intervals themselves were mutable plain objects — the outlier against the services layer's value-object convention (`history-downsample.ts`'s buckets D-081, D-082's retention reports, D-068's rolling bounds). Both construction sites — the peak literal in the D-079 union walk and the `offPeakInterval` helper — now `Object.freeze` at build time: zero per-read cost, and the `/api/peak-hours` route already copies intervals via spread (`{ ...interval }`), so its response mapping and the §13 schema are unchanged. (3) **The closed-vs-half-open range seam is deliberate, documented on both sides, and pinned cross-module.** Peak-hours is half-open `[from, to)` (D-073 — load-bearing: closing it would double-cover every shared edge and break the partition arithmetic); the rolling ranges (D-068) and retention bounds (D-082) are closed `[from, to]` for point membership — a row stamped exactly at `to` is inside the read, a row at the horizon is retained. The two conventions meet at the §13 boundary, where the UI's one numeric `from`/`to` pair serves both the history/events reads and the peak-hours timeline. Normalizing either side is rejected (D-073's partition contract is load-bearing for the calculator; the closed reads are the landed SQL and the strict-before-delete alignment D-082/D-091 already express); instead the seam is stated in all three module headers and pinned by `test/unit/range-inclusivity-seam.spec.ts`, which asserts both conventions over identical numeric bounds, plus the tiling property that forces half-open intervals (adjacent ranges cover the shared edge exactly once) and the both-ends-inclusive predicates that force closed point reads — any silent normalization of either side fails the pin.

**Reasons.** The memo fix over documentation: the verification showed no honest finite-domain contract exists (case variants make even valid-key growth unbounded), so "documenting the growth contract" would have restated the unstated premise instead of pinning it — the task's own clarification names "production-bounded by config" as exactly the class to close. A capacity guard over an eviction scheme (LRU, clear-on-full): stop-caching is one branch, keeps the hot entries of every legitimate workload, and the adversarial scenarios an eviction policy would address cannot reach the seam (config-only keys; hostile traffic has no path to the gate in v1). The freeze follows the sibling convention verified at `history-downsample.ts`'s `makeBucket` — construction-time freeze, matching D-073's existing envelope freezes so the whole returned value now carries one immutability policy. The seam pin over normalization follows the task's clarification verbatim: each side's convention is right for its surface (closed for point membership, half-open for interval tiling), and the cross-module spec — the `history-cross.property.spec.ts` precedent of task 124 — makes the coexistence contractual by asserting the property each side satisfies and the other cannot.

**Consequences.** `ZONE_CHECK_MEMO_CAPACITY` and at-capacity transparency are contract: a tzdb growth past the capacity fails the sizing test (`test/unit/clock.spec.ts`'s D-171 block, which also exercises the at-capacity arm — the below-capacity arm is exercised by every other clock test) and forces a capacity revisit instead of silently uncaching legitimate traffic. The bound is also **observed**, not just executed (review round P2-1): a counting `Intl.DateTimeFormat` double proves a cached name constructs nothing across repeated lookups while a beyond-capacity fresh name pays the construction on every call — deleting the guard, or inverting it, fails the suite; the exact boundary comparison at `size === capacity` alone stays transparent (the Stryker directive's narrowed scope). The frozen intervals and the seam are contract via their pins: `test/unit/peak-hours-intervals.spec.ts`'s deep-freeze block (mixed and empty timelines) and `test/unit/range-inclusivity-seam.spec.ts`, whose closed side reaches the SQL itself — the repository suite's series/events/runs reads each keep an exact-at-`to` row asserted (the events row added by this task's review round, P3-1: series and runs already carried theirs). The seam spec is deliberately named outside the `test:time` filter vocabulary (D-097) — a pure numeric cross-module contract, not a module suite; the module suites themselves run in the §17.1 TZ matrix, and every pin input is an explicit epoch (D-021), so the pin is TZ-invariant by construction. `src/util/README.md` documents the bounded memo. The D-085 critical-module coverage keys stay green: `clock.ts` and `peak-hours*.ts` remain at 100% on all four axes with the new arms exercised. The two other items of the same review round stay refuted and out of scope (verified again in this task): the logger `authheader` vocabulary claim (`src/util/logger.ts`'s sensitive spellings contain it) and the CI LTS-matrix claim (the `test` matrix runs `['22.13.0', '22', '24']` with 24 the current LTS line since October 2026).

## D-172 — The mutation workflow reports a crashed run honestly: the report file's existence (never the step outcome) supplies every verdict claim, the crash body is a first-class renderer output, and the last scored rolling-issue body is irreplaceable by a non-score (spec §4.4, §17.3; task U-046)

**Date:** 2026-11-06 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§4.4](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#44-cicd-and-supply-chain-safeguards), [§17.3](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#173-enforced-quality-thresholds) · **Tasks:** [U-046](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-045 (the daily workflow and rolling-issue contract this repairs), D-054 (the committed-renderer seam the crash body joins), D-055 (the score semantics the crash body explicitly declines to state), U-045 (the Stryker initial-run root cause, deliberately out of scope)

**Decision.** Since 2026-11-01 a daily run that dies in Stryker's initial test run has been reported as a quality regression: `steps.stryker.outcome` is `failure` for ANY Stryker-step failure — a real below-break score and a crash before scoring alike — so the verdict line, the issue title, the run comment, and the final `::error` all claimed a below-break score that was never measured, while the render step's ENOENT left the shell redirect holding an empty body that the upsert fed to `gh issue edit --body-file`, blanking the rolling issue (#7, 2026-11-01→04: title "below threshold", comments promising "full report in the issue body and the run artifact", body empty, artifact empty). Four rules close the class. (1) **One discriminator separates the two worlds: `reports/mutation/mutation.json` existence** — the upsert's crashed-vs-scored verdict, the comment wording, and the final step's `::error` message all branch on the file. The step outcome keeps exactly two honest roles: the job-red trigger (`failure` either way — a crashed gate is not green) and, WITHIN the report-present branch only, the scored below-break/pass distinction (a scored report plus a non-zero exit is a genuine below-break — Stryker writes the JSON before its threshold check exits — and a scored report plus exit 0 is a pass); it can never again distinguish a crashed run from a scored one, because an absent report means no score exists at all. (2) **The crash body is a renderer output, not a workflow heredoc** (D-054's seam): `renderCrashReport({ date, log, reportPath, runUrl })` builds the body — a header naming the crash, a verdict line "**run crashed — no score was measured**", Stryker's own last ERROR line as the cause (ANSI-stripped, clipped) or an honest `unknown`, the failing initial-run tests extracted from the captured log, the Actions run link when the default env vars are present (no link in local renders), and an explicit "this is NOT a below-threshold score" triage pointer to `docs/mutation-testing.md`'s crashed-run case. The extraction (`extractFailedInitialTests`) is pinned against the installed Stryker's `logFailedTestsInInitialRun` source: one `\t<name>` line plus one `\t\t<failureMessage>` line per failed test, the whole list ONE log entry, multi-line failure messages arriving as untabbed continuation lines — so only a timestamped log entry may end a block (a continuation line ending it would drop every later test); the list is capped at 20 with an overflow note, ids clipped at 300 and messages at 200. A missing report (ENOENT only) exits 0 with the crash body; a present-but-unparseable report still aborts loudly (D-054). The Stryker step tees its output to `/tmp/stryker-output.log` under an explicit `shell: bash` (pipefail per D-168's correction, so the pipeline fails when Stryker does, not when `tee` succeeds), and a preservation step copies that log into `reports/mutation/` — exactly when no report exists — so the crash's evidence rides the artifact instead of dying with the 90-day run log (the `! -f mutation.json` guard keeps the large scored-run progress log out of scored artifacts). (3) **The last scored body is irreplaceable by a non-score**: the upsert's ONLY `--body-file` body edit sits in the branch combining a scored report with a non-empty rendered body; a crashed run retitles an existing issue to `crashed (no report produced)` and posts its crash report as the run's comment (the "Run of DATE: …" history line prefixed to the body), creating a fresh issue with the crash body only when none exists. (4) **Never an empty write anywhere**: if the renderer itself produced no body (it aborted — e.g. an unknown mutant status), no `--body-file` call fires at all; the issue keeps its body, the title is retitled, and the comment says the renderer produced no output — the shell-redirect-creates-the-empty-file mechanism that blanked #7 has no remaining path to a body.

**Reasons.** The task's honesty bar is that every published claim (title, body, comment, artifact name, `::error` annotation) is true in both worlds, and the only fact that discriminates them is whether Stryker scored — the report file. Keeping the crash body inside the committed renderer preserves D-054's property exactly (the workflow, the unit tests, and hand verification run the same code); a workflow-side heredoc would re-create the untestable-inline-renderer class D-054 retired. Gating the body edit on non-emptiness rather than "trust the renderer" acknowledges the third failure mode the workflow must survive honestly: the renderer's own loud abort (unknown status) also produces an empty redirect file, and the guard covers it with the same branch. Posting the crash report as the comment (not the body) follows the task's own alternative and the rolling issue's design: the body is the triage surface for the last SCORED report — replacing a survivor list with a crash page destroys the very triage data the task names as harmed, while the comment thread is already the per-run history D-045 established. The Stryker-source verification of the log format was forced by the observed single-test crash log alone being insufficient: the multi-test block shape (continuation lines between tab-indented ids) would silently lose tests under a naive "any untabbed line ends the block" rule.

**Consequences.** The workflow is honest while U-045 persists and unchanged in meaning after it is fixed (a scored run takes the original path verbatim — byte-stable, verified against the last real artifact). The crash-body format, the extraction vocabulary, the 20/300/200 caps, the verdict strings (`crashed (no report produced)`, "no score was measured"), the title-only crash edit, and the report-file discriminator are contract: changing any requires a successor decision. `test/unit/render-mutation-report.spec.ts` pins the no-report path at both seams (pure functions byte-exactly, plus CLI-boundary spawns: missing JSON exits 0 with the crash body; an unparseable report still exits non-zero), and `test/unit/mutation-workflow.spec.ts` (the U-029/U-033 line-scanner guard pattern) pins the workflow's honesty invariants — the tee under `shell: bash`, the log-preservation guard and its ordering before the artifact upload, the verdict branch on the report file, the single `--body-file` edit line, and the final step's two distinct `::error` messages under the report-existence branch. `docs/mutation-testing.md` gains the crashed-run "How to react" case (the maintainer is pointed at the named failing tests, not phantom survivors), the crash-preview one-liner, and the body-preservation note. The live issue #7's blanked body is not retroactively repaired (immutable history; the maintainer's triage comment there already records the incident) — the next crashed run re-renders honestly, and the next scored run restores the body.

## D-173 — Real-launcher test children get a hermetic environment: session-manager variables are stripped at the spawn boundary, and byte-identity assertions dump their evidence (task U-045)

**Date:** 2026-11-06 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§5.3](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#53-init-workflow), [§17.1](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#171-required-test-coverage) · **Tasks:** [U-045](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-162 (the environment-class fix this complements), D-160 (the probed capabilities), D-100 (the reproducibility contract), D-045 (the daily mutation cadence the failures broke)

**Decision.** Three pinned interpretations close the 2026-11-02→04 daily mutation failures (runs 41421143977, 41611856943, 41805574274: Stryker's initial test run died on `cli-init-yes`'s reproducibility cell — `expected 'A password is required before the ser…' to be 'A password is required before the ser…'` — while push CI and `make check` stayed green on the same tips). (1) **The root cause is the child's machine, not the mutation runner**: Stryker was exonerated by run 42002804236 (2026-11-05, the first daily run inside D-162's `node:22.13.0` job container), whose initial test run succeeded over all 3877 tests before the run was cancelled — the divergence existed only in the hosted VM's job environment, the live user systemd every hosted image now ships (D-162's recorded observation). The diverging bytes were re-captured by re-executing the cell's spawn shape in privileged systemd containers reproducing the hosted shape (a `runner` uid 1001, systemd as PID 1, a live user manager, the session environment — built on both Debian bookworm/systemd 252 and Ubuntu 26.04/systemd 257, the failing runs' generation): the two stdouts are byte-identical through the entire collected block — the password-pending line, the whole summary including the guard-blocked `provider-unavailable` connection-test row, and the normalized `Configuration written to` line — and diverge at its first service-setup line, where run 1 prints `Service setup: installed the user service for runner — no sudo needed` (the inherited `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` let the capability probe reach the live user manager, D-160, and the `user-unit` route's `systemctl --user enable --now` exited 0) while run 2 prints the `the user service could not be enabled automatically` fallback (the same command failed: `Job for quotameter.service failed because the control process exited with error code.` — on stderr). The machine-coupling has a second face the same evidence exposes: the probe's own 10-second timeout race. The failing jobs' only red cell was the byte-identity cell while `cli-init-service.spec.ts` — whose children assert the `systemd is not available` text — passed in the same jobs; on a systemd-PID1 host that text is reachable only through the probe timing out (`is-system-running` answering at all, even `degraded`, routes elsewhere), so the probe race demonstrably fired under the dry run's saturation and can split the absent/present routes between the two runs of the byte-identity cell — the one cell that compares two machine-coupled outputs against each other rather than against fixed text (the sibling cells pass whenever their children land in one class consistently, as cli-init-service's did). Both faces share one root: the §5.3 step-7 service-setup output is a function of live machine state a spawned child cannot have pinned — through the stateful unit enable (`Type=exec`, `Restart=on-failure`: the unit's `quotameter run` ExecStart exits 1 immediately — no configuration in the unit's clean environment — so the start-job outcome is machine state at the instant of the call; the captured divergence reproduced under concurrent invocations, the dry run's parallel load, while sequential pairs stayed green on both containers) and through the probe timeout. D-100's consequences sentence had already scoped reproducibility to the collection+rendering path while later steps "legitimately differ between runs": the service-setup step (task 137) is that family, and the test had normalized the output's every dimension except the session. (2) **Hermeticity is enforced at the spawn boundary, because that is the real launcher's only test-reachable knob**: `test/helpers/hermetic-child-env.ts` (`hermeticChildEnv`) builds the child environment minus `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` and the `DBUS_*` session addresses (`DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS`, `DBUS_STARTER_ADDRESS`, `DBUS_STARTER_BUS_TYPE` — belt-and-braces against a re-widened gate), passing everything else through verbatim, into a fresh object that never mutates the parent. With no own `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, the probe never spawns the user query (`userManager: false` by construction) and the step takes the deterministic write-only `user-manager-unavailable` route on systemd machines — no `systemctl --user` query and no user-unit commands, byte-identical output wherever the read-only system-manager verification's own answer is stable; on systemd-less machines (the D-162 job containers and the development container) nothing changes, as the probe returns at the marker before anything is spawned. `cli-init-yes.spec.ts` derives every child env through the helper and pins the contract executably (the strip set, verbatim pass-through, the fresh-object guarantee, the `process.env` default base); the reproducibility assertion itself is unchanged in strength and extended in evidence — identical bytes still required, stderr identity now compared too, and BOTH normalized stdouts plus both stderrs plus the divergence offset dumped in the assertion message. The fixed suite verified green on both live-systemd containers, including 8 concurrent full-suite runs (160/160 cells) under the exact invocation shape that reproduced the failure. The alternative — weakening the assertion (normalizing away the service-setup block) — was rejected: it would silence exactly the machine-dependence the cell exists to notice, shrinking D-100's pin to the prefix the test finds convenient. (3) **Byte-identity assertions must be self-evidencing**: Stryker truncates assertion strings to ~40 characters, and the failure class stayed undiagnosed for four daily runs precisely because neither the logs nor the default diff showed the bytes. The residual is documented, not fixed: on a live-systemd machine the unreachable-manager route still WRITES the unit file under the invoking user's passwd home (env `HOME` cannot redirect the §5.3 owner — D-162's recorded invariant; the write is task 137's own decision), and a saturated live-systemd machine can still flip the system-manager probe between absent and present through its 10-second timeout race — nothing at the env boundary can pin a machine fact, which is exactly why the daily gate's guarantee is D-162's systemd-less job container rather than this helper alone. Making the remaining real-launcher suites session-hermetic (`cli-init.spec.ts`, `cli-init-idempotent.spec.ts`, `cli-init-service.spec.ts` still spawn with the parent environment — their cells' assertions hold in the D-162 systemd-less class, and `cli-init-service` is inherently a D-162-environment suite: its asserted absent-route text is unreachable on any live-systemd machine with or without the helper) remains D-162's open follow-up territory; the helper is the shared seam for that adoption.

**Reasons.** Every competing hypothesis was eliminated against evidence before the fix was chosen: the assertion truncation meant the diverging bytes were not in any log, so the cell's spawn shape was re-executed in privileged systemd containers reproducing the hosted shape on both relevant systemd generations (Debian 252 and Ubuntu 26.04/257, a live user manager for uid 1001, the session environment) — the service-setup block is the machine's only channel into the output, the keyed connection test is guard-blocked into a deterministic class (the guard throws synchronously before any network I/O; the captured prefix proves the whole collected block byte-identical), and the summary/config-path lines are pure functions of the flags. The captured bytes name one face of the mechanism precisely: run 1's `systemctl --user enable --now` exiting 0 against run 2's failing with `Job for quotameter.service failed because the control process exited with error code.` — the start-job outcome of a unit whose ExecStart (`quotameter run`, no configuration in the unit's clean environment) exits 1 and auto-restarts (`Restart=on-failure`) is machine state at the instant of the call, which concurrent invocations demonstrably split between the two runs (sequential pairs stayed green on both containers — the dry run's parallel load is part of the failure's conditions, which is why only the daily gate saw it). The other face, the probe's 10-second timeout race, is not guesswork but deduction from the same jobs' own results: `cli-init-service.spec.ts` passed beside the failing cell, and on a systemd-PID1 host its asserted absent-route text is reachable only through the probe timing out — so the race was firing in those jobs and can split the absent/present routes between two back-to-back runs. The container evidence plus D-162's recorded "live user systemd" observation and the 11-05 green dry run triangulate the same root: the child's service-setup output is machine state, and a spawned child cannot have machine state pinned through its environment alone — the helper removes the session dimension (everything the environment controls: the user-manager gate and the machine-mutating user-unit route), while the machine-fact dimension (the system-probe marker and its timeout) is why the daily gate's guarantee is the D-162 container, not the helper. The spawn-boundary placement follows D-162's own reasoning — the integration suites cannot inject the step's seams, so the environment is the only knob — and it is the robust fix regardless of which session variable a future runner image sets first: the probe's gate (`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`) is the one variable the step's session-determinism turns on, and stripping the set it belongs to cannot break a systemd-less run (the probe returns at the marker before anything is spawned). Scope discipline: the product code is untouched — the step's machine-state dependence is task 137/138's designed behavior, and reproducibility was never promised of it (D-100's consequences); what the test owed was a pinned environment, and that is what landed.

**Consequences.** The daily mutation workflow's initial test run is green again in its job container (D-162 — no systemd, no probe, no race), and `cli-init-yes` is session-hermetic on any machine: deterministic wherever the system-manager probe's answer is stable, machine-mutating never (no `systemctl --user` execution). The next scheduled run is the final confirmation. Future real-launcher suites should derive their child environments from `hermeticChildEnv` from the start (the remaining three still spawn with the parent environment and stay correct only in the D-162 systemd-less class), and any assertion comparing process output byte-for-byte should carry its own evidence in the failure message (the pattern is in the reproducibility cell). A future change that widens the probe's session gate (say, a new session variable) must update `SESSION_MANAGER_ENV_KEYS` — the pin cell names the current set. Nothing in `src/**`, `bin/**`, or `stryker.config.mjs` changes; D-100's contract text needs no successor because its "flags + environment" reading is what this decision implements.

## D-174 — The guard-deadline-coupled interleaving class: in-process test windows constructed behind a product-internal deadline size that deadline from the same rig census (spec §17.1, §5.6; task U-048)

**Date:** 2026-11-06 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§17.1](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#171-required-test-coverage), [§5.6](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#56-process-lifecycle-backups-and-upgrades) · **Tasks:** [U-048](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-086, D-094, D-163

**Decision.** `test/integration/single-instance.spec.ts`'s cell "never removes a live guard captured mid-break and degrades to contention" flaked once in U-030's landing `make check-all` (2026-11-06: `expected '{"pid":4100001}\n' to be '{"pid":4100002}\n'` at the guard-path read; green in isolation ×3 and in a full re-run). Root cause, proven by code trace and executably: the cell constructs D-086's documented one-level-down race through the `isAlive` probe counter — probe #1 judges the stale guard dead, and probe #2 (inside `captureAndDecide`'s removable-decision) installs the live replacement at the freshly vacated guard path, so the captured stale guard is not removable, the restoring link degrades to `EEXIST`, and the stale capture waits aside as crash residue. But `acquireGuard` arms its deadline at entry and checks it right after the FIRST failed `publishGuard` — before any liveness probe — and the cell had left `guardTimeoutMs: 20`: one scratch-write + `link(2)` + scratch-rm through the loaded libuv threadpool can exceed that under full coverage-pool load, and acquisition then degrades to contention BEFORE the mid-break window exists (`isAlive` never runs, no capture happens, the guard path keeps the setup's stale payload) while the refusal itself still lands via the attempt limit — the exact observed payload-identity failure. Pinned interpretations: (1) **Evidence** — the mechanism reproduces deterministically at `guardTimeoutMs: 0` (byte-identical failure, `isAlive` probe count 0) and live at 1-of-10 isolated runs under the six-hog rig at ambient load ~22 (worst measured start→capture span 58 ms isolated-rig — the sizing basis; one warm in-pool sample measured 5 ms, not a worst). (2) **The fix is D-163's verdict applied one level down** — the interleaving hook is already causal (a probe counter inside the product's own decision path, the in-process sibling of a U-001/U-002 marker); the racing deadline is the product's own knob, not a `vi.waitFor`, so the knob is sized from the same rig census per D-094's ≈3× bar: `guardTimeoutMs: 1000` margins the measured worst by ≈17×, and the ~1 s post-capture wait it buys is the pinned semantics itself — the guard loop provably cannot exit against a live holder except by deadline. Payloads, the poll interval, `maxAttempts`, and every assertion are byte-identical, and the probe hook keeps its counter shape with one tightening from the review round (P3-1): the live replacement is installed exactly once, at the capture-decision probe — the pre-existing hook re-ran the install on every later poll, which the old 20 ms budget made ~5 rewrites and the sized deadline ~300, so the final path assertion observed the hook's last write rather than the product keeping the replacement; install-once restores that discriminating power with the terminal state unchanged (the live guard is never removed, the stale capture degrades to kept-aside residue, exactly as before). (3) **The product protocol is sound under every deadline interleaving** — deadline preemption degrades to the same bounded contention refusal (the attempt limit) with every §5.6/D-086 invariant intact (no live guard removed, nothing published into a vacancy); no product change is warranted. (4) **Scope of the class** — only cells whose asserted terminal state is deadline-order-sensitive need sized deadlines: the wedged-guard, dangling-symlink, and abandoned-release cells converge to their asserted states under every deadline interleaving and keep their fast 20 ms values.

**Reasons.** Rewriting the cell as a marker handshake (the U-047/D-167 shape) has no subject here: the whole interleaving lives inside one in-process `acquireLock` call, and the only nondeterminism was the deadline racing the first hook invocation — sizing margins exactly that race (nothing else in the cell was timing-dependent), the same acceptance every sized wait in the census carries: a >1 s stall between `acquireGuard` entry and its first failed `publishGuard` still reproduces the original failure and remains D-163's extreme-burst residual class. Only that first check needs to fit: no deadline check sits between probe #1 and the capture decision at probe #2, so an expiry later in the loop still yields the asserted terminal state. Fixing the product instead (arming the guard deadline at first observed contention rather than at entry) would change §5.6 product behavior to accommodate a test's arbitrary 20 ms budget: the preemption is legal, bounded, and safe, so the test must own its margin, the same verdict D-087 reached for transport deadlines. 1000 ms rather than a rounded ≈3× (≈180 ms) because it equals the product's default guard budget — an equality that is stated, not enforced (`DEFAULT_GUARD_TIMEOUT_MS` is unexported; exporting it would widen the module's API for a documentation claim, so a future default change re-measures per the standing rule instead) — and its post-capture cost (~1 s) is precisely the wait the cell pins.

**Consequences.** The cell's docblock records the mechanism and the measurements; `docs/agents/gotchas.md`'s D-094 census note gains the class (in-process windows behind product-internal deadlines size from the same rig census; deadline-order-convergent cells stay fast). Review round (deepseek-v4.1-flash, one round, 0 P0/P1/P2, 4 P3): all four accepted — the install-once hook (P3-1, folded into (2) above; the reviewer measured 303 hook rewrites at the sized deadline against ~5 at the old one), the margin-not-removal and first-check scoping wording (P3-2), the load-ratio arithmetic and the warm-sample qualifier (P3-3), and the stated-not-coupled default equality (P3-4 — wording over export: no investigation-demanded product seam). Stability matrix at the final value: isolated cell ×3 ambient and ×5 rig green (pre-fix: 1/10 preempted under the same rig); the full suite ×2 ambient (58/58, ~31 s) and ×2 rig (58/58, 69/80 s) green; after the P3-1 hook tightening, the cell green again ambient ×3 and rig ×3 and the full suite green rig ×1 and ambient ×1; full coverage `make check` green under the rig and at ambient. One full coverage `make check` under the rig (pre-tightening) saw this cell pass in-pool while an unrelated real-process marker cell ("makes a second real process exit 1…", the `held` wait) tripped at combined ambient+rig load ~38 — roughly double the D-163 census regime (pool ~14–17, ambient waves ~18), that decision's explicitly recorded extreme-burst residual, recorded here and not chased. No `src/**` file changed; future lock-protocol tests that construct interleavings behind `guardTimeoutMs` (or any product deadline) size from a rig census of the span up to the deadline's first check, per this entry.

## D-175 — Task U-050's real `run` command: the lazy server import for the dispatch graph, exit-code forwarding with the §16 stream untouched, and the answered-request readiness equivalence for foreground children (spec §5.2, §5.6, §16, §5.4; task U-050)

**Date:** 2026-11-06 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§5.2](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#52-cli-commands), [§5.6](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#56-process-lifecycle-backups-and-upgrades), [§16](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#16-logging-and-diagnostics), [§5.4](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#54-systemd-unit-requirements) · **Tasks:** [U-050](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-044 (the dispatch contract the handler plugs into), D-024 (the signal-readiness seam this task's tests express through the public surface), D-095/U-022 (runServer's best-effort stop, kept intact), D-140 (the composition runServer now gets a production caller for), D-098 (the launcher's runtime gate), D-173 (the hermetic child environments the new suite spawns with)

**Decision.** Task U-050 makes `quotameter run` a real leaf command in the new `src/cli/run.ts` and pins four interpretations. (1) **The server entry point is imported lazily, inside the handler** (`defaultImportServerMain`, an injectable seam): `buildCommandTable()` loads for every CLI invocation, and a static `runServer` import would drag the composition root, Fastify, Pino, and `node:sqlite` (whose ExperimentalWarning would then print on every unrelated command) into `--help` — the same graph discipline `doctor`'s lazy `MINIMUM_NODE_VERSION` and the storage-opening commands' lazy connection imports already follow. A failing dynamic import needs no handler code: it propagates to `runLeaf`'s catch and is reported as the standard command failure (`quotameter run: <message>`, exit 1). (2) **Exit-code forwarding with zero handler output.** `runServer` owns the process semantics unchanged — the runtime gate, §6.2's refuse-to-start through its own `quotameter:` stderr channel, §5.6's graceful SIGTERM/SIGINT shutdown, and D-095's awaited best-effort stop; the handler calls it once and returns its code. The handler deliberately writes nothing through the CLI output seam: a foreground service's stdout is §16's structured-log JSON stream journald collects, and CLI chatter there would pollute the log feed systemd's `StandardOutput=journal` exists to collect. §5.2 defines no options and no positionals for the command, so the row declares none and the handler reads nothing from its context. (3) **Readiness for a foreground child is an answered HTTP request.** The real-launcher suite polls `GET /api/health` (§13's public route) until it answers, then signals — the D-024 handshake invariant expressed through the public surface instead of the `onSignalsReady` marker (production never passes the seam; it stays a test/embedder channel). The equivalence is structural, not hoped-for: the listener is the LAST §5.6 component, so an answered request proves `app.start()` settled, and `runServer`'s synchronous post-`await` continuation (keep-alive interval, `installShutdownSignals`) runs on the microtask queue before any macrotask can serve the request — no answered request can precede the handlers. (4) **The stub era ends here**: `notImplemented` and the private `stub` builder are deleted from `commands.ts` — no §5.2 command uses them, they are internal API under `src/cli/` (never package surface), and uncovered leftover exports would fight the coverage gate for no consumer.

**Reasons.** The unit's `ExecStart=<node> <cli> run` (D-103's pinned shape, validated by `expectUnitExecStartRun`) makes the CLI command the service's whole production entry point — but wiring it naively (a static import) would tax every unrelated invocation with the server's module graph and its `node:sqlite` warning, a regression of the load-discipline earlier commands established command-by-command; the dynamic import inside the handler is the minimal shape that keeps both properties (invocation-light graph, real service on `run`). Exit-code forwarding without output follows from who owns each stream: `runServer`'s fatal channel predates the CLI handler and is already the §6.2 diagnosis surface, while stdout's JSON contract belongs to §16 and journald — a handler that "helpfully" announced startup would corrupt the one stream the spec pins. The readiness equivalence matters because the alternative (passing `onSignalsReady` in production to write a marker file) would add test-only file I/O to the production path D-024 explicitly rejected; the microtask-ordering argument gives the same kill-safety guarantee from facts the service already publishes, and the answered `/api/health` doubles as positive proof the composed application (D-140) actually serves — stronger evidence than a marker written beside it.

**Consequences.** A fresh `init` on a systemd machine now installs a unit whose service starts (tasks 196–199's blocker); `quotameter status`'s and `logs`' foreground-run guidance (`quotameter run` as the manual next step) names a working command. The lazy-import seam is `RunCommandDeps.importServerMain` (tests inject a module double; `defaultImportServerMain` itself is covered by resolving it — module load has no side effects). The done-condition is pinned at three levels: `test/unit/cli-run.spec.ts` (forwarding, propagation, the import seam, and the full default path hermetically in-process — `runCli(['run'])` over temp directories refuses on the missing configuration, exit 1, the CLI seam silent), `test/integration/cli-run.spec.ts` (the real launcher: health-answered → SIGTERM → exit 0 with the §5.6 lock released and the fatal channel silent; the invalid-configuration exit-1 route; and the inverse pin — a `--help` child whose stderr carries no `node:sqlite` warning), and `cli-bin.spec.ts`'s `run --help` process-boundary pin. Future commands that need the server graph follow the same lazy-import shape; making any unrelated command load it statically should fail that suite's inverse pin. The systemd unit contract is unchanged (no D-103 interaction); the exported surface (`runRunCommand`, `RunCommandDeps`, `defaultImportServerMain` in `src/cli/run.ts`) is internal API under `src/`, not package surface.

## D-176 — Task U-051's polling composition: the documented component order with the shared tracker and drain, the engine module's account selection, the dual D-064 machine fed in lockstep, the reload feeds beside the config-sync, and the time-compression test seam (spec §7.1, §7.2, §5.6, §6.4, §17.1; task U-051)

**Date:** 2026-11-06 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§7.1](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#71-polling), [§7.2](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#72-retry-and-error-behavior), [§5.6](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#56-process-lifecycle-backups-and-upgrades), [§6.4](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#64-runtime-settings-changes), [§17.1](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#171-required-test-coverage) · **Tasks:** [U-051](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-140 (the composition root whose polling deferral this entry discharges — its recorded plan for the holder/engine split is made concrete here), D-066 (the scheduler whose engine this wires; its "the composition root registers the scheduler as the polling LifecycleComponent with the shared in-flight tracker" consequence lands verbatim), D-069 (the recorder the wiring builds per account; the cancelled-unpersisted rule the shutdown ordering protects), D-064 (the suspension state machine — now instantiated twice, in lockstep), D-020 (the in-flight tracker and the graceful drain's documented order, finally registered), D-128 (the pre-sync seam the reload feeds ride), D-021 (the one shared clock), D-175 (the `run` command whose service now actually collects)

**Decision.** Task U-051 composes the polling engine into the running service as a new composition-root module, `src/server/polling.ts`, and pins six interpretations. (1) **The component order is `shutdown.ts`'s documented list**: `[single-instance-lock, storage, graceful-drain, polling, http-listener]` over one shared `createInFlightTracker()` — the scheduler registers its flights in it (`PollingSchedulerOptions.inFlight`) and the drain waits on it, so reverse-order teardown yields exactly §5.6's sentence: the listener closes (its own D-109 bound), the engine stops scheduling and aborts live flights (prompt, D-066), the drain's bounded wait covers the aborted cycles' actual settlement **while the database is still open** (a settling recorder's write — for a non-cancelled outcome — races no close; a cancelled outcome deliberately writes nothing, D-069), storage checkpoints and closes, the lock releases last. The drain's `onEvent` stream reaches the redacting logger: `drain-timeout` as `warn`, the rest as `debug`.
