## D-184 — The settings password change's fail-secure revocation order: sessions revoked BEFORE the configuration write (refining §15.2/§6.4 for the second password-change path), a failed revocation refusing with nothing written, the revoked-then-failed arm reported exactly, and the shared rationale of both paths given one home (spec §15.2, §6.4; task U-058)

**Date:** 2026-11-07 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§15.2](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#152-passwords-and-sessions), [§6.4](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#64-change-application) · **Tasks:** [U-058](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-118 (`quotameter passwd`'s fail-secure order — the recorded reasoning this entry adopts for the second path), D-124 (the §15.2 session expiry/revocation semantics), D-130 (the `SettingsStore` seam whose `apply` contract gains one clause), D-140 (the composition's stores whose revocation-after-write order this entry supersedes — interpretation (4)'s "the revocation rides the accepted reload" pairing), D-113 (the frozen error registry — the failed arms ride the existing INTERNAL class), D-178/D-183 (the compact-entry precedent)

**Decision.** The 2026-11-06 full-project review found the two password-change paths disagreeing on security semantics: `quotameter passwd` revokes every session before it writes the configuration (D-118's fail-secure order), while `createConfigFileSettingsStore.apply` — the store behind `PUT /api/settings`'s password change — wrote the new `auth.passwordHash` through `owner.mutate` (persist + §6.4 reload) and only then called `repository.deleteAllSessions()`. This entry aligns the settings path with passwd's order and records the semantics both paths now share. (Correction trail: the task's review round — deepseek-v4.1-flash, one round, APPROVE with 1 P2 / 6 P3 — folded in before landing: the arm-true annotation of interpretation (3)'s revoked-then-failed wrapper (the first draft's "the next sign-in still needs the current password" is false in the reload-rejected arm, where the file already holds the new hash a later reload would apply), the seam clause of (5) extended to the second rejection meaning, the zero-count rule restated as the settings path's own (passwd's failure arm prints the count unconditionally), the shared doc's path set widened to init's fresh-password leg and its §6.4 step scoped to the paths that own the process, and the login-in-the-gap residual restated for the compromised-password case.) (1) **Revoke first (§15.2), write second — in the settings store too.** When `apply` carries a `pendingPassword`, the store deletes every session through the repository's `deleteAllSessions` BEFORE entering the serialized file mutation. The order is chosen by the failure-arm calculus: the reverse order's failed-revocation arm leaves the NEW hash effective with every old session still valid — the exact state "changing the password revokes all sessions" forbids, hidden behind a generic INTERNAL error the operator cannot distinguish from a failed write; the chosen order's worst case (revoked, then the write fails) is strictly more restrictive and is reported arm-truly, passwd's own recorded trade. (2) **A failed revocation refuses the change with nothing written.** A throwing `deleteAllSessions` rejects `apply` before anything is queued or written — the incumbent hash stays effective and its sessions stay coherent with it (§6.2's refuse-without-effect, extended to the storage leg). The rejection text is `revoking the sessions failed (the password change was refused, nothing was written): <storage error>`; the endpoint answers the existing INTERNAL envelope (D-113 — no new error code), the detail going to the logs, never the response body. (3) **The revoked-then-failed arm is reported arm-truly, and only when something was revoked.** If the mutation (validation, write, or reload) rejects after a revocation that deleted N > 0 sessions, the error is rethrown wrapped — the cause's own text plus "(the password change did not complete, but N stored session(s) had already been revoked — the running service keeps the current password, and the configuration file may already hold the new hash, which a later reload would apply)", `cause` preserved. The uncertainty is deliberate: what the file holds depends on where the mutation failed (a refused candidate or a failed atomic write leaves it untouched; a rejected reload leaves it ahead of memory, §6.2), and the message must be true in every arm — the review round's P2 corrected the first draft, which claimed the next sign-in needs the current password unconditionally. A zero-count revocation lost nothing and rethrows bare (the settings path's own no-noise rule; passwd's failure arm prints the count unconditionally, zero included). (4) **The revocation runs OUTSIDE the file owner's mutation queue, deliberately.** The queue serializes file read-modify-writes; the revocation is a synchronous storage call that needs no atomicity with the write — every interleaving is fail-secure (worst case: sessions revoked for a change that then fails, arm (3)) — and keeping it outside leaves the mutation callback a pure file edit. (5) **`SettingsStore.apply`'s seam contract gains its revocation clauses** (in `src/server/api/settings.ts`): a rejected promise means the write or reload failed (§6.2, INTERNAL) **or, for a password change, one of the revocation's two arms** — the pre-write revocation itself failed (nothing written; the incumbent hash stays effective with its sessions coherent), or the revocation succeeded and the change then failed (the incumbent hash stays effective, but every stored session is gone). The endpoint's behavior is unchanged otherwise. (6) **The shared rationale of the password-writing paths lives once**, in `docs/security/password-change-revocation.md` (the rule, the failure-arm table of both directions, each path's honest-reporting wording, the residuals); the code docblocks (`passwd.ts`, `init.ts`, the store, the seam), `src/cli/README.md`, `src/server/README.md` (whose "after a password write … the fail-safe direction" sentence was the inverted rationale), and the stale task-144-only mentions in `src/services/sessions.ts`/`src/services/README.md` point at it.

**Reasons.** §15.2's sentence is a security invariant about the state after a password change, not a step order — but only one step order can keep the invariant true in every reachable state: revoking after the write makes the invariant false in the failed-revocation state, and the operator cannot see it (the UI gets a generic INTERNAL, the same class a failed write produces, and the retry a broken database guarantees failing too). Revoking before the write makes the worst reachable state MORE restrictive than the operator asked (logged out, password unchanged) — an inconvenience, not a vulnerability — which is why `passwd` chose that direction in D-118 and why consistency between the two paths is the security property itself: an operator who learns one path's semantics must not be wrong about the other. The outside-the-queue placement follows from what the queue is FOR (file RMW serialization against interleaved section edits, D-140); a storage delete does not participate in that hazard, and placing it inside the mutation callback would do I/O in a contract-documented pure edit and still have arm (3) to report. The zero-count rule keeps the report informative: an annotation about zero revoked sessions states nothing the operator can act on.

**Consequences.** `src/server/config-stores.ts`'s `apply` revokes before `owner.mutate` and drops the old `passwordWritten`-then-revoke tail; the store's and the seam's docblocks state the order and both rejection meanings. Accepted residuals, recorded in the shared doc: the login-in-the-gap window (a sign-in between revocation and write mints a session under the incumbent password that survives the change — every path shares the gap; harmless for a stolen-session attacker under §15.1's single-user model because a sign-in requires the password, but a real narrow leak for the compromised-password attacker the change usually answers — closing it, by a second post-write `deleteAllSessions` or a sign-in gate, must be one successor decision for every path and owns its new failure arm), and the reload-rejected file-ahead state (the file holds the new hash while the running service keeps the old one until a reload, §6.2 — D-140's pre-existing residual, now with sessions already revoked: still fail-secure). D-140's interpretation (4) pairing sentence ("the revocation rides the accepted reload") is superseded by this entry (immutable, superseded here per the house rule). The done-condition is pinned executably in `test/integration/config-stores.spec.ts`: the harness's repository double snapshots the raw file bytes at each revocation (the happy path's snapshot carries no hash — the order proof), an injected rejecting `deleteAllSessions` leaves the file byte-identical with the old `scrypt$` hash and `reload.calls === 0` (the mandated cell), a placement cell pins that the revocation precedes even the mutation's file read (a malformed file plus the failing revocation answers the revocation error, not the read error), a rejected reload after a 2-session revocation carries both facts in one message with the file-ahead state asserted (the file holds the new hash) and the cause chain preserved, and a zero-count revocation rethrows bare. The composition suite's password cells (end state: hash stored, session gone) run unchanged. No public API, wire, or event change — the INTERNAL class, the response contracts, and `passwd` are untouched; the new doc is additive. Changing the order or the failure semantics of any password-writing path again is a successor decision to this entry.

## D-185 — History/events reads tolerate clock-skewed rows: inverted runs skipped and pre-coverage points left unjudgeable at the API composition boundary, with sanitized §16 diagnostics (spec §12.2, §13, §16; task U-057)

**Date:** 2026-11-07 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§12.2](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#122-collection-gaps-and-errors), [§13](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#13-http-api), [§16](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#16-logging-and-diagnostics) · **Tasks:** [U-057](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-034 (the deliberate no-CHECK schema this entry reads back), D-069 (the per-run `interval_seconds` stamps the timeline consumes), D-075 (the gap detector's coverage fail-fast and the fail-safe precedent Rule 2 follows), D-080 (the timeline walk's inverted-cycle fail-fast Rule 1 pre-filters), D-139 (the routes this gate guards)

**Decision.** The §12.2/§13 history reads (`GET /api/history`, `GET /api/events`) tolerate clock-skewed database rows through one explicit gate, `src/services/history-skew.ts`, plus one skew-aware stamp rule in the interval-timeline adapter (task U-057; the verified 2026-11-06 review finding: the schema deliberately permits skewed rows — D-034 rejected an `ended_at >= started_at` CHECK because both stamps are wall-clock reads around one HTTP cycle and a rejected INSERT would lose the run record — but the read stack assumed the ordering, so one NTP step-back could 500 the affected range). The rules, applied where ordinary rows enter the consumers — the API composition, not the pure services: **Rule 1 — a run with `endedAt < startedAt` has its span skipped and its record kept: projected to a zero-duration cycle at its trusted `startedAt`** (`projectInvertedRuns`). §12.2's stopped class is record-based ("periods with no collection-run records at all"), so the row's EXISTENCE is the aliveness evidence and does not depend on stamp ordering; the contradictory SPAN is what cannot be trusted — under a step-back `startedAt` is the pre-correction, positionally anchored read and `endedAt` the post-correction one — so the honest projection collapses the span to zero at `startedAt` (asserting no duration, only the record's existence and start anchor): the record still bounds stopped silence and a failed cycle still emits its error marker at the trusted stamp with `durationMs: 0` (the wire schema carries no minimum; §14.4 places markers on the start stamp alone and renders non-positive durations as `0s`). The first draft SKIPPED the row from the indicator walk; the review round's P1 (grok-4.7-high, high confidence) proved that dropping it lets two sub-threshold neighbor silences merge into one beyond-threshold span and fabricates a hatched outage across a cycle that demonstrably ran (legs of 800 000 ms merging over the 990 000 ms threshold at the 300 s cadence) — the skip was replaced by the projection before landing. **Rule 2 — a valid point whose `collectedAt` precedes the interval timeline's first change (or faces an empty timeline) is unjudgeable** (`dropUnjudgeablePoints`): dropped from the gap detector's input only — the point itself still renders as series data in `/api/history`; no gap is minted from or to it. The bound is inclusive (a change exactly at a point's stamp applies to it — `intervalSecondsAt`'s own resolution). **Rule 3 — a skewed interval change is anchored at `min(startedAt, endedAt)`** (inside `intervalTimelineFromRuns`): an inverted change-run's `startedAt` is late-biased and can sit after the first snapshot collected under the new cadence; trusting it would judge the straddling pairs by the old, tighter cadence and mint false gaps (a 60→3600 grow with a late-biased start is the mirror of the seeding case Rule 2 rejects — the review round's P2). The earlier stamp only widens more pairs (D-075's span-widening direction), never tightens one; the timeline's FIRST entry keeps the raw `startedAt` even when inverted, because it doubles as Rule 2's coverage bound and moving it earlier would seed judgment for points the evidence does not cover; the output stays ascending under an extreme step-back (sorted). Both gate functions are pure and generic-preserving (no run or point lost, duplicated, or reordered; non-inverted rows pass through by reference; inputs untouched), each emitting at most one aggregated sanitized diagnostic. **Where the tolerance lives: the composition boundary.** The pure services' fail-fast contracts stand unchanged — D-075's "every point must fall inside the timeline's coverage … fails loudly" and D-080's inverted-cycle throw remain the wiring-mistake tripwires they were designed as; the routes know their inputs are ordinary database rows under the D-034 lenient schema, and the gate is the single explicit site adapting database reality to the services' contracts (the AGENTS.md state-machine discipline: a fixed classification of evidence, not scattered conditions — the rules table lives in the module docblock). **Diagnostics surface through §16 logging, never the wire**: the routes aggregate the gate's diagnostics (`mergeSkewDiagnostics` — one report per rule per account, counts summed and bounds widened, so a skewed snapshot under a three-metric account logs one `unjudgeable_point` warn, not three; diagnostics of different coverage bounds never merge) and emit them as request-scoped Pino `warn` records (the default level — a skewed row is a data-quality anomaly the operator should see; §16's request-logging debug carve-out is about access logging, not data-quality reports), sanitized by construction — kind, account, count, epoch-millisecond bounds; never a row payload, error message, or key. The response schemas are byte-identical: no public contract changes.

**Reasons.** The rejected alternative for Rule 2 — seed the timeline's first change to cover all earlier instants — fabricates cadence coverage: after a 3600→60 §6.4 interval change, pre-coverage points ten minutes apart would be judged by the seeded 60 s cadence (threshold 198 s) and mint a false gap while the cadence actually in effect (threshold 11,880 s) says none, fabricating exactly the outage §12.2's honest-indicators purpose forbids; leaving the pair unjudged follows D-075's fail-safe precedent (ambiguous schedule evidence resolves to no gap; §12.1's "do not create an event when evidence is ambiguous" spirit) and the timestamps are untrustworthy in a skew-corrupted stretch anyway. The first draft's rejected alternative for Rule 1 — drop the inverted row from the indicator walk — violates §12.2's own definition of the stopped class: the class is record-existence-based, so discarding a record fabricates "no collection activity" across a cycle that ran whenever the merged neighbor silence crosses the threshold (the review round's P1 scenario); swapping the stamps was also rejected — it repairs evidence into a span that never occurred. The zero-duration projection asserts nothing false: no duration is claimed (zero is the explicit unknown-but-bounded value), the marker position rides the start stamp the design already trusts for cadence, and the projection can only under-report silence (the trailing silence starts at the late-biased start anchor, shortening it by at most the skew magnitude — the fail-safe direction). Rule 3's earlier anchor is forced by the same asymmetry that motivates D-075's span-widening: stamping a change EARLIER can only widen pairs (fewer gaps), stamping it late tightens them (false gaps), so the fail-safe direction is the earlier of the two reads. Keeping the tolerance out of the services preserves the fail-fast tripwires for their designed audience (the §13 adapter, tests, wiring) at the one layer that knows the rows are database reality; the empty-timeline arm closes a second latent 500 for free (points with no runs in the evidence set previously tripped the detector's empty-timeline RangeError on the `validPoints.length !== 0` path).

**Consequences.** A clock step-back can no longer 500 the history/events reads; an affected range answers 200 with every real indicator intact and the skew visible as aggregated §16 warns. Under-reporting is the accepted cost and the bounded one: a real outage whose only evidence is a pre-coverage pair is not marked, and an inverted failed cycle's marker carries a zero duration instead of its unknowable true span; the trailing silence after a projected run can under-report by at most the skew magnitude (the fail-safe direction). The exported names (`projectInvertedRuns`, `dropUnjudgeablePoints`, `mergeSkewDiagnostics`, `InvertedRunVerdict`, `UnjudgeablePointVerdict`, `SkewDiagnostic`, `InvertedRunDiagnostic`, `UnjudgeablePointDiagnostic`) and the `intervalTimelineFromRuns` change-anchor rule are contract; changing the semantics requires a successor decision. `test/unit/history-skew.spec.ts` pins the deterministic table (the zero-duration projection with reference passthrough for sound rows, the inclusive coverage edge, 1 ms before it, zero-duration runs, aggregation bounds in unsorted input, the empty-timeline arm, the merge keys); `test/unit/history-skew.property.spec.ts` proves the projection/partition/identity shapes over generated input; `test/unit/api-history-view.spec.ts` pins the change-anchor cells (a skewed grow anchored at the earlier stamp; ascending output under an extreme step-back); the `test/integration/api-history.spec.ts` and `api-events.spec.ts` D-185 blocks seed the mixed clean/skewed world through the real facade write path (`persistCollectionCycle` — no CHECK rejects the skew, which is the point) and assert the 200s, the unjudgeable silence minting nothing beside the real gap, the inverted failed cycle marking at zero duration while a normal failure keeps its true span, the two-legal-legs-never-merge regression (the review P1: exactly the leading and trailing stopped regions, nothing between the inverted run's neighbors), the skewed-change-no-false-gap regression (the review P2: a 60→3600 grow on an inverted change-run with no empty points), and the aggregated sanitized warns on the log sink. The input-contract docblocks (`history-gaps.ts` `intervalSecondsAt`, `history-timeline.ts` `requireRuns` and `CollectionRunInput.endedAt`) carry the database-reality exception notes; `src/services/README.md` gains the module entry. D-075's and D-080's fail-fast clauses are superseded in composition context only — the entries stay untouched (immutable), with this entry as their read-side companion.

## D-186 — The first public release is v0.1.0: a full-cycle rehearsal at 0.x, 1.0.0 as the distinct §19 milestone, pre-1.0 semver semantics, and the release-policy home for first-release numbering (spec §4.4, §19; docs/release.md; task 200)

**Date:** 2026-11-07 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§4.4](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#44-cicd-and-supply-chain-safeguards), [§19](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#19-mvp-acceptance-criteria) · **Tasks:** [200](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-008 (releases published only from CI on version tags — the gate the v0.1.0 rehearsal exercises), D-152 (the release workflow's publish pipeline the rehearsal runs end to end), D-180 and D-183 (the spec-amendment precedent weighed here and deliberately not triggered), D-155 (the name-based license self-exclusion that makes any first-release version bump safe)

**Decision.** The first published release of `quotameter` is **`v0.1.0`**, not `1.0.0`: `docs/release.md`'s versioning paragraph is rewritten accordingly, superseding its prior sentence that "the first tagged release will be `1.0.0` and must satisfy the MVP acceptance criteria in the specification (§19)". The §19↔1.0.0 link survives the change — **`1.0.0` is the distinct milestone release, the one that closes every §19 MVP acceptance criterion** — but the first publication itself is a deliberate full-cycle rehearsal of the release process (version commit → tag → release workflow → trusted publishing → npm publication → clean-container install verification), carrying no §19 completeness requirement and leaving room for iteration before stabilization. Pre-1.0 semver semantics are defined in the same paragraph: while the version is `0.x`, breaking changes and new functionality bump MINOR (`0.Y+1.0`) and PATCH covers backwards-compatible fixes; the MAJOR/MINOR/PATCH rules of the paragraph above apply unchanged from `1.0.0` on. Task 200's text (status untouched, per the cycle rule that only the main session flips statuses) now states the 0.1.0 gates — a working tarball published from the release workflow on a green-CI `master` commit, `npm install -g quotameter@0.1.0` starting successfully in a clean container on the supported runtime — with the full §19 gate expressed as the `1.0.0`-milestone clause inside task 200 (chosen over filing a separate milestone task now; the clause becomes that task when task 199's evidence is complete). Echo corrections in the same commit: the bug-report template's version placeholder reads `quotameter 0.1.0`, and README's scope sentence can no longer be read as the first publication number.

**Reasons.** (1) A first publication at 0.1.0 rehearses the entire release machinery — D-152's workflow, D-008's green-CI tag gate, trusted publishing, provenance, the tarball allowlist, the clean-container install — at a version that promises nothing semantically, which is exactly what a never-exercised pipeline should first carry; discovering the pipeline's operational friction at 1.0.0 would make the stabilization announcement double as the pipeline's shakedown. (2) Semver's own posture for 0.x ("anything may change") is made operational: a user installing a 0.x package is told by the version itself that the contracts are not yet stable, so a breaking change costs a MINOR bump rather than a MAJOR one, and the 1.0.0 promise — "this is the stabilized contract set" — is reserved for the release that has actually satisfied §19. (3) The specification needs no amendment: a repo-wide census (this commit) shows `plan/SPECIFICATION.md` never asserted a first-release number — §4.4's release sentence is version-agnostic ("Publish to public npm **only from CI** on a `vX.Y.Z` tag", "Follow semantic versioning") and remains true — so the D-180/D-183 amendment precedent is not triggered; the first-release number is release-process operational detail, and `docs/release.md` (the release-policy document task 193 created) is its deliberate home. (4) "Version 1.0" in §1.1/§1.2 (and the README sentence that mirrored it) is thereby disentangled from publication numbering: it is the product-scope label of the 1.0.0 milestone — the feature set the 0.x publication line iterates toward — never the number the first npm publication carries.

**Consequences.** `docs/release.md` is the source of truth for the first-release version; changing that policy again (for example, deciding to publish 1.0.0 directly) is a successor decision to this entry. `package.json` stays `0.0.0` until the v0.1.0 release commit (release-checklist step 3 bumps it; D-155's name-based license self-exclusion makes any bump safe), and `.github/workflows/release.yml` needed no change — its tag/version-match and green-CI gates are version-agnostic and guard `v0.1.0` exactly as they would have guarded `v1.0.0`. Pre-1.0 breaking changes (configuration, CLI commands, HTTP API, storage schema, documented behavior) publish as `0.Y+1.0` with a Changed changelog entry; the MAJOR-bump rule resumes at 1.0.0. The 1.0.0 milestone runs as its own release cycle through the same checklist once task 199's §19 evidence is complete, until then carried by task 200's clause. No executable pin asserted the old first-release claim — verified by the census: `test/unit/release-workflow.spec.ts` pins the workflow's structure (pin sync, gate order, trigger shape), not version numbers, and `test/unit/api-health-schema.spec.ts`'s `version: '1.0.0'` is an arbitrary schema-shape fixture — so the change is docs-only and gated by `make format-check` alone (the AGENTS.md docs-only rule). (Numbering note: the tasking brief provisionally named this entry D-184; D-184 and D-185 were already allocated to in-flight parallel tasks, so this entry takes D-186 per the highest-landed-plus-in-flight-plus-one house rule — landed max D-183.)

## D-187 — The §5.3 step-5/7/8 completion: init's fresh-run finalization as an explicit lifecycle (database aborts, service/health are contained), the bounded loopback health-verification seam shared with `service install`, and the step-8 summary contract whose SSH-tunnel hint renders exactly for loopback binds (spec §5.3, §5.4, §15.1, §15.5, §11.4; task U-059)

**Date:** 2026-11-07 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§5.3](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#53-init-workflow), [§5.4](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#54-systemd-unit-requirements), [§15.1](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#151-network-and-authentication-modes), [§15.5](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#155-headers-and-limits), [§11.4](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#114-migrations) · **Tasks:** [U-059](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-112 (the single-instance lock reader the database leg refuses under), D-101 (init's before-write ordering and the pending journey this entry keeps unprobed), D-102 (the step-6 tolerance this entry deliberately does not extend to step 5), D-106/D-108 (the step-7 routing and install machinery the verification half composes into), D-175 (the real `run` that makes a started init service a probe-able thing), D-116 (the dynamic-import `node:sqlite` discipline the database leg follows), D-154 (the guard-gap policy `redirect: 'error'` applies at the new fetch site), D-065 (§11.4's backup-then-migrate sequence, consumed read-only)

**Decision.** Task U-059 completes the three §5.3 halves a full-project review found deferred or advertised-but-absent: step 5's database ("create … the database" — `init-persist.ts` had deferred it to "task 133+", which landed without it), step 7's `/api/health` verification (the installer verified `is-active` only while `renderSystemUnitPlan` advertised both), and step 8's summary (settings values and the config path only). Five interpretations are pinned. (Correction trail: the task's review round — grok-4.7-high through cursor-agent, the first fallback (the deepseek primary timed out at its 1200 s bound with no findings text); one round, REQUEST_CHANGES with 1 P1 / 4 P2 / 5 P3 — is folded into this entry and the same commit, which had not landed when corrected (the D-119/D-122 precedent). Folded: the P1 (the poll's retry sleep was unref'd — mid-poll it is often the CLI process's only pending work, so a first refused attempt let the process drain to exit 0 before the deadline, the failure report, or the step-8 block; the sleep is deliberately ref'd and a child-process cell pins it against the real module), P2-1 (the database leg now reads the data directory's §5.6 lock first and refuses under a **live** holder, naming the pid — init must never run backup or DDL under a running service; an unreadable or invalid lock refuses fail-closed, a dead holder's stale lock proceeds), P2-2 (the data directory is chmod'd to `0700` after the recursive mkdir — `mkdir`'s mode is umask-masked, and `0177` would leave a traversability-less directory; the configuration path's own umask-exempt step), P2-3 (a timeout firing mid-body is a failed attempt with the timeout's own diagnostic, never a "wrong payload" verdict, and a non-200 answer cancels its body), P3-2 (a wildcard bind has no client-usable URL — the step-8 row renders the machine-address placeholder with the every-interface fact instead of `http://0.0.0.0:…`), P3-3 (the attempt result is a discriminated `{ok}` pair, not an empty-string sentinel), P3-4 (the install-side skip line names which of absent and invalid it was, the invalid arm carrying the detection's first problem), and P3-5 (interpretation (3) below supersedes D-108's recorded "deliberately not implemented here" clause explicitly). P2-4 (the refused-connection cell raced a just-freed port) was folded by splitting the pin: the cause-chain unwrapping is pinned deterministically through the real undici error shape, and the real fetcher's network path stays pinned against owned servers only. Two halves were declined with reasons: the symlink-refusal half of P2-2 (the landed service path — the §5.6 lock's own `ensureDataDir` — accepts a symlinked data directory, so tightening only init's copy would make init refuse states the service accepts; a data-dir symlink policy is a service-wide successor decision, and the secret-bearing artifact's symlink policy is already enforced by `enforceConfigPermissions`), and P3-1's stricter alternative (skipping the user-unit `enable --now` for a password-pending configuration — that start is task 137's landed design; this entry records the crash-loop as a residual instead). (1) **A fresh run's finalization is an explicit lifecycle — `write-config → database → service-setup → health-check → summary`, in that order, with exactly one abort rule beyond the write: the database step.** The new `src/cli/init-database.ts` runs after the consented write (the tasking brief's placement; it makes the remedy honest — the file the run just wrote is stated as kept): read the data directory's §5.6 single-instance lock (the landed D-112 reader over the exported `lockFilePath`/`isProcessAlive`; a **live** holder refuses naming the pid, an unreadable or invalid lock refuses fail-closed, a dead holder's stale lock and the fresh machine's absent lock proceed), create the data directory (`0700` — an explicit chmod after the recursive mkdir, umask-exempt), then `openStorageConnection` + `runStartupMigrations` over the canonical `MIGRATIONS` — the composition's own open/migrate pair, consumed through dynamic imports so `node:sqlite` stays out of every dispatch graph (D-116; the child's only new stderr is the module's ExperimentalWarning, the documented property of invocations that actually open a database — the reproducibility pin now normalizes the pid it embeds). Idempotent by construction: a surviving database (the D-141 world) migrates exactly as the service would at start. A failure aborts with exit 1, nothing installed, the written configuration explicitly kept — §5.3 step 5 is a must, not best-effort, and every reachable failure (unwritable data directory, corrupt file at the path, WAL-incapable filesystem, §11.4's newer-schema refusal) leaves an environment no service can start in; installing an auto-restarting unit over it would be the harmful alternative. The step-6 connection-test tolerance is the deliberate contrast: a bad key harms one account, a bad data directory harms the whole service. The remedy line names `quotameter run` (the service creates the database at its own start — re-running init does not retry a fresh-only step). (2) **The health verification is one shared seam, run only after a service was actually started.** `runServiceSetupStep` now returns `{ serviceStarted }` — true only on the user-unit route's successful `enable --now`, the one leg where init's own run put a service on the machine — and that return is init's probe precondition. `verifyServiceHealth` (`service-setup.ts`) is a bounded poll as an explicit two-state machine: one attempt resolves healthy (HTTP 200 **with** §13's `{"status":"ok"}` body) and ends; anything else (other status, network error, per-attempt timeout — a still-booting service refuses connections) is one bounded detail and a retry, until an attempt plus a full interval no longer fits the deadline; at least one attempt always runs. Budgets: 30 s total, 2 s per request (`AbortSignal.timeout`), 500 ms between attempts — sized to a freshly enabled unit's Node boot + database open + listener arm, so a first refusal is startup latency, never a verdict. The production fetcher is global `fetch` with `redirect: 'error'` (D-154's documented guard gap closed by policy at the fetch site). **The probe host is loopback by construction**: the configured host when it is itself loopback, otherwise `127.0.0.1` (a wildcard bind accepts loopback connections). A password-pending configuration is not probed — §15.1 refuses that start by design, the pending remedy line already said so, and spending the budget on a start that cannot happen helps nobody (the D-101 journey stays intact, unprobed). In init a failed probe is honest stderr plus `status`/`logs` guidance and never fails the run (the configuration is written, the unit installed; §5.3's manual fallbacks remain the designed outcome). (3) **`service install`'s system route completes §5.3 step 7's privileged verification — superseding D-108's recorded clause that "the `/api/health` half of §5.3 step 7's verification pair is deliberately not implemented here"** (the immutable entry stays; this paragraph is the successor the house rule requires, named because that clause was a scope decision of D-108's task, not a permanent contract): after `is-active`, the endpoint is resolved **best-effort** from the owner's configuration (the same `ownerUnitDirectories` §6.1 precedence the unit's `ReadWritePaths` use, read through init's own detection pipeline — one validator, no drift; the skip line names which of absent and invalid it was, the invalid arm carrying the detection's first problem) and probed; no usable configuration **skips** the probe with one honest line, never fails the command — D-108's structural independence (no configuration required anywhere in install) survives, because `is-active` already proved the start; a probe that ran and did not pass within its bound fails the install (exit 1) — §5.3's verify is that command's own contract, and the rendered plan's advertisement ("verifies it (systemctl is-active and /api/health)") is now true. The user route of `service install` does not probe: §5.3 prescribes verification for the privileged leg only, while init's own user-unit leg does (contained) because the tasking brief's done-condition binds it there — a spec-anchored asymmetry, recorded here as deliberate. (4) **The step-8 summary contract** (`renderInitNextSteps`, fresh runs only, closing the run): the effective URL (`http://<host>:<port>` — §15.1's service never terminates TLS itself, so the scheme is constant; an IPv6-literal host bracketed; a **wildcard** bind has no client-usable URL and renders the machine-address placeholder with the every-interface fact, review round P3), the SSH-tunnel access, the `quotameter status`/`quotameter logs` command names, and the configuration and data paths. **The tunnel hint renders exactly for a loopback bind**: only a loopback URL is unreachable from another machine, and the SSH tunnel is §15.5's named recommended remote-access method for exactly that world (`ssh -N -L <port>:<bind>:<port> user@<this-host>`, conditional wording that stays honest on a local machine); a non-loopback bind is directly reachable on the network, its §5.3 step-4 password note already renders, and reverse-proxy publication guidance is §15.5's documentation job, not a fresh-run summary's. This overturns the tasking brief's prior that the hint is "only meaningful for non-loopback binds" — the spec's own §15.5 sentence plus the reachability analysis settle the direction. (5) **What init owns vs the service**: init owns the artifacts of a _prepared_ machine — a validated configuration file, a data directory at `0700`, a database at the current schema — and never starts the service itself except through the installed unit's `enable --now`; the service owns everything from its own process start (the lock, WAL checkpointing, the listener). Init's database leg is therefore the service's storage-start sequence in miniature, consumed read-only through the same seams, never a second implementation.

**Reasons.** The abort-rule split follows what each step's failure means: a failed configuration write means nothing landed (abort, nothing written — the landed behavior); a failed database creation means the machine cannot run the service at all (abort loudly before a unit crash-loops under `Restart=on-failure`); a failed service installation or health probe means the operator has manual steps (§5.3 designs the fallback for exactly this, and a probe's timing budget can never prove a service _broken_ — only not-yet-answering — so failing the run over it would misreport). The loopback probe host follows the tasking brief's "bounded loopback GET" verbatim and keeps the probe inside the no-network guard's sanctioned host class, so the production fetcher is testable against a loopback server the suite owns. The pending-skip follows §15.1's own sentence: the refusal to start is _by design_, known before any probe, and already reported — a 30-second wait for it would be the one dishonest act in the flow. The install-side best-effort config read keeps D-108 whole: "independent of init" was recorded as _no configuration required_, and a read whose absence degrades to an honest skip (never a failure) does not make the command require anything. The tunnel-hint condition is reachability, not taste: for a loopback bind the printed URL is the only access path that needs help, and §15.5 names the tunnel as the recommendation; for a non-loopback bind the URL works as printed and the §5.3 step-4 note has already carried the security consequence.

**Consequences.** The exported surface (`InitDeps.createDatabase`/`checkServiceHealth`, `InitDatabaseStep`/`InitDatabaseOutcome` in `init-database.ts`; `ServiceSetupStepResult`, `ServiceHealth`, `ServiceHealthCheck`, `HealthFetcher`, `ServiceHealthSeams`, `verifyServiceHealth`, `healthProbeTarget`, `bracketHostForUrl`, `HEALTH_CHECK_DEADLINE_MS`/`HEALTH_CHECK_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS`/`HEALTH_CHECK_POLL_INTERVAL_MS`, and the three health renderers in `service-setup.ts`; `ServiceCommandDeps.checkServiceHealth` in `service-install.ts`) is internal API under `src/`, not package surface. Three residuals are recorded: a service bound to one specific non-loopback address may refuse the loopback probe while healthy on its own interface (the failure message names the probed URL and `quotameter status`; probing the configured address instead would leave the no-network guard's loopback class), every real-launcher fresh `init` run now prints `node:sqlite`'s ExperimentalWarning on stderr (accepted under D-116's discipline; the reproducibility pin normalizes the embedded pid exactly as it normalizes temp paths), and a password-pending fresh run on the user-unit route still enables the unit — which `Restart=on-failure` then cycles until `quotameter passwd` completes the configuration (skipping that start is task 137's landed design; the review round's P3-1 recorded it here rather than change it). Every init unit-test harness that completes a fresh run must now inject the two new seams (hermeticity: the container pins a shared default data directory) — the three suites' helpers do. The done-condition is pinned executably at every level: unit — the lifecycle order, the database abort (no service step, no summary block, the kept-file remedy), the pending-skip via a throwing probe seam, the probe-host matrix, the poll machine (a modeled clock; healthy/wrong-status/wrong-body/redirect/refused against a real loopback server the suite owns), the install route's pass/fail/skip, and the user-route no-probe; integration — a real launcher leaves a genuinely migrated `quotameter.sqlite` inside the redirected data directory (the migration journal read back), the step-8 block's URL/tunnel/commands/paths render for loopback and non-loopback binds, a squatter file on the data-directory path aborts honestly with the configuration kept, and the PTY run leaves the same artifacts. No public API, wire, format, or event changes; the systemd unit generators, the routing matrix, and `passwd` are untouched. Making the database leg retry on re-runs, probing pending configurations, extending the probe to install's user route, or moving the abort boundary are each a successor decision to this entry.

## D-188 — The §17.3 gate widened to the whole product: the §15.2 auth/session/hashing quartet joins the per-file 100% set at its measured maximum, and the UI tree joins the enforced coverage universe with its own aggregate key at §17.3's floor (spec §17.3, §17.1; task U-060)

**Date:** 2026-11-07 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§17.3](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#173-enforced-quality-thresholds), [§17.1](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#171-required-test-coverage) · **Tasks:** [U-060](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-085, D-089, D-092, D-093

**Decision.** The two gaps the 2026-11-06 deepseek review found in the §17.3 gate are closed by measurement first (the U-016 rule: the make-check coverage report is the arbiter). (1) **The four §15.2 modules join the per-file 100% map at their measured maximum — which is 100 on every axis, so no D-089 exception is needed**: `src/services/password-hash.ts` (39/39 statements, 27/27 branches, 4/4 functions, 39/39 lines), `sessions.ts` (29/29, 10/10, 8/8, 29/29), `session-cookie.ts` (55/55, 38/38, 7/7, 54/54), and `login-rate-limit.ts` (47/47, 20/20, 11/11, 45/45) — the landed suites (the four dedicated unit specs plus auth-routes/cli-passwd integration coverage) already exercise every arm, so the lift-first precondition was satisfied by measurement and there was nothing to write tests for; the keys are `criticalModuleThreshold` (100/100/100/100, `perFile`). (2) **The UI decision is inclusion, not exclusion**: `coverage.include` becomes `['src/**/*.ts', 'ui/src/**/*.ts', 'ui/src/**/*.vue']` and a new `'ui/src/**'` threshold key holds the UI tree's **own aggregate** at 90% on all four axes — a key whose entry lacks `perFile` is judged as one group over the aggregate of its matched files (`coverageMap.getCoverageSummary()` in the installed runner's `resolveThresholds`, vitest 5.1.0 chunk `cli-api.COfZo8lK.js`; semantics identical to the 5.0.5 chunk D-093 verified), while the four global 90% axes keep judging `src` + `ui/src` combined — the runner judges global thresholds over all files including glob-matched ones. Measured baseline at adoption: UI-only statements 95.15 / branches 90.49 / functions 96.84 / lines 96.35 (38 files; branches the tightest margin over the floor), combined 97.98 / 95.39 / 98.02 / 98.44, runner cost unmeasurable (v8 collection is already always-on in `test:ci` since D-085; widening `include` is report-time only — full-run durations 154.5 s src-only vs 143.3 s UI-inclusive, within run-to-run noise). The `.vue` numbers are real: v8 remaps through the vue plugin's sourcemaps (e.g. `SettingsView.vue` 94.73/80.76/100/100 with a genuine uncovered-line list).

**Reasons.** §17.3's "at least 90% line and branch coverage overall" reads on the product, and the UI is a large share of it — but the gate judged only `src/**` because no conscious decision had ever been recorded, which is exactly what the reviewer flagged. Once measured, the documented-exclusion alternative (the task's other branch) had no honest rationale left: the numbers are meaningful, already above the bar, and cost nothing to enforce — an exclusion would have recorded a choice not to look. The UI group key (rather than the combined global gate alone) exists because a combined gate can let UI coverage drift to ~80% under server coverage masking; the group key makes the UI's own floor explicit, and dropping or narrowing it fails the D-093 guard (the map entry). UI per-file 100% keys were considered and rejected: the UI is not a D-085 critical-module class, per-file 100 would demand test-first authorship of every component in a tree whose bootstrap (`ui/src/main.ts`, 0%) and chart runtime wrapper (`ui/src/charts/runtime.ts`, 31%) count honestly inside the aggregate — the floor, not the maximum, is the agreed UI threshold. The four §15.2 keys follow D-085's own consequence ("future auth/session/hashing secret-handling code carries its own key") with the U-016 discipline applied honestly: measured at the maximum first, keys added only because the measurement passed, no new tests invented to justify enforcement (there were no uncovered branches to target — coverage-inflation tests would have been the only alternative and were rejected).

**Consequences.** `make check` (and CI's `test` job) now fail naming any of the four §15.2 files on any new uncovered arm, and naming `"ui/src/**"` when the UI aggregate drops below 90 on any axis — both demonstrated on scratch runs (not committed): excluding `test/unit/login-rate-limit.spec.ts` fails `Coverage for branches (85%) does not meet "src/services/login-rate-limit.ts" threshold (100%)`, and pinning the UI key's branches at 91 fails `Coverage for branches (90.49%) does not meet "ui/src/**" threshold (91%)`. The UI branches margin over the floor is 0.49 pp: a UI change that sinks it must be answered with tests or a conscious re-pin recorded here, never by widening an exclusion. The D-093 guard (`test/unit/coverage-thresholds.spec.ts`) covers every new key — the include pin, the universe walk (`ui/src` `.ts`/`.vue` beside `src` `.ts`), map entries for the four modules and the UI group pattern, a `pm('ui/src/**')` positive control, and a provenance refresh to the installed vitest 5.1.0. `docs/agents/testing.md` carries the three-layer gate description and the UI rationale; `docs/agents/gotchas.md`'s gate parenthetical is updated in step. No production code changed; no new behavioral tests were needed or written (the four modules' coverage is the landed suites' work, re-measured); a UI file with no tests at all still reads 0% and drags the aggregates, exactly as `src/**` files always have.

## D-189 — One D-064 holder in the process: the composition's `AccountSuspensions` store is the scheduler's own state, the observation wrapper is the single manual-test application site, and the reload's engine feed precedes the key-identity report (spec §7.2, §7.3; task FSM-3)

**Date:** 2026-11-07 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§7.2](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#72-retry-and-error-behavior), [§7.3](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#73-account-status-precedence) · **Tasks:** [FSM-3](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-064 (the pure machine, untouched), D-066 (the scheduler whose private machine this removes), D-176 (the dual-holder lockstep being succeeded), D-140 (the holder's original charter), D-062

**Decision.** TZ-fsm §5's audit finding — the D-064 pure machine instantiated twice per process (the scheduler's `AccountEntry.suspension` and the composition's `AccountSuspensions` holder), kept in step only by the `settleWithHolderFeed` wrapper, the `wiringEpochs` staleness rule, and duplicated `auth_error` outcome constants — is closed by making the holder the ONLY store (design (a) of the task's two acceptable designs). Pinned interpretations: (1) **The store is the seam, injected and required.** `PollingSchedulerOptions.suspensions: AccountSuspensions` (fail-fast validated) is the engine's entire D-064 state: every gate reads `suspensionOf`, and every transition the engine used to apply to its private field now flows through the store — the settle path's `polledCycleOutcome` (behind the engine's own entry-identity staleness check, adopted AS the single rule: kept rebuilds feed, removal/re-key/same-key-remove-re-add go stale — the deleted `wiringEpochs` rule agreed on every one of those cases and differs only in the re-key-away-and-back corner recorded below), `setAccounts`' key-identity reports (whose boolean `changed` return is the release re-anchor condition) and leave-the-polled-set drops (`dropAccount` beside the dropped entry), `requestManualTest`'s release application, and the dispatch gate's `admitVerification` (a granted admission persists its re-armed window IN the store, so the pacing survives a lost outcome by D-064's own construction). The entry-identity rule's one divergence from the deleted epoch rule is recorded: a flight under key A whose account was re-keyed A→B→A mid-flight settles as APPLIED (the current wiring's identity equals the flight's snapshot) where the epoch rule bumped on every consecutive identity change and treated it as stale for the old holder — but the old ENGINE applied it too (the same entry-identity check on its private machine), so the unified rule preserves the engine's dispatch semantics exactly and is wire-neutral (the D-070 run-evidence arm keeps the §7.3 display truthful either way); the corner is pinned by the lockstep suite. `AccountEntry` carries no suspension field; the composition creates one `createAccountSuspensions({ clock })` instance and hands the same object to the engine (forwarded to the scheduler), the status routes' `suspensionOf`, and the manual-test observation. (2) **The observation wrapper is the single application site for both manual-test events** (`src/server/providers.ts`): the request's release stays the wrapper's `manualTestRequested` (with the engine bridge's own application retained — a release on a released state is a no-op, D-064's design, so the double application is provably inert while the engine keeps its standalone coherence), and a refusal's re-entry is ONLY the wrapper's `manualTestRejected(accountId, keyIdentityOfSecret(testedSecret))` — the engine-side `manualTestRejected` sheds its outcome application and drops the owed attempt alone. This resolves the audit's mid-rekey divergence (today the holder enters a fresh episode under the tested key while the engine re-arms the wiring's) in the truthful direction: the identity is the key the provider actually refused. The duplicated `MANUAL_TEST_AUTH_ERROR`/`AUTH_ERROR_OUTCOME` constants collapse into one exported factory, `classifyAuthRejection()` in `polling-outcomes.ts` (the vocabulary owner, built from the landed tables). (3) **The reload's follow-up order becomes config-sync → engine feed → key-identity report loop** (was: report → engine): under one store, a report-first loop would pre-release the store and blind `setAccounts`' own application, losing the release re-anchor (a released account resumes immediately, D-066); engine-first lets the engine observe its own release, and the loop after it is the idempotent no-op D-064 designed `reportKeyIdentity` to be — kept because its durable effect is for accounts OUTSIDE the polled set (a key rotation releasing a disabled account's episode). (4) **A joining account inherits the store's episode** (the reachable corner: a manual test on a _disabled_ account is rejected — the test endpoint serves any managed account with a resolvable key — then the account is enabled). Today the engine started `INITIAL` (polled immediately) while the holder showed the episode — exactly the divergence class the audit flags; the unified store honors the pause (§7.2's pause is about the key, not polled-ness) and the probe cadence verifies the refused key at the armed instant. (5) **The design-(b) event tape is rejected on the goal's own words**: §5.2 demands exactly one `AuthSuspensionState` instance per account in the process, and a tape distributing events to subscribers keeps two machines alive — the lockstep problem becomes a subscription-completeness problem, failing the acceptance's structural check; a tape that itself owns the one state degenerates into design (a) plus a notification layer with no consumer (the dispatch loop recomputes from live state every pass; the manual-test bridges already kick).

**Reasons.** The choice between the task's two designs was decided by what each failure mode becomes: under (a), a new event source wired into the wrong place is a missing/extra write to the ONE store — locally wrong, immediately visible in `suspensionOf`; under (b), it is a silent subscription gap between two machines — the audit's exact finding, restated at the tape layer. The risk note's transition-order concern is answered structurally: every event is now exactly ONE pure transition on the one store at a pinned site, and `manualTestRejected` during an in-flight attempt stays legal because each application is a pure D-064 transition on whatever the current state is (the in-flight settle still applies behind the staleness check afterwards — both orders coherent, pinned by the lockstep suite's held-probe scenario). Keeping the engine's `requestManualTest` release while dropping its `manualTestRejected` application is deliberate asymmetry, not oversight: the request transition is double-application-idempotent by D-064's own semantics (release-on-released is a no-op, either order), while two outcome applications under different identities at different readings genuinely drift (a re-arm shifted, or a fresh-episode-then-re-key chain) — the request keeps its inert second application for the engine's standalone coherence (its own tests, a non-composed embedding), the rejection gets the single application the audit demands. The re-key identity choice (tested over wiring) follows the machine's own docblock: an `auth_error` under a different key "begins a fresh episode for that key" — the wrapper's identity names the key that was tried and refused, which is the episode the store should hold. The reload reorder preserves `syncAccountsFromConfig` before the engine feed (the account row lands before any settle can write a run, D-069's FK requirement) — only the report loop moves.

**Consequences.** `src/services/polling-suspension.ts` (the pure machine and its exported contract) is untouched; `src/services/account-suspensions.ts` grows `admitVerification(accountId): VerificationAdmission` (persisting the admission re-arm) and a boolean-returning `reportKeyIdentity`; `src/services/polling-scheduler.ts` loses its private state and the duplicated constant, requiring the store; `src/server/polling.ts` loses `settleWithHolderFeed`/`wiringEpochs`/`buildWiring`'s drop loop (the settle wrapper keeps only its contained-failure diagnostics — D-066's deferred logging site); `src/server/composition.ts` reorders the follow-ups (extracted as the exported, test-pinned `createReloadFollowUps` factory); `src/server/providers.ts` changes docblocks only. Internal API under `src/` only — no wire, format, or event change (`/api/status` behavior is identical in every reachable flow; the unified corner's display differs only where the two machines already disagreed). The exported names (`classifyAuthRejection`, `AccountSuspensions.admitVerification`, `PollingSchedulerOptions.suspensions`, the boolean `reportKeyIdentity`) are internal contract under `src/`. The R5 lockstep suite `test/unit/polling-suspension-lockstep.spec.ts` is the standing proof: scripted sequences (polled 401 → inconclusive probe → manual test → success; polled 401 → reload key change; the held-probe manual rejection; re-key and same-key remove/re-add staleness; the kept same-key rebuild; the re-key-away-and-back corner; the leave/rejoin drop; the joining-inherits corner) run through the REAL engine composition (production scheduler, production observation wrapper, recorder doubles) while a reference machine — the D-064 module itself — computes the expected store, asserted equal after every event and at every decisive reading (armed−1/armed), beside the dispatch-timeline pins (probes exactly at the admitted readings, no normal poll while suspended); the structural single-holder pin (the scheduler factory receives the composition's instance) lives in `server-polling.spec.ts`, and the reload follow-up ORDER of interpretation (3) is pinned at the composition's own definition — extracted as the exported `createReloadFollowUps` factory and sequenced-pinned by `test/unit/composition-reload-follow-ups.spec.ts` (config-sync → engine feed → report loop on one recorded timeline; the behavioral consequence, the release re-anchor's immediate poll, is the lockstep suite's — the order's load-bearing window is a kept entry suspended with a FUTURE due, reachable only through a manual rejection while healthy, a world whose owed attempt races the rejection feed and is therefore pinned at the factory rather than by composed timing). `account-suspensions.spec.ts` pins the admission gate and the boolean report; `polling-scheduler.spec.ts` models the composed manual-test shape (store feed + bridge); the integration suites — including the end-to-end 401/manual-test recovery over the real adapter — pass unchanged, which is R4's wire-identity evidence.

## D-190 — The polling dispatcher's explicit phase model: a held `PollPlan` per account behind an exhaustive observed-`PollPhase` switch, with the D-064 store referenced and never copied (spec §7.1, §7.2; task FSM-1)

**Date:** 2026-11-07 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§7.1](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#71-polling), [§7.2](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#72-retry-and-error-behavior), [§17.1](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#171-required-test-coverage) · **Tasks:** [FSM-1](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-066 (the scheduler whose field scatter this replaces — the successor this entry is), D-062 (the gate the model must keep unconditional), D-064 (the pure suspension machine the model must not duplicate), D-189 (the single D-064 holder the model references), [TZ-fsm §3](plan/TZ-fsm.md#fsm-1)

**Decision.** TZ-fsm §3's flagship finding — "may this account be polled now?" encoded in six independent variables (the entry's monotonic due, its D-062 wall gate, its owed-manual flag, live-flight membership, the sticky hang flag, and the D-064 state in the shared store) behind a critical, type-unprotected check order in `nextAction` (the U-028 missed-gate and P2-3 owed-overwrite lineage) — is closed by a two-layer explicit state machine in the new `src/services/polling-phase.ts`. (1) **The held layer is `PollPlan`, the one value `AccountEntry` stores**: `scheduled{nextPollMonotonicMs, notBeforeEpochMs}` or `manual-owed{nextPollMonotonicMs, notBeforeEpochMs}`. The decisive shape choice: the `manual-owed` variant **carries the dormant normal schedule beside the owed marker** — exactly the fields the flag model kept — so every row of the transition table (`nextPlan(plan, event)`, a pure function over a seven-event discriminated union: `key-released`, `cycle-settled`, `contained-failure`, `manual-test-requested`, `manual-test-rejected`, `interval-changed`, `dispatched`, plus `initialPlan` for §7.1's immediate first poll) is a field-for-field mirror of the D-066 mutation it replaces; nothing is invented, no new clock reading is taken, and the three candidate "don't-care" values the design phase identified (the post-rejection schedule, the dispatch placeholder, the suspended settle's due) all dissolve into "keep what was there" — the same answer the flag model gave. The owe survives `cycle-settled` (P2-3's fix becomes a table row: the settle updates the dormant schedule and the gate, the owed variant stands), `contained-failure`, and `interval-changed`; only `dispatched` (applied at the single site `startFlight`) and `manual-test-rejected` consume it. (2) **The observed layer is `PollPhase`, a transient per-pass projection the dispatcher switches over**: `absent`, `in-flight`, `hung`, `manual-owed`, `manual-gated{untilEpochMs}`, `probe-waiting{untilEpochMs}`, `probe-due`, `probe-gated{untilEpochMs}`, `waiting{untilMonotonicMs}`, `due` — derived by the pure `pollPhaseOf({plan, flight, suspension, wallEpochMs, monotonicMs})`. Time-dependent facts (due vs waiting, the D-064 boundary) and out-of-entry facts (flight membership, the hang flag) are folded here and never stored: a flight outlives its entry (the removed-mid-flight, re-added-while-live corner), so in-flight-ness cannot live in the plan; and R5's rule is held by construction — the suspension state is an **input** to the derivation (the store's own value, read on the same dispatch pass, gone again), so the probe variants project `nextVerificationAtEpochMs` without the plan ever carrying a copy that could drift (the FSM-3/D-189 single-holder guarantee, extended: there is no second authority to keep in step because there is no storage at all). (3) **The dispatcher is an exhaustive `switch` with compile-time totality** (R3, the `classifyTransportError` pattern): `decide()` maps each phase to `skip | wait(ms) | dispatch` with every arm returning, so a future `PollPhase` variant without an arm is TS2366, not a missed gate — the `nextAction` loop only folds decisions. The wait-vs-blocked placement of every arm is the parity contract itself: gated shapes contribute their wait even while the queue is held (the gate opens on its own clock — the manual path's original order), probe and due shapes re-examine after the hold lifts, `manual-gated`/`probe-gated`/`probe-waiting` carry the D-062/D-064 instants, and the U-028 order (the cadence predicate first, the gate second, the admission last) is the derivation's fixed precedence. (4) **The read/roll discipline is part of the contract**: the re-anchor arguments of `cycle-settled`/`interval-changed`/`contained-failure` (`nowMonotonicMs`, with the jittered `nextDelayMs` or the plain `intervalMs`) are **supplied only when a consuming row will read them** (required-unless-`suspended`, required-unless-unowed for containment — fail-fast if a consuming row finds them missing), because D-066's code drew the monotonic reading and the `pollingDelayMs` roll only on the schedule-consuming paths — an eagerly computed argument would consume a reading and a roll on every suspended settle and shift every counting clock seam and scripted-`random` sequence after it; the engine supplies them lazily exactly where the old code read. (5) **Diagnostics (R6)**: `PollingSchedulerOptions.logger?` (a `Pick<Logger, 'debug'>`, default silent) receives one `debug` record per held-plan kind transition — accountId, the event, from → to, never a secret (plans hold timestamps only); the composition passes its shared redacting logger. `PollingScheduler`'s public surface, the wire, formats, and events are untouched (R7); `schedulerFactory` and the composition seams are unchanged except for the additive optional logger. (Correction trail: the task's review round — deepseek-v4.1-flash, one round, APPROVE with 1 P2 / 6 P3 — is folded into this entry and the same commit, which had not landed when corrected. The reviewer's independent differential harness (the pre-refactor engine from the base commit and the reworked one driven through the golden scenarios plus 200 generated command scripts, compared on decision traces and clock-read counts) confirmed byte-identical traces and the wait-vs-blocked placement, the totality (TS2366 verified empirically), and the D-064 boundary — and found the first draft's `nowMonotonicMs` argument evaluated unconditionally (one extra monotonic read per suspended/owed settle, contradicting this entry's parity claim): the P2 fix IS interpretation (4) above (the lazy re-anchor pair, restoring D-066's read counts on every path). Folded P3s: the per-pass flight-presence map (the first draft re-scanned the flight set per account), the event-union docblock continuation prefixes, the `MANUAL_OWED` singleton's spelling, and the no-starvation half of invariant 6 as a second engine property (a permanently hung account while generated advances prove the healthy accounts keep their cadence). One P3 declined with the reason recorded here: skipping the per-pass `suspensionOf` read for flying/owed entries (the old `nextAction` read the store only for other entries) — the store read is a pure in-memory Map lookup over the same single holder with no counting seam, so widening it to every entry is observationally inert; the table's consuming rows already require the suspension input, and partially supplying it would leak the derivation's precedence into the call site.)

**Reasons.** The held-vs-observed split is forced by where the facts live: the six audit variables have three different owners (the entry's schedule, the engine's flight registry, the shared D-064 store), and only a per-pass projection can consult all three without duplicating any — a single stored "phase" holding in-flight or armed instants would either break the flight-outlives-entry corner or re-create the second suspension machine FSM-3 just deleted. Carrying the dormant schedule inside `manual-owed` (rather than dropping it, the design phase's first draft) was chosen because parity under the golden-trace methodology prefers rows with nothing to invent: every transition mirrors an observable D-066 field mutation, so the before/after identity proof reduces to the traces plus the untouched suites. Keeping `waiting` as the gate-folded due (`max(nextPoll, now + gate remainder)`, D-066's arithmetic verbatim) rather than a separate `retry-after-gated` variant follows the same rule — the fold is what the original code computed, and the working set's "Retry-After-gated" state is subsumed without a semantics change. The `absent` arm exists for totality and the derivation's external consumers (the property suite drives it directly); in the dispatch loop it is unreachable by construction and documented as such. The read/roll-consumption pin matters because the seams are injectable: behavior parity is defined at the seam boundary, and a clock or random source that observes consumption is an existing test's tool — D-066's consumption order is therefore part of the parity contract this refactor must preserve bit for bit.

**Consequences.** `src/services/polling-scheduler.ts` keeps every exported name and its entire public behavior; `AccountEntry` is `{account, plan}`; `scheduleNextPoll`, `rescheduleBestEffort`'s field writes, `retryAfterRemainingMs`, and the `pendingManualTest` flag are gone (replaced by `setPlan` invocations of the table); `src/server/polling.ts` passes `logger` into the scheduler options (no behavior change). The exported names of the new module (`PollPlan`, `ScheduledPlan`, `ManualOwedPlan`, `PollPlanEvent`, `initialPlan`, `nextPlan`, `PollPhase`, `PhaseFlight`, `PhaseView`, `pollPhaseOf`) are internal contract under `src/`: changing any requires a successor decision. The standing proofs: `test/unit/polling-phase.golden.spec.ts` — six scripted scenarios over scripted clock readings (the first-poll rounds, the 429-gated manual attempt, the U-028 probe-cadence/gate interplay with the 7 230 000 boundary, the sticky hang with resumption, the mid-flight key change's stale discard, the owed attempt surviving a settle and an interval change) drive the REAL engine and pin the full decision traces (attempt starts, settle classifications, and every wake that actually fires) as literals **captured from the pre-refactor engine and never edited after** — the before/after identity proof TZ-fsm §3.5 demands; `test/unit/polling-phase.property.spec.ts` pins the invariant properties (no per-account overlap under generated command scripts against the production engine with parked attempts and random classified outcomes; a permanently hung account never starving the healthy accounts' cadence under generated advances; owed survival across any surviving-event sequence with consumption exactly at `dispatched`; a shut D-062 gate never deriving a dispatchable phase for any plan/suspension pair with equality admitting; a flying or hung account never dispatchable for any inputs); `test/unit/polling-phase.spec.ts` pins every table row and derivation boundary (the inclusive gate and armed-instant edges, the no-clock-data optionality of the suspended/owed rows — the read-parity pin — and the fail-fast arms of the re-anchor pair). Every pre-existing polling suite — `polling-scheduler.spec.ts` (49 tests), `polling-suspension*.spec.ts` including the FSM-3 lockstep suite, `server-polling.spec.ts`, the integration `composition-polling.spec.ts` — passes **without a single edit** (verified: the diff touches no test file outside the three new specs), which is the no-weakened-assertions evidence. The lockstep suite keeps guarding the D-189 boundary from the other side: the phase model reads the one store, so a scheduler-side suspension re-derivation would fail it. Coverage of the new module is held by the table/property specs at 100% on every axis (it is not a D-085 per-file-100% class; the global 90% axes judge it with everything else). Residuals recorded: the probe-admission disagreement fallback in `decide` remains unreachable through the engine's own math (as it was in D-066's `nextAction`) and is kept as the fail-safe wait-a-tick, not covered by a test — a future divergence-hunting suite would need a deliberately lying store double (its `'not-suspended'` arm waits 1 ms where D-066 waited on the stale armed instant — unreachable, so observably identical); the per-pass `suspensionOf` lookup now touches every entry including flying/owed ones (a pure in-memory Map read over the single holder — no seam, no observable difference, recorded here rather than skipped at the call site); and the settle path reads the monotonic clock once on the non-suspended row inside the event argument where D-066 read it inside `scheduleNextPoll` after the gate write — identical counts, with one theoretical interleaving difference (a non-finite monotonic reading at that instant loses the cycle's gate update where the old code had already written it), unreachable in every observable flow because the dispatch loop dies on its next pass before anything reads the plan again.
