## D-191 — The unified account lifecycle projection: a required rank-0 `archived` input to the §7.3 derivation, the token on the wire, and the attention consuming the verdict (spec §7.3, §8.2, §13, §14.6; task FSM-2)

**Date:** 2026-11-07 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§7.3](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#73-account-status-precedence), [§8.2](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#82-accounts), [§13](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#13-http-api), [§14.6](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#146-statuses-and-authentication-screens) · **Tasks:** [FSM-2](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-180 (spec 1.1's archived-dominance rule this entry implements — the design freedom it left is exercised here), D-070 (the derivation whose input set and vocabulary this entry extends — the successor of record for its `AccountStatusInput` contract), D-061 (archiving's terminality and the config-sync skip, preserved and now pinned end-to-end), D-128 (the accounts surface's two-store merge whose row half supplies the fact), D-130 (the status/quota routes that consume the classifier), D-138 (the attention module that now reads the verdict over the wire), [TZ-fsm §4](plan/TZ-fsm.md#fsm-2)

**Decision.** TZ-fsm §4's cross-store finding — the account state as the product `enabled × archived × configured` smeared across config JSON, SQLite, and process memory, displayed through three projections that could contradict each other (reproducibly: a hand-re-added archived id answering `collecting`/`fresh` on `/api/status` while the accounts view and the UI attention said `archived`, reachable because `syncAccountsFromConfig` skips archived rows per D-061) — is closed by making `deriveAccountStatus` the ONE canonical lifecycle classifier with the storage row's archived fact as a required rank-0 input. (Correction trail: the task's review round — deepseek-v4.1-flash, one round, REQUEST CHANGES with 0 P0 / 0 P1 / 2 P2 / 5 P3 — is folded in before landing: the archived attention copy and the blocked no-snapshot line no longer assert "polling is stopped"/"collection is not running" (the hand-re-add shape keeps an entry the engine polls, interpretation 5 — the sentences now state the lifecycle facts true in every shape); `ui/README.md`'s attention-precedence and badge-count references were rewritten for the verdict-first ordering; the doc/comment sweep landed (the derivation header's consumer census, the quota schema's status description, the accounts section's hand-re-add shape, the suites' "eight statuses" lines); `/api/quota` gained the hand-re-add assertion; the composition test's live-data wording was corrected to what that suite's fail-closed provider double can prove (the dominance-over-live-data half lives in the route matrix's seeded cells); this entry's D-180 reference states the two alternatives as written instead of an invented numbering; and the attention docblock's agreement claim is qualified by load currency. One P3 declined: an e2e archived-badge cell — TZ-fsm §4.4's done-condition names the schema/docs/i18n/component artifacts, not e2e; the badge component matrix iterates the full nine-token list through the real component and the integration suite walks the cube through the real route stack.) Pinned interpretations: (1) **The rank-0 shape — the first of the two alternatives D-180's amendment names ("a rank-0 `archived` input to `deriveAccountStatus`, or merging the facts in the status route")**: `AccountStatusInput` gains `readonly archived: boolean` — REQUIRED, fail-fast validated beside `enabled`/`configured` — and the derivation's first row is `if (input.archived) return 'archived'`, ahead of `disabled` and `not-configured`, formalizing TZ-fsm R1's canonical chain `archived → disabled → not-configured → the §7.3 working ranks`. The route-level merge alternative was rejected: it would leave three derivations alive (the route's merge beside the CLI's and any future consumer's), exactly the scatter the audit flags, while the rank-0 input makes the invariant a property of the one function every consumer already calls. The vocabulary grows to nine (`ACCOUNT_STATUSES` gains `archived` first; `ACCOUNT_STATUS_LABELS` gains `Archived`); an archived row therefore displays `archived` even when the config half still claims enabled/keyed — and outranks `Disabled`/`Not configured` too, so the plain archived row (entry removed) that previously derived `disabled` now honestly reads `archived`. (2) **The wire change is the token, additive**: `ACCOUNT_STATUS_TOKENS` gains `archived`, so the `GET /api/status` row's `status` and `GET /api/quota`'s `status` answer it (the schema-drift pin keeps the wire and derivation vocabularies one list; `docs/openapi.json` regenerated; the token description states the dominance). The routes resolve the fact from the storage half they already merge (`recordsById`/the quota handler's `record`) — never from the configuration entry, which is precisely the half that lies in the hand-re-add shape. Reads of an archived account stay unrefused (§8.2's retained history) and now honestly labeled. (3) **The UI consumes the verdict over the wire (R3)**: `accountAttentionOf`'s archived/disabled branches consult `statusRow.status` first — the classifier's own token — with the raw storage/enable facts (the accounts surface's `status` field and `enabled` flag, the very inputs the server feeds the same ranks) kept beside them as the row-absent fallback and as the cross-load-race tie-breaker in BOTH directions (a stale list cannot outvote a fresher verdict, nor the reverse). The keyless branches are unchanged: the `not-configured` token plus `keySource` keeps discriminating the environment remedy, and the schema-total sourceless fallback keeps its fix-here wording. No precedence is re-derived client-side: the row's token arrives decided. (4) **The CLI reads the fact beside each configured account (R6)**: `readAccountFacts` adds `repository.getAccount(id)?.status === 'archived'` (an absent database reads `archived: false` — no rows exist by construction), so the hand-re-add shape renders `Status: Archived` and agrees with the web UI; the CLI's account list stays configuration-driven (its §5.2 charter is the configured set; an archived-without-entry id remains unlisted — absence is not a contradiction, and the two surfaces that DO list it agree). (5) **Terminality and the sync skip are preserved and pinned (R5)**: `syncAccountsFromConfig` is untouched, and a composition test now walks the full hand-re-add lifecycle — archive through the real API, hand-edit the file re-adding the id, restart — proving the row is not resurrected (`createdAt` unchanged), the label not mirrored (the skip's `continue`), and both §13 surfaces answer `archived` (that suite's provider double fails `fetchSnapshot` closed — D-069's fail-fast shape persists nothing — so the dominance-over-live-data half is pinned where fresh runs are seedable: the status suite's matrix cells that archive an account beside successful cycles still answer the lifecycle token). The engine's pollable set is deliberately NOT filtered by the row's lifecycle: the audit's finding is display consistency, the normal archive path stops polling through entry removal (D-128's archive), and widening the polled-set rule would change §6.4 behavior beyond this task's contract — which also means the hand-re-add shape KEEPS polling in production, so the UI's archived wording was made lifecycle-safe (the review round's P2: "polling is stopped"/"collection is not running" would be false copy there; the attention sentence and the blocked no-snapshot line now state facts true in every shape). (6) **Residuals**: an unarchive policy (forbid forever vs a separate explicit operation) stays out of scope per TZ-fsm R5 — the recorded stance is that any reactivation primitive is D-061's named future decision and would arrive as a facade method or third lifecycle operation, not through display unification; and the hand-re-add shape keeps polling (interpretation 5) until such a decision says otherwise — visible, but no longer contradictory.

**Reasons.** The design freedom D-180 left ("a rank-0 `archived` input to `deriveAccountStatus` or a route-level merge") resolved on the audit's own unit of analysis: the finding is that THREE projections existed at all, so the fix must reduce the projection count, not add a fourth merge site. The rank-0 input puts the invariant inside the one total function whose precedence every consumer already trusts (D-070's consumer census: the status routes, the CLI, and — through the row's token — the UI), makes it exhaustively testable as a table (the matrix), and lets the property suite prove dominance over generated evidence. Making the input required rather than optional follows the house fail-fast rule and forces every caller to state the fact — the CLI's seam extension and the routes' `recordsById` are one-line resolutions because the row half was already in hand. The wire addition is additive (a new token value in a closed union; no shape change), the package's only consumers are the bundled UI and CLI (§13's "internal to the web interface"; the package is unreleased — D-130's recorded risk posture), and the drift/schema/component guards keep every artifact in lockstep mechanically. Keeping the attention's raw-fact fallbacks (rather than deleting them for verdict-only purity) is the honest reading of the load reality the module already documents: the accounts list and the status rows are independent loads, and the row-absent window plus both race directions each have a truthful answer from the raw facts — the same inputs rank 0–2 consume server-side, so the module re-derives nothing the server decided; it consults the verdict when present and the identical facts when not. The CLI's configured-only list stays because widening it would change which accounts `quotameter status` reports (a §5.2 behavior question with its own consumer expectations), while the audit's contradiction — two surfaces disagreeing about the SAME listed account — is fully closed without it.

**Consequences.** `deriveAccountStatus`'s input contract changes (D-070's exported names stand; `AccountStatusInput.archived` is required — internal API under `src/`, every caller updated in this commit); the nine-token vocabulary is the new §13 wire contract (`archived` first); the badge renders "Archived" in the neutral tone through the new `overview.status.archived` catalog key (i18n completeness and the badge's tone/label component matrix grow the row automatically from `ACCOUNT_STATUS_TOKENS`). The accounts surface's own wire shape is unchanged — its `status: 'active' | 'archived'` field is the raw lifecycle fact (the storage half the classifier consumes), and the accounts page's archived notice/selector marking keep their existing behavior. The standing proofs: the §4.1 contradiction as a red-then-green regression (`test/integration/api-status.spec.ts` — the reproducible shape seeded through the route harness answered `fresh` before the fix and `archived` after, the red run captured in the commit body); the `enabled × archived × configured` matrix over every pure projection (`test/unit/account-lifecycle-matrix.spec.ts` — the derivation, the accounts view, and the attention assert the same table, plus the both-directions is-archived agreement law and the race-honesty cells), through the route (the same eight cells in the status suite, one world), and through the CLI (`Status: Archived` for the hand-re-add shape); the derivation suites grow the rank-0 evidence/dominance/validation cells, the archived column of the transition matrix, and the archived-dominance property (`test/unit/polling-status.property.spec.ts` generates the fact like every other input); the composition suite pins the hand-re-add lifecycle end-to-end. The attention truth table gains the verdict-driven cells (a row's `archived` over a stale active list, a row's `disabled` over a stale enabled list). A future unarchive decision supersedes interpretation (6) and owns both the storage primitive and the display consequence; until then an archived row can never display a runtime status anywhere.

## D-192 — Polling-loop death made observable: one `error` record at the loop-death retention site through the widened D-190 logger seam, the authenticated `polling: { running }` health diagnostics behind the §15.1 grant rule, the CLI's stale-silence warning, and the process-exit residual rejected (spec §13, §16, §5.2, §15.1; task FSM-4)

**Date:** 2026-11-07 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§13](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#13-http-api), [§16](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#16-logging-and-diagnostics), [§5.2](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#52-cli-command-surface), [§15.1](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#151-network-and-authentication-modes), [§12.2](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#122-collection-gaps-and-errors) · **Tasks:** [FSM-4](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-180 (spec 1.1's amendment naming the polling engine among health's permitted diagnostics — the normative basis this entry implements), D-111 (the health route and its closed response contract, extended here), D-121 (the §15.1 classifier and credential seam the grant rule reuses verbatim), D-182 (the session reader's single-source injection pattern this route's scope wiring follows), D-190 (the scheduler's logger seam this entry widens — the R1 design's foundation), D-114 (the CLI status report whose exit-code discipline the warning respects), D-178 (the `gapThresholdMs` silence threshold the CLI suspicion reuses as its one source), [TZ-fsm §6](plan/TZ-fsm.md#fsm-4)

**Decision.** TZ-fsm §6's dead-state finding — the scheduler can die of a broken seam (`loopError`) with `running=false` consumed by nobody, `/api/health` answering the literal `{"status":"ok"}` in every state, the process staying alive so systemd's `Restart=on-failure` never fires, and the owner learning only from eventual `Stale` — is closed on three surfaces plus one explicit non-decision. (Correction trail: the task's review round — deepseek-v4.1-flash, one round, REQUEST CHANGES with 0 P0 / 1 P1 / 1 P2 / 5 P3 — is folded in before landing: the grant rule consults the credential seam only on the `required` verdict (the P1 — the first draft consulted it on every non-`not-required` verdict, so a still-valid session row could surface diagnostics on the passwordless proxied cell the guard 403s without any credential question; the reviewer reproduced the hole against the real route, the fix is the structural verdict-table mirror below, and the missing matrix cell joined the suite); the CLI suspicion is judged per account against its own evidence-widened expectation (the P2 — a `Retry-After` deferral of up to an hour and the D-064 hourly probe cadence legitimately outlast the bare three-interval threshold, so the first draft warned straight through both; the allowances read the newest run row's own `retry_after_seconds` and `auth_error` shape); the `assessEngineLiveness` fail-fast validation and the `service install` success line's stale literal-body claim were folded in as well, and the pin accounting is stated precisely (the route-suite unauthenticated pins unchanged; the production-composition sweep pin moves to the granted branch). Two P3s declined with reasons: extending `PollingRunEvidence` with the latest run's stamp (the evidence read already fetches that row internally — the CLI keeps one extra bounded, indexed read per account rather than rippling a D-070 exported-contract change through the derivation suites and property generators for a single consumer; a successor can extend the evidence type when a second consumer needs the stamp), and filtering archived accounts out of the liveness set (the engine POLLS a hand-re-added archived id — D-191's interpretation 5 records exactly that — so the set matches the engine by including them).) (1) **R1's seam choice: the D-190 logger seam widened, not a new channel.** `PollingSchedulerOptions.logger` widens from `Pick<Logger, 'debug'>` to `Pick<Logger, 'debug' | 'error'>` (fail-fast validated like every seam), and the engine emits exactly ONE `error` record at the existing loop-error retention site — inside `start()`'s `loopPromise.catch`, beside `loopError = error`: `'polling engine died: the dispatch loop exited unexpectedly; scheduling has stopped'` with the retained error as data (redaction and destination are the composition's — the shared §16 logger it already passes; message and level are the engine's). TZ-fsm's parenthetical alternatives were assessed against the post-FSM-1 ground its affected-files list predates: an `onLoopDied` callback would open a second notification channel beside the logger D-190 already injected for exactly the single required reaction (the record), and a `running` poll in the composition would need its own timer, add detection latency, and keep a second clock alive — strictly less precise than firing at the rejection itself. No-spam holds by construction: a promise rejects at most once, so the handler runs at most once per death event (a restarted loop that dies again is a new promise and a new event). The no-logger embedding stays silent — the default's `error` no-op, same semantics the `debug` half always had. (2) **R2's grant rule: diagnostics for exactly the requests the §15.1 layer would grant any protected route.** `HealthResponseSchema` gains an OPTIONAL, closed `polling: { running: boolean }` block (`HealthPollingDiagnosticsSchema`, `additionalProperties: false` at both levels); the unauthenticated payload `{ status: 'ok' }` serializes byte-exact because the compiled serializer omits absent optional properties entirely — the D-111 leak guard now admits exactly one declared block and still structurally drops everything else. The route distinguishes granted from ungranted by REUSING the §15.1/§15.2 seams: `classifyAuthMode` over the same facts the guard reads (injected by the `/api` scope from its own required `auth` options — D-182's single-source pattern at its second consumer), granting on the `not-required` verdict (auto mode, loopback bind, no proxy indication: the local operator's trust cell, the same boundary that serves `/api/status` without a password — withholding diagnostics there would hide them in the DEFAULT configuration, and in a passwordless deployment no session could ever exist to unlock them), else on the same `isAuthenticated` seam instance the guard consults (the composition wires `createSessionAuthenticator` once, both consumers share it). Every other shape keeps the literal: the credential seam is consulted ONLY on the `required` verdict — the guard's own decision table — so the passwordless proxied request (§15.1's 403 class for protected routes, which the guard refuses without any credential question) is refused STRUCTURALLY, regardless of what a still-valid session row would say (the hash is a live §6.4 fact, and removing it by hand does not revoke existing rows — the review round's P1, reproduced against the real route before the fix); `required` mode without an accepted session reads the seam's false and stops. The diagnostics source is optional wiring (`ApiRoutesOptions.health`, the scope's no-half-wired rule): an unwired construction answers the literal in every state — the task-147 contract the route-suite pins hold unchanged (the production-composition sweep pin moves to the granted branch, whose direct loopback call is §15.1-granted by construction). The value is read per request from the live getter the composition wires (`PollingEngine.running`, delegating to the scheduler's), so a death between two probes flips the wire answer on the next request. (3) **R3: `quotameter status` warns from the run evidence.** A separate process cannot probe the engine, so the new pure `assessEngineLiveness({ serviceRunning, accounts, intervalSeconds, nowEpochMs })` reads the same silence §12.2's timeline reads — judged PER ACCOUNT against the silence that account's own evidence makes legitimate: the base is `gapThresholdMs(intervalSeconds)` (D-178's three-jitter-expanded-interval threshold imported as the ONE source, strict on the boundary exactly as the gap rule is), widened per account by two facts the newest run row itself carries — an `auth_error` newest run is the D-064 suspended shape (the §7.2 hourly verification cadence, `AUTH_SUSPENSION_VERIFICATION_INTERVAL_MS` imported from the machine's own module), and a stored `retry_after_seconds` is the provider's requested §7.2 pause (the stored evidence widens the tolerance; the engine's gate is never re-derived from it, D-069's evidence-not-gate rule). Suspicion ⟺ the lock is held by a LIVE pid AND EVERY pollable account's silence exceeds its own expectation — one provably-live account clears the whole suspicion (the loop dispatched for it within its expectation). "Pollable" is the CLI-side approximation (enabled, secret resolvable in the invocation's environment): a disabled or unconfigured account never runs, so its silence is not evidence — the provider-unknown corner (an account the registry lacks, skipped with a `warn` at startup) can still false-positive and is accepted as advisory noise; any run OUTCOME counts, because a failing cycle still proves the loop alive. No runs at all, a stopped service, a stale lock, an absent store, or no candidate accounts answer `no-evidence` (a stopped service's old cycles are EXPECTED — the Running line already explains them; a fresh install's silence is §12.1-grade ambiguity). The warning is one advisory line after the accounts block — the last cycle's §10-formatted timestamp plus the `quotameter logs` pointer — and is exit-neutral by construction (D-114: states never fail a status question). (4) **R4 preserved:** `stop()`'s dead-loop rethrow is untouched — the record fires inside the retention handler, `await loopPromise` in `stop()` still re-surfaces the error, re-pinned beside the record assertion. (5) **R5: the process-exit option is considered and REJECTED/DEFERRED.** Exiting non-zero on loop death (to arm `Restart=on-failure`) is rejected for now: a dead loop is not a dead service — the HTTP API, retention, and the UI stay up, and the owner can now SEE the death (the error record, the wire diagnostics, the CLI warning) and restart deliberately; an automatic restart would also destroy the failure's evidence (journald keeps it, but the operator stops looking when the service self-heals) and race in-flight state the graceful drain exists to protect. The observability landed here is the prerequisite any restart decision needs; restart semantics stays TZ-fsm §6.6's recorded residual — a separate future decision with its own entry.

**Reasons.** The seam choice follows the ground FSM-1 built: D-190 already made the injected logger the scheduler's diagnostics channel and the composition already passes the shared redacting logger, so the "composition seam" TZ-fsm asks for IS that injection — widening it by one level costs no new wiring and no new channel, while either alternative adds machinery (a callback to wire and contain, or a poll timer with latency and its own liveness question — a poll loop that itself dies would recreate the finding one layer up). The grant rule is forced by §13's own split: the row's "unauthenticated response contains only…" is a prohibition, its "authenticated response MAY include…" a permission whose honest boundary is the §15.1 trust decision already computed per request — re-deriving a second notion of "authenticated" (cookie-presence-only, say) would make health's grant disagree with the guard's on exactly the proxy cells §15.1 exists for. The optional-property mechanism (not a second route, not `nullable`) is the only shape that keeps one schema, one route, and one serializer while the two bodies differ — and the byte-exactness proof stays the serializer's own, re-pinned by the untouched integration tests. The CLI's threshold reuse follows D-178's one-source rule and the audit's own framing: a dead engine IS a permanent stopped-service region, the same §12.2 silence the events surface already names, so the suspicion reads it from the same function rather than inventing "N intervals" a second time. The exit-neutrality keeps D-114's contract intact — a suspicion is a state, and states never fail a status question; an operator scripting against the warning has the text to grep, not an exit code to parse.

**Consequences.** The health wire contract changes additively (the optional `polling` block; the unauthenticated body byte-identical): `docs/api.md` and `docs/openapi.json` are updated in this commit (the operation description names the conditional diagnostics), the schema contract suite grows the accepted/rejected `polling` cells, and the route suites pin the grant matrix — the `not-required` cell with both running values and the per-request liveness flip, `required` mode through the credential seam (granted and refused), the passwordless proxied cell kept literal BOTH seam-false and seam-accepting (the structural refusal), the HEAD twin bodyless on the granted branch — beside the untouched byte-exact pins of the unwired construction (the production-composition sweep pin moves to the granted branch, and the composition suite pins the production wiring end-to-end: the granted body `{"status":"ok","polling":{"running":true}}` and the fail-closed proxied literal through the same construction). The scheduler's death path is pinned in its own suite: the broken-seam death fires exactly one `error` record carrying the retained error, no further record follows (one per death event), `running=false`, `stop()` still rethrows (R4), the no-logger embedding stays silent, and a `logger` without `error` fails at assembly. The CLI gains the exported `assessEngineLiveness`/`EngineLiveness`/`EngineLivenessInput`/`EngineAccountSilence` (internal API under `src/`), its table test (the strict boundary at the threshold, the interval following the configured value, the per-account `retry_after_seconds`/`auth_error` allowances with one live account clearing the suspicion, the stopped-service and no-runs `no-evidence` arms, and the fail-fast input validation) and the handler tests (the warning line with the §10 timestamp, exit 0, silence for current cycles/stopped services/stale locks/the suspended shape/non-pollable accounts). `PollingEngine` gains the `running` getter and `ApiRoutesOptions` the optional `health` member (the drift guard's `Required<…>` boot wires a refusing source, so a future family stays visible to every guard arm). The exported names (`HealthPollingDiagnosticsSchema`, `HealthRouteOptions`, `HEALTH_RESPONSE` unchanged) are internal contract under `src/` and wire contract under §13; changing either requires a successor decision. The restart residual stays open: a future "exit on death" or supervised-restart decision supersedes interpretation (5) and owns its own trade record.

## D-193 — The live restart-pending diff in settings: the reloader's own `pendingRestart()` getter as the single source, a required additive GET field, the UI's class-vs-state distinction, and the follow-up inconsistency kept at the log level (spec §6.4, §13, §14.5; task FSM-5)

**Date:** 2026-11-07 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§6.4](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#64-change-application), [§13](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#13-http-api), [§14.5](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#145-settings) · **Tasks:** [FSM-5](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-180 (spec 1.1's amendment this entry implements — §13's settings row and §14.5 now distinguish class from state), D-026 (the reload semantics whose diff vocabulary and startup baseline this entry exposes — the interpretation whose seams are consumed here), D-130 (the settings routes and `SettingsStore` seam whose snapshot gains one member), D-140 (the composition that wires the store), D-178 (the `appliedRetentionDays` precedent for an additive required GET envelope member), [TZ-fsm §7](plan/TZ-fsm.md#fsm-5)

**Decision.** TZ-fsm §7's stale-marker finding — `GET /api/settings`'s `restartRequired` flags are static §6.4 class markings (always `true` for host/port/auth.mode) while the actual effective-vs-startup diff surfaced only in the PUT response and the reload log, leaving a hand-edited file plus `quotameter reload`/SIGHUP invisible to the UI — is closed with the reloader's own diff as the single source. (Correction trail: the task's review round — deepseek-v4.1-flash, one round, APPROVE with 0 P0 / 0 P1 / 0 P2 / 5 P3, every invariant independently verified and 8 suites run by the reviewer — is folded in before landing: the third row binding and the multi-field notice join get their own component cells (a copy-paste error in the `auth.mode` row's binding passed every first-draft test), the PUT-outcome/live-standing coexistence is pinned as the production shape (the two notices are both true with distinct roles — the request outcome and the standing state — so neither is suppressed or reworded), and the pending state joins the WCAG e2e scan as its own cell; two P3s declined with reasons: deriving `RestartField` from a server type import (the module's documented plain-literals-plus-drift-pin pattern is the guard — the pin fails the suite on divergence, so the "second place to update" concern is already mechanical) and the defensive `?? []` fallback (it would mask exactly the contract break the required-field decision exists to surface).) (1) **The seam is a getter on the reloader, not a consumer-side recomputation.** `ConfigReloader.pendingRestart(): readonly RestartRequiredField[]` is `findReloadChanges(startup.config, current.config).restart` — the same function and the same two baselines a reload's own `restartRequired` result uses, read against the current effective configuration instead of a reload candidate. Both baselines are the reloader's private state, so the "which pair of configurations means pending" knowledge (D-026 interpretation 3) never leaves `src/config/reload.ts`; a consumer cannot pair the wrong baselines. The identity invariant — between reloads `current` is stable, so after a successful reload the getter equals that reload's `restartRequired` — is pinned by test, which is precisely the guarantee that the GET list and every PUT outcome answer the same question. Fresh process: `startup === current` → `[]`. A rejected reload: `current` untouched (§6.2) → unchanged. An environment-pinned restart field never enters the effective configuration from a file hand-edit, so overrides add nothing to the list — the diff measures what the process runs, exactly the honest reading. The production wiring is a live thunk in the D-130 pattern: `createConfigFileSettingsStore` takes `pendingRestart: () => readonly RestartRequiredField[]` (the `effective` precedent — consulted on every `read()`), the composition passes `reloader.pendingRestart`, and the route serves `snapshot.pendingRestart` verbatim. The test double in the route suite mirrors the composition with the reloader's own `findReloadChanges`, the same mirroring it already performs for `apply`. (2) **The wire addition is required, not optional.** `SettingsResponseSchema` gains `pendingRestart: Array<Union(Literals(SETTINGS_RESTART_FIELDS)))` — the closed §6.4 trio vocabulary already drift-pinned against `RESTART_REQUIRED_FIELDS` (the constant moves above the GET schema in `src/schemas/api/settings.ts`, its docblock now naming both consumers). Required rather than optional because §13's only consumer is the bundled UI shipping in the same commit (the `appliedRetentionDays` precedent, U-053/D-178) and the server always sends it; the package is unreleased, so there is no cross-version reader to protect. The PUT response is unchanged — it already reports the same list as of its own reload. (3) **The UI distinguishes class from state, both truths visible at once (§14.5's sentence).** The static per-row `restartRequired` markers and the static section hint (the class: "changing this setting requires a restart") stand untouched; a non-empty served `pendingRestart` additionally renders a per-row "restart pending" marker beside exactly the named fields and a section notice — "Changed and adopted by a reload, waiting for the process restart: {fields}. Run quotameter restart." — through the new `settings.facts.restartPending`/`restartPendingNotice` catalog keys. The notice appears and disappears with the served value across page reloads (the served truth is the single source, the D-135 failed-load rule unchanged). The operator-facing field labels are shared with the PUT outcome notice through `createRestartFieldLabels` in `ui/src/settings-fields.ts` (static-literal `t()` calls only, the D-132 both-directions rule; the field paths mirror `SETTINGS_RESTART_FIELDS` as plain literals, the `LOG_LEVELS` no-runtime-import precedent, drift-pinned by the component suite) — the two surfaces name one field identically. (4) **TZ-fsm R3's optional follow-up inconsistency indicator is rejected; observation stays at the log level.** The "config adopted, storage/polling lagging" window already has its surface: the §16 `error` record the reload fault containment emits (D-140/D-177 — "configuration reload applied but its follow-up application failed; storage and polling may lag the effective configuration"). A `followUpsConsistent` health flag was rejected because the window is transient (the next successful reload re-runs the follow-ups), self-healing, and — unlike the dead-engine finding it parallels — actionable only by re-running `quotameter reload`, which the error record already tells the operator; a flag would add a health surface (with its own grant-rule and freshness questions) for a state with no distinct remedy. This is the recorded minimum R3 sanctions.

**Reasons.** The getter-over-recomputation choice follows the audit's own unit of analysis: the finding is that the live diff existed (in the reloader) but was unreachable (only inside a reload result), so the fix must publish it, not fork it — a consumer-side `findReloadChanges(startup, current)` would duplicate the baseline-pairing semantics at every future consumer and invite the wrong-pair drift the single source forecloses. The identity invariant makes the seam self-checking: the reloader suite pins getter-equals-result after every reload class, so a future change to the diff (a new restart-requiring field, a different baseline) fails coherently in one place. Required-over-optional follows the project's own additive-extension precedent and the "internal to the web interface" scope of §13 — optionality would buy nothing for a same-commit consumer pair and cost every reader a third arm. The per-row-plus-notice UI shape keeps the class marking honest (the trio's markers are contract facts, not state) while making the state unmissable and actionable; a notice alone would leave the row-level "which value?" question to the operator's memory. The R3 rejection mirrors D-192's exit-neutrality reasoning: a diagnostic surface must either change what the operator does or sharpen what they see; the error record already does both for this window.

**Consequences.** `ConfigReloader`'s exported surface gains `pendingRestart()` (internal API under `src/`; changing its semantics is a successor decision); `SettingsSnapshot` and `ConfigFileSettingsStoreOptions` gain the corresponding member (every implementor updated in this commit — the route-suite double, the composition, the store); the settings GET wire contract changes additively but strictly (`docs/api.md` and `docs/openapi.json` regenerated in this commit; the drift guard's freshness row enforces the regeneration); the UI catalog gains two facts-section keys with the i18n completeness suite covering them automatically. No PUT contract, refusal, or validation change; no reload behavior change — the getter reads state the reloader already maintains. The standing proofs: the reloader suite's getter cells (fresh/live-only `[]`, the reload-result identity, persistence across reads and no-change reloads, the rejected-reload no-op, the return-to-startup settle), the route suite's three acceptance scenarios (fresh `[]`; the hand-edit+reload shape `["server.host"]` persisting across GETs; live-field PUTs adding nothing, both from empty and beside a pending change), the store suite's per-read liveness pin (three reads, three thunk calls, each serving the moment's value), the composition SIGHUP suite's end-to-end pin (the real composition over a hand-edited file and `applyReload()` — the production seam, not a double), the sweep suite's fresh-composition `[]`, the schema suite's required/closed envelope rows, and the component suite's class-vs-state distinction (markers alone when empty; exactly the pending rows marked; the notice's names and remedy; the appear/disappear lifecycle; the label drift pin). The follow-up inconsistency window stays log-level per interpretation (4); reopening it as a health fact is a successor decision that must answer the remedy question recorded here.

## D-194 — The finalized npm manifest: version `0.0.0` until the release commit, no `exports` for a CLI-first package, `ui/dist` in `files` (allowed-but-not-required) with the npm README-basename trap removed by renaming `ui/README.md` → `ui/OVERVIEW.md`, and the dependency audit's exact nine (spec §3, §4.2, §4.4, §5.1; task 184)

**Date:** 2026-11-07 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§3](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#3-technology-and-packaging), [§4.2](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#42-package-name), [§4.4](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#44-cicd-and-supply-chain-safeguards), [§5.1](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#51-supported-environment) · **Tasks:** [184](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-186 (the first release is `v0.1.0` and `package.json` stays `0.0.0` until the release commit — the version decision this entry executes, not reopens), D-152 (the release workflow's build → check → publish order the `ui/dist` allowlist entry completes), D-008 (green-CI-tag publishing the manifest's version field feeds), D-098 (the `engines.node` single-source contract, unchanged and now cross-pinned against the Dockerfile), D-015 (the published `schema/config.schema.json` whose deep-importability the no-`exports` choice preserves), D-109/D-125 (the rate-limit plugin plan the in-house limiter superseded — why no `@fastify/rate-limit` dependency exists), D-127 (the build verification the release path runs before packing), D-155 (the name-based license self-exclusion that keeps any version bump safe)

**Decision.** Task 184 finalizes the public manifest as follows. (1) **Version stays `0.0.0`** — the deliberate D-186 execution: the release checklist's version commit (step 3) is the only writer, the release workflow's tag/version-match and green-CI gates guard the bumped number, and an in-tree literal `0.1.0` would preempt both gates and promise a release that has not been rehearsed. The executable pin couples instead of freezing: `test/unit/package-manifest.spec.ts` requires exact `X.Y.Z` semver (no prerelease/build suffixes — they would flow into tags) and requires any non-`0.0.0` version to have its `## [X.Y.Z]` section in `CHANGELOG.md` (the checklist's fold-then-bump order, made structural). (2) **No `exports` and no `main`** — the package is a CLI plus embedded web service (§4.2, §5.2); `bin` is the only consumer surface, and with no exports map the deep import `quotameter/schema/config.schema.json` (D-015's published artifact) stays available to validators and editors. Declaring `"exports": {}` would seal the package; declaring entry paths would invent a library API nothing consumes. Adding either is a successor decision to this entry. (3) **`files` gains `ui/dist/`** — the prebuilt UI (§3: the frontend is built before publication; §17.2's no-install-time-build): the release workflow already builds and verifies the UI before `check:package` and publish (D-152's landed step order, pinned by `release-workflow.spec.ts`), so the published tarball ships it with no workflow change. The entry is **allowed but not required** in `scripts/check-package.mjs` (exact entries + an `ALLOWED_PREFIXES = ['ui/dist/']` class, npm listing each built file individually): the CI `package` job packs without building and the dev container routes builds to `DIST_DIR` — npm silently skips allowlisted-but-missing paths (the LICENSE/NOTICE precedent), and the required set stays `package.json`, `bin/quotameter.mjs`, `schema/config.schema.json`. The **boundary against tasks 185/186**: the compiled server graph — whatever the shipped CLI comes to resolve to beyond `bin/` + `schema/` — is deliberately not declared yet; task 185 owns the resolving entry point and grows `files` + the allowlist together (the new agreement test makes a half-update fail `make check`), task 186 owns the clean-container no-build verification. (4) **`ui/README.md` is renamed `ui/OVERVIEW.md`** — the empirically verified npm trap this task surfaced: whenever npm's pack walker walks a directory for a `files` entry — **with or without a build present** (both reproduced: a tree without `ui/dist`, and a tree with the real built `ui/dist`; the review round additionally reproduced it on npm 10.9.2) — it force-includes any README-family basename from the partially-packed parent directory into the tarball, so `ui/README.md`, a 69 kB development document, would have shipped in the **release tarball itself**, and **no `files` spelling or `!` negation can exclude it** (verified across `ui/dist/`, `ui/dist`, `ui/dist/**`, combined forms, parent-with-negations — and the force is not limited to directory entries: a scratch `schema/README.md` packs beside the exact-file entry `schema/config.schema.json`). (Correction trail: the task's review round — deepseek-v4.1-flash, one round, APPROVE with 1 P2 / 7 P3, the P2 and six P3s folded in before landing — disproved this entry's first-draft empirical claim that the trap fires only when the packed subdirectory is absent at pack time; the corrected, unconditional statement above is what the rename's necessity rests on, and the same round closed the agreement pin's missing prefix⊆`files` direction (the release tarball could have silently lost the UI with every gate green), widened the forced-basename pin to exact-file parents (`schema/`), tightened the metadata pins to exact values, widened the audit extractor (`require()`, digit-leading names), and updated the Node-bump procedure docs and `docs/architecture/package-layout.md`'s "export paths" promise. One P3 declined: hardening `check-package.mjs`'s main guard against symlinked invocation — the guard is byte-identical to `render-mutation-report.mjs`'s house pattern, and no project invocation path (container `/app`, CI checkout) traverses a symlink; a divergence would be a whole-pattern change, not a one-file fix.) Shipping a dev doc would violate §4.4's "do not ship development-only artefacts", and allowlisting it would make the gate's meaning context-dependent, so the basename is removed instead: the UI tree's documentation lives on as `ui/OVERVIEW.md` (the in-place convention kept; the two living references updated — `ui/src/account-selection.ts`, `src/server/README.md`), and the manifest spec pins the invariant structurally: no README/license-family basename may exist in any directory that packs only part of its content, so the trap cannot silently return under any future npm version. (5) **The dependency audit's result is exact nine**: every `dependencies` key is imported by `src/` or `bin/` and every bare non-`node:` import of that graph roots to a declared dependency (pinned by test, both directions — the second direction is the published-package crash a devDependency-in-graph would cause). The UI's runtime libraries (vue, vue-router, vue-i18n, echarts) stay devDependencies by design: the shipped artifact is the prebuilt bundle, so they are build-time inputs, not install-time requirements. `@fastify/rate-limit` is deliberately absent — §3's plugin row was superseded by D-125's in-house limiter (D-109 had planned the registration). (6) **Metadata completes the public shape**: `repository` (`git+https://github.com/yepbro/quotameter.git` — `npm publish --provenance` refuses to run without it, the release.md task-184 dependency note satisfied), `bugs`, `homepage`, and `author: Den Brooks <denis@yepbro.pro>` (§4.3's attribution on the npm page; NOTICE remains the in-tarball attribution). `private: true` stays in-tree — the release workflow's `npm pkg delete private` is the only remover (D-152), so no local publish can ever succeed. `engines.node` stays exactly `>=22.13.0` (the §20 shape D-098's gates fail closed on; now also cross-pinned against the Dockerfile's `FROM node:` tag by the new spec, joining ci-workflow.spec.ts's CI-site pins).

**Reasons.** (1) A "final" manifest that hardcodes the release number would make the version commit — the release process's own checkpoint, where the changelog folds and the tag is cut — meaningless: the gates D-008/D-152 built guard a version the tree already claims. The placeholder-with-coupling keeps the release process the single writer while making the fold-then-bump order executable. (2) npm's exports map is a sealing device; sealing a package whose only documented surface is `quotameter` (§4.2, §5.2) buys strictness for an API that does not exist while breaking the one deep import (D-015's schema) real consumers could use today. (3) Deferring `ui/dist` to 185/186 — the alternative the boundary question posed — was rejected because the release pipeline's step order (build before check and publish) is already landed and pinned, waiting only for the allowlist entry; and the README-trap discovery is a property of `ui/dist`'s participation in packing, so it belongs to the task that adds that participation. Allowed-not-required mirrors reality: two of the three pack contexts legitimately produce no UI build, and requiring it there would either break CI's smoke-test job or force a pointless build into it — the release tarball (the only published artifact) carries the UI unconditionally. (4) The rename is structural where the alternatives are conventional: an allowlist entry for a file npm sometimes forces in is a gate whose meaning depends on the walker's version and the build state, while a tree with no forced basenames under `ui/` makes "the tarball is exactly `files`" true in every context — the project's D-036-style rule that stated properties should be structural, not context-dependent. (5) The audit exists because §3 demands minimal runtime dependencies while the graph that proves minimality keeps growing: a test that walks `src/` + `bin/` imports keeps the manifest honest as 185/186 change what ships, rather than freezing today's list.

**Consequences.** `package.json` (name/version/engines/bin unchanged; +`ui/dist/` in files; +repository/bugs/homepage/author), `scripts/check-package.mjs` (exported `ALLOWED_EXACT`/`ALLOWED_PREFIXES`/`REQUIRED_ENTRIES`, prefix matching, main guard — importable by the spec, the `openapi-document.mjs` pattern), `scripts/check-package.d.mts` (the type surface), and `test/unit/package-manifest.spec.ts` (the ten pins) are the executable contract; extending `files` without the allowlist, or vice versa, fails `make check`, and so does a README-family file in any partially-packed directory, an undeclared graph import, an unused runtime dependency, an `exports`/`main` addition, or a version bump without its changelog section. `ui/OVERVIEW.md`'s header documents why it is not `README.md`. docs/release.md's task-184 dependency note is rewritten to the remaining 185/186 boundary; the release workflow's and release-workflow.spec.ts's forward-looking comments updated. Historical mentions of `ui/README.md` in landed DECISIONS/CHANGELOG entries are history and stay. Tasks 185/186 inherit: whatever the packaged CLI resolves to must join `files` + `ALLOWED_*` in one change, and if its build output nests under a partially-packed directory, the forced-basename pin already guards the same trap. The published-tarball contract from v0.1.0 on: exactly the allowlisted entries — the launcher, the schema, the prebuilt UI when built before packing, the license set, and npm's root README/package.json.

## D-195 — The packaged CLI: tsc-emitted `dist/` behind the launcher's dist-first resolution, AST-planned specifier normalization, and actionable startup errors for every broken layout (spec §3, §5.1, §17.2; task 185)

**Date:** 2026-11-07 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§3](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#3-technology-and-packaging), [§5.1](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#51-supported-environment), [§17.2](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#172-installationpackage-tests) · **Tasks:** [185](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-194 (the manifest boundary this entry executes — `files` + the tarball allowlist grow together, in one change, as required), D-098 (the runtime gate whose before-any-load ordering the new resolution preserves), D-161 (the version-gate-before-import discipline re-pinned for the dist path), D-116 (the dynamic-import discipline the emitted graph preserves by construction), D-152 (the release pipeline whose step order gains the CLI build, pinned), D-186 (the v0.1.0 rehearsal this packaging feeds)

**Decision.** Task 185 makes the installed `quotameter` command resolve to a packaged CLI with no source checkout and no install-time build (§5.1, §17.2), as four landed parts. (1) **The build is `tsc` emit plus a specifier-normalization pass, not a bundler and not shipped sources.** `npm run build:cli` (`scripts/build-cli.mjs` + `tsconfig.build.json`) compiles `src/` into `dist/` as type-erased ESM mirroring the source tree one-to-one, then normalizes the emitted specifiers to the forms plain Node ESM requires — extensionless relative imports to `.js` (the `src/` tree's deliberate bundler-resolution style, `moduleResolution: "bundler"` + jiti in development, is preserved verbatim by `tsc`), relative directory imports to `/index.js` (`src/server/providers.ts`'s `../providers/zai-coding-plan` barrel), and a fail-closed rejection of extensionless deep bare imports — the class jiti resolves through CJS extension guessing and real Node ESM refuses (`ajv/dist/2020`, verified live on the pinned 22.13.0 during design: it builds under jiti and crashes with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` in a clean ESM load; the one live value import of that module already carries `.js`, the extensionless form is type-only and erased). Rewrites are planned with TypeScript's own parser over the emitted JavaScript — AST positions (the literal's inner span derived from `end - 1 - text.length`, because `StringLiteral.start` is `null` on the pinned compiler line), never regexes — so prose strings containing `from './x'` and docblock `{@link import('./x')}` references are structurally invisible and cannot be corrupted (pinned by unit test with exactly those adversarial fixtures). The interop the published artifact depends on was verified on the pinned runtime during design: named imports from CJS dependencies (`pino.pino`, `pino.stdSerializers`, `fastify.LogController`, `luxon.DateTime`, `umzug.Umzug`) all resolve under real Node ESM — the compiled graph is the first non-jiti ESM execution of this code, and it works. (2) **The launcher resolves dist-first with actionable errors for every broken layout (§5.1's name-the-requirement-and-the-fix).** After the runtime gate and the `--version` fast path, `bin/quotameter.mjs` probes `../dist/cli/main.js` (the packaged build, plain Node, no jiti) and falls back to `../src/cli/main.ts` (the source checkout through jiti, the unchanged development contract — the './'-prefixed `.js` specifier is jiti's loader-hook requirement, and the probe/import split keeps absolute `file://` URLs out of jiti's CJS require). Both candidates absent names both locations and the reinstall; a dist entry that loads but exports no callable `runCli` is an unusable entry module; an `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` behind an existing dist entry is a damaged installation to reinstall; a source checkout reached without jiti names the loader and `npm run build:cli`. Dist-first is deliberate: the installed package carries only `dist/`, and a checkout that also built `dist/` should exercise the packaged shape — the accepted developer footgun is a stale in-tree `dist/` shadowing live `src/` until removed (`dist/` is gitignored; the build's own clean-outDir re-creates it on every rebuild). The gate ordering (D-098/D-161) is preserved and re-pinned for the dist path: a below-minimum runtime refuses before any entry is loaded, proven with a fixture entry that would die on a syntax error if ever evaluated. (3) **The manifest grows per D-194's boundary, in one change:** `package.json` `files` gains `dist/`, `scripts/check-package.mjs`'s `ALLOWED_PREFIXES` gains `'dist/'` — allowed-but-not-required, the `ui/dist/` precedent: the 184 agreement pin (`package-manifest.spec.ts`) is generic over the constants, so the pair cannot half-update without failing `make check`, and `REQUIRED_ENTRIES` deliberately stays `package.json`/`bin`/`schema` because the required class asserts on-disk existence in every pack context while `dist/` is build output (the enforcement chain instead: `npm run verify:build` now requires `dist/cli/main.js` and a non-empty `dist/cli/*.js`, and every pack context builds first — CI's `package` job and the release pipeline before `check:package`, `make build` before `make package` in `check-all`). (4) **Every pack context builds, and the clean global-install test proves the command.** CI's `build` job and `make build` gain `build:cli` before `verify:build`; the `package` job builds before `check:package` and `npm pack` (so the smoke-test tarball carries `dist/`); the release workflow builds after `build:ui` and before `verify:build`/`check:package`/publish (pinned by `release-workflow.spec.ts`'s new order pin); and the `install` job gains the real-command step — `quotameter --help` through the installed package, asserting the rendered §5.2 command table — because the pre-existing `--version` fast path never loads the command modules and proves nothing about the packaged CLI (a dist-less tarball fails the step loudly; `ci-workflow.spec.ts` pins the step and the package-job build order). The committed suites prove the same offline: `test/integration/cli-bin-dist.spec.ts` runs the real build into a fixture package root (bin + dist + package.json, the tarball's shape, the repository's `node_modules` symlinked in as the dependency tree a real install provides — the suite stays inside the no-network guard) and drives `--help` (the whole compiled dispatch graph, with empty stderr pinning that `node:sqlite` stayed behind the dynamic storage imports in the SHIPPED artifact — the D-116/D-161 discipline holding by construction in the emitted graph), `--version`, and `status` (the lazy dynamic-import edges) through the real launcher under plain Node; a second describe pins every actionable-error layout with fixture packages. `test/unit/build-cli-script.spec.ts` pins the pure seams (`mapRelativeSpecifier`'s two bundler fallbacks, `isDeepBareImport`'s classification with `node:` builtins exempt, the AST planner's import-form coverage and adversarial-string precision, the offset-adjusted splice), and `verify-build-script.spec.ts` gains the missing-dist-entry rejection. Rejected alternatives: shipping `src/` with jiti as a runtime dependency (transpiles the CLI graph on every invocation, ships ~115 source files as the product, and adds a build tool to `dependencies` against §3's minimal-runtime-dependency posture); bundling with esbuild/rolldown/tsdown (a new dev dependency, and chunking/tree-shaking semantics that would have to be re-verified against every landed laziness and confinement pin — tsc emit keeps the shipped graph structurally identical to `src/`, so the `node:sqlite` storage gate, the lazy `run`-handler server import, and the gate ordering hold in the artifact by construction rather than by re-proof). Two further design-phase findings are recorded as build-script behavior: the incremental-emit trap (an incremental `tsc` reusing a rewritten outDir silently skips emission for unchanged sources — `tsconfig.build.json` pins `incremental: false` and the script always cleans the outDir), and `import.meta.resolve`'s uselessness as a build-time probe on this runtime (it fabricates URLs for nonexistent paths — `ajv/dist/nope` "resolves" — so the deep-import check is the AST classification, not a resolution probe).

**Reasons.** The spec's constraint pair — installed-command-works (§5.1, §17.2) and no install-time build (§3, §17.2) — admits exactly three shapes (ship compiled output, ship sources plus a runtime transpiler, ship a bundle), and the project's own precedents decide among them: the launcher's original docblock anticipated "the published build is real ESM with named exports", the dev container reserves `/dist` in every ignore list, and the D-194 dependency audit exists precisely to keep the runtime manifest honest while what ships changes shape. Emit-not-bundle keeps every behavioral pin true without re-verification: the artifact's module graph IS the source graph, so the confinement and laziness properties the suites have pinned for years transfer to the package, and the only new machinery (specifier normalization) is a pure, unit-pinned function whose defect classes were found and closed during design, not after publication. Dist-first resolution makes the packaged artifact the tested artifact: whatever a developer or CI packs, the command runs the same code an installed package runs. The actionable-error contract follows §5.1's own rule (the spec's init-workflow sentence "display a helpful next step instead of failing cryptically" is the house style for every startup failure): each message names the requirement (the two candidate entry locations, the compiled graph's completeness, the jiti loader) and the remedy (reinstall, or the development build command) — and the messages are pinned executably so they cannot decay into stack traces.

**Consequences.** New: `tsconfig.build.json` (emit config, `incremental: false`), `scripts/build-cli.mjs` + `build-cli.d.mts` (the build and its pure seams), `test/unit/build-cli-script.spec.ts`, `test/integration/cli-bin-dist.spec.ts`. Changed: `bin/quotameter.mjs` (dist-first resolution and the four error messages; the old "missing the CLI command modules" wording retires), `package.json` (+`dist/` in `files`, +`build:cli`), `scripts/check-package.mjs` (`ALLOWED_PREFIXES` + docblock), `scripts/verify-build.mjs` (the CLI half, `CLI_DIST_DIR`), `Makefile` (`build` target), `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (build/package/install jobs), `.github/workflows/release.yml` (the CLI build step), the workflow-pin specs, `verify-build-script.spec.ts`, `package-manifest.spec.ts`'s boundary docblock, `src/cli/README.md`, `docs/release.md`. The published-tarball contract updates D-194's closing sentence: exactly the allowlisted entries — the launcher, the compiled CLI under `dist/`, the schema, the prebuilt UI when built before packing, the license set, and npm's root README/package.json. Task 186 inherits: the deeper §17.2 clean-container verification (`init --yes`, install/start, restart-after-failure, reboot enablement, user service with linger) now runs against a tarball whose command genuinely works; the `ui/dist` serving path (`../../ui/dist` from `dist/server/` resolves to the package root exactly as `src/server/` did — same depth by construction) is exercised by a service start, and this entry's design-phase verification (not a landed test) covers it only as analysis. The dev-container `dist/` default stays in-tree-but-ignored (compose does not redirect `CLI_DIST_DIR`): a local `npm pack` after `npm run build:cli` packs the compiled CLI, mirroring the release shape; the stale-dist footgun is the recorded cost of dist-first, and removing an in-tree `dist/` is `rm -rf dist` (the build's own clean-outDir does it on every rebuild; `make clean` removes only the container volumes and does NOT touch it — the review round's correction of this entry's first-draft claim). (Correction trail: the task's review round — glm-5.3#max, one round, APPROVE with 1 P2 / 7 P3 after the deepseek primary timed out with no findings body and cursor-agent was quota-blocked — is folded into this entry and the same commit, which had not landed when corrected. The P2: the dist-over-src ordering — this entry's defining resolution decision — had no executable pin (every fixture had only one candidate present, so inverting the launcher's if/else kept the suite green); the both-entries fixture now pins the choice. Folded P3s: `ERR_UNSUPPORTED_DIR_IMPORT` (a directory sitting at the entry path — reproduced by the reviewer as a raw internal-error leak) joins `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` in the damaged-install arm; the source-branch message now covers jiti-present-but-module-missing checkouts, not only jiti absent; the planner identifies dynamic-import specifiers by argument position (a two-argument `import('./x', { with: … })` is planned, not silently skipped) and self-verifies its splice span against the raw code, refusing escaped specifiers instead of corrupting them; `runVerifyBuild`'s auto-companion tree lives inside the cleaned temp root (90 leaked sibling dirs measured); the build refuses a `CLI_DIST_DIR` naming the repository or an ancestor before its recursive clean; README's `make build` row names both build halves; and the `make clean` remedy claim above is corrected. No findings were declined.)

## D-196 — The no-install-time-build proof: the compiler-free install matrix, the lifecycle-script ban, and the pure-JS dependency-closure audit (spec §3, §17.2; task 186)

**Date:** 2026-11-08 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§3](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#3-technology-and-packaging), [§17.2](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#172-installationpackage-tests) · **Tasks:** [186](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-195 (the compiled-in-tarball packaging whose no-build promise this entry verifies end to end), D-194 (the manifest boundary whose lifecycle half this entry pins), D-157 (the install job's SHA-verified runtime whose matrix this entry hardens), D-152 (the release pipeline whose tarball the matrix proves), D-098 (the runtime gate already proven on the same matrix)

**Decision.** Task 186 closes §3/§17.2's "Do not use `postinstall` scripts or native modules" as verified fact, in three layers. (1) **The environment: the existing CI `install` matrix becomes the compiler-free proof — extended, not duplicated.** The stock `ubuntu:22.04`, `ubuntu:24.04`, and `debian:stable` images were verified compiler-free live at design time (`command -v` over gcc, cc, g++, clang, make, python3, python — none present on any of the three), so §17.2's "clean Ubuntu 22.04, Ubuntu 24.04, and Debian containers … verify no native compilation and no `postinstall`" lands where the spec places it: the task-053 job. A new step ("Verify the container ships no build toolchain") turns the property from incidental into checked — it runs after the prerequisites install (so apt dragging a toolchain in fails too) and exits non-zero on any of the seven probed tools, so a base-image change that ships a compiler breaks CI loudly instead of silently weakening what the matrix proves; the pinned tool list is an exact pin in `ci-workflow.spec.ts`. The tarball install gains `--foreground-scripts`: the structural pins below assert no dependency script exists, so any script that ever appears runs visibly in the job log rather than as hidden detached output. Three post-install steps verify the installed package on the machine npm actually wrote: the installed manifest carries none of preinstall/install/postinstall/preprepare/prepare/postprepare/prepublish (npm's complete install-time set); the installed-package tree — the root manifest's directory and every package under any `node_modules` child, scoped or plain — is scanned for `*.node` binaries, `binding.gyp` recipes, and preinstall/install/postinstall manifest keys (because a consumer's install re-resolves the dependency ranges against the live registry, the lockfile not traveling with a tarball — the scan reads what npm resolved on THIS run, and only REAL package manifests: fixture `package.json` files a dependency ships inside its test tree, like `resolve`'s `test/resolver/multirepo`, are never read by npm and never scanned — verified live), so the script-carrying and native classes fail the job instead of merely logging under `--foreground-scripts`; and `dist/cli/main.js` is present — the tarball-already-contains-`dist/` fact (D-195) asserted directly at the installed end, not only transitively through the `--help` step. (2) **The structural pins make the guarantee regression-proof.** The root manifest's own ban (`package-manifest.spec.ts`, the task-184 family): none of preinstall/install/postinstall/preprepare/prepare/postprepare/prepublish may appear in `scripts` — npm's complete install-time lifecycle set, not just `postinstall`, because an install-time build under any of those names is still an install-time build (the first three run on every consumer install; the prepare trio and the deprecated prepublish on git-URL and local installs; `prepublishOnly` is publish-time and stays owned by the release pipeline). The dependency side (`install-time-build.spec.ts`, new): a lockfile-driven, npm-style closure walk over exactly the edges npm follows on a consumer install — the root's `dependencies` AND `optionalDependencies`, then each entry's dependencies, optionalDependencies, and the REQUIRED `peerDependencies` npm 7+ auto-installs (optional peers skipped, per `peerDependenciesMeta`) — with every name resolved against the parent `node_modules` chain (lockfile keys are the real `npm ci` paths) — over two layers: no closure package may carry npm's own `hasInstallScript` flag (the flag npm computes for exactly the scripts that run when a dependency installs, node-gyp recipes included — catches the regression at lockfile-update time), and no closure package on disk may declare preinstall/install/postinstall, ship a `binding.gyp`, or contain a `*.node` binary (independent of npm's flag semantics, so a future npm redefining `hasInstallScript` cannot silently weaken the audit). (3) **The audit result, recorded exactly:** the production closure is 112 lockfile entries, all pure JavaScript — zero install scripts, zero `hasInstallScript` flags, zero native recipes or binaries (the only `hasInstallScript` in the whole lockfile is `fsevents`, dev-only and macOS-only, outside the closure and outside the published tree; every peer dependency in the closure is optional today, so the required-peer edge is covered ahead of need). Sixteen closure packages (luxon, cookie, glob, minimatch, …) carry `prepare`-only scripts; npm does not execute a dependency's `prepare` when installing from registry tarballs — only preinstall/install/postinstall run for dependencies — verified live: the `--foreground-scripts` install of the packed tarball into the compiler-free container shows zero script activity. `prepare` is therefore NOT banned for dependencies (banning it would false-positive on 16 legitimate registry packages) but the full prepare trio IS banned for the root package (a git-URL install of quotameter itself would run it). The genuine proof ran before landing: `npm run build:cli` + `npm pack` in the worktree container, then a stock `ubuntu:24.04` container — toolchain absence confirmed, Node 22.13.0 installed from the official binaries against D-157's pinned digest, `npm install --global --prefix /usr/local --foreground-scripts ./quotameter-0.0.0.tgz` (114 packages, no script output), `quotameter --version` → `0.0.0`, `quotameter --help` rendering the full §5.2 command table, and the three installed-tree checks all passing.

**Reasons.** The extension-over-new-job choice follows the spec's own placement (§17.2 names exactly these three containers for exactly this verification) and the supply-chain ground D-157 laid: a separate compiler-free job would re-implement the SHA-verified Node-install machinery to prove the same tarball in a weaker environment, while the stock distro images already are the target installations of §5.1 — the honest environment is the one users get. The strictness of the dependency pins is deliberate: §3 demands minimal runtime dependencies and no native modules, and the D-194 audit exists to keep the manifest honest as the tree changes — the natural failure mode of a dependency audit is decay at the next `npm install`, so the pin is total (ANY install script or native artifact in the closure fails `make check`) with the escape hatch being a successor decision, not an allowlist entry that would rot. The two-layer pin (lockfile flag + on-disk scan) mirrors the project's D-036 rule that stated properties should be structural, not tool-dependent: the lockfile layer catches the regression early with npm's own semantics, the disk layer keeps the guarantee even if those semantics drift. The compiler-free container is the third, environment-level layer of the same defense: with no toolchain present, even a dependency that slipped every structural pin and a semantics change that ran its `prepare` stub still could not compile anything — the install would fail loudly at the script, which is the proof §17.2 asks for ("installation works in a clean, compiler-free container"), not the weaker "nothing tried to compile". The deterministic-gate leg (part 4) chose pinning over the alternatives for the same structural reason: making the compiled graph load under jiti's hooks would mean depending on jiti/Node hook-bridge internals (the request that dies is inside jiti's own runtime resolution — not ours to fix), and Makefile leg-ordering or a `rm -rf dist` sweep would leave every direct `npx vitest run` invocation ambient-dependent — only pinning each suite's entry mode makes the suites' subject independent of tree state, which is the D-162/D-173 discipline (a suite's premise is named, not inherited from the machine) applied to the launcher's resolution.

**Consequences.** Changed: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (the install job's toolchain step, `--foreground-scripts`, the three verification steps — the tree step scanning every installed `package.json`, not just the root manifest), `test/unit/ci-workflow.spec.ts` (four new pins: the toolchain step's exact tool list and fail-closed shape before the install, the `--foreground-scripts` line, and the verification trio's assertions, failure expressions, `continue-on-error` ban, and order), `test/unit/package-manifest.spec.ts` (the lifecycle ban over npm's complete install-time set, the `scripts` field), `bin/quotameter.mjs` (the `QUOTAMETER_CLI_ENTRY` override: invalid values and forced-but-missing modes fail closed with actionable messages; the auto order and every existing error message untouched, re-pinned), `src/config/env.ts` (`LAUNCHER_VARIABLES` — the reserved-name carve-out), the 13 real-launcher suites' spawn envs (`CLI_ENTRY_SOURCE`), `DECISIONS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/release.md` (the boundary note: the no-install-time-build proof landed; tasks 195/196 own the remaining §17.2 service-lifecycle matrix), `docs/agents/gotchas.md` (the dist+jiti pitfall), `src/cli/README.md` and `src/config/README.md` (the override and the reservation). New: `test/unit/install-time-build.spec.ts`, `test/unit/launcher-source-mode-pin.spec.ts`, and the entry-mode describe in `test/integration/cli-bin-dist.spec.ts` (both-entries fixtures proving the 'source' pin wins over dist-first, explicit 'dist', both forced-but-missing remedies, and the fail-closed invalid-value arm; `runBin` grew `nodeArgs` for the single jiti-bearing cell). Verification of the deterministic gate, per the re-landing bar: the six previously failing suites green WITH a built `dist/` present (74/74), then `make check` twice consecutively with `dist/` present (both green — the second run sees the first's dist by construction), then `rm -rf dist` and one more green `make check` — both ambient states proven. Accepted residuals: (a) the 16 `prepare` stubs stay in the closure — they never execute on registry installs, and the compiler-free container plus the lockfile flag cover the semantics-change scenario; (b) arm64 is proven architecturally (a pure-JS closure has no platform surface; the install job's Node digests cover arm64 runners) but the matrix evidence run is x64 — an arm64 runner joins the matrix only when GitHub-hosted arm64 containers become the cheaper option; (c) `fsevents` and the other dev-time natives stay out of scope — devDependencies never reach the consumer; (d) the lockfile pins guard the SNAPSHOT — a consumer's tarball install re-resolves dependency ranges against the live registry (verified live during review: the proof container's install resolved `@fastify/static` 10.1.10 and a glob 14 line newer than the lockfile's, including one transitive package absent from the lockfile entirely), so a dependency release published between lockfile updates can carry an install script no static layer has seen; the per-run CI scan of every installed `package.json` catches it on the next CI run, and the compiler-free container means nothing that slips through entirely could compile — the residual window is "a consumer installing exactly a post-release bad version before any CI run sees it", accepted for a pure-JS dependency tree. Adding any dependency whose install runs a script or ships a native addon — including prebuilt-with-install-script packages (the esbuild shape) — is a successor decision to this entry. `node:sqlite` needs no audit row: it is a runtime builtin imported as `node:*` (exempt in the D-194 audit's extractor), already probed by the install job's runtime-verification step on the declared minimum. (4) **The deterministic-gate design: the launcher gains `QUOTAMETER_CLI_ENTRY`, the real-launcher suites pin the source mode, and the landing's ambient-dist nondeterminism is closed.** The 2026-11-08 landing exposed what D-195 recorded as the stale-dist "developer footgun" in its gate-scale form: `make check-all` runs its test leg BEFORE `build:cli`, so the first run after a clean tree was green (launcher resolved `src/` through jiti) and every consecutive run was red — the built `dist/` flipped the launcher's dist-first resolution into the compiled graph, and under the real-launcher suites' `--import jiti/register` preload that combination is fatal: jiti's register hook stays installed process-wide, the compiled graph loads as native ESM, and when its CJS dependency `umzug` loads through Node's ESM→CJS translator, a request for jiti's own ESM runtime (`lib/jiti.mjs`) must be satisfied synchronously (`ModuleJob.runSync`) — impossible under the async MessagePort hooks, so every server-touching command died with `request for '…/node_modules/jiti/lib/jiti.mjs' is not in cache` (26 real-launcher failures across six suites; reproduced with a full stack trace through a driver importing `dist/server/main.js` under the harness's exact flags; the same import under plain Node — no jiti hooks — succeeds, which is why the installed package and `cli-bin-dist`'s children were never affected). The fix pins each suite's premise instead of ordering Makefile legs (ordering would leave every direct `npx vitest run` ambient-dependent): `QUOTAMETER_CLI_ENTRY` ('dist'/'source', any other value refused fail-closed with the §5.1-style message, forced-but-missing modes naming their remedy) pins the launcher's choice before the probe — at once the D-195 footgun's explicit remedy for humans (force the live source tree next to a stale built `dist/` instead of deleting it) and the suites' contract; every suite that spawns the launcher with jiti (13 of them) spreads `CLI_ENTRY_SOURCE` into the child env (the one suite that deliberately strips `QUOTAMETER_*` re-sets the literal explicitly), so the general suites always test the source-through-jiti development contract and the compiled mode keeps its dedicated jiti-free suite — nothing any test proves is weakened, each mode is now tested deterministically instead of whichever the ambient tree allowed. Two supporting pins make the design regression-proof: `test/unit/launcher-source-mode-pin.spec.ts` scans `test/` for files that spawn the launcher under jiti (the `'jiti/register'` + `'bin/quotameter.mjs'` literals — precise: runner-spawning suites and fixture strings do not match) and fails on any without the pin, and `src/config/env.ts` reserves the variable in its known-names set (the `PATH_VARIABLES` precedent — `LAUNCHER_VARIABLES`), because the closed `QUOTAMETER_*` vocabulary would otherwise reject it (`QUOTAMETER_CLI_ENTRY: unsupported environment variable` — the second failure layer the fix's first verification round caught); the carve-out is pinned by `config-env.spec.ts` beside the directory-variables precedent. (Correction trail: the task's review round — deepseek-v4.1-flash, one round, APPROVE with 0 P0 / 0 P1 / 2 P2 / 4 P3, every finding verified by the reviewer with live reproduction — is folded into this entry and the same commit, which had not landed when corrected. The P2s: the four new guard pins asserted string presence but not fail-closedness (a `continue-on-error` or a deleted failure branch kept them green — the D-157 rule now asserted for every new step, failure expressions pinned), and the closure walk followed only dependencies/optionalDependencies — npm 7+ auto-installs REQUIRED peerDependencies (the reviewer reproduced a required-peer install live; every current closure peer is optional, so the gap was latent — the walk now covers required peers and the root's optionalDependencies, a no-op on today's closure, re-verified at 112 entries). The P3s: the audit count was wrong in this entry's first draft (106, a flat name-dedup undercount — the real walk resolves 112 lockfile entries); the root ban omitted npm's `preprepare`/`postprepare` companions of `prepare` (both lists now carry the complete set, `prepublishOnly` excluded as publish-time); the static pins' snapshot scope is now recorded as residual (d) with the CI per-run installed-tree scan closing it per run; and docs/release.md's boundary note claimed the matrix "pins that the install executes no lifecycle script" — reworded to what each layer actually checks. Re-running the genuine proof after folding the review in caught two defects the first proof pass had not exercised in their final form: the reviewer-suggested whole-tree `package.json` scan crashed on a `try` with no `catch` (a syntax error the guard pins' substring checks could not see), and — with that fixed — it FALSE-POSITIVED on a real resolved dependency: `resolve` ships its own test fixtures (`resolve/test/resolver/multirepo/package.json` carries a `postinstall` npm never reads), so the scan was re-scoped to the installed-package tree — the root manifest's directory and every package under any `node_modules` child (scoped or plain), checking each REAL package's manifest for install scripts and its file tree for `*.node`/`binding.gyp`; the final proof run passes on the real resolved tree (which contains `resolve`'s fixtures) and the scanner is self-tested in both directions (a planted offender under `node_modules` is caught, a resolve-style fixture and a prepare-only stub are not). No findings were declined.)
