A second correction round followed the 2026-11-08 landing rollback: `make check-all` came back red on the main tree (26 real-launcher failures, `request for '…/jiti/lib/jiti.mjs' is not in cache`) while the task's own `make check` had been green — the gate was ambient-state-dependent (clean tree green, built-`dist/` tree red), the mechanism and the deterministic-gate design are part (4) above, and the fix's own verification caught the second failure layer (the closed `QUOTAMETER_*` vocabulary rejecting the new variable) before it could reach CI; the amended commit carries the triple-run evidence (suites green with `dist/`, `make check` ×2 consecutive with `dist/`, `make check` after `rm -rf dist`).

## D-197 — The configuration reference's home, drift-guarded agreement with the shipped schema, and the complete `QUOTAMETER_*` vocabulary (spec §6, §18; task 187)

**Date:** 2026-11-08 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§6](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#6-configuration-and-secrets), [§18](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#18-documentation-deliverables) · **Tasks:** [187](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-014 (the contract whose interpretations the reference renders), D-015 (the generated schema artifact the reference must agree with, and the freshness-test precedent for the guard), D-011/D-012 (the path-resolution semantics the reference states), D-023 (the environment override layer whose table the guard pins), D-026/D-193 (the §6.4 classification and the live pending state the Applies column renders), D-093 (the stated-properties-are-executable precedent), D-196 (the launcher variable the vocabulary documents as reserved)

**Decision.** Task 187 completes the §18 "Configuration reference" deliverable as a new `docs/configuration.md`, with three pinned choices. (1) **Home.** A dedicated page, not an extension of `docs/config-schema.md`: §18 names the reference, the published JSON Schema, and the sample config as separate deliverables, and the existing page is the schema-_artifact_ doc (editor association, regeneration) — the reference links to it and to `docs/config.example.json`, `README.md` links to both, and `docs/config-schema.md` links back, so the operator path and the artifact path stay discoverable from each other without either page absorbing the other's role. (2) **Agreement is executable, not asserted.** The done condition ("the reference and shipped JSON Schema agree") is enforced by `test/unit/configuration-reference.spec.ts` — the D-093/D-015 rule that a stated property is a structural pin: the guard parses the reference's field tables and compares them against a walk of `CONFIG_SCHEMA_DOCUMENT` (equivalent to the shipped `schema/config.schema.json`, which D-015's freshness test keeps identical to the document) — field inventory in both directions, the Type and Default columns exactly, the schema's constraint tokens (ranges, enum members, patterns, `minLength`/`minItems`/`uniqueItems`) as contained facts of the Validation column, the requiredness marker (a leading `required` token — a word-boundary match would false-positive on the `auth.mode` enum value), the Environment override column exactly against `ENV_OVERRIDES`, and the Applies column against `RELOAD_FIELDS` (the code's `'live'` class rendered by its operator-facing word `reload`; prefix matching carries §6.4's wholesale `accounts`/`providers` scope rows down to their fields). Beyond the tables, the guard is behavioral where behavior is the claim: each reserved `QUOTAMETER_*` name must actually pass the environment scan (`loadConfigWithEnv` with only that name set reports no `unsupported environment variable` problem) before the reference may list it, each documented cross-field rule must actually fire in `findConfigProblems`, and the operating sentences the tables cannot carry (the `app`-only-required-section rule, precedence, empty-means-unset, `~` not expanded, the `0700`/`0600` modes, the restart trio with its `quotameter restart` remedy, the unknown-name rejection, the read-only marking, the provider key charset) are pinned as normalized-prose presences — the `spec-timestamp-rule.spec.ts` shape. A docs-only change therefore cannot silently diverge: the full `make check` gate applies because the test ships with the reference (the docs-only format-only relief is consciously not taken — the guard is the deliverable's value). (3) **The environment vocabulary is complete in one place.** The reference documents the entire `QUOTAMETER_*` namespace: the seven override variables (guarded verbatim — names, fields, coercions), the two path variables, and the launcher variable `QUOTAMETER_CLI_ENTRY` — reserved names get their consumer and one line each, with the launcher's dist/source mechanics left to the CLI packaging docs (D-195/D-196) and pointed at; the rationale is that an operator meeting any `QUOTAMETER_*` name in the wild must find it in the reference, while the entry-mode mechanics belong to the packaging documents that own them. Secrets are documented by shape only (§6.3/§15.4): `apiKey`/`apiKeyEnv`/`passwordHash` carry their storage, masking, and write-only facts, never values or examples.

**Reasons.** (1) §18's deliverable list is the spec's own separation; folding the reference into the artifact page would bury the field tables under editor tooling and make the sample-config pointer incidental. (2) The project's drift history (D-183's finding — a spec sentence quietly contradicting the wire — and D-093's coverage-key guard) says a one-off cross-check decays at the first schema change; a guard makes "the reference and the schema agree" an invariant of `make check`, costs nothing at runtime (a pure file+walk comparison), and — because D-015 already locks the artifact to the document — one comparison site covers both the shipped file and the contract. The docs-only gate relief was weighed and declined: the reference's central claim IS the agreement, and only an executable check proves it continuously. (3) A closed vocabulary documented anywhere less than completely invites the exact failure the strict scan exists to prevent (a typo'd or undocumented name mystifying an operator); the reserved trio belongs in the reference because the scan's rejection behavior makes them public facts of the namespace, while their internals stay with their owning documents.

**Consequences.** New: `docs/configuration.md` and `test/unit/configuration-reference.spec.ts`. Changed: `README.md` (the Key documentation entry), `docs/config-schema.md` (the cross-link), `.env.example` (its stale "only supported environment overrides at this stage" claim — true before D-023's seven override variables landed — replaced by a pointer to the reference), `docs/providers/zai-coding-plan.md` (its quotation of D-014's "seeded by `init`" wording annotated with what the landed tree actually does — `init` writes no provider data), `DECISIONS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`. Adding a configuration field now requires a reference row (the guard's inventory check names the miss), and changing a default, range, enum, pattern, override, or §6.4 class fails `make check` until the reference follows — the documentation upkeep rule of AGENTS.md made structural for the configuration surface. Rewording a Validation cell is free as long as the canonical tokens and the leading-`required` convention survive; the guard's negative direction was verified live at landing (a corrupted `server.port` default fails with `server.port Default: expected '8788' to be '8787'`). Changing the table grammar (column set, header wording) or the reference's home is a successor decision. (Correction trail: the task's review round — deepseek-v4.1-flash, one round, REQUEST CHANGES with 2 P1 / 4 P2 / 7 P3, every finding verified against the code before folding — is folded into this entry and the same commit. The P1s: the walk's provider and root levels were name-pinned, so a new provider-level field would have shipped undocumented while every gate stayed green — the walk is now generic (one recursion over properties and array items) with keys assertions at the root and provider levels so any structural growth fails loudly; and the reference repeated D-014's "seeded by `init`" wording although `init`'s assembly writes only `server`/`app` plus the optional account and password (`buildInitConfig`/`init-persist`) — the example config is the sole carrier, reworded here and in the dossier. The P2s: the `QUOTAMETER_` prefix was presented as configuration validation although only `init --yes`'s input boundary enforces it (D-100) and the environment scan rejects unknown names rather than the prefix as such — now stated as the input rule plus namespace guidance; the blanket "value-free problems" claim is scoped (schema and JSON-parse problems never echo values; cross-field messages may quote non-secret values, never secrets); the UI's `apiKeyEnv` marking does not show the variable's name (the account wire shape carries only `keySource: 'environment'`, the card a fixed string) — the claim dropped; and duplicated field rows collapsed silently in the guard's map — the row count is now pinned against the map size. All seven P3s folded: the env-only mode's practical `QUOTAMETER_APP_TIMEZONE` requirement, retention's startup-and-daily cadence, the example-config phrasing beside the seeded `0.5`, the dangling "CLI packaging docs" pointer replaced with the launcher's own fail-closed refusal, per-case message fragments in the cross-field pins, `apiKeyEnv` introduced as a variable name rather than a secret value, and the permission paragraph's refusal conditions completed (foreign ownership, symlinks, wrong type, undeterminable uid). No findings were declined.)

## D-198 — The deployment/operations guide's home in the README, the container-walkthrough verification split, and the command-table drift guard (spec §18; task 188)

**Date:** 2026-11-08 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§18](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#18-documentation-deliverables), [§5](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#5-installation-cli-and-service-lifecycle), [§15](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#15-security), [§11.4](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#114-migrations-and-backup-behavior) · **Tasks:** [188](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-197 (the guide's cross-linking sibling — configuration field tables are linked from the guide, never duplicated, and the D-093 stated-properties guard pattern this entry extends to the README), D-187 (the step-8 init summary whose tunnel/paths contract the guide renders for operators), D-107 (the linger guidance whose exact command the guide reproduces), D-120/D-115 (the Host allowlist and Origin guard whose interaction defines the only working reverse-proxy shape), D-192 (the dead-engine warning the troubleshooting section explains), D-196 (the no-build install proof the installation section cites)

**Decision.** Task 188 completes the §18 README deliverable with three pinned choices. (1) **Home: the guide lives in `README.md` itself**, not a `docs/deployment.md`/`docs/operations.md` page. §18's deliverable line names `README.md` explicitly for exactly this topic list (installation, init prompts, the Z.ai key, multiple accounts, lifecycle/status/logs, system vs user service and linger, VPS deployment, SSH tunnel, nginx/Caddy TLS with `auth.mode: required`, time-zone/polling changes, paths, backups/restores, updates, troubleshooting), the npm front page is where the one-person VPS operator lands first, and a split page would leave the spec's named deliverable without its named home — the same reading D-197 gave its own line (the deliverable names its home; the deep docs it cross-links do not absorb it). The README is restructured operator-first: the new "Install and operate" section group sits between "Key documentation" and "Project status", and the existing development content moves below it unchanged; the guide links to `docs/configuration.md` for every field table (D-197's cross-link-don't-duplicate rule), to `docs/providers/zai-coding-plan.md` for the key/endpoint research, and to `docs/api.md` nowhere it is not needed. The reverse-proxy subsection documents strictly the code-verified contract — `auth.mode: required` because proxy headers always demand a password (the §15.1 presence-only indicator rule of `api/auth.ts`), the public hostname as `server.host` because the §15.3 Host allowlist (`createHostAllowlist`) admits exactly `localhost`/`127.0.0.1`/`[::1]`/the configured host while the Origin guard requires the browser's `Origin` authority to equal the received `Host` (the intersection has exactly one non-loopback solution: the public name as the configured host, preserved by the proxy), `X-Forwarded-Proto` forwarding because the `Secure` cookie verdict rides it (`session-cookie.ts`) — and lands on the **loopback-pin shape**: `/etc/hosts` resolves the public name to `127.0.0.1` and the proxy forwards to `127.0.0.1:8787` with the Host preserved, so the service binds loopback (the D-187 install-time health probe passes, the app port is never public) while the Host/Origin rules still see the public name; the public-address bind variant is documented as inferior with its D-187 false-failure called out. Direct concrete-address binds are documented as working but not recommended, wildcard binds as unusable (the allowlist rejects concrete interface names — D-120's own record). (2) **Verification is the in-container walk-through, honestly split.** The done condition ("a fresh Linux VPS can be configured using only the docs") cannot be executed on a VPS from the development environment, so the walk verifies everything the container genuinely allows and the doc claims nothing the walk did not observe: the complete `--help` surface of every command (compared against the dispatch table), a fresh-directory `init --yes` with an environment-sourced dummy key (the real provider call answering HTTP 401, the honest error-state arm, `0700`/`0600` verified by `stat`, the config storing only the variable name, the step-8 summary with the exact tunnel line), a foreground `run` with `GET /api/health` answering `{"status":"ok","polling":{"running":true}}` (the FSM-4 grant on the §15.1 not-required cell), and `status`/`reload`/`passwd`/`doctor`/`service install`/`logs` executed with their real outcomes recorded — the systemd-less arms included (install refuses with the foreground alternative, logs explains there is no journal, doctor marks `timedatectl` unavailable without failing). The VPS-only remainder — `systemctl enable --now` actually starting a unit, linger keeping a user manager alive, nginx/Caddy serving TLS, and the systemd environment-delivery facilities (`systemctl edit` drop-ins, `environment.d`, `import-environment`) the guide's `apiKeyEnv` path needs — is documented as expectations and templates with explicit honesty notes; no invented URLs, no untested behavior claims. (3) **The guide's drift-prone surface is pinned executably.** `test/unit/readme-command-table.spec.ts` (the D-197/D-093 stated-properties precedent extended to the README) compares the guide's command table row-for-row against `buildCommandTable()` — names, dispatch order, and the exact summaries `--help` prints — asserts exactly one table per expected header and the `init` options table's row count beside its option-set equality in both directions, and pins the operational literals as prose presences: the system unit path from `SYSTEM_UNIT_INSTALL_PATH`, the user unit path from `USER_UNIT_NAME`, the linger and SSH-tunnel commands (the tunnel and the documented defaults derived from `CONFIG_DEFAULTS` and `INIT_RESTART_SEC_SECONDS` rather than duplicated), the `backups/backup-*.sqlite` directory-and-grammar from `AUTOMATIC_BACKUP_DIRNAME`, the `0600`/`0700` modes, and the `quotameter restart` remedy. The guard's bite was verified live twice (a corrupted summary fails the suite; the first mutation attempt's no-op substitution taught the check to assert the substitution itself). Because the test ships with the guide, the docs-only format-only relief does not apply: the task's gate is the full `make check`.

**Reasons.** (1) §18's naming is the deciding fact for the home, exactly as it was for D-197's "a dedicated page" (the spec names its deliverables' homes; the tasking brief's "follow §18's deliverable naming" points the same way), and the operator-first restructure serves the §1 audience — one person on their own VPS — without touching the development documentation below it. (2) The Host-allowlist × Origin-guard × proxy-header interaction is the deployment's least obvious contract: documenting "any nginx config that proxies to 127.0.0.1" would have been the conventional advice and would produce a login-broken deployment (the browser's Origin can never match a rewritten loopback Host), so the guide documents the one shape the code admits, derived from `createHostAllowlist`, `classifyOriginRequest`, `proxyIndicatorPresent`, and the `Secure`-cookie transport facts rather than from proxy-tool folklore. (3) A guard over the command table is warranted where a link-checker would not be: the dispatch table is the surface that has actually churned (tasks 128–145 + U-042 + U-050 each added rows or flags), the project already has both the precedent (D-093, D-197) and the exact comparison source (`buildCommandTable()` is pure data), and a stale flag in an operator guide is precisely the "configured using only the docs" failure the done condition forbids.

**Consequences.** New: `test/unit/readme-command-table.spec.ts`. Changed: `README.md` (the "Install and operate" section group; the development content below it is untouched), `CHANGELOG.md`, `DECISIONS.md`. A command, flag, default, summary rewording, or unit-path change in the CLI now fails `make check` until the guide follows; adding a documented operational literal is a coordinated guide+guard change, the D-197 row-inventory discipline on the command surface. Rewording a Purpose cell is free only by editing both files together. The proxy examples and the systemd environment-delivery steps stay templates until a VPS-shaped verification exists (a successor task owning a real proxy/service deployment may promote them, which would be a successor decision to this entry); the guide deliberately does not document `QUOTAMETER_CLI_ENTRY` or any development-surface variable (D-197's reference owns the vocabulary), and it states no provider-console URLs beyond the dossier-sourced key-list page. Known residual: the walkthrough's provider call exercised the genuine API endpoint with a rejected key — the happy path with a valid key (snapshots, UI charts) remains covered by the E2E suites, not by this doc's verification, which is the operator-facing surface only. (Correction trail: the task's review round — deepseek-v4.1-flash, one round, REQUEST CHANGES with 2 P1 / 4 P2 / 4 P3, every finding verified against the code and the live machine before folding — is folded into this entry and the same commit; no findings were declined. The P1s: the guide's first draft presented `sudo quotameter init` as a system-service install, but a privileged init writes root-owned configuration under root's home and installs nothing (the `system-unit` route only prints the plan — `renderSystemUnitPlan`; D-108's own record that the supported flow is regular-account `init` plus `sudo quotameter service install`), so the system-service bullet now carries that sequence with the user-unit removal step and the sudo-scoped control verbs; and the `apiKeyEnv` quickstart omitted delivery — a systemd unit inherits no shell exports and carries only `Environment=NODE_ENV=production` (the validators reject any other line), so the documented quickstart would have produced a `Not configured` account — the guide now states the `systemctl edit` drop-in / `environment.d` / `import-environment` delivery paths (labeled standard-systemd, container-unverifiable), recommends the config-file key as the simple default, and carries a `Not configured` troubleshooting row. The P2s: the proxy recipe originally bound the public address directly, which falsely fails the install-time loopback health probe (D-187's recorded residual) and leaves the app port public — the loopback `/etc/hosts` pin replaces it; the backup row missed the `backups/` subdirectory (`AUTOMATIC_BACKUP_DIRNAME`, now pinned in the guard); the account secret-source sentence claimed `apiKeyEnv` precedence (the resolvers prefer `apiKey`) and "exactly one" where the enforced rule is at-most-one; and the update/Node-upgrade remedies omitted that unit-kind follows privileges — a plain `service install` beside a system unit would create a second service — so the sequence is branched by scope. The P3s: `reload`'s "reports what applied" softened to the live-vs-restart classification with the service's log line as the authority (D-112), `doctor`'s exit-1 sentence now includes the pre-flight arm (D-119), the direct-bind paragraph now distinguishes concrete addresses (working, not recommended) from wildcards (unusable), and the guard gained the table-count pins, the option-row count pin, and the `CONFIG_DEFAULTS`/`INIT_RESTART_SEC_SECONDS`-derived default pins.)

## D-199 — The Z.ai provider dossier's audit-first completion: evidence conventions, the landed-state summary, and the citation guard (spec §8.3, §9.1, §18; task 189)

**Date:** 2026-11-08 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§8.3](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#83-zai-coding-plan-integration-contract), [§9.1](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#91-official-zai-schedule), [§18](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#18-documentation-deliverables) · **Tasks:** [189](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-038 (the verified source whose claims the audit re-verified), D-040/D-049 (the fixture policies whose corpus the inventory renders), D-042/D-048 (the transport and classification seams the error-behavior summary states), D-043 (the provenance-in-docs precedent this entry's guard extends), D-047 (the mapping contract re-verified line-by-line), D-053 (the two failure surfaces), D-062/D-064/D-189 (the `Retry-After` and suspension behavior summarized as landed), D-137 (the metric catalog the summary adds), D-179 (the timeout wiring), D-197/D-198 (the sibling §18 completions whose guard pattern this entry follows)

**Decision.** Task 189 completes §18's provider-documentation deliverable ("verified API/usage-statistics behavior and peak-hours source") as an **audit-first** round over `docs/providers/zai-coding-plan.md` with three pinned choices. (1) **The dossier stays append-only; a new dated section states the landed state.** The audit classified every claim in the nine dated sections (tasks 093–097, 100, 101, 112, 127) into: (a) backed by in-repo evidence (fixture path, test file, source file, or decision), (b) backed by an external official source with URL and access date, or (c) unbacked. The outcome: **no unbacked claim was found — nothing was removed or reworded**; the two weakest-evidence items (D-047.2's capture-time consumption context, recorded as given evidence; the task-093 ZCode `app.asar` grep counts, a dated observation of a local binary) were already honestly labeled and stand. Re-verification was performed in-repo, no live request to Z.ai: the 096 mapping tables re-checked line-by-line against `mapping.ts`/`snapshot.ts`, the "concrete observed-state outputs" against `sanitized/zai-quota-limit.json`, the transport claims against `transport.ts`, the timeout wiring against `src/server/providers.ts` and `schema/config.schema.json` — all agree. The one staleness class found was tense, not fact: dated sections speaking of then-future tasks in the future tense (task 105's kind→outcome mapping, task 106's retry layer); those sections stay as history, and the new "Contract summary and evidence audit — 2026-11-08 (task 189)" section is the current-state summary — endpoints, authentication, envelope, units and quota mapping, error behavior, configuration knobs, fixtures inventory, peak-hours reference, test map — with every claim's evidence named inline per the dossier's existing convention. The coverage gaps it closes (behaviors shipped after 096 that no dated section described as landed): the §7.2 error behavior (D-048 classification table, D-059 retries 3× 2/4/8 s + ≤500 ms jitter, D-062 `Retry-After` 429-only 0–3600 s, D-064/D-189 suspension with the 60-minute cadence, §7.4 retention D-041/D-051/D-063/D-067), the D-137 metric catalog, and the complete fixtures inventory in one place; D-192's dead-engine observability is explicitly scoped out as engine-level, not provider contract. (2) **Evidence conventions are stated in the dossier itself.** (a) in-repo evidence by exact name, (b) numbered official sources with URL and access date (the peak schedule carries three: 2026-10-28/30/31), (c) assumption-ledger labels (A1–A10) with reopen triggers for everything unverified — nothing inferred is presented as observed, nothing invented (§8.3); a future contract change appends a new dated section and supersedes the summary there, never silently rewriting it. A live re-check of the peak schedule was deliberately not performed (the recorded 2026-10-31 evidence stands; a re-check belongs to a dedicated round against dossier source 15). (3) **The load-bearing claims are pinned executably.** `test/unit/provider-dossier.spec.ts` (the D-043/D-093/D-197/D-198 stated-properties precedent): the four production endpoint URLs appear verbatim as `composeSnapshotUrls(DEFAULT_API_BASE_URL)`/`composeCredentialCheckUrl(DEFAULT_CODING_BASE_URL)` compose them (doc ↔ `provider.ts`); the summary's identities table equals `ZAI_METRIC_CATALOG`'s key/label pairs exactly, in catalog order (doc ↔ `mapping.ts`); the summary's fixtures inventory equals the committed corpus as a set — both directions, 27 files: 3 sanitized + 22 synthetic Z.ai + 2 provider-neutral — and every `test/fixtures/...` path cited anywhere in the dossier exists; every cited test suite exists, with the test map's eight suites (the provider's seven plus the example-config provenance test) required by name inside the summary; every cited `D-NNN` (30 distinct) is a real `DECISIONS.md` heading; and the summary carries the §9.1 essentials (canonical overview URL, teamplan corroborator, the 2026-10-31 latest check, the verbatim window/zone sentence, `multiplier: 1.0`, `offPeakMultiplier: 0.5`). Because the guard ships, the docs-only format-only relief does not apply: the task's gate is the full `make check`.

**Reasons.** The done condition — "no endpoint/schema is described without evidence" — is a property of the whole dossier, so the honest execution is an audit that classifies and reports rather than a rewrite; the audit's result (nothing unbacked) is itself recorded, with the re-verifications named so the claim is checkable. The append-only rule is the dossier's own constitution (its intro), and rewriting dated sections to fix tense would destroy the record-as-of quality that makes it evidence; a summary section that cites the dated sections as provenance gives §18's reader the current contract in one place without amputating history. The guard is warranted by the same drift history that justified D-197/D-198's guards: this very file needed coordinated edits at D-169, D-179, and D-187/D-197 when code changed under it, and its most load-bearing claims (endpoint URLs, metric identities, fixture names) are pure machine-comparable strings — the exact shape where a guard costs nothing and a stale prose claim is a real contract error (a renamed fixture or endpoint would silently orphan the doc's evidence links). The peak-schedule pin extends task 112's own `example-config.spec.ts` precedent rather than duplicating it: the 112 test pins the 112 section's provenance table, the new test pins the summary's §9.1 essentials.

**Consequences.** New: `test/unit/provider-dossier.spec.ts`. Changed: `docs/providers/zai-coding-plan.md` (intro index extended; the task-189 section appended — the only edits), `DECISIONS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`. Renaming a fixture file, changing an endpoint default or the reset-cards query encoding, adding or renaming a metric identity, deleting a cited test, or renumbering decisions now fails `make check` until the dossier follows — the D-197 row-inventory discipline on the provider surface. Adding a fixture requires citing it in the dossier (the inventory's both-directions check names the miss). The summary's prose claims beyond the pinned strings (per-endpoint policy, suspension interplay, retention bounds) remain prose — the D-097/D-198 boundary: a guard pins what is mechanically comparable, not every sentence. A future capture that falsifies a ledger entry still requires the D-047/D-049 successor process (new fixtures, a new dated dossier section) before code changes; the summary section then supersedes itself in that new section. Known residual: the audit verified the dossier against the repository, not against Z.ai's live surface — the sources' continued validity rests on the three recorded checks (latest 2026-10-31) and the 127 section's falsifiers. (Correction trail: the task's review round — deepseek-v4.1-flash, one round, REQUEST CHANGES with 1 P1 / 2 P2 / 4 P3, every finding verified against the code before folding; none declined — is folded into this entry and the same commit. The P1: the summary's suspension bullet omitted the **automatic release on a successful verification probe** (`polling-suspension.ts` releases on any `success` outcome while suspended — the primary recovery path) and mislabeled "every non-auth outcome" a no-op, when the no-op set is the non-**success** non-auth outcomes; the bullet now states all three release events and the exact no-op set. The P2s: one broken in-document anchor (`#peak-hours-official-reference-91-1` → the correct `…-91` slug, the file's only broken one), and the guard's "both directions"/"exactly" claims were one-directional in two places — fixture citation was checked against the whole dossier (nine fixtures are also cited in dated sections, so the new inventory could silently drop them) and the identities check was catalog→doc only — now the inventory's backticked `.json` names must equal the committed corpus as a set inside the summary, the identities table is parsed and compared with the catalog exactly and in order, and the suite citations are scoped to the summary. The P3s: "eight dated sections" → nine; the "(105, 106, 107, 110)" future-tense list trimmed to the two tasks the record actually names; the module-level `expect` moved into tests with a throwing helper and the write-only array removed; "Nothing is inferred" reworded to "nothing inferred is presented as observed" (the ledger's assumptions are labeled inferences); and the error table's timeout/network rows scoped to endpoint 1, since soft endpoints-2/3 failures are absorbed inside the cycle and never reach the classifier or the retry wrapper.)

## D-200 — The example unit files' home, the every-line generator pin, and the representative-value placeholder convention (spec §5.4, §18; task 190)

**Date:** 2026-11-08 · **Status:** Accepted · **Spec:** [§5.4](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#54-systemd-unit-requirements), [§18](plan/SPECIFICATION.md#18-documentation-deliverables) · **Tasks:** [190](plan/tasks.md) · **References:** D-103/D-104 (the generators whose output the examples must track, and the validators' `Environment=`-only-`NODE_ENV` rule the annotations restate), D-107 (the linger guidance the user example quotes), D-093 (the stated-properties-are-structural precedent), D-197/D-198/D-199 (the sibling §18 deliverables whose repo-file guard pattern this entry reuses), D-198 (the README guide section the examples link from, whose environment-delivery documentation the headers point at)

**Decision.** Task 190 completes §18's "example system and user systemd unit files" as `docs/examples/quotameter.service` (system) and `docs/examples/quotameter-user.service` (user), with three pinned choices. (1) **Home.** §18 names the deliverable without naming a path — unlike the README line D-198 kept in `README.md` — so the examples join the docs tree as first-class files rather than code blocks inside a page: they are copy-paste starting points an operator edits, and a file, not a markdown fragment, is what `cp` and editors consume. Distinct names in one directory are a docs-namespace necessity (both units _install_ as `quotameter.service`, in different manager namespaces); each file's header states its install path. The published tarball is untouched — D-194/D-195's manifest allowlist governs it, and docs ship repository-only, "as appropriate" per §18's opening sentence. (2) **"Consistent with the generated units" is an executable every-line pin, not a review assertion.** `test/unit/systemd-unit-examples.spec.ts` (the D-198 `readme-command-table.spec.ts` shape) renders both units through the real `buildSystemUnit`/`buildUserUnit` with one representative input and compares the committed examples against the output after stripping only the annotation layer — full-line comments and blank lines — so every section and directive line is pinned exactly, in order, with zero per-line exceptions: a generator change (a new directive, a reorder, a reworded value) or a hand-edit of either example fails `make check` until the two agree again. The default restart delay derives from `INIT_RESTART_SEC_SECONDS` (the D-198 no-duplication rule). A second leg runs the raw annotated files through `validateSystemUnit`/`validateUserUnit` — the same §5.4 read-back validators `doctor` uses on installed units — proving the annotations remain valid unit syntax and carrying the mechanical no-secrets rule (any `Environment=` line other than `NODE_ENV=production` is a problem, and the generator inputs carry no secret-shaped field at all). Hygiene pins close the guard: exactly one trailing newline, exactly the two files in `docs/examples/`, and both paths linked from the README guide. The guard's bite was verified live in both directions: editing the example's `RestartSec` fails the equality leg, and editing the generator's `UNIT_DESCRIPTION` fails both units' equality legs. (3) **Placeholders are representative concrete values, not `<angle>` markers.** systemd has no template syntax (`$` and `%` are live expansion characters; an unedited `<path>` unit fails cryptically instead of loudly), and byte-exact agreement with the generator is only expressible with concrete values — so the examples are literally the generated units for a documented representative install (service account `quotameter`, Node under `/usr/local`, the default npm global prefix, `RestartSec` at the CLI default), and each header names exactly what to replace (`User=`, both `ExecStart` paths, the `ReadWritePaths` pair) beside the standing advice to prefer `service install`, which fills the values from the machine. No real account data ships: the task-134 fixture account is a real person's and stays in tests. The per-directive annotations (what each line does, why it is there, and — for the §5.4 hardening set — that the set is the contract the project's checks enforce: `doctor` fails a relaxed unit with the `service install` remedy, the validators accept only the exact values, and `ReadWritePaths` is never widenable) state only facts already verified in-repo: D-103/D-104's systemd.exec(7)-checked constraints, the validators' environment rule, D-107's linger command; no new systemd behavior is claimed.

**Reasons.** (1) A file per unit beats an in-page code block for the deliverable's actual use — an operator on a systemd-less bootstrap copies the example to `/etc/systemd/system/` and edits four values; a markdown fragment adds a copy-paste hop and cannot carry a per-file header. (2) The alternative consistency forms are strictly weaker: a review-time diff (the task's literal "reviewed against the generator output") decays the day after the review, a pinned-exceptions comparison (placeholders skipped) lets exactly the lines most likely to be hand-tuned drift silently, and generating the files at build time is banned by the tracked-tree rule (generated output never enters the repository; gotchas.md) — the committed-template-plus-guard form is the project's standing answer (D-093 through D-199) and costs one small suite. (3) Angle-placeholder syntax would either break the equality pin (exceptions again) or break the unit when pasted unedited; representative values make the example simultaneously a working unit shape, an honest picture of what `service install` writes, and byte-comparable — the honest template is the generated artifact itself.

**Consequences.** New: `docs/examples/quotameter.service`, `docs/examples/quotameter-user.service`, `test/unit/systemd-unit-examples.spec.ts`. Changed: `README.md` (two links in "Service scope: system or user, and linger"), `DECISIONS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`. Any generator change in `src/cli/systemd-unit.ts`/`src/cli/systemd-user-unit.ts` (or the `INIT_RESTART_SEC_SECONDS` default) now fails `make check` until the examples follow — the coordinated-change rule D-198 established for the README guide, extended to the unit surface; a D-103/D-104 successor decision must amend the examples in the same task. Rewording an annotation, moving a comment, or re-spacing blank lines is free (the documented unpinned residual: the pin covers the directive skeleton — comment and blank-line placement — not the annotation layer's wording). Adding a third file to `docs/examples/` requires updating the directory pin. The README links are themselves pinned, so the examples cannot be orphaned by a guide edit.
